title: Causes of Death in Veterans With Posttraumatic Epilepsy
abstract: Background and Objectives Veterans with posttraumatic epilepsy (PTE) experience higher rates of mortality compared to those with nontraumatic epilepsy (NTE). An understanding of the causes of death responsible for the difference in mortality would lay the groundwork for mortality-reducing interventions in individuals with PTE. Methods We analyzed a previously identified cohort of Veterans with epilepsy, initially diagnosed from 2005 to 2022. PTE was identified if there was a diagnosis code for traumatic brain injury (TBI) within the 5 years preceding epilepsy diagnosis. Causes of death were identified using the VA/DoD Mortality Data Repository and were classified using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) hierarchy. NTE controls were matched with Veterans with PTE by 2:1 nearest-neighbor matching based on age at onset, sex, and year of diagnosis. Cause-specific hazard ratios were computed using univariate Cox proportional hazards regression. Results A cohort of 210,065 Veterans with epilepsy (median age at onset 61.5 years [IQR 49.4–71.7], 8.3% female) was identified. After matching, covariates were balanced between 28,815 Veterans with PTE (median age at onset 53.6 years [IQR 37.4–65.2], 7.4% female) and 57,630 NTE controls (median age at onset 53.6 years [IQR 37.8–65.2], 8.0% female). The causes of death that were more common in Veterans with PTE compared with NTE controls were injuries (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.84, 95% CI 1.68–2.02), self-harm and interpersonal violence (HR = 1.57, 95% CI 1.37–1.80), stroke (HR = 1.38, 95% CI 1.20–1.59), and dementia (HR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.32–1.58). In contrast, idiopathic epilepsy (HR = 0.60, 95% CI 0.44–0.82) and neoplasms (HR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.63–0.70) were more common among Veterans with NTE. Discussion Veterans with PTE experienced higher mortality due to injuries, stroke, and dementia. These are frequently overrepresented causes of death in epilepsy cohorts, and the present findings clarify that Veterans with PTE are even more vulnerable. The explanations for these findings are likely multifactorial, but the findings are consistent with previously reported associations. Idiopathic epilepsy and neoplasms were less common in PTE, possibly due to competing risks from other causes and because brain tumors are a cause of intractable NTE. Since a Veteran population was analyzed in this study, women and children were underrepresented; furthermore, these results cannot be generalized since the risk factors facing Veterans differ from those experienced by the general population.

title: Association of childhood mild traumatic brain injury with mental and behavioral health outcomes later in life among U.S. Veterans: A LIMBIC-CENC study.
abstract: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is a common injury across all age groups and populations, with a high prevalence among military service members and Veterans. The purpose of this cross-sectional study was to use a large, prospective cohort of Veterans to examine the association between childhood mTBI and multimodal mental and behavioral health outcomes, and among those with childhood mTBI, evaluate sociodemographic characteristics associated with worse outcomes. Data came from the Long-term Impact of Military-relevant Brain Injury Consortium-Chronic Effects of Neurotrauma Consortium (LIMBIC-CENC) prospective longitudinal study. This cohort included 1,286 Veterans, 61.3% of whom sustained a childhood mTBI. After adjustment for demographic, behavioral, and military history factors, Veterans with childhood mTBI had higher PTSD symptom scores (Mean Ratio[MR] = 1.36, 95%CI: 1.22-1.51), higher anger scores (MR = 1.08, 95%CI: 1.05-1.10), higher depression scores (MR = 1.31, 95% CI: 1.17-1.46), higher anxiety scores (mean difference [MD]= 4.3, 95% CI: 2.9-5.6), emotional-behavioral dyscontrol scores (MD = 3.2, 95% CI: 2.2-4.3), worse sleep quality (MD = 1.6, 95% CI: 1.1-2.2), worse neurobehavioral symptoms (MD = 6.8, 95% CI: 5.2-8.5), lower satisfaction with life (MD = -1.2, 95% CI: -2.1 to -0.27), and lower resilience scores (MR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.94-0.99). There were no significant differences after adjustment for alcohol or drug use scores. Among individuals with a history of childhood mTBI, several mental and behavioral health outcomes were worse among those who sustained multiple mTBIs and better among those who were physically active and had higher education. These findings suggest markers of increased riskpresent before military enlistment that may warrant targeted prevention, screening, and treatment strategies. Increased awareness among healthcare providers may help identify Veterans with childhood mTBI history who would benefit from evidence-based treatment and support.

title: Vitiligo-associated variants and genes beyond immune-related loci: A genome-wide association and Mendelian randomization meta-analysis.
abstract: Although past genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified over 50 susceptible loci associated with vitiligo risk, few have systematically explored causality among potentially associated variants and genes. To address this, we analyzed summary statistics from 3 large-scale genomic resources, including the Million Veteran Program, United Kingdom Biobank, and FinnGen. Cases were defined using ICD-9 code 709.01 or ICD-10 code L80, including all studies that contributed genome-wide summary statistics and limiting analyses to loci with ≥1 common variant (minor allele frequency ≥1%). METAL was used to conduct a fixed effects inverse variance-weighted meta-analysis with kinship adjustment. Variant-to-gene (V2G) mapping was performed using the Open Targets V2G framework. Potentially causal effects were assessed using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and genome-wide significant protein and expression quantitative trait locus instruments across 16 datasets. Genome-wide significance was defined as P < 5 x 10-8. Among 3,134 vitiligo cases and 1,383,912 controls, 5,482 genome-wide significant variants were identified, mapping to 23 distinct loci. MR found 18 potentially causative genes, 5 of which had not been previously associated with vitiligo: GDF11, ACO2, MEI1, OR2W1-AS1, GABBR1. To our knowledge, this study identifies several previously unreported potentially causal variants and genes associated with vitiligo, as well as pathogenic pathways beyond autoimmunity.

title: A living systematic review, meta-analysis, and open data resource of trials of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD.
abstract: 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) has emerged as a potential treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). However, rapidly changing evidence in a fast-moving field can be challenging to integrate. Here, we present a living systematic review and open-data meta-analytic resource on MDMA treatment for PTSD. In this initial release, 6 randomized controlled trials comprising 286 participants are included in the database. All six studies included in the review to date are sponsored by the Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies (MAPS). Our primary model uses inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis of standardized mean differences on primary outcomes of PTSD. Compared to control conditions, MDMA-assisted therapy (MDMA-AT) showed a greater reduction in PTSD symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.71). Meta-regressions on dosing variables were explored. Treatment with MDMA-AT as compared to placebo also resulted in higher response (risk ratio [RR] = 1.35) and remission (RR = 2.25) rates. Most studies included in the database had a low risk of bias according to Cochrane guidelines, though these fail to capture pertinent challenges in the field such as expectancy, functional unblinding, potential issues with study conduct, and safety. The current findings were assigned an overall low certainty rating using the GRADE approach. Together, this systematic review and meta-analysis suggests that MDMA-AT results in short-term decreases in PTSD symptoms across studies to date. This living systematic review, meta-analysis, database, and online dashboard ( sypres.io ) will continue to be updated as evidence emerges, providing a valuable, open, and transparent resource for researchers in a rapidly evolving field.

title: Multi-center, randomized controlled efficacy and comparative-effectiveness study evaluating ketamine, stellate ganglion blocks, combination treatment, and sham treatments for posttraumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injury-associated headache: a study protocol.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and traumatic brain injury (TBI) are conditions that share common mechanisms and are highly co-prevalent with each other and chronic pain. This pragmatic study will compare ketamine infusions to stellate ganglion blocks (SGB), their combination, and a placebo-sham-controlled arm.
METHODS: A double-blind study conducted at 3 U.S. and Ukrainian sites will be performed. Two hundred ten patients with PTSD and/or TBI-associated headache will be allocated in a 2:2:2:1 ratio to receive SGB/placebo ketamine, ketamine/sham SGB, ketamine/SGB, and placebo/sham. The bivariate co-primary outcome will evaluate change in Headache Impact Test and PTSD Checklist depending on diagnosis, at 4 weeks. Participants who experience a positive binary outcome will remain in the study through 6 months or until their outcome becomes negative.
DISCUSSION: Because PTSD and TBI have no discrete pathophysiological mechanisms and are co-prevalent with pain and psychopathology, they are associated with poor outcomes, polypharmacy, and high non-adherence rates, indicating a need for minimally invasive treatments that obviate these barriers. Whereas both therapies have evidence underpinning efficacy, results in clinical trials are conflicting. This study will provide real-world evidence in generalizable populations on the efficacy and comparative-effectiveness of ketamine and SGB, alone and in combination, with the possibility of changing clinical guidelines.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT06608277.

title: Tele-Emergency Care Reduced Emergency Department Visits and Shifted Care to Primary Care Settings in the Veterans Affairs System.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of tele-emergency care (TEC) on emergency department (ED) use, downstream care, and costs among patients triaged as needing urgent evaluation.
STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We studied TEC within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) using a regression discontinuity design that exploited brief, routine operational pauses in TEC availability. Patients who called a nurse advice line shortly before a pause were substantially more likely to receive TEC than otherwise comparable patients who called shortly after the pause began.
DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: We used VHA records, including VA-provided and VA-paid community care encounters, for 35,249 nurse triage calls with an urgent recommendation placed during business hours at VA facilities offering TEC between December 2023 and June 2025.
PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Calling just after a pause began raised the probability of an ED visit within 3 days by 7.5 percentage points (baseline, 45.8%). Scaling by the first stage, TEC reduced ED visits within 3 days by 27.5 percentage points, with the reduction concentrated at VA-paid community care facilities (-18.4 percentage points). TEC increased primary care visits within 7 days by 9.3 percentage points. Thirty-day mortality and inpatient admission were unchanged. Total 30-day health care costs were not significantly different (+$983 per recipient; SE, $822).
CONCLUSIONS: Tele-emergency care reduced avoidable ED visits and redirected patients toward primary care without detectable effects on mortality or admission. Health systems should consider TEC to redirect avoidable ED visits.

title: Rifamycin use and gut microbial antibiotic resistance genes in cirrhosis: Results from a double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) carriage is associated with poor outcomes in patients with liver cirrhosis, which is worsened by repeated antibiotic exposure and hospitalizations. While the semi-synthetic rifamycin derivative, rifaximin, has recently been linked to ARG expansion preclinically, the effects of rifamycin SV MMX (RiVM) on the gut resistome remain unknown. We evaluated longitudinal resistome changes with RiVM in cirrhosis. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RIVET trial (15 RiVM, 15 placebo) included compensated cirrhosis patients who underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing before/after 30 days of therapy. ARGs were annotated using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database. The longitudinal resistome was evaluated using univariable and multi-variable methods (LEfSe, paired-Wilcoxon testing, and MaAsLin3), and machine learning (ML) was used to determine ARG changes at subject and group levels. RiVM induced minimal perturbation of the gut resistome, without significant change in ARGs versus after FDR adjustment. Complementary approaches (univariable and multivariable) identified a trend towards lower vancomycin resistance ARGs, including vanW and vanT operon-associated genes, after RiVM exposure. In contrast, several Enterobacteriaceae-associated multidrug efflux regulators (including evgS, emrK, and mdtA) showed nominal increases post-rifamycin that did not withstand FDR. Group-level ML demonstrated limited discrimination between groups; however, within-subject longitudinal models achieved improved classification performance. No increase in infections or treatment-related safety concerns was observed. We conclude that rifamycin MMX was not associated with infections and did not enrich antimicrobial resistance genes compared to placebo in a small randomized 30-day clinical trial in patients with compensated cirrhosis. There was a tendency towards reduced vancomycin resistance and ARG reduction after rifamycin exposure. Registration: NCT04082780 www.clinicaltrials.gov.

title: Abstract 4672: Validation of the PREVENT-HF Risk Prediction Equation in the Veterans Health Administration
abstract: Background: Accurate prediction of heart failure (HF) risk is critical to prioritize high-risk individuals for primary prevention. The American Heart Association's PREVENT-HF equation was developed to predict 10-year HF risk, but its performance in populations with disproportionately high cardiovascular disease burden, such as US Veterans, is not well characterized. We sought to validate the PREVENT-HF equation for prediction of incident HF among Veterans without known HF or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Methods: We constructed a retrospective national cohort of Veterans aged 30-79 years as of 1/1/2012 using electronic health record data from the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) and Medicare. Inclusion required at least one outpatient visit between 2009 and 2011 and documented blood pressure, weight, height, cholesterol, and creatinine during that period. We excluded individuals with known HF or ASCVD. Incident HF was defined as one primary inpatient or two total inpatient/outpatient ICD HF diagnosis codes in VHA or Medicare data. We assessed calibration by comparing model-predicted versus observed 10-year probability of incident HF. We tested discrimination with Wolber's C-statistic in a time-to-event framework accounting for the competing risk of all-cause death. Calibration and discrimination were calculated overall and by rurality, sex, race, ethnicity, and diabetes status. Results: The cohort comprised 1,990,002 Veterans (23.1% rural/highly rural; 8.8% female; self-identified race and ethnicity: 0.8% Asian, 19.5% Black, 0.9% Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, 70.1% White, 5.4% Hispanic; 20.1% with diabetes). Over 10 years of follow-up, we observed 160,400 incident HF cases (incidence rate: 8.9 cases/1,000 person-years). The PREVENT-HF equation demonstrated excellent calibration (slope: 1.03, 95% CI 1.02-1.05; Figure ) and good discrimination (C-statistic: 0.81, 95% CI 0.80-0.82). The equation performed similarly in urban and rural Veterans but underpredicted risk in female Veterans and those without diabetes and overpredicted risk in Asian and Hispanic Veterans ( Table ). Conclusion: The PREVENT-HF equation demonstrated excellent overall calibration and good discrimination in a national cohort of nearly two million Veterans, a high-risk population within the nation’s largest integrated healthcare system. However, performance varied by sociodemographic characteristics. Validation of HF prediction models in diverse populations is a prerequisite for effective primary HF prevention, a critical need given the rising morbidity, mortality, and costs associated with this prevalent disease and the availability of proven therapeutics that reduce HF risk.

title: Multivariate genome-wide association study of post-traumatic stress disorder, alcohol use, and alcohol use disorders.
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) commonly co-occurs with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Comorbid PTSD and AUD is associated with poorer outcomes including worse treatment prognosis and significant physical health consequences. Both PTSD and AUD are polygenic in nature and genetically overlap. Previous work showed negative or non-significant associations between PTSD and alcohol consumption but positive genetic associations between PTSD and AUD. This work highlights the need for more nuanced examination of the similarities and distinctions in the associations between PTSD and alcohol consumption versus AUD. We leveraged the latest large-scale GWAS data to perform a multivariate GWAS of alcohol consumption (ALCC), problematic alcohol use (ALCP), and PTSD using GenomicSEM. Partial genetic correlations revealed that ALCP and PTSD were associated with each other (rG = 0.39, p = 4.38 × 10-60) and with other psychiatric problems, medical conditions, and pain, while ALCC was only weakly correlated with PTSD (rG = -0.08, p = 2.03 × 10-4) and uncorrelated with most traits after accounting for its genetic overlap with ALCP and PTSD. We examined associations between GenomicSEM-derived polygenic scores (PGS) and their corresponding phenotypes in participants from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism (COGA). PGS for ALCC were unrelated to PTSD diagnosis and PGS for PTSD were unrelated to drinks in a typical week. PTSD is more strongly related to alcohol problems, and much of the overlap in PTSD and consumption is accounted for by its overlap with alcohol problems. These results help demonstrate the complex partial overlaps of PTSD, AUD, and alcohol consumption.

title: Perturbation-based propagation of bacterial composition uncertainty improves robustness and reproducibility of microbiome differential abundance analysis
abstract: Abstract Differential abundance (DA) analysis remains the analytical bottleneck of microbiome science; despite dozens of available methods, results remain poorly reproducible across tools, datasets, and study designs. Three intertwined challenges drive this failure: compositional data structure, stochastic count uncertainty, and complex experimental design; yet no existing method addresses all three simultaneously. Here, we introduce PARALLAX (Perturbation-based Assessment of Robustness Across Latent Logical Axes), a unified DA framework that resolves this gap by propagating compositional uncertainty through per-replicate linear mixed modeling across a structured scale perturbation grid, then summarizes inference through two stability-based metrics: P post (effect consistency across Monte Carlo replicates) and R scale (robustness to scale perturbation). PARALLAX retains uncertainty through the complete inferential pipeline while natively supporting repeated measures and multifactorial designs. Under repeated subsampling, PARALLAX identified fully stable DA taxa in 14.4% of cases, versus 1.7% and 0% for comparators. We applied PARALLAX to two independent longitudinal shotgun metagenomic datasets from mechanistically distinct mouse models: Gulf War toxicant exposure and repetitive head trauma. In both, PARALLAX resolved robust, sex-specific, and time-dependent genus-level shifts while accommodating repeated measures and multifactorial design, tasks that challenged both comparator frameworks. PARALLAX is released as an open-source, AI-compatible R workflow, lowering the barrier to rigorous microbiome DA analysis across complex study designs. Importance Microbiome studies link gut microbes to immune, metabolic, and neurological health, but identifying microbes that truly change with disease or treatment remains difficult. Differential abundance results often vary across computational tools because microbiome data are noisy, sparse, and compositional, especially in longitudinal or multifactorial studies. This instability limits reproducibility and creates difficulty in prioritizing microbes for biological interpretation. PARALLAX addresses this gap by focusing on consistency rather than relying on a single model fit. It analyzes data under multiple plausible representations that capture uncertainty in counts and composition, then identifies bacteria with consistent effects using stability and robustness metrics. Using ground-truth simulations and two mechanistically distinct mouse models, Gulf War toxicant exposure and traumatic brain injury, PARALLAX recovers microbial signals that remain reliable across complex study designs. This open-source R workflow provides a more reproducible path from microbiome sequencing to biological insight.

title: Posttraumatic stress disorder evidence-based psychotherapy utilization among lesbian, gay, bisexual, and queer veterans receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to evaluate sexual orientation-based differences in utilization of cognitive processing therapy (CPT) and prolonged exposure therapy (PE) among veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration.
METHOD: Data were extracted from the Veterans Health Administration electronic health records of veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder identified as lesbian, gay, bisexual, or queer (LGBQ) or heterosexual. Veterans were matched 3:1 using propensity score matching, yielding an analytic sample of 114,372 veterans (25% LGBQ). The odds of utilizing CPT or PE and achieving the minimum dose (i.e., eight or more sessions), adjusting for service connection, military sexual trauma, and Charlson Comorbidity Index score, were examined.
RESULTS: LGBQ veterans had higher rates of military sexual trauma, higher Charlson Comorbidity Index scores, and a lower likelihood of being service-connected at 51%-100% compared to heterosexual veterans. LGBQ veterans had higher odds of any CPT utilization (adjusted odds ratios = 1.13, 95% CI [1.06, 1.20], p < .001) and PE utilization (adjusted odds ratios = 1.24, 95% CI [1.11, 1.37], p < .001). In adjusted analyses, there was no relationship between sexual orientation and achievement of minimum dose of CPT or PE.
CONCLUSIONS: LGBQ veterans are accessing evidence-based treatments for posttraumatic stress disorder in the Veterans Health Administration at higher rates compared to heterosexual veterans, but receipt of a minimum dose for either treatment is low for both LGBQ and heterosexual veterans. title: CYP2D6-Guided Opioid Therapy for Chronic Pain: A Multi-Center Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: The analgesic effectiveness of several opioids depends on CYP2D6-mediated metabolism to more active opioid receptor agonists. CYP2D6 activity is impacted by genetic variability and medications that inhibit CYP2D6. We conducted a pragmatic, multi-center, randomized, controlled trial to determine whether CYP2D6-guided opioid prescribing improves chronic pain. Participants were adults recruited from primary care or pain specialty clinics with at least 3 months of chronic pain treated or considered for treatment with tramadol, hydrocodone, or codeine. Participants were randomized to the usual care or CYP2D6-guided arm, in which CYP2D6 pharmacogenetic testing was performed. Healthcare professionals were recommended to avoid tramadol, hydrocodone, or codeine in patients with CYP2D6 intermediate or poor or ultra-rapid (for safety) metabolizer phenotypes based on either genotype or drug interactions. The primary outcome was the change in composite pain intensity scores from baseline to 3 months. Of 1048 enrolled participants, 282 had an actionable CYP2D6 phenotype. In this group, CYP2D6-guided recommendations did not improve the change in composite pain intensity scores from baseline to 3 months compared with usual care (mean [SD] -0.8 [2.4] vs. -0.7 [2.3]) or improve drug-gene concordance (26.8% vs. 27.1%) in the CYP2D6-guided versus usual care arm, respectively. In an exploratory analysis, participants whose therapy changed to align with their CYP2D6 phenotype had significantly improved pain scores. In conclusion, incorporating CYP2D6-guided recommendations for opioid therapy into routine practice did not change prescribing sufficiently to assess its impact on chronic pain control, suggesting that EHR-integrated CYP2D6 guidance is insufficient to change opioid prescribing for chronic pain.

title: Association between telehealth utilization and buprenorphine treatment retention among rural Veterans with opioid use disorder.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Opioid use disorder (OUD) remains a major public health challenge that disproportionately impacts Veterans, 34% of whom live rurally. Buprenorphine medication treatment for OUD (B-MOUD) is a first-line treatment and telehealth expansion has improved its access. This study aimed to determine whether the extent of telehealth use is associated with differences in B-MOUD retention among rural Veterans with OUD.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of rural Veterans who initiated B-MOUD within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) from 2021 to 2024. Telehealth utilization within a B-MOUD episode of care (EoC) was categorized based on the proportion of encounters delivered via telehealth (TH): no TH (0%), minority TH (>0%&≤50%), and majority TH (>50%). Retention was measured as the number of days from EoC start to treatment discontinuation (final day covered before >30-day gap). Restricted mean retention time (RMRT), defined as the mean time retained in treatment up to 90- and 180-days, was estimated using adjusted Kaplan-Meier curves.
RESULTS: There were 10,875 B-MOUD EoC among 7012 Veterans. At 90 days, RMRT was 73.0(95% CI 72.0-73.3) days for no TH, 82.6(81.9-83.0) for minority TH, and 82.6(82.0-82.9) for majority TH groups. At 180 days, RMRT was 115.1(112.7-116.2), 148.3(146.4-149.4), and 143.2(141.4-144.2) days, respectively. Median number of days to discontinuation was longest for minority (338[314-366]), followed by majority (247[233-269]) and no TH (119[113-126]) groups.
CONCLUSION: Telehealth utilization was associated with greater B-MOUD retention compared to no telehealth utilization among rural Veterans, with the highest retention observed when telehealth comprised ≤ 50% of visits, supporting the value of flexible, multimodal care delivery.

title: Co-designing embodied extended reality telehealth for veteran mental health: from movement care to whole health.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Veterans in rural and underserved communities face persistent care barriers from provider shortages, travel burdens, and the digital divide. Within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the Clinical Resource Hub (CRH) National Telehealth Program delivers primary, mental health, specialty, surgical, and rehabilitative care into veterans' homes and rural clinics, while VA Immersive scales extended reality (XR) across the system. Embodied XR telehealth, where provider and patient meet as full-body avatars in a shared immersive environment, intersects these programs and introduces new design requirements. This study extends our embodied XR codesign series from physical rehabilitation to mental health and whole health.
METHODS: Stakeholders from VA, academia, and industry ( N = 30 ), drawn from Boise and other participating CRHs, joined a 3-day codesign at the Boise VA Medical Center in June 2026, including shadowing telehealth workflows, a full-day workshop with five teams, and a half-day debrief with program leads. Seven usability task ratings, 164 four-axis ideas (Raise, Reduce, Eliminate, Create), 95 debrief proposals, 188 prioritization votes, and 19 discussion transcripts were analyzed through descriptive statistics and reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Perceived task ease was high among a cohort with mixed VR experience across seven tasks (tutorial, joining a telehealth room, exercise completion, movement recording, environment and interactable customization, and spatial drawing), each above 4.1 of 5 on the Single Ease Question, led by customizing virtual environments ( M = 4.84 ± 0.37 ). Stakeholders most endorsed minimalist defaults, onboarding resources, and out-of-the-box readiness, followed by embodiment with personalized environments, disability representation, and veteran identity markers. The debrief prioritized breathing and grounding, graded exposure, psychoeducation, and whole-health movement, delivered through headsets paired to an in-clinic tablet or monitored home deployment. Infrastructure compatibility, workforce fit, and governance emerged as pervasive constraints. Workshop satisfaction was high ( M = 4.82 ± 0.53 of 5) with 88% requesting follow-up; platform-specific ratings were favorable but lower and more variable (e.g., user-friendliness M = 3.76 ± 0.97 of 5).
DISCUSSION: We propose candidate design principles for extending an embodied XR telehealth platform, built for physical rehabilitation, to mental health and whole health care for veterans, and discuss implications for platform design, piloting, and deployment.

title: Abstract 6548: Sodium Glucose Co-Transporter Inhibitors and Limb Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Target Trial Emulation
abstract: Introduction: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are at increased risk of cardiovascular events, and this risk is further magnified in those with concomitant diabetes. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated profound cardiovascular benefits in diabetes. However, their benefit in patients with PAD remains uncertain because of increased risk of limb amputation observed in the CANVAS trial. Methods: We emulated a sequence of 47 target trials using data from the Peripheral Artery Disease: Long-term Survival (PEARLS) study, a longitudinal registry of Veterans with PAD defined based on abnormal ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices. The registry captures rich data on demographics, co-morbidities, laboratory studies, vital signs and dispended medications, with comprehensive follow up using VA, community care and Medicare data. Starting January 1 2018, a clinical trial was emulated each month among patients with PAD and diabetes comparing those initiating SGLT2i with controls during the month. The primary outcome was limb event defined as chronic limb threatening ischemia or major amputation. Cardiovascular event, defined as hospitalization for myocardial infarction or stroke, was a confirmatory endpoint. Patients were censored if they were lost to follow up or died. Trial components are outlined in Table 1. We estimated the observational analogue of the intention-to-treat (ITT) effect using a pooled logistic regression model including baseline and time-varying covariates with inverse probability of censoring weights applied to outcome data. To estimate per-protocol (PP) effect, we additionally applied inverse probability treatment weights to outcome data to account for confounders of non-adherence. Both analyses adjusted for a total of 41 confounders. Results: Among 782,697 person-trials, 4,977 were in the SGLT2i arm and 777,620 were in the usual care arm. Baseline demographics were similar between the groups, but SGLT2i users had higher Hba1c levels, were on more antidiabetic medications, and had higher rates of most co-morbidities especially coronary artery disease and heart failure. Our ITT analysis demonstrated a 17% reduction in cardiovascular events in the SGLT2i arm (HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.76 - 0.90). In the PP analysis, we found a similar effect (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.71 - 0.88). In both ITT and PP analyses, there was no effect of SGLT2i on limb events. Conclusion: In a real-word population of Veterans with established PAD and diabetes, SGLT2i reduced rates of cardiovascular events, with effect estimates comparable to major randomized controlled trials, but had no impact on limb events. Despite prior concerns regarding amputation risk, providers should consider the use of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with PAD based on overall clinical context, especially given significant evidence of cardiovascular benefit.

title: A generalizable deep learning model for predicting opioid use disorder using language modeling for cross-EHR data harmonization
abstract: Abstract The opioid use disorder (OUD) epidemic in the United States has been a major public health crisis. We developed OUD-REY ( OUD R isk E valuator at 1 Y ear) - a deep learning model that uses longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from the All of Us research program to predict risk of OUD at one year for patients with an opioid prescription. On internal validation, OUD-REY achieved an AUROC of 91.2% and AUPRC of 77.0%. We leveraged a pretrained language model to accommodate thousands of unseen, out-of-vocabulary clinical features in a patient’s longitudinal EHR history. We externally validated our model on a new dataset released by All of Us that was temporally separated from our development set and on a dataset containing ~6 million patients from medical centers of the Veterans Affairs (VA) nationwide over a span of 20 years. On external validation, our model had an AUROC and AUPRC of 86.4% and 23.1% (OUD prevalence of 2.9%), respectively, on our temporally separated All of Us validation set. It had an AUROC and AUPRC of 85.5% and 19.5% (OUD prevalence of 3.5%), respectively, on the VA dataset. Our fairness auditing showed that the model was generally fair for patients with different genders, race, and ethnic backgrounds. This model may potentially improve prevention and care of OUD.

title: Alzheimer's disease target and drug discovery by leveraging multiomics and electronic health data.
abstract: Despite prolific genomic data from individuals with Alzheimer's disease (AD), translation into treatments has lagged. Here we applied Mendelian randomization to multiple AD genome-wide association studies and functional multiomics datasets to nominate druggable targets, identifying 19 targets for individuals of European ancestry and 7 for African ancestry. This included epoxide hydrolase 2 (EPHX2), for which we identified a protective missense variant (p.Arg287Gln). Experiments in induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons and cerebral organoids from patients with AD validated the protective role of p.Arg287Gln via reduced levels of EPHX2 and phosphorylated tau (pTau-181). Pharmacological inhibition of EPHX2 improved cognitive performance in the 5xFAD mouse model of AD. Finally, by leveraging electronic health data from 111,680 patients with mild cognitive impairment, we identified 12 drugs associated with reduced AD incidence, including trazodone (targeting ADRA1A) and baclofen (targeting GABBR1). Thus, integrating multiomics data, functional validation and electronic health data identifies new approaches for treating AD.

title: Common Genetic Variants Near SLC2A2 and Glycemic Response to Glimepiride in the GRADE Comparative Effectiveness Clinical Trial
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Optimizing second-line therapy for type 2 diabetes remains challenging because of interindividual variability in response. Current treatment selection does not consider personal genetic profiles. To address this gap, we conducted a pharmacogenomic genome-wide association study (GWAS) in a randomized comparative effectiveness trial to identify genetic predictors of glycemic response to insulin glargine, glimepiride, liraglutide, and sitagliptin when added to metformin. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In the Glycemia Reduction Approaches in Type 2 Diabetes: A Comparative Effectiveness Study (GRADE), we performed a GWAS for the time to reach primary (glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c] ≥7%) and secondary (HbA1c >7.5%) metabolic failure. We conducted replication in independent cohorts, performed fine mapping of the top variants near SLC2A2, evaluated them for physiologic impact using oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT) and response to acute glipizide challenge, and characterized glycemic response to glimepiride in an slc2a2-mutated zebrafish model. RESULTS: rs2129019 in SLC2A2 encoding GLUT2 was enriched in African/African American participants and conferred a 38% increased risk of metabolic failure per A allele on glimepiride (P = 1.55 × 10-8). Carriers had impaired β-cell function, evidenced by a lower C-peptide index during OGTT, and diminished glucose-lowering response to acute sulfonylurea challenge. Genetic manipulation in zebrafish confirmed that slc2a2 disruption attenuated the glucose-lowering effect of glimepiride. CONCLUSIONS: Genetic variation influences glycemic response to glucose-lowering medications, with SLC2A2 emerging as a genetic factor that modulates sulfonylurea response. These findings warrant further study to evaluate whether low-response allele carriers would benefit from alternative glucose-lowering therapies to advance precision diabetes care.

title: Abstract 11766: Multi-Ancestry Genomic Analyses in Over 4 Million Individuals Prioritize Putative Drug Targets for Heart Failure and Its Major Subtypes
abstract: Background: Heart failure (HF) is a major contributor to global morbidity and mortality with limited options for primary prevention. Although disease-modifying therapies exist for both HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), the treatment landscape remains less established for HFpEF, and substantial residual morbidity and mortality persist across both subtypes. Multi-ancestry genomic analyses provide a framework for elucidating biological mechanisms that inform drug target prioritization for HF and its subtypes, while distinguishing subtype-specific disease architecture. Methods: We conducted a multi-ancestry genome-wide association study (GWAS) of HF, including 344,838 cases and 4.12 million controls of European, African, Asian, Hispanic, and Admixed American populations, from the Million Veteran Program (MVP), large biobanks, and international consortia, as well as subtype-specific GWAS of HFpEF (47,192 cases and 1.5 million controls) and HFrEF (46,934 cases and 1.7 million controls). We subsequently conducted large-scale, systematic proteome- and transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization analyses and leveraged orthogonal biological evidence to prioritize genes relevant to HF and cardiomyopathy biology. Results: Across HF, HFrEF, and HFpEF, we identified 383 genomic risk loci (166 novel) and 568 putative causal genes (375 novel), substantially expanding the genetically supported landscape of these conditions. Among these, 125 genes were characterized as druggable or potentially druggable, including 16 that are targets of approved or investigational cardiovascular therapies. We identified novel associations at GUCY1A1 , ATP1B2 , and PDE3A , which encode targets of vericiguat, digoxin, and milrinone, respectively. Inflammation and metabolism, among others, emerged as promising therapeutic targets. The scale of these multi-omic analyses enables high-resolution characterization of the biological pathways implicated in HF pathogenesis. Conclusions: This study represents the largest genomic investigation of all-cause HF, HFrEF, and HFpEF to date. We substantially expanded the catalog of associated genetic loci, identified repurposing opportunities for existing cardiovascular therapies, and highlight the distinct genetic architectures underlying HFrEF and HFpEF, providing a framework for prioritizing novel therapeutic targets for HF prevention and management.

title: X and Y chromosomes as determinants of aging and disease.
abstract: Sex differences have traditionally been attributed to gonadal hormones, but accumulating evidence shows that sex chromosomes exert distinct, cell-autonomous effects on health, aging, and disease. XX and XY complements alter gene dosage, epigenetic programming, immune signaling, metabolism, and cellular stress responses, which shape aging and disease trajectories in women and men. This Review integrates mechanistic advances in sex chromosome biology-including escape from X chromosome inactivation, X reactivation, parent-of-X-origin, X-skew, X- and Y-linked gene functions, and Y loss-with aging, neurologic disease, immunity, cancer, and cardiometabolic disease. We highlight insights from mouse models, human studies, and emerging technologies that disentangle hormone-driven effects from chromosome-mediated effects and discuss translational implications for diagnostics, biomarkers, therapeutics, and clinical trial design, emphasizing the integration of sex chromosome biology into precision medicine.

title: Telemedicine in Rheumatology in the United States: A Scoping Review of Modalities, Outcomes, and Costs in Support of a Hybrid Model of Care.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shortages and geographic maldistribution of rheumatologists limit access to rheumatology care in the United States. Tele-rheumatology grew from targeted rural and Veterans Affairs programs into mainstream practice during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, and its postpandemic role remains unsettled.
OBJECTIVE: To map the modalities, settings, and reported outcomes of telemedicine in US rheumatology.
DESIGN: Scoping review following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (Supplemental Digital Content 1, https://links.lww.com/RHU/A996) reporting.
SETTING: MEDLINE/PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched.
PARTICIPANTS: Sixty US reports from 48 programs involving adults and children with rheumatic diseases, caregivers, and rheumatology clinicians.
INTERVENTION: Video and telephone visits, clinic-to-clinic telemedicine, electronic consultation (eConsult), remote monitoring, and hybrid care.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Access, clinical effectiveness, patient and clinician experience, cost, safety, and equity.
RESULTS: Telemedicine reduced travel and patient-borne costs, improved appointment completion, and shortened the path to specialist input through eConsult triage. Disease activity was comparable to in-person care in established patients, and structured telephone and e-visit programs improved gout treatment targets. In the largest randomized trial, satisfaction and medication toxicity monitoring were lower with telemedicine; remote joint assessment remained unreliable; and uptake was lower among older, non-English-speaking, Black, and low-income patients. Health-system savings are unproven.
LIMITATION: Predominantly observational, pandemic-influenced evidence.
CONCLUSION: Telemedicine complements rather than replaces in-person rheumatology care. A hybrid model anchored by face-to-face evaluation, with structured visit selection and safety monitoring, should be tested in pragmatic trials with full economic and equity evaluation.

title: Abstract 13694: Notification of High-Risk Veterans for Access to Heart Failure Prevention: Design of the NOVA-HF Trial
abstract: Background: Rural populations experience higher rates of incident heart failure (HF) and reduced access to cardiovascular care. Evidence-based therapies can reduce HF risk, but they remain underutilized in high-risk populations. We designed the Notification Of High-Risk Veterans for Access to Heart Failure Prevention (NOVA-HF) trial to test a risk-guided strategy to improve uptake of preventive therapies among rural Veterans. Methods: NOVA-HF is a pragmatic randomized controlled trial conducted within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Electronic health records data were used to identify rural Veterans aged 30-79 years without documented HF or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with a primary care visit and no cardiology visit within the prior 2 years. Veterans will be prioritized for enrollment based on predicted 10-year HF risk calculated by the PREVENT-HF equation and a novel prevention opportunity score, identifying opportunities to initiate or intensify evidence-based preventive therapies (Table 1). Participants will be randomized 2:1:1 to: (1) usual care; (2) notification of elevated HF risk to Veterans and their primary care providers with pended cardiology referrals (“notification”); or (3) notification plus care navigator outreach. Randomization will continue until 100 Veterans in the intervention arms have been referred to cardiology. The primary outcome will be the number of new preventive therapies initiated or intensified at 6 months. Secondary outcomes will include cardiology referral completion, changes in cardiovascular risk factors, medication adherence, and implementation outcomes. The intervention will be tested in the VHA region including northern and central California, Nevada, Hawaii, and the Pacific Islands. Results: Among 640,417 eligible rural Veterans nationally on 1/1/2026, the quintile with the highest HF risk included 128,083 Veterans with a mean predicted 10-year HF risk of 21.6% (SD 0.07%). Mean age was 74 years (SD 5.4) with 15% living in highly rural regions and 41% diagnosed with diabetes, 15% with chronic kidney disease, 47% with obesity, 62% with hypertension, 37% with hyperlipidemia, and 44% with tobacco use (Table 2). The mean prevention opportunity score was 2.9 (SD 1.7). Conclusions: NOVA-HF is a pragmatic randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate whether HF risk stratification, combined with patient and provider notification and facilitated early cardiology referral, can increase uptake of evidence-based preventive therapies among rural Veterans. Eligible Veterans at highest risk had a substantial burden of comorbidities and multiple opportunities to optimize preventive care. The intervention to be tested represents a scalable strategy for risk-based primary HF prevention in underserved populations within integrated health systems.

title: Abstract 10657: Association Between AHA’s Life’s Essential 8 Score and Telomere Length in the VA’s Million Veteran Program
abstract: Background: Telomeres are repetitive DNA sequences located at chromosome ends that protect chromosomal integrity and shorten with aging. Leukocyte telomere length (LTL) is a marker of biological aging and has been associated with cardiovascular disease risk. We examined the association between LTL and the American Heart Association’s Life’s Essential 8 (LE8) score and its individual components. Methods: This cohort included VA Million Veteran program (MVP) participants with whole-genome sequencing data who completed the MVP Lifestyle Survey to derive LE8 score (0-100; higher = better cardiovascular health). LTL was estimated using the bioinformatic tool TelSeq from existing whole-genome sequencing data. Age-residualized LTL was used in linear and logistic regression analyses to assess associations with LE8 score, LE8 categories (low, moderate, high), and LE8 components, adjusting for sex, race, and ethnicity. A binary telomere phenotype was defined based on the odds of having younger- versus older-than-expected LTL. Results: Among 62,709 participants, 94.5% were male; 79.7% were White, and 13.7% were Black. The mean age (SD) at enrollment was 67 (12). Median (IQR) LE8 score was 59 (19), with 6.3% classified as high (80-100), 69.0% moderate (50-79), and 24.7% low (0-49). Compared with low LE8 score, high LE8 score was associated with greater odds of younger-than-expected LTL (OR 1.17, P=1.08х10 − 5 ). Every 10-point increase in LE8 score was associated with a 0.0081-unit increase in LTL (P=6.97х10-10), corresponding to the estimated effect of being one year younger chronologically. Among LE8 components, every 10-point increase in diet score (β=0.0038, P=4.64х10 − 1 1 ), sleep score (β=0.0027, P=4.6х10 − 4 ), and BMI score (β=0.0022, P=8х10 − 5 ) was associated with increased LTL. Conclusions: Higher LE8 scores were associated with longer LTL and greater odds of younger-than-expected telomere length. Among LE8 components, diet, sleep, and BMI demonstrated the strongest associations with LTL. These findings suggest that better cardiovascular health, as measured by AHA’s LE8, is associated with more favorable biological aging profiles.

title: Lifestyle factors and the incidence of premature major adverse cardiovascular events in the VA Million Veteran Program
abstract: Background Premature cardiovascular disease remains an important cause of mortality. Among US Veterans specifically, the association of combined low-risk lifestyle factors with premature major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) is not yet characterized. Methods We analyzed 71,968 Million Veteran Program participants free of CVD at baseline, including 45,820 males aged 21–54 years and 26,148 females aged 19–64 years, with complete data on 8 low-risk lifestyle factors: higher-quality diet, physical activity, not smoking, restful sleep, no excessive alcohol intake, good stress management, social connection and support, and no opioid use disorder. Premature MACE was defined as nonfatal stroke, nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), or CVD death before age 55 in males or 65 in females. Results During 358,835 person-years of follow-up, 1,161 premature MACE cases occurred, including 481 MI, 467 stroke, and 238 CVD deaths. All 8 low-risk lifestyle factors were associated with lower premature MACE risk. After multivariable adjustment, higher low-risk lifestyle scores were associated with lower risk of premature MACE [hazard ratio (HR) comparing 7–8 versus 0–2 factors = 0.37; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.27–0.52; P trend <0.0001], MI [HR 0.45; 95% CI: 0.27–0.75], stroke [HR 0.54; 95% CI: 0.33–0.87], and CVD death [HR 0.18; 95% CI: 0.07–0.46]. Associations were consistent across sex, age, race, income, and obesity subgroups. Conclusions Greater adherence to a low-risk lifestyle was associated with a lower risk of premature MACE in a dose-response manner among US Veterans.

title: Longitudinal measurement invariance of the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale Screen among treatment-seeking veterans.
abstract: The Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale Screen Version is a suicide screening measure used in health care settings across the United States; no study has assessed the stability of its measurement properties over time (i.e., longitudinal measurement invariance). The present study examined the longitudinal measurement invariance of the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale Screen Version in a sample of 1,944 military veterans who participated in a randomized controlled trial for major depressive disorder. Longitudinal invariance was examined across six administrations both within the total sample and within subgroups separated by sex and race to ensure that full-sample results were not driven by the larger demographic subgroups. Although full invariance was not supported, measurement inconsistencies over the six assessments were minimal and limited to the initial assessment. Full-sample and subgroup analyses supported configural, threshold, and metric invariance over time. Full scalar invariance was not supported, but partial scalar invariance was supported with minor model modifications. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

title: Replication of claudin-5 epigenetics in association with PTSD severity in the VA Million Veteran Program.
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with neurocognitive decline and disease but the pathways linking these conditions are unclear. Recent preclinical and clinical research focused on depression and PTSD has suggested that the claudin-5 (CLDN5) protein, which comprises the tight junction proteins that seal the blood brain barrier, may relate to susceptibility to these stress-related conditions and associated neuropathology. We evaluated if we could replicate associations between CLDN5 DNA methylation and PTSD symptom severity in a large cohort of 22,835 Veterans enrolled in the VA Million Veteran Program. In the full cohort, we found evidence of replication for cg17411190 after adjustment for multiple testing (B = 2.76E-05, β = .017, p = .001, p-adj = .026), with cg05460329 replicating at the level of nominal significance (p = .023). In age-stratified analyzes, there was replication at cg17411190 and cg21872764 (ps = .046 and .009, respectively) at the nominally significant level in the age 65+ group. All associations replicated the effect directions seen in prior work. Results highlight the relevance of CLDN5 epigenetics for stress-related psychopathology and suggest that methylation of this gene in blood may be a useful biomarker for symptom severity and could potentially help to explain the association between PTSD and neuropathology.

title: Brain Stimulation as a Treatment for Apathy: A Scoping Review of Effects and Safety.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Apathy is a neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by impairment of goal-directed behavior, cognition, and emotional responsiveness. In this scoping review, the authors evaluated the literature on brain stimulation for the treatment of patients with apathy across diagnostic categories and provide recommendations to guide future research and practice.
METHODS: The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, and PsycInfo for studies involving brain stimulation for apathy as a primary or secondary outcome.
RESULTS: From 1,209 records, 52 studies evaluating brain stimulation were included; of these, 10 systematic reviews or meta-analyses were synthesized separately. Modalities included repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS; N=26), deep brain stimulation (DBS; N=7), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS; N=6), electroconvulsive therapy (N=1), transcranial alternating current stimulation (N=1), and transcranial pulsating electromagnetic field therapy (N=1). Populations included patients with schizophrenia (N=477), Parkinson's disease (PD; N=289), depression (N=288), Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) (N=210), Huntington's disease (N=42), PD with MCI (N=28), traumatic brain injury (N=28), stroke (N=14), COVID-19 (N=12), and dementia with Lewy bodies (N=6) (total N=1,366). rTMS improved apathy measures, most consistently in AD, with positive trends in depression, MCI, stroke, and schizophrenia. tDCS showed variable effects, with some benefits for schizophrenia. DBS showed mixed results, varying with stimulation location. Observed adverse events were mild and modality specific.
CONCLUSIONS: Investigations into brain stimulation as a treatment for apathy show some promise. Conclusions were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous study designs, and variable outcome measures. Randomized trials with common validated apathy instruments, standardized stimulation parameters, and harmonized diagnostic measures may help advance the field.

title: A multi-stage validation framework for trustworthy large-scale clinical information extraction using large language models
abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) show promise for extracting clinically meaningful information from unstructured health records, yet real-world deployment is constrained by limited scalable, trustworthy validation approaches. Conventional evaluation relies on annotation-intensive reference standards and incomplete structured data, limiting population-scale use. We propose a multi-stage validation framework for LLM-based clinical information extraction that enables rigorous assessment under weak supervision by integrating complementary validation strategies. The framework combines prompt calibration, rule-based filtering, semantic grounding, judge-LLM evaluation, expert review, and predictive validity analysis to quantify uncertainty without exhaustive manual annotation. We applied this framework to extract substance use disorder (SUD) diagnoses across 11 substance categories from 919,783 clinical notes. Rule-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14.59% of LLM-positive extractions that were unsupported or structurally implausible. For high-uncertainty cases, the judge LLM showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert. Using judge evaluations as references, the primary LLM achieved an F1 score of 0.80. LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured-data baselines. By unifying complementary validation strategies, this work presents a generalizable human-in-the-loop framework for establishing the trustworthiness of LLM-based clinical information extraction at scale while minimizing the need for exhaustive manual annotation.

title: Editorial: Community series in unveiling the next generation of cancer immunity & immunotherapy in lung cancer, volume II.
abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, despite major advances in screening, diagnosis, and treatment. Approximately 85% of lung cancers are non-small cell lung cancers (NSCLC), while the remaining cases are small cell lung cancers (SCLC), which tend to grow and spread more rapidly, leading to poorer outcomes. Over the past two decades, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), especially those targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway, have significantly changed how lung cancer is treated. These therapies have improved survival in many patients and established immunotherapy as a standard treatment option alongside conventional therapies. However, only few patients had long-lasting responses, while others respond briefly or develop resistance over time. These differences could be due to the complex relationship between tumors and the immune system, highlighting the need to better understand what drives treatment success and resistance. Collectively, the studies assembled in this Research Topic reflect the rapid evolution of lung cancer immunology by integrating mechanistic discoveries, therapeutic innovation, biomarker development, and clinical translation into a comprehensive perspective on the next-generation cancer immunotherapy (Figure 1).The contemporary view of cancer immunity has expanded far beyond the classical concept of immune surveillance. Lung tumors are now recognized as dynamic ecosystems in which malignant cells continuously interact with immune cell populations, stromal components, vascular networks, metabolic pathways, and resident microbial communities. These interactions collectively shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), influencing immune cell recruitment, activation, exhaustion, and ultimately, therapeutic responsiveness. Consequently, effective immunotherapy is increasingly viewed not simply as the restoration of T-cell function alone, but as the coordinated modulation of an intricate biological network. Recent advances in immunometabolism, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, microbiome research, and non-classical immune checkpoints have substantially broadened our understanding of immune escape mechanisms while revealing new therapeutic opportunities. This shift-from targeting isolated immune pathways to comprehensively remodeling the tumor ecosystem-represents one of the defining concepts emerging from this collection.A parallel transformation is occurring in precision oncology. Although PD-L1 expression and tumor mutational burden have become important biomarkers for guiding immunotherapy, their predictive value remains limited by the remarkable biological heterogeneity of lung cancer. The integration of multi-omics technologies, including genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and single-cell analyses, is providing unprecedented insights into the molecular networks that regulate tumor progression and antitumor immunity. These approaches are enabling the development of increasingly sophisticated prognostic models that integrate molecular and clinical information to improve patient stratification and therapeutic decision-making. At the same time, advances in computational biology and machine learning are accelerating the discovery of novel immune-related biomarkers capable of capturing the dynamic complexity of the tumor ecosystem. Rather than relying on individual biomarkers, future immunotherapeutic strategies are expected to integrate multiple biological dimensions to guide personalized treatment.Therapeutic innovation has progressed alongside these biological discoveries. Beyond conventional immune checkpoint blockade, rational combination strategies incorporating antiangiogenic agents, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and emerging immunotherapeutic platforms seek to overcome primary and acquired resistance by simultaneously targeting complementary mechanisms of immune regulation. Furthermore, clinical studies, prospective protocols, systematic reviews, and case reports of exceptional responders provide valuable evidence supporting the translation of these advances into routine clinical practice. Together, the contributions to this Research Topic illustrate a clear transition from conventional checkpoint inhibition toward ecosystem-based precision immunotherapy, in which therapeutic success depends on integrating mechanistic insights, biomarker-guided patient selection, and multidisciplinary clinical management. In this Editorial, we synthesize these advances and discuss how they collectively define the future direction of cancer immunity and immunotherapy in lung cancer.The clinical success of immune checkpoint inhibitors has transformed lung cancer therapy, yet the observation that only a subset of patients achieves durable responses underscores the complexity of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Rather than functioning as isolated therapeutic targets, immune checkpoints operate within a dynamic ecosystem comprising malignant cells, immune infiltrates, stromal fibroblasts, endothelial cells, extracellular matrix components, vascular networks, metabolic pathways, and microbial communities. These interconnected elements collectively determine immune surveillance, tumor progression, and responsiveness to therapy. Consequently, understanding the biological complexity of the TIME has become fundamental to the development of next-generation immunotherapeutic strategies.Several studies in this Research Topic highlight emerging regulators of the lung tumor ecosystem that extend beyond the classical PD-1/PD-L1 axis. Growing evidence indicates that the intratumoral microbiota actively influences immune activation, inflammatory signaling, and therapeutic responsiveness, while non-classical immune checkpoints, including CD137/CD137L and CD200/CD200R, further expand the regulatory networks governing antitumor immunity. In parallel, stromal remodeling and angiogenesis create both physical and immunological barriers that restrict immune cell infiltration and promote therapeutic resistance. These observations support the concept that vascular normalization and stromal modulation are not merely complementary to immunotherapy but integral to restoring effective immune surveillance. Likewise, advances in immunometabolism demonstrate that metabolic reprogramming shapes both tumor cell survival and immune cell function, linking nutrient utilization, hypoxia, and mitochondrial activity to treatment response. Collectively, these findings redefine the TIME as a highly integrated biological ecosystem in which microbial, metabolic, vascular, stromal, and immune signaling networks converge to regulate tumor evolution. Rather than targeting individual pathways in isolation, future therapeutic strategies will likely require the coordinated modulation of multiple components of this ecosystem to achieve durable clinical benefit.Advances in our understanding of the TIME have driven a paradigm shift from single-agent immune checkpoint blockade toward rational combination immunotherapy. The studies included in this Research Topic demonstrate that integrating immune checkpoint inhibitors with antiangiogenic therapy, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and stromal-modulating approaches can simultaneously address complementary mechanisms of immune resistance while enhancing antitumor immunity. In particular, evidence supporting the combination of PD-1/PD-L1 blockade with VEGF-targeted therapies illustrates how vascular normalization can improve immune cell trafficking and potentiates checkpoint inhibition. Similarly, strategies incorporating angiotensin receptor blockade seek to remodel the stromal microenvironment, whereas radiotherapy is increasingly recognized as an immunological partner capable of inducing immunogenic cell death, enhancing antigen presentation, and promoting systemic immune activation. Together, these studies reinforce the concept that effective immunotherapy increasingly depends on biologically informed combinations that target multiple components of the tumor ecosystem rather than individual immune pathways alone. This therapeutic evolution is equally evident in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), where real-world studies and comprehensive reviews demonstrate continued progress in optimizing chemoimmunotherapy, treatment sequencing, and patient selection. Emerging evidence support the integration of immune checkpoint inhibitors with anti-angiogenic agents and other multimodal approaches while highlighting the importance of individualized clinical management beyond standardized treatment algorithms. At the same time, innovative platforms such as oncolytic virotherapy exemplify how direct tumor lysis can be coupled with activation of innate and adaptive immunity to convert immunologically "cold" tumors into treatmentresponsive lesions. Complemented by exceptional responder case reports and multidisciplinary treatment strategies, these advances collectively emphasize that the future of lung cancer immunotherapy lies in adaptive, ecosystem-based therapeutic approaches that integrate mechanistic understanding with clinical innovation. Rather than relying solely on increasingly potent immunotherapeutic agents, the next generation of treatment will depend on intelligently combining complementary modalities to maximize durable antitumor immunity, while minimizing therapeutic resistance. This evolving therapeutic landscape naturally leads to the next challenge in lung cancer immunology: identifying robust biomarkers capable of guiding precision immunotherapy for individual patients.Despite the remarkable success of immune checkpoint inhibitors, accurately predicting which patients will achieve durable clinical benefit remains one of the greatest challenges in lung cancer immunotherapy. Although biomarkers such as PD-L1 expression and tumor mutational burden have improved patient selection, their predictive value remains limited because they capture only a fraction of the biological complexity underlying tumor-immune interactions. The studies assembled in this Research Topic collectively demonstrate a shift from reliance on single biomarkers toward integrated precision immunotherapy, in which molecular, immunological, and clinical information is combined to better characterize tumor heterogeneity and therapeutic responsiveness. Multi-omics approaches-including transcriptomic profiling and, immune landscape analyses, together with machine learning-based prognostic models-provide increasingly sophisticated insights into the molecular networks governing immune regulation, disease progression, and treatment outcomes. Likewise, metabolism-related signatures and computational risk models illustrate how systems biology can identify clinically relevant biomarkers associated with immune infiltration, prognosis, and responsiveness to immunotherapy. These advances support a broader vision of precision oncology in which biomarker discovery extends beyond individual molecules to encompass the dynamic interactions among tumor cells, immune populations, metabolism, and the surrounding microenvironment.Importantly, precision immunotherapy should be viewed as a continuously evolving process rather than as a single diagnostic decision. Dynamic assessment of treatment response, immune remodeling, and metabolic adaptation may ultimately provide greater clinical value than static baseline measurements alone. The integration of artificial intelligence, computational pathology, single-cell technologies, and longitudinal molecular profiling offers unprecedented opportunities to refine patient stratification and optimize therapeutic sequencing throughout disease progression. Collectively, the studies presented in this Research Topic reinforce the concept that future therapeutic decisions will be guided by comprehensive biological profiling of the tumor ecosystem, enabling more individualized and adaptive treatment strategies that bridge mechanistic discovery with clinical implementation.The contributions within this Research Topic clearly demonstrate that the next generation of lung cancer immunotherapy will depend not only on scientific discovery but also on the successful translation of these advances into routine clinical practice. Despite substantial progress in understanding the tumor immune microenvironment, developing combination immunotherapies, and identifying novel biomarkers, therapeutic resistance, tumor heterogeneity, and dynamic immune adaptation continue to limit durable clinical responses. Overcoming these barriers will require greater integration of mechanistic biology with prospective clinical trials, real-world evidence, and multidisciplinary patient management. Rather than evaluating therapeutic strategies in isolation, future research should emphasize rational treatment sequencing, biomarker-guided patient selection, and adaptive therapeutic approaches capable of responding to the evolving biological characteristics of individual tumors.Emerging technologies are expected to accelerate this transition toward precision oncology. Single-cell and spatial multi-omics, longitudinal immune monitoring, computational pathology, and artificial intelligence are transforming our ability to characterize the temporal and spatial complexity of tumor-immune interactions. At the same time, innovative therapeutic platformsincluding oncolytic virotherapy, engineered cellular therapies, novel immune checkpoint modulators, and rational multimodal treatment strategies-continue to expand the therapeutic landscape beyond conventional checkpoint inhibition. The integration of these technologies with molecular profiling, clinical expertise, and real-world data has the potential to generate truly personalized therapeutic strategies that continuously adapt throughout the course of disease. Ultimately, the studies highlighted in this Research Topic demonstrate that the next generation of lung cancer immunotherapy will emerge through the convergence of systems biology, translational research, computational medicine, and multidisciplinary clinical collaboration, providing a comprehensive framework for individualized cancer care and improved long-term patient outcomes.The studies presented in the Community Series in Unveiling the Next Generation of Cancer Immunity & Immunotherapy in Lung Cancer: Volume II collectively demonstrate the remarkable evolution of lung cancer immunology from mechanistic discovery toward precision, patient-centered immunotherapy. Together, they illustrate that effective cancer immunotherapy extends far beyond immune checkpoint blockade and increasingly depends on understanding the complex interplay among tumor cells, immune populations, stromal architecture, angiogenesis, metabolism, microbiota, and the broader tumor immune ecosystem. By integrating fundamental biology with translational research, clinical investigations, and real-world evidence, this collection highlights how complementary scientific disciplines are converging to improve patient stratification and therapeutic outcomes.A central message emerging from this Research Topic is that the future of lung cancer immunotherapy will be driven not by incremental improvements in individual therapeutic agents, but by the integration of biologically informed combination therapies, multidimensional biomarker discovery, and adaptive precision medicine. Advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence, computational biology, and longitudinal immune profiling provide increasingly sophisticated tools for characterizing tumor heterogeneity and guiding individualized therapeutic decisions. Equally important, the continued integration of laboratory discoveries with prospective clinical trials, real-world evidence, and multidisciplinary collaboration will be essential for translating scientific innovation into durable clinical benefit.Collectively, the contributions summarized in this editorial reinforce a paradigm shift toward ecosystem-based precision immunotherapy, in which treatment decisions are informed by comprehensive molecular, immunological, and clinical profiling rather than isolated biomarkers or single therapeutic modalities. As our understanding of the tumor immune ecosystem continues to expand, integrating biological insight with therapeutic innovation and clinical implementation will be fundamental to overcoming treatment resistance and improving long-term outcomes. This evolving framework provides a strong foundation for the next generation of personalized immunotherapeutic strategies and offers renewed optimism for advancing the care of patients with lung cancer.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Detection and Management of Physiological Instability in Heart Failure: Results of the Randomized LINK-HF2 Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled wearable monitoring can detect individualized physiological deviations preceding heart failure (HF) decompensation, but whether these signals can be translated into improved outcomes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility of integrating AI-generated notifications with a structured clinician response algorithm into postdischarge HF care and to explore their association with HF events following hospitalization.
METHODS: LINK-HF2 (Detection of Physiological Anomaly Using Artificial Intelligence and Prevention of Heart Failure Hospitalization) was a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint study conducted at 5 Veterans Affairs medical centers. Adults hospitalized for acute HF were enrolled at discharge and assigned to AI-guided monitoring with clinician notification or to standard care. All participants wore a continuous multisensor patch for up to 90 days. A personalized similarity-based model detected deviations in cardiorespiratory and activity signals and generated notifications. Implementation outcomes included feasibility, acceptability, and usability. The main exploratory clinical endpoint was HF rehospitalization. Secondary exploratory clinical endpoints included the composite outcome of all-cause unplanned rehospitalizations, emergency department visits, and all-cause mortality. All clinical endpoints were compared through Cox proportional hazards models over the follow-up period.
RESULTS: Among 171 analyzed participants, 80 (46.8%) were assigned to intervention and 91 (53.2%) to control. Median monitoring adherence was 72.4% of follow-up days; clinicians responded to communicated notifications within a median of 1 day (range: 1-5 days), and qualitative analysis demonstrated high patient acceptance and clinician engagement, whereas identifying workflow integration and response uncertainty as the primary barriers to implementation. In exploratory analyses, HF rehospitalization occurred in 13 (16.3%) patients in the intervention group and 17 (18.7%) in the control group (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.43-1.84; P = 0.76). The composite clinical endpoint also did not differ between groups (HR 1.03; 95% CI: 0.63-1.70; P = 0.89). The intervention group had a lower rate of AI-detected physiological instability than controls (HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.60-0.97; P = 0.025).
CONCLUSIONS: AI-enabled continuous physiological monitoring was feasible and reduced AI-detected physiological instability. Although this feasibility study did not demonstrate a reduction in exploratory clinical events, these findings highlight that accurate physiological risk detection alone may be insufficient to modify clinical risk without mechanistically aligned and trusted therapeutic responses. (Detection of Physiological Anomaly Using Artificial Intelligence and Prevention of Heart Failure Hospitalization [LINK-HF2]; NCT04502563).

title: Emergency medicine pharmacotherapy literature of 2025.
abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize pharmacotherapy-related emergency medicine (EM) literature indexed in 2025. Articles were selected using a modified Delphi approach. The table of contents from predetermined journals were reviewed and independently evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by paired authors. Pharmacotherapy-related publications deemed to be GRADE 1A and 1B were reviewed by the collective group for inclusion in the review. This article synthesizes and evaluates findings from 7 randomized controlled trials, 10 guidelines, clinical policies, position statements, or consensus recommendations, and 11 meta-analyses, providing critical insight into their potential clinical impact. Covered topics include guideline or policy updates on advanced cardiac life support, rapid sequence intubation, tranexamic acid in trauma, acute coronary syndromes, and hypertension. Randomized controlled trials covering sedative use in rapid sequence intubation, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and bacterial vaginosis, sodium bicarbonate for severe acidemia and acute kidney injury in the critically ill, and thrombolytic therapy beyond traditional time windows for ischemic stroke are also reviewed. Additional topics include nebulized and low-dose ketamine for analgesia, erector spinae plane block for renal colic, two-bag versus three-bag acetylcysteine regimens for acetaminophen overdose, QT prolongation in antipsychotic overdose, and naltrexone for opioid dependence.
