title: Understanding veteran perspectives surrounding implantable cardioverter- defibrillator decision-making.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2018, the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) mandated the use of evidence-based shared decision-making (SDM) tools for cardiovascular decisions, including implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) implantation for primary prevention in patients with systolic heart failure. Military Veterans are a unique population with experiences including combat, and heightened rates of anxiety, depression and post-traumatic stress disorder. Understanding Veteran perspectives on ICD decision-making processes is necessary to inform the Veteran Health Administration's (VHA) ICD care model.
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To understand factors influencing Veterans' ICD decision-making, semi-structured interviews were conducted with Veteran patients with an ICD (Implanters), those referred for consideration (Deliberators), and those who declined (Decliners).
METHODS: Interviews explored experiences with being offered an ICD, understanding of the device, and factors influencing personal decisions. Data were analyzed using content and thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Interviews with 13 participants revealed four primary themes that guided ICD decision-making: (1) desire for information and involvement in personal decisions, (2) quality of life values, (3) views of spirituality (4) Decliners and Deliberators accepted natural death and expressed desire to not intervene medically to prolong life.Participants valued consultation with providers and personal networks, yet ultimately prioritized autonomy. The role of mental health experiences and cohort-level differences on decision-making was inconclusive.
CONCLUSION: Participants' ICD implantation decision-making were influenced by considerations around quality of life, spiritual beliefs, and reluctance to invasively interfere with disease progression. These insights highlight the importance of personalized patient-provider interactions and the need for decision-support tools tailored to VHA Veteran care.

title: The role of white matter microstructure in the association between childhood maltreatment and adult post-traumatic symptoms.
abstract: Childhood maltreatment (CM) is a risk factor for adult post-traumatic symptoms and white matter (WM) alterations. It remains unknown how WM microstructure is affected alongside two common military conditions, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). Data from 299 participants (53% male, 35.69 ± 12.23 years of age) of the Injury and Traumatic Stress (INTRuST) clinical consortium was analyzed. The study included 56 individuals with PTSD (41 with comorbid mTBI), 107 with mTBI, and 136 controls (no PTSD and/or mTBI). Diffusion parameters (mean, axial, and radial diffusivity, MD, AD, RD; fractional anisotropy, FA) in major WM tracts were extracted from diffusion MRI. CM was assessed using the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ). Multiple regression models examined associations between CM severity and WM diffusion. Moderation analyses assessed the effect of PTSD and/or mTBI on these associations. Mediation analyses examined how WM diffusion affects the associations between CM and both PTSD and post-concussive symptom severity. Greater CM severity was associated with lower MD and AD, independent of PTSD and/or mTBI. WM diffusion, particularly in the corpus callosum and the superior longitudinal fasciculus, mediated the associations between CM severity and both PTSD (MD bab = 0.022, AD bab = 0.019-0.034) and post-concussive symptoms (MD bab = 0.028-0.040, AD bab = 0.032-0.047). Findings suggest that WM alterations are more strongly associated with CM itself than with either PTSD and/or mTBI. Mediating effects in regions critical for sensory integration highlight the role of WM microstructure as a neurobiological pathway through which CM might predispose to post-traumatic symptoms.

title: Chronic post-traumatic stress disorder-related behavioral traits develop in female rats exposed to repetitive low-level blast injury and are reversible with (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Many military Veterans who experienced blast-related injuries during military service suffer from chronic cognitive and mental health problems. Women constitute more than 15% of active-duty U. S. military personnel and are the fastest-growing population of U. S. Veterans. For more than a decade, we have studied a rat model of repetitive low-level blast exposure designed to mimic the type of blast-related exposure that is common in military settings. Male rats develop chronic cognitive and post-traumatic stress disorder-related traits that appear in a delayed fashion and persist for more than 1 year after exposure. These traits can be reversed with a single dose of (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine [(2R,6R)-HNK]. This study aimed to determine whether female rats develop a similar set of neurobehavioral alterations.
METHODS: Ten-week-old female rats were exposed to 75.1 kPa blast overpressures delivered once per day for three consecutive days. We tested female rats behaviorally between 1 and 4 weeks after blast exposure and again at 28 and 29 weeks. Rats were tested in an elevated zero maze, light-dark emergence task, and novel object recognition task, as well as contextual and cued fear learning and a Barnes maze. We tested how females would respond to a single dose of 20 mg/kg (2R,6R)-HNK administered intraperitoneally.
RESULTS: Following blast exposure, female rats developed chronic cognitive and behavioral traits. The full behavioral phenotype developed with a delay. Treatment with a single dose of (2R,6R)-HNK reversed behavioral changes in female rats, and beneficial effects on behavior were sustained for 4 weeks without additional drug administration. As in male rats, female rats showed elevated metabotropic glutamate receptor mGluR2. Elevations of mGluR2 were reversed by (2R,6R)-HNK treatment. Similar to male rats, the serotonin receptor 5-HT2AR was decreased in blast-injured female rats but levels were not affected by (2R,6R)-HNK treatment.
CONCLUSION: These studies show that female rats develop a similar behavioral profile as previously observed in male rats using the same blast exposure conditions. They further support (2R,6R)-HNK as a promising therapeutic candidate for treatment of blast-induced neurobehavioral effects, even when administered after traits are well established.

title: The Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study measured hepcidin, cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic outcomes in chronic kidney disease
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Abnormal iron homeostasis plays a critical role in extra-hematopoietic disorders. The relationship of hepcidin, the master iron regulator, to clinical outcomes, has not been characterized in a large cohort of chronic kidney disease (CKD). METHODS: To determine if plasma hepcidin level predicts cardiovascular (CV), kidney, and metabolic outcomes in patients with CKD, we studied 3826 patients enrolled in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study. Hazard ratios for hepcidin tertiles were estimated from Cox Proportional Hazards regression for primary outcomes of incident heart failure (HF), end stage kidney disease (kidney failure) or halving of the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and new onset diabetes or prediabetes. Secondary outcomes included atherosclerotic events and all-cause and CV mortality. RESULTS: The median and interquartile range of plasma hepcidin level was 43 (22, 77) ng/mL. Higher plasma hepcidin levels were associated with older age, male sex, non-Hispanic Black race, diabetes, lower eGFR, higher albuminuria, increased plasma levels of iron indices, C-terminal fibroblast growth factor 23, and markers of inflammation (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and interleukin-6). We found no association between plasma hepcidin level and the risk for incident HF or prediabetes/diabetes. However, compared to the middle tertile, the highest hepcidin tertile was independently associated with increased risk for kidney outcomes (hazard ratio 1.19; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.30) and atherosclerotic events (hazard ratio 1.34; 95% confidence interval 1.09, 1.64), while the lowest hepcidin tertile was associated with increased risk for all-cause and CV mortality in fully adjusted multivariable models including iron indices and inflammation. CONCLUSION: Both low and high plasma levels of hepcidin are associated with adverse clinical outcomes.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and adverse outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic viral hepatitis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are a novel class of anti-diabetic drugs that can treat obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). T2D and chronic viral hepatitis (CVH) frequently coexist and worsen liver and non-liver outcomes, but effective pharmacological therapies are limited. We aimed to evaluate the effect of GLP-1RA on liver and non-liver complications among patients with T2D and CVH in the United States.
METHODS: Patients with T2D and CVH initiating GLP-1RA were included (2013-2022) in Merative™ Marketscan® Research Databases. Primary outcomes included (1) hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cirrhosis, and (2) cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and non-liver cancer. Cox proportional hazards models were conducted to estimate hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: A total of 9,499 patients with T2D and CVH were included after 1:4 propensity score matching. Compared with non-GLP-1RA (N=7,366), GLP-1RA use (N=2,133) was associated with significantly lower risks of any liver-related outcomes (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.57-0.87; P=0.001), HCC (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.31-0.93; P=0.028), cirrhosis (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.56-0.86; P<0.001), CKD (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53-0.84; P<0.001). A trend toward a lower risk of CVD (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.66-1.03; P=0.089) and non-liver cancer (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.53-1.01; P=0.055) was observed among GLP-1RA users, although the association did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and CKD among patients with T2D and CVH, with nonsignificant trends toward lower risks of CVD and non-liver cancer.

title: Comparative and Sex-Specific Assessment of Proteomics, Clinical, and Genomic Data on Visceral Adipose Tissue Volume Using Machine Learning in UK Biobank: Advancing Precision Medicine
abstract: BACKGROUND: Visceral adiposity is a key driver of insulin resistance, which in turn is a strong risk factor for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. METHODS: We investigated the overall and sex-specific associations between plasma proteomics and visceral adipose tissue volume, and their intersection with clinical and genomic data to identify critical candidate proteins for visceral adiposity possibly linked to insulin resistance. We analyzed data from UK Biobank participants, using multistep machine learning to establish linear and nonlinear associations. RESULTS: The combined model, integrating clinical, proteomic, and polygenic data, accounted for 67% of visceral adipose tissue variance. Our research revealed significant protein interactions with environmental factors and identified sex-specific proteins correlated with visceral adipose tissue variance in both males and females. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that a small number of plasma proteins explain a significant portion of the variance of visceral adipose tissue beyond nonproteomic measures, offering a potential single-source, personalized measurement of visceral adiposity that is easily accessible and may facilitate improved prediction and understanding of the biology of insulin resistance.

title: Military-specific factors and incident melanoma diagnoses among active duty participants in the millennium cohort study, 2000 - 2021
abstract: Service members experience unique occupational hazards that may increase their risk for melanoma. This longitudinal study aimed to determine associations between deployment status, environmental exposures, and solar exposures and incident melanoma among active duty service members. Millennium Cohort Study survey data (2001-2021) were linked with deployment and military health care records (2000-2021). Adjusted Cox proportional hazards models estimated effects of exposures and covariates on incident melanoma. Risk of melanoma diagnosis by age (early vs late onset) and anatomical site (sun-protected vs sun-exposed skin) were also estimated. Among 115,512 service members, 184 were diagnosed with melanoma during the study period (61% were <40 years old and 77% diagnosed on sun-protected skin). Melanoma risk by demographics was consistent with civilian studies. Among this military population, those who deployed (adjusted hazard ratio [AHR] 0.55 [95% CI 0.40, 0.75]) had reduced melanoma risk. Conversely, those who self-reported being exposed to occupational hazards (AHR 1.43 [95% CI 1.05, 1.95]) had elevated melanoma risk. Findings were consistent with the "healthy deployer effect," while self-reported occupational hazards were associated with an increased risk of melanoma. Results may be informative for understanding melanoma etiology, risk counseling, and screening.

title: Psychoplastogens to Reduce Persistent Cognitive Symptoms for Traumatic Brain Injury as a Chronic Condition
abstract: There are currently no available effective pharmacological therapies for treating chronic cognitive deficits after traumatic brain injury (TBI). Psychoplastogens, including atypical psychedelics, classical serotonergic psychedelics, and neuroplastogens, are a class of small molecule drugs that can enhance neuroplasticity by inducing rapid and sustained effects on neuronal architecture and function, with the potential to have broad therapeutic effects. Ketamine, psilocybin, and dimethyltryptamine (DMT) have demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for treating multiple psychiatric conditions, and their ability to enhance neuroplasticity is hypothesized to be the primary mechanism. However, the administration of psychoplastogens for the treatment of cognitive impairments in TBI and other neurodegenerative diseases is nascent. In this review, we discuss the following: (1) relevant TBI pathologies and how neuroplasticity is impaired following TBI, (2) psychoplastogens and their use in neural repair models, and (3) the potential of psychoplastogens as treatments for TBI to alleviate various pathologies and improve cognitive behavioral outcomes. The underlying pathologies observed after TBI, including impaired neuroplasticity, synaptic dysfunction, neuronal atrophy, altered neurotransmission, and cellular dysfunction, are shared with several psychiatric disorders. Based on the multiple pathophysiological targets, there is a critical unmet need to investigate psychoplastogens as therapeutic interventions during the chronic phase of TBI for cognitive outcomes and underlying impact on neuroplasticity.

title: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Epigenome-Wide Association Studies in the Million Veteran Program.
abstract: Genomic studies have improved our understanding of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) biology. Epigenetic differences in DNA methylation can reflect environmental influences, which are critical in PTSD etiology, and may additionally differentiate between PTSD cases and controls or distinguish severity of PTSD symptoms. We conducted epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) of PTSD in 22,141 subjects from the United States V.A. Million Veteran Program (MVP), using the PTSD Checklist (PCL-C), including 17,674 European ancestry (EUR), 3,430 African ancestry (AFR), and 1,037 admixed American descent (AMR) individuals. We evaluated the 17-item PCL-C and its symptom subdomains (re-experiencing, avoidance, and hyperarousal) and used our previously-reported algorithmically-defined PTSD diagnoses validated against clinical records. There were 9,413 total cases of Lifetime PTSD and 27,257 controls, with 5,184 cases and 19,382 controls in EUR, 3,095 cases and 6,240 controls in AFR, and 1,134 cases and 1,635 controls in AMR. We identified a total of 272 epigenome-wide-significant associated CpG sites across all PTSD traits, or 28 after adjusting for smoking status. We replicated 5 out of 11 CpG sites reported in a prior (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium) PTSD EWAS. There was significant enrichment of genes downregulated in somatostatin interneurons and of genes expressed in GABAergic interneurons. Regression analyses showed that PTSD case status was significantly correlated with accelerated DNA methylation aging. Contrary to previous PTSD EWAS findings, smoking status stratification suggested that the association between PTSD and methylation of the AHRR gene may be confounded by smoking status. This is the largest-scale PTSD EWAS in multiple ancestries and the first large PTSD EWAS on symptom severity. We replicate findings from previous EWAS and greatly extend knowledge of the epigenetics of PTSD.

title: Gaps in Access to Home and Community-Based Services Following Inpatient Rehabilitation for Traumatic Brain Injury in Older Adults.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with traumatic brain injury (TBI) often experience residual self-care and mobility limitations after discharge from inpatient rehabilitation facilities (IRFs). Occupational therapy (OT) and physical therapy (PT) in home health or outpatient settings can address these limitations, yet access is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: Determine whether need for OT (self-care limitations) and PT (mobility limitations) at IRF discharge is associated with community rehabilitation utilization, and whether non-clinical factors are independently associated with utilization.
DESIGN: Cohort study using Medicare claims and assessment data. Modified Poisson regression estimated receipt of home health OT, home health PT, outpatient OT, and outpatient PT post-IRF discharge as a function of self-care and mobility performance, non-clinical factors, and clinical covariates.
PARTICIPANTS: Community-dwelling older adults who received inpatient rehabilitation for TBI from 2020 to 2022 (n = 23,036).
INTERVENTIONS: Not applicable.
MAIN MEASURES: Clinical need was defined using discharge Section GG self-care and mobility performance scores. Receipt of community rehabilitation was identified within 90 days post-IRF discharge.
KEY RESULTS: Most rehabilitation occurred via home health (OT 52%; PT 67%); only 15% received outpatient OT and 27% received outpatient PT. Worse self-care was associated with home health and outpatient OT use. Worse mobility predicted home health PT, but mobility did not predict outpatient PT use. Non-clinical factors were independently associated with a decreased likelihood of home health utilization, including younger age; Hispanic ethnicity (vs. White, non-Hispanic); and rurality. Similarly, beneficiaries who were older; identified as Black or Hispanic (vs. White, non-Hispanic); unmarried; or eligible for Medicaid were less likely to receive outpatient rehabilitation.
CONCLUSIONS: Community rehabilitation was common, but care was concentrated in home health. Clinical need was not a dominant driver of utilization, and non-clinical factors shaped access. Findings highlight gaps in utilization of beneficial rehabilitative care upon discharge and reveal targets for improving transitional services.

title: Treatment of PTSD in the military health system: Which patients receive evidence based psychotherapy?
abstract: The goal of this study was to identify patient-level factors associated with receiving evidence-based psychotherapy (EBP) for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the military health system (MHS). We used machine learning models (LASSO, RFE, Elastic Net) to examine predictors of initiation (at least one session) and minimally adequate dosage (three sessions in 90 days or eight sessions in 14 weeks) of EBP defined as prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, or eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy. Participants (N = 3,459) were diagnosed with PTSD and receiving behavioral health services at one of eight military treatment facilities between July 2018 and December 2021. Predictors included patient demographics, treatment experiences (e.g., session spacing), and clinical characteristics (e.g., comorbidities). Results showed that 51.3% of patients initiated EBP, 25.7% received three sessions in 90 days, and 7.5% received eight sessions in 14 weeks. The strongest predictors of EBP receipt were the total number of sessions, military service branch, and comorbid mood disorder. Specifically, those who received a greater total number of all psychotherapy sessions were more likely to initiate and receive a minimally adequate dosage of EBP. EBP receipt was lower through the Navy and Army compared to the Air Force, and among those with comorbid mood disorder. Findings emphasize the influence of treatment experiences in EBP receipt and point to the need for further research on provider- and system-level determinants of EBP receipt. Identifying predictors can inform efforts to improve the quality of PTSD care in the MHS, ensuring access to effective treatments.

title: Semaglutide, Tirzepatide and Clinically Recorded Alcohol-Related Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract:
AIMS: To compare the risk of incident alcohol use disorder (AUD) among adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) initiating semaglutide, tirzepatide or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation using de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX research network (June 2022-January 2025). Adults with T2D newly initiating semaglutide, tirzepatide or an SGLT2i were included. The primary outcome was clinically recorded hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visits for AUD. Cox proportional hazards models with 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses as well as secondary outcomes assessed the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 0.81-1.02 years, the incidence rates (IRs) of clinically recorded hospitalization or ED visits for AUD were 2.42 versus 4.53 per 1000 person-years for semaglutide versus SGLT2i, with an HR of 0.54 (95% CI, 0.45-0.64). Similarly, the IRs were 2.34 versus 3.98 per 1000 person-years for tirzepatide versus SGLT2i, with an HR of 0.61 (95% CI, 0.46-0.83). In the direct comparison of semaglutide versus tirzepatide, IRs were 2.43 and 2.36 per 1000 person-years, respectively, with no difference in risk (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.73-1.31). Results were consistent across sensitivity and subgroup analyses and secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with T2D, semaglutide and tirzepatide were associated with lower rates of clinically recorded AUD-related outcomes than SGLT2i, with no difference between the two GLP-1RA medications.

title: Engagement and outcomes of veterans endorsing suicidal ideation in a couple‐based treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder
abstract: Abstract Approximately half of veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) experience suicidal ideation (SI), and many report intimate relationship problems. Historically, there has been hesitation to engage veterans with SI in PTSD treatment for fear that trauma‐focused interventions could potentially exacerbate SI. Additional concerns include that veterans with SI would not be fully psychologically present, engaged in, and benefiting from treatment. This secondary analysis of data from a clinical trial of brief cognitive‐behavioral conjoint therapy for PTSD (bCBCT) examines engagement, retention, and PTSD and relationship satisfaction outcomes for 92 veterans and their intimate partners. Veterans were grouped by baseline report of SI in the past year ( n = 35) versus no SI ( n = 57). Treatment dropout did not significantly differ between veterans who reported SI and those who did not, χ 2 (1, N = 92) = 0.50, p = .479. Significant reductions in PTSD during treatment were observed for both veterans with, d = ‐1.34) and without SI, d = ‐0.87. Partners also reported reductions in veterans’ PTSD symptoms for veterans with SI, d = ‐0.46, and without SI, d = ‐0.82. PTSD symptom reduction did not differ significantly by SI status according to veteran or partner report. In contrast, we found no evidence of systematic change in relationship satisfaction for veterans or partners regardless of baseline SI status. There were no suicide‐related adverse events. The findings suggest that couples in which the veteran endorses SI can engage in and benefit from couple‐based PTSD treatment.

title: Repetitive blast TBI drives chronic sex-dependent paroxysmal motor behaviors and sleep disruption.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Repeated blast-induced traumatic brain injury (rbTBI) is a major cause of chronic neurological morbidity in military populations, with post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) representing a significant long-term complication. While blast exposure is implicated in epileptogenesis and development of PTE, the direct effects of rbTBI on chronic seizure burden remains poorly understood. This study examined chronic paroxysmal motor behaviors of uncertain origin (PMBs), sleep outcomes, and neuropathology following rbTBI, incorporating sex as a biological variable.
METHODS: Male and female Sprague Dawley rats underwent repeated blast exposure (~20 psi, 24-h intervals) or sham procedures using the McMillan Blast Device. Beginning 4 months post-injury, animals were housed in piezoelectric sleep/seizure monitoring cages for longitudinal assessment of spontaneous PMBs, including myoclonic jerks, wet-dog shakes, and rapid circling/running, and sleep architecture (percent sleep, total sleep, bout length, and sleep-wake transitions) over a 4-week period. At 5 months post-injury, animals were euthanized for immunohistochemical and western blot analysis of astrocytic end-feet expression (AQP4) and glial markers (GFAP, IBA1) in cortex, hippocampus, and corpus callosum.
RESULTS: A high proportion of rbTBI animals (80%) developed PMBs, with males showing greater PMB prevalence, frequency, and burden than females. PMBs predominantly occurred during the dark period for both sexes after rbTBI. rbTBI produced chronic sex-specific, transient alterations in sleep architecture, with males showing increased weekly and light-period sleep alongside increased sleep consolidation (longer bout lengths, fewer transitions) from 4 to 5 months post-rbTBI. Females showed a transient reduction in weekly sleep at 4 months post-rbTBI. AQP4 expression was preserved across brain regions regardless of injury or PMB status, indicating chronic recovery of astrocytic end-feet vascular coverage after rbTBI. Hippocampal GFAP was selectively elevated in PMB-positive animals, while whole-brain GFAP protein was significantly increased in rbTBI animals overall, driven primarily by the female rbTBI group, independent of PMB burden. IBA1 expression was unaffected by injury or PMB status.
CONCLUSION: rbTBI produces chronic PMBs and transient disruptions in chronic sleep architecture in male rbTBI animals. Hippocampal astrogliosis is linked to PMB in rbTBI animals and a broader increase in astrogliosis is observed in rbTBI animals, driven by the female rbTBI group. These findings demonstrate persistent sleep and astrocytic alterations alongside chronic paroxysmal motor behaviors after rbTBI, supporting a potential relationship to post-traumatic epileptogenesis.

title: How leaders make decisions about implementing health interventions in the Veterans Health Administration.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many effective health interventions remain unimplemented, delaying patient benefits. This is true even within integrated health care systems such as the U.S. Veterans Health Administration (VHA). Little is known about how leaders decide to adopt new interventions.
PURPOSE: This study explored organizational leaders' thought choices to implement or forego new health interventions within VHA.
METHODOLOGY: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 13 organizational leaders across local, regional, and national levels. Data were analyzed with content analysis and aligned to the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research.
RESULTS: VHA leaders' thought processes differed if health interventions were mandated versus discretionary. Participants described two implementation processes for successful change: top-down, usually featuring policy mandates, and bottom-up, driven by clinician-generated interest. Facilitators included intervention fit, alignment with performance measures, and effectiveness evidence. Barriers comprised upfront staffing and training costs and organizational challenges such as leadership turnover and resource limitations.
CONCLUSIONS: Before implementing, organizational leaders wanted an intervention to have a positive impact on patients and considered budget impact and/or cost-effectiveness as a second priority. This decision-making process was balanced by circumstances for costly interventions addressing imminent needs, for example, pandemic ills and suicide risk.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: VHA organizational leaders believed successful implementation required top-down directives and bottom-up clinician engagement, but approached the process differently depending on whether implementation was mandated or discretionary. Implementation, systems redesign, or quality improvement personnel might ease practice change by noting mandated versus discretionary context and addressing leaders' needs explicitly. Organizational leaders wanted multiple types of information about intervention effectiveness, fit to context for nonresearch audiences.

title: Validation of the PREVENT-HF Risk Prediction Equation in US Veterans.
abstract: One in four adults in the United States will receive a diagnosis of heart failure (HF) in their lifetime (1), highlighting an urgent need for expanded prevention.Accurate prediction of HF risk is critical to prioritize high-risk individuals for targeted intervention.The American Heart Association's PREVENT-HF equation is a novel HF risk prediction tool (2).However, it is unclear how well this model generalizes outside of its development cohort.This is important for populations with disproportionately high risk of HF, such as US Veterans (3).Prior validation in this population has focused on other endpoints (e.g., atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease [ASCVD]) and limited outcome ascertainment to Veterans Health Administration (VHA) data, which didn't capture diagnoses from Medicare or VHA-paid community care claims (4).To address this gap, we validated PREVENT-HF in US Veterans.

title: Abstract 5929: Trends in Cardiac Rehabilitation Participation and the Role of Home-Based Programs Among US Veterans Between 2012 and 2022
abstract: Background: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a guideline-recommended secondary prevention program that reduces morbidity and mortality among patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) yet remains underutilized. Over the past decade, the Veterans Health Administration (VA) has implemented strategies to increase CR participation, including automatic referral, CR liaisons, and virtual home-based CR (HBCR) programs as alternatives to traditional center-based CR (CBCR). Objective: To examine temporal trends and factors associated with CR participation among Veterans with IHD from 2012 through 2022. Design, Setting, and Participants: In this observational study, we examined national VA electronic health record data to evaluate CR participation among Veterans hospitalized for IHD, identified using ICD-9 or ICD-10 codes. Exposures: Availability of CR delivery models at VA facilities, including referral to community care programs only, VA CBCR, or VA HBCR. Main Outcomes and Measures: The main outcome was participation in CR within 12 months of the index event, identified using CPT codes and VA stop codes from VA-provided, purchased, or Medicare-claimed services. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with participation. Results: Among 405,907 Veterans with IHD, 63,185 (15.6%) participated in CR. Participation increased from 9.6% in 2012 to 17.1% in 2022 (P for trend <.001), with a peak of 19.7% in 2018. In 2022, participation was higher at facilities offering HBCR (20.0%) compared with those offering CBCR without HBCR (14.8%) or referral to community care programs only (14.3%). In adjusted analyses, Veterans treated at facilities offering HBCR had nearly double the odds of participation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.90; 95% CI, 1.86-1.95), while those at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR had higher odds of participation (aOR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.24-1.29), compared with referral to community care programs only. As compared with those who did not participate, Veterans who participated in CR were slightly younger and more likely to be male, white, married, obese, and with higher income. They were more likely to have MI, PCI, CABG, COPD, diabetes, and kidney disease but less likely to have heart failure or peripheral vascular disease (p<0.01 for all). Conclusions and Relevance: Between 2012 and 2022, CR participation among Veterans with IHD nearly doubled, coinciding with the expansion of VA HBCR programs. However, fewer than 1 in 5 eligible Veterans received any CR and low CR participation remains a significant gap in care. Broader implementation of HBCR may be an effective strategy to improve CR participation within large health systems.

title: Importance of Capturing Risk Adjustment Data for Veterans Using Multiple Healthcare Systems
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Examine whether incorporating non-Veterans Health Administration (VA) and social determinants of health (SDOH) variables into the Gagne comorbidity measure improves model performance given VA enrollees' increased use of care outside VA. STUDY SETTING/DESIGN: Three-year observational study (10/1/2019-9/30/2022) of two Veteran cohorts who received care in VA or through VA-purchased care ("CC"): (1) those receiving total hip/knee arthroplasties (THA/TKA) and (2) those with serious mental illness (SMI) who had behavioral health (BH) hospitalizations. Outcomes included 30-day, all-cause readmissions. We ran descriptive statistics to examine the extent to which each data source (CC, Medicare, and Medicaid) identified additional Gagne comorbidities and readmissions. We fit logistic regression models to examine the impact of adding comorbidities, outcomes, and SDOH first to VA outcomes, and then after each new data source was added. We examined model discrimination and calibration to compare predicted risk with observed outcomes. DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: We used administrative/claims data from VA's Corporate Data Warehouse and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Our sample included 75,684 THA/TKA and 152,427 BH index admissions. PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: The greatest increase in the number of comorbidities and readmissions came from adding CC data (e.g., percent increases in comorbidities and readmissions were > 30% for both cohorts; THA/TKA, readmissions increased by 153%). Adding new data sources and SDOH variables had little effect on model discrimination; changes in c-statistics were 0.01-0.03. Both models calibrated well (e.g., mean predicted vs. observed readmissions in the first and tenth deciles for THA/TKA were 0.014 vs. 0.012, and 0.090 vs. 0.075, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Adding CC data had the greatest impact on identifying additional comorbidities and outcomes, reflecting Veterans' increased use of CC. Incorporating non-VA and SDOH variables into risk-adjusted models had minimal impact on model discrimination (individual-level predictions) and model calibration (mean predicted vs. mean observed readmissions).

title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism.
abstract: The heart possesses a dynamic capacity to oxidize a variety of fuels, including glucose and lactate, to meet its energetic demands under diverse dietary, exertion and injury stressors1. Oxidation of carbohydrate substrates is thought to converge on the cytosolic generation of pyruvate, which is transported by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) for entry into the tricarboxylic acid cycle2. Here we find that glucose-derived carbon is oxidized in mouse myocardium even when the MPC is genetically ablated. Using genetic and pharmacological tools, we demonstrate that lactate monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by Slc16a1) is required for the oxidation of glucose carbon by MPC-deficient myocardium. We further observe that MCT1, traditionally localized to the plasma membrane, also resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane of mouse and human cardiomyocytes. Together with matrix-localized LDHB, MCT1 enables mitochondrial lactate conversion to pyruvate and NADH, directly fueling the electron transport chain. Loss of MCT1 impairs lactate oxidation, disrupts metabolic flexibility and accelerates the development of heart failure with increased mortality after hyperactivation of the neurohormonal axis or ischemia-reperfusion injury. Thus, the existence of a parallel lactate-based pathway for carbohydrate oxidation can sustain cardiac energetics and maintain myocardial structure and function under diverse stress conditions.

title: Reduced inhibition of hippocampal adult-born granule cells by parvalbumin interneurons after TBI.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is one of the leading causes of acquired temporal lobe epilepsy. TBI drives hippocampal circuit rearrangements that may contribute to increased seizure risk, such as altered inhibitory circuit function and aberrant post-traumatic neurogenesis. In the hippocampal dentate gyrus, adult-born dentate granule cells (DGCs) acquire inhibitory synaptic inputs from parvalbumin-expressing (PV) interneurons early in their maturation. PV inputs are important for circuit integration and feedforward inhibition of adult-born DGCs. We used genetically modified mice, retroviral vectors, and optogenetics to study adult-born and mature DGCs after a Controlled Cortical Impact model of TBI. We tested whether TBI altered PV-mediated inhibition of DGCs that were born after TBI. DGCs born after TBI acquired inhibitory synaptic inputs during their maturation, but PV-mediated inhibition of adult-born DGCs was persistently reduced following TBI. In contrast, mature granule cells did not have a reduction in PV-mediated inhibitory synaptic inputs following TBI. The density of PV cells in the dentate gyrus was not different after TBI, therefore functional changes were not due to loss of PV neurons. The deficit in PV-mediated functional innervation of adult-born DGCs was associated with a transient reduction in release probability at these synapses, which normalized as DGCs matured despite ongoing reduction of functional PV input. Surprisingly, although spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic currents were reduced for mature granule cells after TBI, there was no difference in spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic currents in adult-born DGCs. Taken together, these data demonstrate distinct differences in the de novo development and maintenance of PV synapses in the dentate gyrus after TBI. The addition of neurons with reduced PV interneuron-mediated feed-forward inhibition to the dentate gyrus could contribute to hippocampal hyperexcitability after severe brain injury.

title: TBI drives astrocytic mitochondrial transfer associated with neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction: therapeutic potential of astrocytic EV-mito
abstract: Abstract Mitochondria are dynamic organelles essential for neuronal survival and synaptic function, and their dysfunction is a key consequence of excitotoxicity following traumatic brain injury (TBI). While intercellular mitochondrial transfer and exogenous mitochondrial transplantation have emerged as mechanisms to restore cellular bioenergetics, its in vivo relevance in the central nervous system remains incompletely understood. Here, we used astrocyte and neuron-specific mitochondrial reporters (GFP or Dendra2) in mice to assess cell-type-specific mitochondrial morphology, bioenergetics, and transfer 24 h after TBI. Neurons exhibited marked mitochondrial dysfunction, including altered morphology and reduced bioenergetic capacity across somatic, synaptic, and non-neuronal fractions. In contrast, astrocytic mitochondria showed morphological changes but preserved bioenergetic function. Concomitantly, astrocyte-to-neuron mitochondrial transfer was significantly increased following injury, although transfer to synapses remained limited. Single-cell RNA sequencing of astrocytes revealed upregulation of genes involved in extracellular vesicle (EV) biogenesis and mitochondrial translation following injury compared to controls. In vitro co-culture studies confirmed that astrocytes transfer mitochondria to neurons via EVs containing mitochondria (EV-mito). Isolated EV-mito from astrocyte-conditioned media improves neuronal mitochondrial function under NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) induced excitotoxic conditions. Together, these findings demonstrate that TBI drives astrocyte-mediated mitochondrial transfer as an adaptive response, occurring alongside neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction. This process preserves neuronal bioenergetics in the soma and neurites but not at synapses, highlighting both its therapeutic potential and spatial limitations.

title: Suicide Prevention and Intervention With Military Personnel and/or Veterans: An Overview of Systematic Reviews
abstract: Background Suicide prevention among military personnel and veterans is a public health priority, yet evidence regarding effective interventions is dispersed across systematic reviews of varying scope and quality. Objectives To systematically identify, appraise, and synthesize reviews of suicide prevention and treatment interventions for military personnel and veterans and assess the applicability and quality of the evidence. Methods We searched eight bibliographic databases, organizational websites, reference lists, and forward citations and consulted subject-matter experts for reviews published from 2004 onward. Searches were completed in June–July 2024. Eligible reviews synthesized interventions intended to prevent or treat suicidal ideation or behavior and either focused on military personnel or veterans or included an identifiable subset of studies involving these populations. Two reviewers independently conducted full-text screening and data extraction. Findings were synthesized narratively. Review quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2 and primary-study overlap using the Corrected Covered Area Index. Results Twenty-three reviews met eligibility criteria. Across reviews, findings regarding intervention effectiveness were mixed, with some favorable findings for particular approaches, but the evidence did not support confident conclusions about the effectiveness of specific suicide prevention interventions for military personnel or veterans. Review quality was poor: 22 reviews were rated critically low quality and one low quality. Heterogeneity in interventions, populations, study designs, and outcomes, along with inconsistent assessment and incorporation of risk of bias, further limited interpretation. The reviews contained 323 unique primary studies; however, only 48 specifically evaluated a suicide prevention or treatment intervention in a military or veteran population and reported a suicide-specific outcome, and only 18 (38%) of these were randomized controlled trials. Conclusions Despite a substantial review literature, directly applicable, methodologically trustworthy evidence remains limited. More rigorous primary studies and systematic reviews focused specifically on suicide prevention in military and veteran populations are needed. Registration PROSPERO CRD42024549878.

title: The Effect of Stimulant Medications on Symptom and Treatment Outcomes in Adults With Comorbid Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity and Substance Use Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveSymptoms of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) are increasingly recognized among adults and frequently co-occur with substance use disorders (SUD). Changing guidelines and complexity of treatment merit a review of approaches for managing this diagnostic overlap among adults.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review for randomized controlled trials (RCT) and nonrandomized comparative studies (NRCS) focused on the benefits and harms of non-stimulant/nonpharmacological ADHD treatment compared to psychostimulant medications for those with comorbid ADHD and SUD by searching: Medline (via PubMed), Embase, and PsycINFO from inception to December 14, 2023, the Cochrane library from inception to January 30, 2024, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to February 23, 2024. After screening, evidence from eligible studies was qualitatively and quantitatively synthesized by a multidisciplinary team of researchers and clinicians.ResultsOf 6,419 unique records screened, six RCTs and one NRCS were eligible for review, analyzing a total of N = 662 people. There was no evidence of differences in ADHD treatment adherence, substance use, SUD symptom change, or substance abstinence in people with co-occurring ADHD and SUD who were not prescribed stimulant medications compared to people prescribed stimulants (low confidence for all). No significant difference was observed in the proportion of individuals with improved scores on the Clinical Global Improvement scale based on a pooled analysis of three studies (pooled OR = 1.27 [0.32, 5.09]). Although trending in a clinically positive direction, studies provide insufficient evidence (no conclusion) for ADHD symptom change, SUD treatment adherence, medication misuse/diversion, and measures of depression and anxiety. There was no evidence of a difference in various measures of adverse events (strength of evidence not assessed).ConclusionsSignificant limitations in the evidence base prevent the ability to draw substantial conclusions, and additional inquiry is recommended in future research. Available data, while limited, may indicate increased maintenance in SUD treatment for long-acting stimulants, and there is insufficient data to support the efficacy of non-stimulants for ADHD treatment in SUD patients. Though literature is minimal, a cautious interpretation suggests that current evidence does not support concerns that stimulant medications can precipitate substance-related problems in adults with co-occurring SUD and ADHD.

title: Quantifying and Addressing Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Lower-Limb Prosthesis Prescriptions Among US Veterans.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Black and Hispanic Veterans undergo lower-limb amputations at higher rates than White Veterans, yet it remains unclear whether they receive equitable access to prosthetic devices within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA).
OBJECTIVE: To quantify racial and ethnic disparities in lower-limb prosthesis (LLP) prescriptions among Veterans and identify factors contributing to these disparities.
RESEARCH DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using generalized Kitagawa-Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition and prescriptive disparity analysis with double/debiased machine learning.
SUBJECTS: Veterans who underwent major lower-limb amputation within the VHA from 2010 to 2022 (n=16,157; 66.2% White, 27.4% Black, 6.4% Hispanic).
MEASURES: Prescription of any LLP and advanced LLP within 12 months postamputation.
RESULTS: Black and Hispanic Veterans were 5.7 percentage points (pp) [95% confidence limits (CLs): 4.0, 7.5] and 5.6 pp (95% CLs: 2.4, 8.8) less likely than White Veterans to receive any LLP prescription, respectively. For advanced LLPs, disparities were 1.7 pp (95% CLs: 0.8, 2.6) for Black Veterans and 3.0 pp (95% CLs: 1.5, 4.5) for Hispanic Veterans. Facility-level factors explained 58.2% of the White-Black disparity in any LLP prescriptions. Measured factors fully explained the White-Black disparity in advanced LLP prescription, with preamputation clinical factors contributing most. Prescriptive analysis revealed that targeted quality improvement at facilities serving high proportions of Black Veterans could reduce disparities by 32.5%, while interventions addressing end-stage renal disease could reduce advanced LLP disparities by 33.6%.
CONCLUSIONS: Targeted resource allocation to facilities serving high proportions of racial and ethnic minority Veterans and integrated care pathways for Veterans with complex comorbidities represent actionable interventions for reducing prosthetic care inequities.

title: Tri-sector Partnership for Military Suicide Prevention: Developing, Testing, and Scaling Wingman Guardian Connect.
abstract: Our tri-sector partnership (Department of the Air Force, University of Rochester, and SafeSide Prevention, LLC) developed, tested, and scaled up Wingman Guardian Connect (WGC), the first RCT-validated program shown to reduce suicide risk, depression, and occupational problems in a broad military population (Wyman et al., 2020). Using the Exploration, Preparation, Implementation, Sustainment (EPIS) framework (Aarons et al., 2011) adapted for a military context, we trace the partnership from an initial Department of Defense grant (2014) through data-driven program development, a cluster RCT demonstrating efficacy (N = 1500 active-duty personnel), extension to operational installations, and ongoing force-wide scale-up across 72 installations. The partnership produced three outcomes addressing long-standing barriers to reducing military suicides: (1) a network enhancement training model that replaced lecture-based prevention programming, (2) methods enabling randomized trials of universal prevention in non-clinical military populations, and (3) a data-informed implementation strategy incorporating a National Institute of Mental Health-funded hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial. We describe how the tri-sector model-combining academic research rigor, governmental policy authority, and private-sector operational capacity-overcame challenges including leadership turnover and intervention fidelity at scale. We conclude with recommendations for partnerships seeking to advance evidence-based prevention within governmental agencies.

title: Narrowing the research to practice gap for trauma-focused psychotherapies in the Veterans Health Administration: A narrative review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The US Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has almost twenty years of experience implementing trauma-focused psychotherapies (TFPs) for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Yet, the potential of TFPs to alleviate the burden of PTSD has not been fully realized. Previous reviews focused primarily on clinician uptake and patient perceptions of TFPs with limited examination of service delivery challenges.
METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the evidence describing practice gaps specific to TFPs within VHA, factors that contribute to these evidence gaps, and recommends strategies and research to address modifiable contributing factors.
RESULTS: TFP practice gaps include limited or variable reach to patients, high dropout, and reduced effectiveness compared to randomized clinical trials. Contributing factors span patient, clinician, and healthcare organizational levels. To bridge these practice gaps, we recommend: (1) Taking patient preference and heuristic approaches to treatment decisions into account; (2) Testing novel strategies to augment patient sustained engagement through treatment completion; (3) Developing empirically adapted clinician training and consultation programs; (4) Designing clinics to facilitate delivery of these proven interventions; (5) Developing scheduling and other organizational strategies to facilitate an adequately intensive treatment course; (6) Enhancing local leadership support and the implementation climate for TFPs; and (7) Evaluating how clinician burnout symptoms impact treatment delivery and outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Narrowing the research-to-practice gap for TFPs within VHA requires addressing multi-level determinants to maximize patient engagement and facilitate effective intervention delivery. Without optimizing the conditions for intervention delivery, TFPs will remain limited in their capacity to reduce the systemic burden of PTSD.

title: Using multi-trait polygenic scores to predict lithium responsiveness in patients with bipolar disorder
abstract: Background The predictive power of polygenic scores (PGSs) for lithium treatment response in bipolar disorder remains limited. Aims To enhance the prediction of lithium responsiveness by developing a multi-trait PGS (mt-PGS) combining genetic information from multiple phenotypes implicated in lithium response and/or bipolar disorder aetiology. Method We analysed data collected from bipolar disorder patients who had received lithium treatment for at least 6 months and participated in the International Consortium on Lithium Genetics study ( N = 2367). The Alda scale was used to assess lithium responsiveness, and treatment outcome was defined as continuous total Alda score (0–10) and categorical outcome (favourable ≥7 versus unfavourable response). PGSs were calculated for 60 phenotypes grouped into 5 clinical–biological clusters: psychiatric and behavioural (#23 phenotypes), cardiometabolic (#17), autoimmune/inflammatory (#5), neurocognitive (#8) and renal function (#7). We applied cross-validated machine learning regression approaches in both outcomes within each cluster, with the selected features from each cluster subsequently combined to construct the final mt-PGS models. Model performance was assessed using explained variance ( R 2 ) for the continuous outcome, and both McFadden’s pseudo- R 2 and standard classification model parameters for the categorical outcome. Results mt-PGS explained between 5.70% (continuous outcome) and 9.11% (categorical outcome) of the interindividual variability in lithium responsiveness. Classification accuracy (area under the curve) for the categorical outcome was 68.24% (95% CI: 64.98–71.66), with a Brier score of 0.257. Of the 5 clusters, the PGSs for psychiatric and behavioural phenotypes were most strongly associated with lithium responsiveness, accounting for 3.67–6.52% of its variability. Conclusions By integrating PGSs for multiple relevant phenotypes, predictive accuracy for lithium response improved substantially compared with single-trait methods. Future research incorporating larger, more diverse populations and combining genetic scores with clinical data holds promise for further enhancing prediction and advancing clinical implementation.

title: An examination of chronotype associations with symptoms of depression, PTSD, and sleep disturbances in US military veterans.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronotype is associated with depression and PTSD, which are common mental health conditions among military veterans. Few studies have examined chronotype in this population, which is known to also have more severe sleep difficulties than non-veteran community-residing adults.
METHODS: In the current study, self-reported sleep and mental health symptoms were examined by chronotype using data collected from US military veterans (N = 144) participating in a multi-site post-deployment health repository. Analysis of covariance was used to assess symptom measure differences by chronotype after adjusting for age and sex.
RESULTS: Consistent with prior research, evening types endorsed greater symptomology across measures of depression and PTSD as compared to morning types. Evening types also endorsed more severe insomnia symptoms and poorer sleep quality, and these relationships were not mediated by sleep duration. Chronotype was not associated with trauma-associated sleep disturbance.
CONCLUSIONS: Consideration of chronotype may be important for case conceptualization in military veterans and those with elevated depression, suicidality, and/or trauma. Assessing chronotype may be important for identifying phenotypes at increased risk of greater psychiatric symptom burden, in addition to understanding treatment response to interventions targeting sleep timing, such as cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia.
CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Few studies have examined chronotype in military veterans, a population known to have more severe sleep difficulties than non-veteran community-residing adults. In this study, a registry of US military veterans serving since 911 was leveraged to examine chronotype relationship to mental health symptoms.
STUDY IMPACT: Evening types endorsed greater symptomology across self-report measures of insomnia severity, sleep quality, PTSD, and depression. Consideration of chronotype may be important for case conceptualization among military veterans and for identifying phenotypes at increased risk of greater psychiatric burden. Assessment of chronotype may also be important for understanding response to interventions targeting sleep timing, such as cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBTi).

title: Home-Based Programs and Cardiac Rehabilitation Participation Among Veterans With Ischemic Heart Disease.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a guideline-recommended secondary prevention program that reduces morbidity and mortality among patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) yet remains underutilized. Over the past decade, the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has implemented strategies to increase CR participation, including expansion of virtual home-based CR (HBCR) programs as alternatives to traditional center-based CR (CBCR).
OBJECTIVE: To examine temporal trends and factors associated with CR participation among veterans with IHD.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used national VHA electronic health record data to evaluate CR participation among veterans hospitalized for IHD, identified using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9), ICD-10, or Current Procedural Terminology codes from 2012 to 2022. Data were analyzed from October 25, 2025, to July 25, 2026.
EXPOSURES: Availability of CR delivery models at Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities, including referral to community care programs only, VA CBCR, or VA HBCR.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the proportion of eligible veterans with acute myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft surgery who participated in any type of CR within 12 months of the index event, identified using Current Procedural Terminology codes and VA stop codes from VA-provided, VA-purchased, or Medicare-claimed services. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with CR participation.
RESULTS: Among 405 907 veterans with IHD (mean [SD] age, 68.5 [11.1] years; 391 998 men [96.6%]), 63 185 (15.6%) participated in CR. Participation increased from 9.6% in 2012 to 17.1% in 2022, with a peak of 19.7% in 2018. In 2022, participation was higher at facilities offering HBCR (20.0%) compared with those offering CBCR without HBCR (14.8%) or referral to community care programs only (14.3%). The adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of participation among veterans treated at facilities offering HBCR was 1.80 (95% CI, 1.75-1.84), whereas the AOR of participation at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR was 1.29 (95% CI, 1.26-1.32) compared with referral to community care programs only.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of veterans with IHD, participation in CR nearly doubled between 2012 and 2022. Patients who had index events at facilities offering HBCR had higher CR participation than those at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR, or at facilities offering only referral to community care. Broader availability of HBCR programs may help improve participation within large health systems.

title: Mild traumatic brain injury promotes chronic cerebrovascular inflammation and glymphatic suppression.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Repetitive exposure to mild traumatic brain injury (r-mTBI) increases the risk for chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) and vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID). Given the strong association between head trauma exposure, persistent inflammatory endothelial damage, and glymphatic impairment, we hypothesized that cerebrovascular inflammation following r-mTBI may play a causal role in mediating post-traumatic gliovascular dysregulation, and the development of VCID pathology.
METHODS: To provide insight into potential mechanisms and upstream regulatory factors, we first examined the gliovascular transcriptional profile in post-mortem chronic human mTBI and r-mTBI tissue. Experimental validation was performed in a mouse model of chronic r-mTBI using transcriptomic, ultrastructural, biochemical, and functional assessments.
RESULTS: We observed chronic cerebrovascular inflammation following r-mTBI, characterized by cerebrovascular macrophage recruitment, eNOS dysregulation, oxidative stress, hypoxia, and mitochondrial damage. This coincided with a temporal shift in macrophage activation, resulting in the emergence of a chronic, pro-inflammatory, oxidative cerebrovascular profile. Notably, we showed that chronic r-mTBI also deteriorates the cerebrovascular basement membrane components that anchor astrocyte endfeet to the cerebrovasculature, manifesting in perivascular AQP4 mislocalization and glymphatic suppression.
CONCLUSION: These results suggest that repetitive head trauma can induce robust, persistent endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysregulation, that disrupts perivascular waste elimination pathways at the gliovascular interface early in the post-injury disease process.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1186/s44477-026-00053-w.

title: Dendrimer-delivered shRNA against CCL20-CCR6 attenuates complement-mediated synaptic loss and neuroinflammation after repetitive brain injury
abstract: Repetitive traumatic brain injury (rTBI) induces persistent microglial activation and chronic neuroinflammation, yet the upstream signals driving long-term synaptic injury remain unclear. In this study, we identify the CCL20-CCR6 chemokine axis as a critical regulator of sustained microglial activation and complement-dependent synaptic loss after rTBI. Proteomic profiling at 30 days post-injury (dpi) showed broad normalization of complement-linked inflammatory and synaptic pathways in the cortex and hippocampus, underscoring a mechanistic link between chemokine signaling, microglial activation, and synaptic vulnerability. To therapeutically target this axis, we developed a dendrimer-based shRNA platform (shCombo-DPX) that simultaneously silences CCL20 and CCR6. Intranasal and intravenous delivery in rTBI mice effectively reduced CCL20-CCR6 expression, attenuated chronic microgliosis and astrogliosis, and suppressed complement activation. Treatment limited microglial synaptic engulfment, preserved synaptic proteins, restored BDNF levels, and improved motor, anxiety-related, and cognitive outcomes. In microglia-neuron coculture systems, CCL20 silencing reduced LPS-induced complement signaling and prevented synaptic loss, neuronal apoptosis, and BDNF depletion. Conversely, exposure to recombinant CCL20 induced dendritic degeneration, caspase-3 activation, microglial reactivity, complement dysregulation, and synaptic injury both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, these findings establish CCL20-CCR6 as a key upstream driver of chronic complement-mediated synaptic degeneration after rTBI and support dendrimer-delivered shRNA therapy as a targeted strategy to mitigate long-term neurodegeneration.

title: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract Tumour-promoting inflammation and immune evasion are key features of cancer, but prospective evidence linking specific immune pathways to prostate cancer risk remains limited. Here we show that circulating proteins involved in immune regulation may influence prostate cancer development. We analyse 368 immune- and inflammation-related proteins measured in blood samples from men in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), including 1434 cases and matched controls, and combine these results with data from UK Biobank. While no proteins are associated with risk in EPIC alone after multiple testing correction, meta-analysis identifies several proteins linked to prostate cancer risk, including IL15 and FLT3LG, in particular, in blood taken long before diagnosis. Higher levels of immune surveillance-related proteins, particularly those involved in natural killer and T cell activity, are associated with lower prostate cancer risk, whereas genetic evidence implicates PARP1, SPINT2 and NME3 in increased risk. These findings suggest that immune pathways play a role in prostate cancer development and highlight potential targets for prevention.

title: From Evidence to Practice: A Systematic Review of Implementation of Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy
abstract: Background: Evidence supporting psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) for treating posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and other historically difficult to treat mental health disorders is growing rapidly. Interest from the public and within the US government to provide access to these treatments has also grown. Considering the gap between discovery of effective treatments and implementing them in clinical settings, it is important to synthesize current knowledge of implementing these complex treatment modalities to aid efforts for systematic implementation going forward. Objectives: The specific objectives of this systematic review were to: (1) identify extant literature on implementation of PAP, and (2) synthesize and present findings to understand current implementation knowledge and inform future directions. Methods: This systematic review followed the procedures outlined in Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. Six databases were searched using a string developed with the keywords "implementation," "psychedelic (methylenedioxymethamphetamine, psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide, ketamine)," and "psychotherapy" along with Elsevier expansions and synonyms. The study only included peer-reviewed research on PAP, which reported on the implementation of the interventions. The implementation science framework, the Practical, Robust, implementation and Sustainability Model, guided the data extraction and synthesis about implementation-relevant factors. Results: A total of 2,406 articles were identified, and 2,074 of these were screened by title and abstract after the initial elimination of duplicates and sources that were not peer-reviewed research articles (e.g., gray literature). Forty-seven were retrieved for full text review, and 20 studies were included in the review. Most studies (15) were cross-sectional surveys and/or qualitative interviews assessing organizational perspective. The remaining (5) presented included aspects of patient perspective (2), infrastructure (2), and patient characteristics (1). Conclusion: There is a noticeable gap in implementation-focused research on best practices for translating PAP from academic settings into accessible clinical programs. Addressing this gap is essential to support the safe and effective implementation of PAP in real-world settings.

title: Primary language as a moderator of social integration and functional independence after traumatic brain injury in U.S. older adults
abstract: PURPOSE: This study examined whether primary language moderates the relationship between social integration and functional independence among older adults in the U.S. following traumatic brain injury (TBI). METHODS: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from the Traumatic Brain Injury Model System National Database (TBIMS-NDB), including 1,030 individuals aged 65-88 with mild, moderate, or severe TBI. Of these, 88.3% reported English as their primary language, while 11.7% reported a non-English language. Social integration was assessed using the Participation Assessment with Recombined Tools-Objective, and functional independence was measured via the Functional Independence Measure. Primary language was categorized as English or non-English. Hayes's PROCESS macro was used for moderation analysis. RESULTS: < .01) indicated that the relationship was stronger among non-English speakers. CONCLUSION: Primary language plays a moderating role in the link between social integration and functional independence post-TBI. These findings highlight the need for culturally and linguistically tailored interventions to improve outcomes for older adults with TBI.

title: Association of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists with mortality and renal outcomes in patients with diabetes and chronic kidney disease: the diabetic nephropathy management and outcome (DINAMO) study
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at high risk for kidney failure and death. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes; yet, their real-world use in patients with diabetic CKD is incompletely characterized and they remain underutilized. Methods This nationwide, real-world cohort study conducted in Israel evaluated patients with T2D and a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio of more than 30 mg/g, using data from January 1, 2019 to December 31, 2024. Patients were stratified according to baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 or ≥ 30 ml/min/1.73 m 2 and categorized according to treatment status (SGLT2i alone, GLP-1RA alone, combined therapy, or neither therapy). The primary composite outcome was death from any cause or end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Results A total of 240,734 patients with T2D and CKD were included. Of these, 132,693 patients (55.1%) were not treated with either a GLP-1RA or a SGLT2i. In contrast, 30,803 patients (12.8%) received both agents, 44,007 (18.3%) received a GLP-1RA alone, and 33,231 (13.8%) received an SGLT2i alone. Among patients with an eGFR of ≥ 30 ml/min/1.73 m 2 , the adjusted hazard ratios for the primary outcome, as compared with no treatment, were 0.37 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.36–0.38) with SGLT2i alone, 0.51 (95% CI 0.49–0.53) with GLP-1RA alone, and 0.32 (95% CI 0.31–0.33) with combined therapy. In multivariable models, heart failure emerged as the strongest predictor of the composite outcome regardless of baseline kidney function (eGFR ≥ 30 or < 30 ml/min/1.73 m 2 ). Beyond the effects of the study treatments, treatment with aspirin, ACE inhibitors or ARBs was independently associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome. Conclusions In this nationwide, real-world cohort of more than 240,000 patients with T2D and CKD, combined SGLT2i and GLP-1RA therapy was associated with up to a 68% reduction in the risk of death or ESKD compared with no treatment. Importantly, these benefits were also observed in patients with advanced CKD, a population often underrepresented in clinical trials. Additionally, over half of eligible high-risk patients did not receive either therapy, highlighting a substantial implementation gap between clinical guidelines and routine practice.

title: Clinical impact of cardiomyopathy-associated rare variants and cardiovascular comorbidities in multi-ancestry populations
abstract: Abstract Background Recent studies highlight the adverse clinical impact of rare cardiomyopathy (CMP) gene variants at a population level, supporting the increased utilization of genetic screening in clinical care. However, most discovery and clinical association studies of pathogenic CMP gene variants have focused on individuals of European (EUR) genetic ancestry and do not consider the impact modifiable cardiovascular comorbidities on penetrance. Purpose To assess the clinical impact of established rare CMP gene variants and cardiovascular comorbidities in diverse multi-ancestry cohorts using large-scale genomic and phenotypic data from the UKB Biobank (UKB), All of Us Research Program (AllofUs), and Million Veteran Program (MVP). Methods Genetic sequencing data was used to identify carriers of disease-causing CMP gene variants in each dataset. This analysis focused on ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in genes with strong evidence for dilated, hypertrophic or arrhythmogenic right-ventricular cardiomyopathy, and truncating variants with an established gene-disease mechanism. Multi-variable time-to-event analyses were used to compare the clinical impact of CMP gene variants and cardiovascular comorbidities – type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and obesity - among European (EUR) and non-European (NEUR) ancestry participants. Results A total of 392,224 UKB participants (mean age 57 years; 94% EUR) 283,612 AllofUs participants (mean age 55 years; 53% EUR), and 101,571 MVP participants (mean age 66 years; 70% European) were included. Pooled fixed-effect meta-analysis showed that CMP gene variant carriers (CMPgeno+) in all datasets had a significantly higher risk of a composite cardiovascular outcome – including heart failure, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, and ventricular tachycardia – compared to non-carriers: EUR (HR: 1.72 [1.63 – 1.81], p = 0.0003) and NEUR (HR: 1.88 [1.71 – 2.08], p = 0.0009) (Figure 1). CMPgeno+ participants with ≥ 2 cardiovascular comorbidities had between a ~1.5-3.4-fold higher risk of a cardiovascular composite outcome compared to those with none across UKB, AllofUs, and MVP – for example in AllofUs: EUR (HR 2.88 [ 2.37 – 3.52], p <2E-16 vs. HR 4.61 [4.01 – 5.31], p <2E-16) and NEUR (HR 3.39 [2.25 – 5.09], p <2E-16 vs. HR 11.44 [9.51 – 13.76], p < 2E-16) (Figure 2A-F). In multi-variable analysis, hypertension was most consistently associated with increased risk of a cardiovascular composite outcome. Conclusion In large multi-ancestry population-based cohorts, both EUR and NEUR ancestry CMP gene variant carriers demonstrated an elevated risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. The presence of common cardiovascular comorbidities – in particular hypertension – was consistently shown to moderate this risk. These findings support the clinical utility of genetic testing and highlight the importance of addressing comorbidities to prevent adverse events.Figure 1Figure 2

title: An integrative roadmap for a new era of kidney replacement therapies.
abstract: Innovation in kidney replacement is entering a transformative era. Although precision medicine has driven major breakthroughs in disease-specific therapies, progress in translating next-generation kidney replacement strategies into practice has lagged. This updated Roadmap highlights a shift toward bold, integrative approaches that merge engineering, biology and patient-centred design. Emerging directions include reimagining filtration and tubular function through biomimetic membranes, cellular systems and organ-on-chip technologies, and simultaneously exploring microbiome modulation and sorbent-based strategies to reduce the uraemic toxin burden. Beyond improving survival, new solutions are being shaped by priorities of mobility, sustainability and quality of life, pointing toward wearable and implantable systems that move care beyond the clinic. Biologic frontiers such as xenotransplantation and stem cell regeneration are opening pathways to potentially curative therapies, although challenges in safety, equity and scalability remain. Central to these efforts is the need to embed patient perspectives and ensure that innovations align with lived experiences. This integrative approach calls for renewed investment, regulatory clarity and cross-sector collaboration to accelerate translation of advances into equitable therapies redefining the future of kidney health.

title: Next-Generation Psychedelic Drug Development.
abstract: Psychedelic medicine has gained rapid popularity for the treatment of a variety of neuropsychiatric disorders, including depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder. As novel psychedelic analogues and treatment regimes emerge, increasing numbers of variables are being tested. Here, we review various approaches and considerations for novel psychedelic therapies, including the strengths and limitations of current assays and models. Finally, we provide guidance and considerations for next-generation psychedelic drug development.

title: Mental Health Symptom Severity Is Positively Associated With Rehabilitation Needs in Veterans and Service Members With Polytrauma, Including Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Veterans Affairs Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the relationship between rehabilitation needs and mental health symptoms in Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, including history of mild traumatic brain injury (TBI).
SETTING: Five Veterans Affairs (VA) Intensive Evaluation and Treatment Programs.
PARTICIPANTS: Veterans and Service Members enrolled in the VA TBI Model Systems study who completed a follow-up greater than 6 months postprogram.
DESIGN: Cohort study.
MAIN MEASURES: Primary regression analyses included rehabilitation needs (Rehabilitation Needs Survey) and post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSD Checklist-Civilian version). Age, sex, months from rehabilitation to follow-up interview, preinjury mental health, disability level (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended), and number of comorbidities were included as covariates. Secondary analyses applied the same model structure to assess the relationship between rehabilitation needs and anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7) and depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9) symptoms.
RESULTS: Most Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, including mild TBI, reported a current need for services to control physical symptoms (55%) and greater than one-third endorsed a current need for services to improve memory (46%), manage emotions (45%), improve health (44%), manage daily stress (42%), and solve daily problems (38%). Adjusted regression analyses revealed that rehabilitation needs were significantly and positively associated with post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and depression self-report symptoms. These relationships were maintained when analyses were repeated with mental health-related items removed from the Rehabilitation Needs Survey, suggesting the finding was not solely because of mental health needs. Higher comorbidity burden and disability were also independently associated with higher rehabilitation needs.
CONCLUSIONS: Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, especially those with elevated post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and/or depressive symptoms in the context of mild TBI, could benefit from ongoing access to evidence-based psychotherapies and other specialty care, rehabilitation, and support services to manage long-term care and rehabilitation needs in the chronic phase of injury.
