title: Caveolins, cavins, and caveolae: lessons from human mutations.
abstract: Caveolae are specialized plasma membrane invaginations enriched in cholesterol and sphingolipids, playing vital roles in signal transduction, lipid regulation, membrane trafficking, and mechanoprotection. Their formation and function depend on two protein families: caveolins and cavins. Caveolins are integral membrane proteins that contribute to the membrane's curvature and serve as scaffolds for diverse signaling molecules. Cavins support caveolins at the cytoplasmic surface to stabilize caveolar architecture and regulate key processes, including insulin signaling, nitric oxide synthase activity, and lipid droplet formation. Mutations in caveolin or cavin genes can disrupt caveolae formation and function, often impairing cholesterol handling and perturbing key signaling pathways. This has been observed in a spectrum of pathologies such as muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, lipodystrophies, and various cancers. Given the importance of caveolins and cavins in membrane organization, understanding how specific mutations alter caveolin and cavin function is critical for elucidating the molecular basis of various disorders and for the development of targeted therapies. This review explores how caveolin and cavin mutations affect caveolae morphology, function, and signaling, thereby impacting physiology.

title: Evaluating selected gene therapies for cardiovascular diseases: an updated scoping review and evidence map of randomised controlled trials.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gene therapies are increasingly being developed and evaluated to treat complex diseases with multiple genetic causes, including cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). However, these studies have not yet been reviewed systematically. We aimed to conduct a scoping review of randomised controlled trials of gene therapies for CVDs and create an evidence map of the included literature.
METHODS: We searched six databases for studies published from November 2018 to March 2025. Our search yielded 9106 records, and 1864 publications were reviewed at the full-text level.
RESULTS: We included 28 randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating interventions delivered by RNA interference (13 RCTs; 46%), antisense oligonucleotides (9 RCTs; 32%), plasmids (4 RCTs; 14%) and other vectors (adeno-associated virus and adenovirus; 2 RCTs; 7%). Cardiovascular indications included dyslipidaemia (12 RCTs; 43%), ischaemia (4 RCTs; 14%), transthyretin amyloidosis (4 RCTs; 14%), heart failure (2 RCTs; 7%) and other CVDs (6 RCTs; 21%). Samples included an average of 183 participants (range: 5–655); studies followed these participants for an average of 13 months (range: 3–97). Interventions were efficacious in most (22 RCTs; 85%) of the 26 studies that reported efficacy outcomes, but effects lasted less than 1 year in most studies (69%; 18 RCTs). Serious adverse events varied widely by study (range: 0%–62% of intervention group participants), but 19 RCTs reported that less than 10% of intervention group participants experienced a SAE.
CONCLUSIONS: Gene therapies for CVDs were reported to be efficacious in most RCTs, but their effects lasted less than 1 year in 69% of studies. Gene therapies for CVDs show promise in their efficacy and relative safety, but more research is needed to evaluate their long-term effects and risks.

title: COVID-19 pleiotropy with brain imaging-derived phenotypes highlights novel insights into the biology shared between immune function and brain variation.
abstract: This study investigated the pleiotropy and the underlying biology linking COVID-19 outcomes to brain variation, leveraging genome-wide data from the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative and multimodal brain-wide magnetic resonance imaging from the UK Biobank. In our analyses, COVID-19 outcomes showed evidence of polygenic overlap with respect to 11 imaging-derived phenotypes (IDPs) related to brain structure (e.g. parahippocampal and entorhinal cortical thickness) and connectivity (e.g. Broca's area and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex). Among these, the genetic liability to COVID-19 hospitalization and SARS-CoV-2 infection was inversely related to the area of pars opercularis. We also identified local genetic correlations between COVID-19 outcomes and brain IDPs within five loci mapping genes involved in inflammatory response, immune regulation, brain development, and neuropsychiatric disorders (e.g. LAMP3, SOX2, and TSHZ2). Additionally, we uncovered colocalized variants linking COVID-19 outcomes to brain structural variation (rs13107325 with entorhinal mean thickness) and brain transcriptomic regulation of immune-related genes (e.g. IL6R in brain cortex and HLA-C in caudate basal ganglia). Our drug-repurposing analysis based on gene ontologies shared between COVID-19 outcomes and brain IDPs uncovered 41 compounds, including psychiatric medications that appear to also have antiviral and immunomodulatory activity. Overall, the present findings contributed to dissecting the biological mechanisms shared between COVID-19 and brain variation, highlighting the systemic nature of their relationship.

title: How Veterans Describe Military Environmental Exposure-Informed Care: A Quality Improvement Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Care for environmental hazards is a particular concern for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), which has encouraged "exposure-informed care" (EIC). A recent Delphi study conceptualized 6 core components of EIC (e.g., build trust, assess and document). The current quality improvement project used qualitative interviews with Veterans to understand if and how these core components of EIC are reflected in patient perspectives of their military environmental exposure care at the VA to guide the development of future Veteran-centered tools and education to support the implementation of EIC.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Participants (N = 53) were Veterans who received care at the VA for military environmental exposures. Veterans were interviewed and the team iteratively developed an initial codebook using quotes and supportive statements. The codebook was then applied to the previously established EIC core components and the team identified statements that suggested the presence or absence of EIC.
RESULTS: Findings suggest that when asked broadly about their care for exposure-related conditions, EIC core components are reflected in patient perspectives. The presence and absence of all 6 EIC components were found in Veterans' perspectives of their exposure-related healthcare. Veterans described specific actions from their providers and VA that were important to EIC. Their descriptions suggest the core components work synergistically to impact perceptions of care for military exposures.
CONCLUSIONS: The results of this project suggest that future tools to support the implementation of EIC should address EIC core components. Veterans described actions from providers and VA identified as EIC and may be used to design strategies to implement EIC. These strategies should consider incorporating multiple core components into implementation efforts, since Veterans' descriptions suggest the core components synergistically work together to impact care for military exposures.

title: Gene-by-Sleep Duration Interaction for Glycemic Traits in More Than 480,000 Individuals
abstract: Both short and long sleep duration have been associated with poor glycemic control and an increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Although sleep duration may differentially modify the effects of genetic risk factors for type 2 diabetes, this has not been systematically investigated. In the current study, we conducted genome-wide gene-by-sleep duration meta-analyses, separately assessing interactions of short and long sleep, for fasting glucose, fasting insulin, and hemoglobin A1c in up to 489,309 individuals without diabetes from seven different population groups. In total, 16 loci were identified to interact with sleep duration—6 with short sleep and 10 with long sleep. Of these, four loci were identified through cross-population meta-analysis. Mapped genes exhibited pathway connections to pericyte apoptosis, N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor activity, the GLUT1 receptor, neurological health, and sleep architecture. Eleven loci (VRK2, PCDH7, TFAP2A, CAP2, PAPPA, ZCCHC2, MYH9, SGIP1, JAKMIP3, RRAS2, and MAPT) have not been reported in previous glycemic trait genome-wide association studies. Interaction loci identified divergent biological mechanisms for short and long sleep duration influencing glycemic control, suggesting specific pathways of intervention for precision medicine approaches to diabetes prevention and management. Article Highlights The biological mechanisms of how sleep duration impacts type 2 diabetes pathogenesis and glycemic control are unclear. This study reveals 16 loci (11 novel) that interact with either short or long sleep duration to influence hemoglobin A1c, fasting glucose, or fasting insulin. Short and long sleep duration loci were nonoverlapping. Regulation of copper and diacylglycerol levels appear as distinct cellular mechanisms implicated by long and short sleep duration loci, respectively. Identified gene targets present insight for potential type 2 diabetes therapeutic design approaches related to JIP1–c-Jun N-terminal kinase interaction disruption, pericyte health, N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor activity, anti-inflammatory and leptin-enhancing dietary supplements, and serpins.

title: Ventriculo-arterial coupling in acute heart failure: prognostic and therapeutic insights - a systematic review and meta-analysis of multivariable-adjusted data.
abstract: In acute heart failure (AHF), non-invasive ventricular-arterial coupling (VAC) surrogates, including right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) and left ventricular-arterial (LV-Ao) coupling, have emerged as practical bedside indices, but their prognostic significance remains largely unknown systematically. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the prognostic significance of non-invasive VAC assessment, in patients hospitalized with AHF. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, HF hospitalization, length of hospital stay, use of therapies, the composite of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, and in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and odds ratios (aORs) were pooled using random-effects. Subgroup-analyses were performed according to follow-up duration and left ventricular ejection fraction. Thirty-six studies comprising 36,989 patients were analysed. Twenty-eight studies evaluated RV-PA coupling, predominantly the TAPSE/PASP ratio, and eight evaluated LV-Ao coupling, mainly using non-invasive Ea/Ees estimates. RV-PA uncoupling was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (aHR 1.90; 95% CI 1.42-2.56; I²=49%), with consistent associations at 12 months (aHR 2.03; 95% CI 1.44-2.85) and long-term follow-up (aHR 1.67; 95% CI 1.06-2.64). Associations with HF hospitalization, hospital stay, and the composite endpoint were directionally consistent but not statistically significant. LV-Ao uncoupling was associated with increased in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events (aOR 1.70; 95% CI 1.29-2.24). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of these findings. RV-PA uncoupling predicts mortality, whereas LV-Ao uncoupling identifies patients at increased risk of in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events, supporting VAC-risk-stratification in AHF and future evaluation of VAC-guided therapeutic strategies.

title: Trainings and Recommendations for Physician Firearm Secure Storage Counseling for Suicide Prevention: A Scoping Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suicide is a public health crisis in the USA. Secure storage of firearms can reduce suicide risk by putting time and distance between a suicidal crisis and access to a firearm. However, physicians often do not provide counseling to patients. This scoping review examines educational interventions that provide physicians and physicians-in-training skills to counsel patients about firearm secure storage.
METHODS: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review methodology and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) format. A literature search was conducted across Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, Cochrane Library, CINAHL Plus with Full Text, and Web of Science and included publications through April 9, 2025. Eligibility criteria included articles that (1) involved trainings on firearm secure storage for suicide prevention or provided commentary on what should be included in potential trainings; (2) had study populations that included physicians; and (3) were available in English.
RESULTS: Forty articles were included: 21 commentaries providing suggestions on physician firearm secure storage counseling education and training and 19 articles involving development and implementation of physician education and training. Training varied and included conversation strategies, facts about suicide, and storage methods and devices. Nineteen articles included study participant details, with emergency medicine (four studies), pediatrics (four studies), and psychiatry (three studies) most included. Most reported increased knowledge relating to firearms, improvements in attitudes and beliefs on importance of speaking with patients about firearm safety, and improvements in confidence and comfort in counseling.
DISCUSSION: This review found limited but promising literature on training physicians to provide firearm secure storage counseling for suicide prevention. Limitations include that only records published in English were included and that, as a scoping review, the quality of individual studies was not assessed. Standardized, evidence-based curricula are needed for broader implementation.

title: Childhood Trauma and APOEε4 Are Associated With Patterns of Developmental Frontal Alpha Connectivity, Posttraumatic Stress, and Alcohol‐Related Outcomes
abstract: Childhood trauma affects neurodevelopment and lifelong risk for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and alcohol use disorder (AUD). Changes in brain structures and function are observed in young carriers of APOEε4, the genetic factor most associated with Alzheimer's disease. Longitudinal studies of APOEε4, childhood trauma, and neural connectivity in adolescence have not been explored. We studied 837 trauma-exposed participants (53% female) from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism prospective sample, using latent growth curve models to assess associations of childhood trauma and APOEε4 on repeated measures of frontal alpha EEG coherence (EEGc) throughout adolescence and young adulthood. Young adult AUD and PTSD symptoms were also examined. Results indicate childhood sexual assaultive trauma (CSAT) and APOEε4 are linked to neural connectivity, with effects differing by brain region and direction. CSAT was associated with a higher EEGc baseline but less growth in three EEGc pairs, while APOEε4 associated with lower left frontocentral (LFC) EEGc baseline and higher slope. EEGc patterns and symptoms of PTSD and AUD were robustly associated. A significant interaction between CSAT-by-APOEε4 interaction also emerged, such that among APOEε4 carriers, childhood sexual assaultive trauma was associated with higher baseline PFI and diminished growth in PFI and LFC EEGc. No significant direct links between APOEε4 and PTSD or AUD were observed. Findings highlight how EEGc may help explain connections between genetics, trauma, and psychopathology, guiding at-risk group identification and informing prevention strategies.

title: Discriminant and Prognostic Validity of the Multimodal Exertional Test (MET) for Athletes with Concussion
abstract: BACKGROUND: Exertional tests have become an informative tool to assist with clinical concussion management and return-to-sport medical decisions. However, current tests are resource intensive and thus, we developed a widely accessible, multimodal exertional test (MET). The objectives of this study were: (1) To evaluate the discriminant validity of the MET by examining sex-stratified differences in symptoms, heart rate (HR), and performance metrics between concussed and healthy athletes; and (2) To assess the predictive (prognostic) validity of the MET by determining whether week 1 MET performance predicts time to medical clearance. METHODS: This study was conducted at a single academic institution and affiliated sport medicine clinic in Toronto, Canada, with participants recruited between August 2022 and November 2024. 115 interuniversity athletes (female n=49, male n=66) completed the MET at off-season and 55 interuniversity athletes with concussion (female n=37, male n=18) completed the MET up to six times at 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, and 8-weeks post-injury. Average and maximum HR, symptoms, performance metrics, and MET pass/fail status were measured prior to and during the protocol. Probabilistic hierarchical models were implemented to estimate differences between concussion and healthy athletes (discriminant validity) and negative binomial analyses were used to examine whether MET performance predicted time to medical clearance (predictive validity). RESULTS: At 1-week post injury, concussed athletes exhibited greater symptom provocation during the MET compared to healthy athletes, with differences after each task. MET failure rates were highest during weeks 1 (63%) and 2 (49%) and declined through week 8. Athletes who passed the MET at week 1 recovered 20.6 days faster (90% Credible Interval [CrI] = 4.9-36.8 days, posterior probability [pprob] > 0 = 97.7%) than those who failed. CONCLUSION: The MET demonstrates discriminant validity by eliciting greater symptom provocation in athletes with concussion compared to healthy athletes. Improvements in symptoms and completion rates over 8 weeks indicate recovery-related gains in exertional tolerance. The MET also demonstrates predictive validity, as passing the test at week 1 was associated with faster time to medical clearance, supporting its potential utility as an early prognostic tool in concussion management.

title: A retrospective cohort analysis of risk of drug overdose deaths among US Vietnam War-era veterans, 1979-2021.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Drug use among United States military veterans has clinical and public health implications. This study determined the risk of post-military service drug overdose mortality (1979-2021) among all veterans who served in the military during the 1961-1975 Vietnam War-era.
DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study compared the risk of drug overdose mortality among all United States military veterans that served in Vietnam during the Vietnam War (theater veterans) to that of all veterans who served during the Vietnam War but not in Vietnam (non-theater). This comprehensive population assessment included veterans born between 1900 and 1958, alive as of 1979 and with military service between 1961 and 1975. Participants included 9 496 285 Vietnam War-era veterans (2 443 567 theater; 7 052 718 non-theater).
MEASUREMENTS: Mortality outcomes included all, accidental and intentional drug overdoses (1979-2021) and drug overdoses involving opioids and/or stimulants (1999-2021). Drug overdose mortality risks were assessed using Cox Proportional Hazards models that generated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) adjusted for covariates. Trends of overdose mortality rates over time for theater vs. non-theater veterans were assessed by calculating average annual percent change (AAPC) in crude rates/100 000 persons (CRs).
RESULTS: Average age at baseline approximately 33 years. Most veterans were male (~97%), Caucasian (>75%) and Army (~50%). There were 9148 theater veteran drug overdose deaths (CR = 10.01) and 33 322 among non-theater veterans (CR = 12.87). Compared with non-theater veterans, theater veterans had increased risks of all drug overdose mortality (HR = 1.03, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.01-1.06) and accidental drug overdose mortality (6427; 23 347, respectively) (HR = 1.08, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.05-1.12); risk of intentional drug overdose mortality was lower (1683; 6435, respectively) (HR = 0.90, P < 0.001; 95% CI = 0.85-0.95). Theater veterans had increased risk of accidental drug overdose deaths involving opioids without stimulants (HR = 1.10, P = 0.0005; 95% CI = 1.04-1.17), stimulants without opioids (HR = 1.20, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.12-1.29) and opioids and/or stimulants (HR = 1.13, P < 0.0001; 95% CI = 1.08-1.17). CRs for all drug overdose mortality (1979-2021) increased for theater veterans (CR = 4.06, 1979; CR = 15.48, 2021; AAPC = 2.70, P < 0.001) and non-theater veterans (CR = 4.32, 1979; CR = 24.05, 2021; AAPC = 3.94, P < 0.001). Theater and non-theater veterans had increased CRs of overdose deaths (1999-2021) involving stimulants without opioids (AAPC = 5.30, P < 0.013 and AAPC = 6.28, P < 0.006, respectively).
SUMMARY: United States military veterans who served in Vietnam during the Vietnam War have a small increased risk of drug overdose mortality compared with veterans who did not serve in Vietnam.

title: PIWIL2: A new link between RNA biology, inflammation, and ischemic brain injury
abstract: Ischemic stroke begins with a sudden interruption of blood flow to the brain, but the damage does not stop when blood flow is restored. The initial ischemic insult triggers a series of secondary events, including inflammation, oxidative stress, cell death, and disrupted genomic regulation. These can continue to damage the brain well beyond the initial vascular event. Mapping the molecular pathways that link ischemic stress to this secondary injury remains one of the persistent challenges in stroke research.

title: Abstract 10262: Impact of Achieving Artificial Intelligence-Derived Individualized Systolic Blood Pressure 3 Months from Baseline on 1-year Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events
abstract: Introduction: Using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based approach, we previously identified individualized systolic blood pressure (SBP) ranges associated with the lowest 1-year risk of major adverse cardiovascular (CV) events (MACE) among 671,465 Veterans (AUC 0.84) treated for hypertension (HTN). However, it is unknown whether patients who are not initially at their optimal SBP but subsequently achieve it within 3 months experience lower risk of future MACE. Objective: Leveraging cross-linked electronic health record (EHR) system within the Department of Veterans Affairs, we sought to determine whether achievement of individualized AI-derived optimal SBP within 3 months of baseline measurement is associated with lower 1-year MACE risk compared with those who did not. Methods: The study sample comprised of 265,307 Veterans without a heart failure (HF) diagnosis treated for HTN from 2000-2024 who did not have an AI-derived optimal SBP at a randomly chosen baseline but had a follow-up BP measurement within 3 months. Patients were tracked via EHR for a year (15 months post baseline) for MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, HF hospitalization, death). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling adjusted for demographics, co-morbidities, laboratory values and CV medications, were used to compare the risk of 1-year MACE between patients who achieved optimal SBP at 3 months vs. those who did not. Results: Of the 265,307 patients, 23,841 (9.0%) achieved optimal 3month SBP, whereas 241,466 (91.0%) did not. Patients achieving optimal SBP were slightly older (70.7±8.5 vs 70.1±9.5 years), had lower rates of prior MACE (1.7 vs. 3.5%), hospitalization in the prior year (14.8 vs 24.6%), ischemic stroke (5.5 vs 9.0%), myocardial infarction (3.7 vs 6.3%), chronic kidney disease (13.5 vs 16.3%), depression (26.0 vs 30.3%), and smoking (26.2 vs 32.4%). In patients who achieved optimal SBP, 7628 (32.0%) increased the number of anti-HTN agents, 4325 (18.1%) decreased the number of anti-HTN agents, and 1596 (6.7%) changed to another class of anti-HTN agent. Dose change within agents were not investigated. In patients not achieving optimal SBP, 77572 (32.1%) increased, 45868 (19.0%) decreased the number of anti-HTN agents, and 21907 (9.1%) changed to another class of anti-HTN agent.Achievement of individualized optimal 3 month SBP was associated with a lower 1-year MACE risk compared with failure to achieve optimal SBP (8.4% vs 15.1%; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.70-0.77; p<0.001) (Figure). There was a significant interaction between achievement of optimal SBP and corresponding diastolic BP [DBP] measures (optimal SBP х DBP interaction, p<0.001). Conclusion: Achievement of AI-derived individualized optimal SBP within 3 months was associated with lower 1-year MACE risk and varied by the corresponding DBP. These findings support the potential role of AI-guided individualized BP targets to improve CV outcomes.

title: Examining the multivariate genetic architectures of posttraumatic stress disorder and cardiovascular disease phenotypes
abstract: Abstract Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, but the extent of shared inherited liability is unclear. Large genome‐wide association studies (GWAS) allow for multivariate evaluation of common genetic architecture. We analyzed European‐ancestry GWAS summary statistics for PTSD ( N _eff ≈ 1.22 million), CVD outcomes (CVD outcomes ; coronary artery disease, stroke, hypertension; N _eff = 126,000–574,000), and CVD risk factors (CVD risk ; high‐density lipoprotein, triglycerides, fasting glucose, waist circumference; N = 211,000–526,000). Using genomic structural equation modeling, we modeled latent genetic structure across PTSD and CVD phenotypes and conducted multivariate GWAS of latent factors with gene and gene‐set annotation. A three‐factor model distinguishing PTSD, CVD risk , and CVD outcomes best fit the data, χ 2 = 256.9, CFI = .990, SRMR = .040. PTSD showed a moderate genetic correlation with CVD risk , rg = .340, p < .001, and a significant but negligible genetic correlation with CVD outcomes , rg = 0.030, p < .001, suggesting minimal shared genetic liability at the latent‐factor level. Multivariate GWAS identified seven loci for PTSD, 96 for CVD risk , and 51 for CVD outcomes . Gene‐based tests implicated 85, 910, and 390 genes, respectively, with 18 overlapping between PTSD and CVD risk . Enrichment highlighted RNA metabolism for PTSD and lipid/vascular pathways for CVD traits. Additional locus‐level overlaps emerged, including a genomic hub in the major histocompatibility complex region on Chromosome 6 for both phenotypes. PTSD shares moderate polygenic overlap with CVD, particularly CVD risk , but many loci are trait‐specific, implicating lipid metabolism, vascular tone, immune/inflammatory pathways, and RNA regulation as potential links.

title: Associations of Coexisting Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sarcopenia-Related Abnormalities With Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Obesity States.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with adverse liver and non-liver outcomes, but the impact of coexisting sarcopenia-related abnormalities (e.g., low muscle strength [MS], muscle mass, and physical performance) remains unclear. In a prospective UK Biobank cohort (n = 438,748), we evaluated their joint associations with incidence and risks of all-cause mortality, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), non-liver cancers, and obesity-related cancers across MASLD and sarcopenia-related abnormality status. Over a median follow-up of 13.8 years, 401 HCC, 1714 cirrhosis, 39,534 CVD, 19,637 CKD, 38,240 non-liver cancers, 12,536 obesity-related cancers, and 34,801 deaths occurred. A stepwise increase in both incidence and adjusted risk of liver and non-liver outcomes was observed across MASLD and sarcopenia strata. Within the coexistence group, the obesity (vs. non-obesity) subgroup generally had higher risks. For example, for cirrhosis, adjusted hazard ratios increased from 3.93 to 7.36 then 8.48 with MASLD alone, coexisting MASLD with low MS overall and coexisting MASLD, low MS and obesity, respectively. Similar findings were observed in external validation analyses using the 2011-2018 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort. Together, these observations inform risk stratification strategy and management of MASLD to include sarcopenia assessment.

title: A sex-specific platelet switch controls anti-tumor immunity in glioblastoma
abstract: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8 + T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8 + T cell activity, whereas CD8 + T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8 + T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

title: Development of gemcitabine-modified miR-15a as a novel, multimodal treatment strategy to overcome 5-FU and oxaliplatin resistance in colorectal cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Resistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-based chemotherapy is a major clinical obstacle in colorectal cancer (CRC), highlighting the urgent need to overcome established resistance mechanisms. MicroRNA-based therapeutics have emerged as compelling candidates in this context, given their inherently pleiotropic mode of action; however, their clinical translation remains hindered by poor stability and suboptimal delivery. Methods To address these limitations, Gem-miR-15a, a unique gemcitabine-modified tumor-suppressor microRNA-15a was designed to synergistically integrate the tumor-suppressive activity of miR-15a with the chemotherapeutic potency of gemcitabine into a single molecular entity. Therapeutic efficacy of Gem-miR-15a was evaluated across a spectrum of preclinical models, including parental and drug-resistant CRC cell lines, 3D tumor spheroids, patient-derived organoids and in vivo metastatic models. Cell viability, apoptosis and cell cycle analyses were performed, along with RNA sequencing and protein validation. Statistical analyses were conducted using Student’s t-test or two-way ANOVA with mixed effects, and data were presented as mean ± SD. Results Gem-miR-15a exhibited potent anti-proliferative activity with IC 50 values in the low nanomolar range, achieving ~ 100-5000-fold greater potency relative to 5-FU and oxaliplatin. Importantly, it retained efficacy in both 5-FU- and oxaliplatin-resistant CRC models, effectively overcoming acquired chemoresistance. Mechanistically, Gem-miR-15a induced S-phase cell cycle arrest, eliminated the G2-phase cell population, and triggered apoptosis, accompanied by suppression of key oncogenic targets including WEE1, CHK1, YAP1 and BMI1. RNA-seq analysis further demonstrated modulation of pathways such as p53 signaling and reversal of resistance-associated gene expression, that were corroborated at the protein level. In vivo , Gem-miR-15a significantly reduced tumor growth at a dose ~ 12-fold lower than gemcitabine, with no observable toxicity. Conclusion Gem-miR-15a represents a potent, multi-targeted therapeutic strategy capable of overcoming chemoresistance in CRC. Its enhanced stability, effective delivery and robust efficacy across resistant models and a favorable safety profile highlight its strong potential for clinical translation.

title: Repetitive low-level blast exposure and brain health: State-of-the-science and clinical priorities in 2026
abstract: Low-level blast (LLB) exposures generated by weapons systems and explosives use are now recognized as an occupational hazard for many military and law-enforcement communities. Although individual exposures often fall below thresholds for clinically diagnosable concussion, accumulating data from human and animal studies suggest that repetitive LLB can produce subtle but durable changes in neurobehavioral function, neuroimaging markers, and blood- and CSF-based biomarkers, as well as cardiovascular and neurovascular health. At the same time, the field remains fragmented, with heterogeneous exposure metrics, characterized by non-standardized exposure quantification methods, variable outcome measures, and inconsistent longitudinal follow-up intervals. This state-of-the-science review synthesizes current evidence on LLB with a deliberate emphasis on clinical aspects that matter to Servicemembers, Veterans, and clinicians focusing on posttraumatic outcomes (e.g., psychological, cognitive, physical), reduction of risk of neurodegenerative disease, and practical pathways for exposure prevention and mitigation. We first describe contemporary definitions and patterns of LLB exposure across operational communities, followed by a critical appraisal of epidemiological studies linking LLB to symptoms, functional outcomes, and health-care utilization. We then summarize converging evidence for neurodegenerative and neurovascular risks, integrate mechanistic insights from neuroimaging, neuropathology, and animal models, and highlight emerging biomarker and computational approaches. Finally, we outline pragmatic strategies for exposure assessment, screening, and follow-up in clinical settings and identify high-priority research and policy directions. Rather than asking whether LLB is "safe" or "unsafe" in absolute terms, we focus on vulnerability and context as a roadmap for scientific and clinical development while balancing mission requirements with long-term brain health.

title: PTHrP induces breast cancer bone metastases via microbial-dependent expansion of TNF/IL-17-producing T cells.
abstract: Bone metastases are a frequent complication of breast cancer, leading to reduced quality of life and increased morbidity. By intratibially injecting PyMT breast cancer cells in mice, we showed that the presence in the gut microbiome of segmented filamentous bacteria (SFB), a taxon that induces IL-17-producing Th17 cells and TNF-α (TNF)-producing T cells (TNF+ T cells), accelerated intraosseous tumor growth. SFB increased the activity of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP), a known driver of breast cancer bone metastasis produced by breast cancer cells. SFB promoted the PTHrP-induced expansion of intestinal Th17 cells and TNF+ T cells, their migration to bone marrow (BM) in tumor-bearing bones, and the BM expression of TNF, IL-17, and RANKL, cytokines that promote bone resorption. Demonstrating the functional relevance of IL-17 and TNF, silencing of either IL-17 or TNF blunted the growth of bone lesions in SFB+ mice. Thus, the abundance of SFB in the microbiome of mice and of SFB-like taxa in humans may determine the potency of PTHrP and the rate of growth of bone metastasis in breast cancer. Targeting the gut microbiota may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for breast cancer bone metastasis.

title: Minocycline attenuates gulf war illness-related pain sensitization and preserves descending control of nociception in mice
abstract: Gulf War Illness (GWI) is a chronic multisymptom condition characterized by widespread pain. In a murine model of GWI-related chemicals exposure for one month, the efficiency of endogenous pain control systems, latent pain sensitization and anxiety state were examined. Circulating cytokines were quantified with multiplex assay and ELISAs. Effects of minocycline treatment were evaluated in GWI mice. We observed robust periorbital sensitization after exposure to the bright light stress (BLS headache model), increased hindpaw allodynia in osteoarthritis and musculoskeletal pain models in GWI mice. Minocycline reduced or eliminated the GWI chemical-related excess sensitization and loss of descending control of nociception (DCN), suggesting the drug preserves a key component of endogenous pain modulation. GWI-related chemical exposure caused a mild anxiety-like state not prevented by minocycline. Multiplexed analysis of plasma cytokines revealed no significant differences 3 months after completion of chemical administration between control mice and other treatment groups. However, a more sensitive ELISA demonstrated elevation of circulating MCP-1 in GWI chemical-treated mice, which was blocked by co-treatment with minocycline. Our findings suggest that the widespread pain-related complaints characteristic of GWI may be due to loss of DCN. Minocycline, potentially through its anti-neuroinflammatory activity, prevents damage to endogenous pain control systems.

title: Quantitative Flow Ratio– vs Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
abstract: Importance: Whether the association of quantitative flow ratio (QFR)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with long-term outcomes differs according to multivessel disease (MVD) status is uncertain. Objective: To assess the association of QFR-guided vs angiography-guided PCI with 3-year outcomes according to MVD status. Design, Setting, and Participants: In this prespecified secondary analysis of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial, patients were screened across 26 centers in China from December 25, 2018, to January 19, 2020. Eligible participants were adults undergoing PCI for stable or unstable angina or for myocardial infarction (MI) occurring at least 72 hours before screening who had at least 1 lesion with 50% to 90% diameter stenosis in a vessel of 2.5 mm or larger. The analysis compared QFR-guided with angiography-guided PCI according to MVD status. MVD was defined by involvement of at least 2 epicardial vessels or the left main coronary artery. The primary analyses of the current prespecified secondary analysis were completed in October 2024. Interventions: Randomization 1:1 to QFR-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary end point of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, MI, and ischemia-driven revascularization. The current analysis evaluated 3-year MACE. Results: Among 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population (mean [SD] age, 62.7 [10.0] years; 2699 [70.6%] male), 2066 (54.0%) had MVD. In the MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 124 of 1023 patients (12.1%) in the QFR-guided group and 188 of 1043 patients (18.1%) in the angiography-guided group (hazard ratio, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.52-0.81; P < .001), driven by lower rates of MI and revascularization. In the non-MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 76 of 890 patients (8.6%) and 95 of 869 patients (11.0%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.04; P = .09). The treatment × MVD interaction was not statistically significant (P for interaction = .35). The findings of landmark, per-protocol, competing-risk, sensitivity, and hierarchical win-ratio analyses were directionally consistent with the main findings. Conclusions and Relevance: In this prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial of patients undergoing PCI, QFR-guided PCI was associated with a lower 3-year MACE rate among patients with MVD; however, no significant interaction was observed between treatment effect and MVD status. These findings provide longer-term randomized evidence supporting QFR-guided PCI across MVD strata and warrant further confirmation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03656848.

title: Video Decision Support and Advance Care Planning in Older Adults With Advanced Kidney Disease
abstract: Importance: Older adults with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) face consequential decisions about whether to initiate dialysis, yet advance care planning (ACP), the communication that prepares patients for such decisions, is documented infrequently in ambulatory settings. Objective: To determine whether a video decision aid about treatment options for advanced CKD, combined with patient-created video declarations, increases ACP documentation among older adults with advanced CKD. Design, Setting, and Participants: This multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial was conducted at 12 ambulatory clinics from June 2021 to March 2025, with 12-month follow-up. Participants were adults 65 years or older with advanced CKD. Outcome assessors were masked to group assignment. Data were analyzed in April 2026. Interventions: Intervention participants viewed a certified video decision aid depicting 3 treatment options for advanced CKD (hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and conservative kidney management) and then created a video declaration, a recorded statement of goals, values, and treatment preferences in video, audio, or written format, that was sent to their treating clinician. Control participants received usual medical care. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was ACP documentation in the electronic health record within 12 months of enrollment or death, whichever came sooner. Documentation was ascertained by validated natural language processing-assisted human adjudication. Prespecified secondary outcomes included documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options and stated treatment preferences. Results: A total of 453 patients were included (228 intervention [50.3%] and 225 control [49.7%]; mean [SD] age, 78.8 [6.4] years; 190 women [41.9%]; 4 American Indian or Alaska Native [1.1%], 8 Asian [1.8%], 38 Black [8.4%], 35 Hispanic or Latino [7.7%], 3 Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander [0.7%], and 375 White [82.8%] individuals). At 12 months, ACP documentation was higher in the intervention group than the control group (56.6% vs 40.0%; rate difference, 16.6%; 95% CI, 7.5%-25.7%; P < .001), as was documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options (46.1% vs 31.6%; rate difference, 14.5%; 95% CI, 5.6%-23.4%; P = .001). After viewing the video, fewer intervention participants than controls at enrollment were undecided about treatment (30 of 227 [13.2%] vs 92 of 223 [41.3%]), and more preferred conservative kidney management (115 of 227 [50.7%] vs 71 of 223 [31.8%]; P < .001 for the overall distribution). Conclusions and Relevance: This randomized clinical trial found that, among older adults with advanced CKD, a video decision aid increased ACP documentation and reduced the proportion of patients who were undecided about treatment. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04347629.

title: A Water-Soluble Pro-Drug of Acetaminophen Has Increased Intracellular Delivery of Active Drug and Anti-Cancer Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background/Objectives. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are two of the deadliest adult cancers. High-dose acetaminophen (AAP) has anti-cancer activity when given in conjunction with CYP2E1 inhibitors to block liver toxicity. However, the administration of high doses of AAP presents practical challenges stemming from limited water solubility, making it difficult to create a concentrated treatment solution in limited volume. Propacetamol (PROP) is a water-soluble AAP pro-drug that has been used clinically as an IV AAP formulation for analgesia. Methods. We sought to investigate the pharmacokinetics, safety and anti-cancer activity of PROP in comparison to AAP using transplantable syngeneic models of TNBC and PDAC. Results. In vivo, PROP was rapidly converted to AAP within minutes of administration. PROP demonstrated enhanced effectiveness in suppressing tumor growth in the TNBC and PDAC syngeneic murine tumor models compared to AAP. The enhanced efficacy of PROP appears to stem from increased cellular uptake, leading to intracellular AAP concentrations that are 2.7-fold higher within 5 min compared to cells treated with unmodified AAP. PROP demonstrated enhanced modulation of intracellular JAK/STAT signaling, a key mediator of AAP anti-cancer activity, using both murine and humanized models. STAT3 and STAT6 inhibition by PROP led to modulation of macrophage polarization, likely contributing to its anti-TNBC and anti-PDAC activity. While parenteral administration is the preferred route of administration for PROP in anti-cancer indications, we also evaluated the safety and efficacy of oral PROP in comparison to AAP. High-dose PROP demonstrated improved safety following oral administration compared to AAP in the BALB/c murine model while maintaining anti-cancer activity in vivo. Conclusions. PROP, an AAP pro-drug, demonstrates enhanced intracellular delivery of AAP and in vivo anti-cancer activity compared to unmodified AAP, setting the stage for investigation as an anti-cancer drug across different indications.

title: Large Language Model-Generated Synthetic Data for Parole and Probation Detection in Clinical Notes: Development and Evaluation Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying individuals on parole or probation can help inform care pathways and ensure continuity of care in health care systems. However, this sensitive justice-related information is often absent from structured electronic health record fields and is instead documented in narrative clinical notes. Developing automated parole and probation detection (PPD) systems typically requires expert-annotated clinical data, but manual annotation is costly, time-consuming, and constrained by data sparsity and privacy concerns.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a synthetic-only training paradigm for PPD from clinical text that eliminates the need for expert-annotated training data while maintaining strong performance and cross-domain transfer to real-world data.
METHODS: We developed Synth-PPD, a synthetic dataset comprising 7579 labeled clinical notes generated using large language models (LLMs), redundancy filtering, and automated quality evaluation. Dataset quality was assessed through human review of 1517 synthetic notes by 2 annotators. The primary outcome was the macro-F1-score for PPD. We evaluated Synth-PPD across unsupervised and supervised learning settings using LLMs, traditional machine learning models, and transformer encoders. Performance was assessed on 293 expert-annotated real-world clinical notes from the US Department of Veterans Affairs.
RESULTS: Synth-PPD achieved 90.05% human-LLM alignment. In the unsupervised setting, Llama 3.3-70B-Instruct with chain-of-thought prompting and few-shot examples from Synth-PPD achieved a macro-F1-score of 87.22%, outperforming both the corresponding zero-shot model (80.10%) and the best rule-based baseline (77.55%; P<.001 for all comparisons). In the supervised setting, Llama 3.1-8B fine-tuned on Synth-PPD achieved a macro-F1-score of 81.43%, exceeding the best rule-based baseline (77.55%; P<.001) and achieving a numerically higher score than the substantially larger zero-shot Llama 3.3-70B-Instruct model (80.10%; P=.08). In contrast, traditional machine learning models and transformer encoders exhibited greater performance degradation under domain shift and derived limited benefit from increasing synthetic training data. Additional experiments showed that increasing synthetic training data improved cross-domain performance for LLM-based models but yielded comparatively smaller gains for traditional approaches.
CONCLUSIONS: Synthetic data generated by LLMs can serve as a scalable, cost-effective, and privacy-preserving alternative to expert-annotated real-world clinical data for PPD from clinical text. The findings demonstrate successful cross-domain transfer to real-world US Department of Veterans Affairs clinical notes.

title: Spatial Molecular Signatures of Canine Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma with and Without Locoregional Metastasis with Cross-Species Comparison to Human Samples.
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of locoregional spread in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is critical for prognosis and treatment planning. However, the currently available pre-surgical staging modalities often fail to detect occult nodal metastasis, necessitating nodal extirpation for accurate pathologic staging. This approach carries no clinical benefit and introduces unwarranted morbidity in patients with nonmetastatic lymph nodes (pN0 neck). The aim of this study was to define the molecular landscape of HNSCC in a spontaneous model of disease (pet dogs) with and without pathologically confirmed locoregional metastasis to identify biomarkers that may improve risk stratification and guide nodal management. Spatial transcriptomic profiling revealed a distinct metastatic tumor signature characterized by downregulation of PTEN, EPSTI1, CD99, MAPKAPK2, OAZ1, and upregulation of LOC477699. The tumor microenvironment of metastatic tumors demonstrated reduced JAK1 and trends consistent with T-cell exhaustion. Metastatic lymph node deposits conserved transcriptomic signatures matched to the primary tumor, and peri-metastatic lymph nodes displayed potentially permissive molecular alterations, including reduced F13A1 and DLA88 expression. Cross-species comparisons with human datasets identified conserved molecular and pathway-level features. Collectively, these findings identify candidate biomarkers and biological pathways associated with locoregional metastasis and support future prospective validation in canine and human HNSCC.

title: What do AI chatbots do after users decline therapeutic redirection for suicide thoughts?
abstract: Safety evaluations of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots focus on therapeutic redirection, statements urging users who disclose suicide thoughts to seek help from crisis lines or other human sources. How chatbots respond when users refuse that help is unclear. This cross-sectional audit ran 2,550 scripted multi-turn conversations in September 2026. Each conversation opened with a disclosure of suicide thoughts at 3 levels of severity, answered every referral with up to 10 standardized refusals and then changed the subject. All 2,550 conversations included a referral, 2,542 (99.7%) in the first reply. However, mean persistence ranged from 0.01 to 9.94 refusals across chatbots. Newer versions of all 5 chatbots tested in 2 versions persisted less than older versions (each P < .05). Compared with passive ideation, a disclosure of intent was associated with 1.26 more refusals sustained (95% CI, 1.06-1.46) and higher odds of renewed referral after the topic change (odds ratio, 10.07; 95% CI, 7.43-13.66). Chatbots that persisted less in referral more often presented themselves as the user's support (Spearman rho = -0.80; P < .001). Of 8,818 refusal-phase replies urging outside help, only 173 (2.0%) asked about barriers to seeking it. Chatbots uniformly recommended outside help after disclosures of suicide thoughts but varied widely in persisting in those recommendations, with newer versions persisting less. Safety evaluations should test what happens after a crisis referral is refused, not only whether one is offered.

title: Pharmacokinetic-Modifying Linker Design Modulates Performance of Multivalent PSMA/GRPR-Cell-Targeting 177Lu Radiopharmaceuticals.
abstract: Background/Objectives: A series of PSMA/GRPR-targeting compounds were selected based on modifications to their respective pharmacokinetic-modifying linking groups and the structure of the PSMA-binding moiety, to examine how these alterations impact binding affinity and specificity for preclinical prostate cancer models. Methods: The multi-receptor targeting heterodimers PSMA/2PSMA-X-DOTA-Y-BBN (where X is 6-aminohexanoic acid (6AHX) or polyethylene glycol-4 (PEG4) and Y is either 8-aminooctanoic acid (8AOC) or carboxy piperidine (CP)) were radiolabeled with the theranostic isotope [177Lu]Lu. Each heterodimer construct was evaluated through characterization, stability, whole-cell in vitro studies, biodistribution in tumor-bearing mice, and in vivo small animal SPECT/CT molecular imaging. Results: In vitro evaluation of 2PSMA-6AHX-DOTA-8AOC-BBN demonstrated moderate IC50 values of 200 ± 20 nM in LNCaP cells and 21 ± 1 nM in PC3 cells. Subsequent biodistribution studies demonstrated selective tumor uptake at 4 h post-intravenous injection with uptake of 9.52 ± 2.59%ID/g in GRPR[+] PC3 tumors and 6.37 ± 0.64%ID/g in PSMA[+] PC3-PIP tumors. At 24 h post-injection, high tumor-to-blood ratios (874.0 ± 276 in PC3 and 344.3 ± 85 in PC3-PIP) and tumor-to-muscle ratios (739.8 ± 277 in PC3 and 403.5 ± 66 in PC3-PIP) were observed, further supporting the theranostic feasibility of the radiolabeled heterodimer. Small animal SPECT/CT imaging confirmed tumor targeting specificity of the heterobivalent peptide. Conclusions: Evaluation in PSMA/GRPR-expressing tumor models identified 2PSMA-6AHX-DOTA-8AOC-BBN as a leading candidate, having enhanced tumor uptake and favorable pharmacokinetics in tumor-bearing mice. These investigations advance structure-activity relationship understanding and support heterobivalent radiopharmaceuticals for precision imaging and targeted prostate cancer therapy.

title: Population pharmacokinetics modeling of albendazole and its active metabolite, albendazole sulfoxide in mass drug administration against lymphatic filariasis.
abstract: Albendazole (ALB), a benzimidazole antiparasitic, is widely used in mass drug administration (MDA) campaigns against lymphatic filariasis (LF). It is rapidly metabolized to its active form, albendazole sulfoxide (ALB-OX), which exhibits considerable interindividual variability (IIV) in pharmacokinetics (PK). This variation may affect ALB efficacy in MDA programs. We developed a population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model characterizing ALB and ALB-OX exposure and identifying demographic and clinical covariates contributing to IIV in patients with LF and healthy individuals. Plasma concentration-time data were pooled from three clinical studies involving ALB co-administered with ivermectin and diethylcarbamazine. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling was conducted using Phoenix NLME. Covariate effects (e.g., sex, age, infection status) were assessed, and model validation employed visual predictive checks and bootstrapping. Simulations explored covariate impact on exposure. A joint two-compartment model with transit absorption for ALB and pre-systemic ALB-OX formation best described the data. Sex significantly influenced ALB-OX clearance and volume of distribution, with males exhibiting higher clearance and lower exposure. Body weight, age, and LF infection status did not significantly affect PK parameters. Simulations confirmed 33% lower ALB-OX levels in males compared to females following a 400 mg oral ALB dose. This is the first PopPK model of ALB and ALB-OX in LF-endemic populations. It highlights sex as a key covariate explaining IIV in ALB-OX exposure, with implications for optimized dosing in MDA programs. Further studies incorporating pharmacogenetics and pediatric data are warranted.This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT04410406, NCT02845713, and NCT03664063.

title: Advance Care Planning for Black and White Older Adults With Serious Illness: The EQUAL ACP Randomized Trial.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Advance care planning (ACP) helps individuals communicate preferences for future medical care. Many adults do not participate in ACP, and Black adults are less likely than White adults to participate.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effectiveness of facilitated vs self-guided ACP interventions.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: EQUAL ACP was a multisite, cluster randomized trial conducted in 10 primary care (n = 9) and geriatrics (n = 1) clinics in the South of the United States. Participants were community-dwelling Black and White adults 65 years or older with serious illness. Within each clinic and study group, participants were randomized to a racially concordant or discordant ACP facilitator.
INTERVENTIONS: Clinics were randomized to Respecting Choices First Steps, a facilitated ACP approach, or Five Wishes, a self-guided approach. Both were delivered by lay ACP facilitators.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: ACP completion within 12 months after the baseline survey, defined as new formal (advance directive, clinician note, or orders for life-sustaining treatment form in the medical record) and/or new informal ACP (participant-reported discussion with family about end-of-life care preferences). The primary analysis compared the effectiveness of the self-guided approach with the facilitated approach within each racial group. Other analyses assessed interaction between race and treatment in the combined sample and the association of participant-facilitator racial concordance with ACP.
RESULTS: Of 791 participants, 427 were Black and 364 were White; 409 were in clinics with the facilitated approach and 382 in clinics with the self-guided approach. Among Black participants, 152 of 213 (71%) in facilitated clinics and 131 of 213 (62%) in self-guided clinics completed ACP within 1 year (adjusted risk ratio [RR], 1.15 [95% CI, 0.83-1.59]). Among White participants, 133 of 196 (68%) in facilitated clinics and 131 of 167 (78%) in self-guided clinics completed ACP (adjusted RR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.65-1.18]). Among 789 in the pooled sample, 547 (69%) completed ACP, including 130 of 789 with formal ACP and 523 of 668 with informal ACP. In the pooled sample, the interaction between race and intervention group was significant (adjusted RR, 1.32 [95% CI, 1.03-1.69]), indicating greater effectiveness of the facilitated vs self-guided approach among Black relative to White participants. Participant-facilitator racial concordance was not associated with ACP in either racial group.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: ACP completion within 1 year did not differ significantly between facilitated vs self-guided ACP approaches within Black or White racial groups.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03516994.

title: Factors Associated With Fall-Related Head Impact Among Older Adults: A Scoping Review
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To map and synthesize the extent, range, and nature of existing research concerning factors associated with fall-related head impact among older adults. DESIGN: Scoping review. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Older adults aged 60 years and older. METHODS: A comprehensive search across 4 databases (PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Embase) was conducted to identify peer-reviewed research reporting factors associated with head impact during falls. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts. Data were extracted by 1 reviewer and verified by another, and results were synthesized into 3 domains: individual-, environmental/situational-, and task-level factors. RESULTS: Thirteen of 2921 studies met the inclusion/exclusion criteria and were included. Most applied observational analyses of video-recorded falls in long-term care settings, with only 1 interventional study. Female sex, forward-initiated, and forward-landing falls were consistently linked to higher odds of head impact. Findings for age and other individual factors were mixed or insignificant. There was limited evidence that fall timing, activity (eg, walking), and object contact were associated with impact risk. Movement patterns during fall descent (body rotation away from the initial direction and upper limb movements) were associated with lower odds of head impact. One randomized controlled trial reported that older adults could learn protective movements and reduce the odds of head impact during experimentally induced falls. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Most factors associated with fall-related head impact were nonmodifiable (eg, sex). Training the use of protective fall movements, environmental design (including protective equipment), and education hold promise in reducing the risk of head impact. Future research should prioritize testing modifiable approaches in real-world settings for reducing fall-related head impact and, ultimately, preventing head injuries in the aging population.

title: Urine cell-free RNA for bladder cancer detection and treatment response prediction.
abstract: Urine biomarkers promise to improve noninvasive detection and molecular characterization of genitourinary malignancies. Here we describe urine random priming and affinity capture of cell-free RNA (cfRNA) fragments for enrichment analysis by sequencing (uRARE-seq), a liquid biopsy method for urine cfRNA profiling, and apply it to 683 urine samples from patients with cancer and controls. Urine cfRNA contained transcripts from genitourinary tissues and, in patients with prostate, kidney or bladder cancer, tumor-derived transcripts. uRARE-seq demonstrated 95% sensitivity at 90% specificity for detecting localized bladder cancer. The method outperformed urine tumor DNA analysis and was unaffected by the presence of field-effect mutations. Urine cfRNA analysis also sensitively detected minimal residual disease and distinguished complete molecular responses after surgery from those after intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG). Pretreatment urine from complete responders to BCG was enriched for T cell and other immune signatures, suggesting a preexisting antitumor immune response, whereas nonresponders showed higher expression of proliferation-related genes. In pretreatment urine from 114 patients, this biological difference enabled development of a biomarker predicting likelihood of response to BCG versus chemotherapy (area under the curve 0.93) that was strongly associated with risk of recurrence. Urine cfRNA analysis is therefore a promising biomarker approach for bladder cancer and potentially other urologic malignancies, although prospective studies are needed to assess its clinical utility.

title: ERX-208 Induces Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Suppresses DNA Damage Repair to Enhance Chemotherapy Sensitivity.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, driven in part by intrinsic and acquired therapeutic resistance to DNA-damaging chemotherapies. We previously demonstrated that ERX-208 targets the protein encoded by lysosomal acid lipase to induce catastrophic endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in ovarian cancer models. As ERX-class compounds advance to clinical development, rational combination strategies are needed to maximize therapeutic efficacy. To address this question, we conducted an unbiased in vitro screen of the combination of ERX-208 with 147 FDA-approved agents. We identified that DNA-damaging chemotherapies, including anthracyclines, oxaliplatin, and paclitaxel, were most synergistic in combination with ERX-208. Reanalysis of our transcriptomic data in ovarian cancer cells revealed coordinated suppression of DNA damage repair, DNA replication, and checkpoint pathways following ERX-208 treatment. Together, these data support a narrative that ERX-208 may selectively suppress DNA repair pathways and potentiate cytotoxicity by DNA-damaging agents. To test this hypothesis, we used platinum and paclitaxel, two standard-of-care agents in ovarian cancer. We found that ERX-208 synergized with platinum and paclitaxel across multiple ovarian cancer models, enhancing apoptosis and suppressing proliferation, clonogenicity, and invasion. Mechanistically, combination treatment increased DNA damage and amplified ER stress and apoptotic signaling. Importantly, ERX-208-based combinations showed enhanced antitumor activity in patient-derived explant, and xenograft models. These findings support a model in which ERX-208 impairs DNA damage response pathways and sensitizes ovarian cancer cells to DNA-damaging chemotherapy. Collectively, these findings provide a strong rationale for the combination strategy in clinical translation.
SIGNIFICANCE: This study demonstrates the clinical utility of ERX-208 in enhancing chemotherapy efficacy in ovarian cancer. By inducing sustained ER stress and a functional DNA repair-deficient state, ERX-208 sensitizes treatment-naïve and treatment-resistant tumors to platinum and taxanes. Findings support the rapid clinical development of ERX-class combinations, offering a rationale for pairing with standard regimens. This strategy may enable dose reduction, overcome resistance, expand options, and support biomarker-guided patient selection.

title: Sex Differences in Mortality Among Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Sex is a well-recognized factor associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence, but its association with mortality is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between sex and the risk of overall, liver-related, and non-liver-related mortality among patients with HCC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients with HCC in 17 centers from 5 countries and regions (2000-2023). Male and female patients with HCC who had balanced baseline characteristics via inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were included, with a propensity score-matched cohort included for sensitivity analyses. Data were analyzed between July 10 and September 8, 2025.
EXPOSURES: Male vs female sex.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Overall, liver-related, and non-liver-related mortality.
RESULTS: Among 8594 patients with HCC (mean [SD] age, 63.3 [10.9] years; 6214 male [72.3%]; 5644 Asian [65.7%], 458 Black [5.3%], 615 Hispanic [7.2%], and 1784 White [20.8%]), 4567 were from Asia (53.1%), 6327 had cirrhosis (73.6%), and 6617 had viral etiology (77.0%). In the unmatched cohort, males had a higher overall mortality rate per 100 person-years than females in the total cohort (15.9 [95% CI, 15.3-16.4] vs 13.3 [95% CI, 12.5-14.1]; P < .001) and in Asian (14.1 [95% CI, 13.5-14.7] vs 11.1 [95% CI, 10.3-12.0]; P < .001), Asia region (14.4 [95% CI, 13.6-15.2] vs 10.8 [95% CI, 9.9-11.8]; P < .001), cirrhosis (17.6 [95% CI, 16.9-18.3] vs 14.4 [95% CI, 13.5-15.4]; P < .001), and hepatitis B (13.6 [95% CI, 12.7-14.5] vs 10.0 [95% CI, 8.6-11.5]; P < .001) and C (15.8 [95% CI, 15.0-16.6] vs 13.4 [95% CI, 12.4-14.6]; P < .001) subgroups. In the IPTW-matched cohort, male sex was associated with increased overall mortality in the full cohort (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.14 [95% CI, 1.05-1.23]; P = .002) and in Asian (aHR, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.10-1.36]; P < .001), Asia region (aHR, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.09-1.39]; P < .001), cirrhosis (aHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 1.08-1.29]; P < .001), and viral (aHR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.05-1.26]; P = .004) subgroups. Additionally, sex differences varied by liver disease etiology, with male sex having the highest aHR in the association with overall mortality among individuals with alcohol-associated liver disease (aHR, 1.90 [95% CI, 1.02-3.54]; P = .04), followed by those with hepatitis B (aHR, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.01-1.47]; P = .04) or C (aHR, 1.13 [95% CI, 1.02-1.26]; P = .03), but there was no association in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. There was no significant sex difference for non-liver-related mortality.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, sex disparities in HCC mortality existed but were heterogeneous across ethnic background and liver disease etiologies. These findings support incorporation of sex-based considerations in HCC management.

title: Symptom burden and interventions in veterans enrolled in the Proactive Response for Individual Symptom Management (PRISM) program.
abstract: 575 Background: Proactive Response for Individual Symptom Management (PRISM) is a Veterans Health Administration (VHA) program designed to improve early identification and management of cancer-related symptoms among Veterans receiving systemic anti-cancer therapy. Peer-support specialists conduct weekly telephone assessments and triage moderate, severe, or worsening symptoms to a nurse practitioner (NP) for intervention. We evaluated symptom burden and NP intervention frequency and types to inform program scale. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of PRISM documentation, including peer assessments, symptom scores, NP follow-up, and interventions. NP interventions were categorized as patient education, medication or laboratory management, referral to a new specialty or higher level of care, and notification of oncology or other specialty teams. Encounters with multiple intervention types were classified accordingly. Descriptive analyses characterized symptom frequency, NP interventions, and referral patterns. Results: From May 22, 2025, to June 10, 2026, 43 Veterans were enrolled. Peer specialists completed 734 surveys using the Veteran Symptom Assessment System (VSAS), with 452 assessments (61.6%) requiring NP intervention. The most common symptoms were fatigue (475/734, 64.7%), dyspnea on exertion (378/734, 51.5%), and drowsiness (345/734, 47.0%). Mental health symptoms were frequent, including anxiety (216/734, 29.4%), distress (199/734, 27.1%), and depression (172/734, 23.4%). Patient education alone was the most common NP intervention (313/452, 69.2%), followed by education with medication or laboratory management (101/452, 22.3%). Sixteen encounters (3.5%) required no intervention after NP review. Referrals included optometry (n=4), social work (n=2), dermatology (n=2), nutrition (n=2), occupational therapy (n=1), mental health (n=1), physical therapy (n=1), prosthetics (n=1), and one emergency department referral. Detailed categories are shown in Table 1. Conclusions: PRISM enabled proactive symptom monitoring and timely intervention between oncology visits. Veterans reported substantial physical and psychological symptom burden. Most NP encounters involved education, with others requiring medication management, referrals, or care coordination. These findings support a feasible, team-based model to enhance supportive oncology care and improve identification of unmet needs. title: Multisystem Outcomes of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Active Comparators in Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Target Trial Emulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) beyond cardiometabolic outcomes are incompletely characterized against active comparators in type 2 diabetes (T2D). We compared GLP-1RA with sulfonylureas (SUs), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4is) in adults with T2D.
METHOD: In a multicenter target trial emulation across 5 University of California academic medical centers (2012-2025) using harmonized electronic health record data, adults with T2D newly initiating GLP-1RA, SU, SGLT2i, or DPP4i were propensity score-matched 1-to-1 within site via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (>11 000 covariates), with up to 5-year follow-up. We screened 181 prespecified incident outcomes across 15 body systems, pooling hazard ratios by random-effects meta-analysis. Robustness required leave-one-medical-center-out stability, E-value ≥1.5, and false discovery rate-adjusted P < .10.
RESULTS: Among 70 982 matched adults, 118 robust associations were identified (65 for reduced risk and 53 for increased risk). Risk reductions were most consistent for cardiovascular outcomes, including myocarditis/cardiomyopathy (summary hazard ratio, 0.38 [95% CI, 0.32-0.44] vs SGLT2i), acute myocardial infarction (0.53 [0.42-0.66]), heart failure (0.71 [0.58-0.88] vs DPP4i), and thromboembolism (0.69-0.72), and for nephritis/nephrosis (0.73 [0.67-0.79]), nutritional anemia (0.70-0.81), coagulation disorders (0.73-0.81), and tobacco-related disorders (0.60 [0.49-0.74]). Risk increases were found for musculoskeletal conditions (22 associations); osteoarthritis 1.48 (1.29-1.68), stress fractures 1.68 (1.15-2.47), diverticular disease (1.18-1.33), sleep-wake disorders (1.27-1.54), and menopausal disorders (1.32-1.52).
CONCLUSIONS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist initiation was associated with reduced cardiovascular, renal, hematologic, and tobacco-related risk, consistent with outcome trials. Increased risks for musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, and sleep-wake disorders warrant monitoring as the clinical use of GLP-1RAs continues to expand.

title: Incremental cardiovascular benefit of GLP-1RA added to SGLT2i in type 2 diabetes: a target trial emulation in the US veterans health administration
abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction SGLT-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) reduce major cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes and are increasingly used together in clinical practice. Whether initiation of GLP-1RA as add-on therapy to SGLT-2i provides incremental cardiovascular benefit beyond SGLT-2i alone remains uncertain. Purpose To determine whether initiation of GLP-1RA as add-on therapy to SGLT-2i, compared with DPP-4i (a comparator with neutral cardiovascular effects), reduces major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes. Methods We emulated a target trial using national US Veterans Health Administration data (2013–2024). Adults with type 2 diabetes receiving background SGLT-2i who newly initiated GLP-1RA were compared with active-comparator new users of DPP-4i. Inverse probability of treatment and censoring weights were used to adjust for baseline and time-varying confounding in a marginal structural modeling framework. The primary analysis estimated the per-protocol effect. The primary outcome comprised the composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or stroke over a follow-up of up to 2 years. Hospitalization for heart failure was a pre-specified secondary endpoint. Results Among 79,792 adults (53,339 GLP-1RA; 26,453 DPP-4i), the mean age was 65 years, and 39% had prevalent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Background SGLT-2i use was predominantly empagliflozin (>99%). Eighty-seven percent of GLP-1RA initiators received semaglutide; 94% of DPP-4i initiators received alogliptin. After weighting, baseline characteristics were well balanced (all standardized mean differences <0.1). GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower risk of the composite cardiovascular outcome compared with DPP-4i (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.63, 0.99), corresponding to an absolute 2-year risk reduction of 1.57% (95% CI -3.06%, -0.04%). GLP-1RA was also associated with a lower risk of myocardial infarction (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.50, 0.95). Associations for all-cause death (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.62, 1.07), stroke (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.49, 1.10), and hospitalization for heart failure (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.58, 1.06) were directionally consistent but did not reach statistical significance. Findings were consistent across pre-specified high-risk subgroups, including body mass index, prevalent cardiovascular disease, and baseline AHA PREVENT 10-year cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk equation. Conclusions In this large target trial emulation of adults with type 2 diabetes receiving SGLT-2i therapy, add-on GLP-1RA was associated with significant reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events compared with DPP-4i, with consistent directional reductions across individual cardiovascular outcomes. These findings support combination GLP-1RA and SGLT-2i therapy as a strategy to further reduce residual cardiovascular risk in clinical practice.Figure

title: Safety and Efficacy of Omecamtiv Mecarbil by QRS Duration and Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in GALACTIC-HF.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged QRS duration portends worse outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). In GALACTIC-HF, omecamtiv mecarbil (OM) reduced the primary composite endpoint of first heart failure (HF) event or cardiovascular death.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate whether QRS duration and the presence of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) modify the treatment effect of OM.
METHODS: GALACTIC-HF enrolled patients with symptomatic HF, HFrEF (≤35%), and elevated natriuretic peptides. Baseline QRS duration was available in 8,089 of 8,232 participants (98.0%), who were classified into 3 groups: QRS duration <120 ms without CRT (n = 3,724), QRS duration ≥120 ms without CRT (n = 3,225), and CRT regardless of QRS duration (n = 1,140). The authors assessed whether the effect of OM on the primary composite endpoint, first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death differed across these groups.
RESULTS: Patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT and those with CRT were older, had lower EF, worse health status, and higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels than those with QRS <120 ms without CRT. When modeled as a continuous variable, baseline QRS duration was associated with clinical outcomes among patients without CRT but not among those with CRT. Among patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT, OM appeared to confer less benefit for the primary composite endpoint (Pinteraction = 0.072), for cardiovascular death (Pinteraction = 0.003), and for all-cause death (Pinteraction = 0.009). In contrast, among patients treated with CRT, OM was beneficial regardless of QRS duration.
CONCLUSIONS: In GALACTIC-HF, OM appeared less effective in patients with prolonged QRS duration who did not have CRT, whereas it remained beneficial in CRT-treated patients. (Global Approach to Lowering Adverse Cardiac Outcomes Through Improving Contractility in Heart Failure [GALACTIC-HF]; NCT02929329).
