title: Stress First Aid: A Peer Support Framework for Addressing Occupational Stress Injury in Military and Other High-Risk Occupations
abstract: Background Prolonged deployments, hybrid warfare, and expanding disaster-response missions expose service members to cumulative occupational stress that erodes readiness, retention, and long-term health. Between universal resilience training and formal clinical care lies a persistent gap: practical actions that peers and leaders can take when a coworker is strongly affected by stress. Stress First Aid (SFA) is a flexible, peer- and leader-delivered framework derived from the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps Combat and Operational Stress First Aid program and organized around five empirically supported protective elements in the recovery from ongoing adversity—safety, calming, connectedness, self-efficacy, and hope—translated into seven core actions. Methods This commentary summarizes the conceptual foundations of SFA and reviews published evaluations of SFA adaptations conducted between 2022 and 2025, encompassing 17 studies and over 3,000 participants across healthcare, fire service, nursing education, and related high-stress occupations, together with implementation findings relevant to military adoption. Results Across designs ranging from cluster randomized trials to a 12-month multi-hospital longitudinal evaluation, SFA shows consistent improvements in proximal outcomes—stress recognition, peer-support self-efficacy, group cohesion, perceived organizational support, and use of well-being resources—with more modest and less consistent effects on distal outcomes such as posttraumatic stress symptoms and burnout. Benefits appear strongest among younger workers and in settings with higher implementation fidelity. Conclusion SFA offers military organizations a scalable, low-burden, culturally adaptable layer of stress-injury care that complements both momentary acute stress protocols and formal treatment. Rigorous effectiveness trials in military settings are the priority next step.

title: Detection and characterization of in cellulo protein-RNA complexity by irCLIP-RNP, irCLIPv2 and Re-CLIP.
abstract: Transcriptome-wide methods to map RNA-protein interactions in living cells provide powerful tools to unravel the complexity of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) assemblies and their roles in post-transcriptional regulation. Here, we present three interconnected cross-linking and immunoprecipitation (CLIP)-based procedures, irCLIP-RNP, irCLIPv2 and Re-CLIP, that enable the identification and characterization of RNA-dependent associated proteins (RDAPs) in proximity to a target RNA-binding protein (RBP). After the construction of the infrared (IR) biotinylated DNA adapter, these methods combine UV cross-linking, partial RNase digestion, protein-specific immunoprecipitation and 3' DNA adapter ligation, followed by distinct downstream workflows: mass spectrometry for RDAP identification (irCLIP-RNP), RNA sequencing to map binding regions (irCLIPv2) or a second immunoprecipitation with sequencing for interaction validation (Re-CLIP). Custom bioinformatics pipelines analyze enriched RDAPs or significant binding sites, offering mechanistic insights into proximal RNA-protein interactions. Compared to conventional CLIP methods, these protocols resolve adjacent interactions, linking RBPs to their RDAPs with greater precision. The workflow is applicable across diverse contexts such as cell state transitions and stimulus responses. It requires expertise in RNA biochemistry, next-generation sequencing and computational analysis. The entire process, from cell harvesting to data analysis, can be completed in 7-10 d, providing a robust toolkit for investigating post-transcriptional regulatory networks.

title: Impact of Air Quality Index on Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in South Asians: A Narrative Review.
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines whether worsening air quality, as represented by the Air Quality Index (AQI), and its constituent pollutant exposures, is associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk in South Asia. South Asian populations have a genetic predisposition to cardiovascular disease and several modifiable risk factors; however, research examining the interaction between air quality and these factors remains understudied.
RECENT FINDINGS: Large population-based health studies consistently demonstrate a positive correlation between elevated levels of air pollutants, including PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂, CO, O₃, and NO, and ASCVD risk. Poor air quality may compound traditional ASCVD risk factors. Policy and pollution-reduction efforts may help, but evidence for South Asia-specific interventions remains limited. This review synthesizes evidence from population studies to establish air quality as a potentially modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and stresses the need for improved surveillance and targeted risk-mitigation strategies to address the ASCVD burden in South Asia.

title: Antimicrobial-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the USA: implications of a national surveillance gap.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surveillance data for Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the USA are distributed across systems designed for different purposes, potentially limiting standardized national surveillance of high-priority resistant phenotypes. We evaluated whether the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS) can support surveillance of multidrug-resistant (MDR) P. aeruginosa and synthesized available CDC surveillance data to characterize the residual surveillance gap.
METHODS: We reviewed the 2026 NNDSS list of nationally notifiable conditions for P. aeruginosa. Because neither P. aeruginosa infection nor a resistant phenotype was present, NNDSS case counts were unable to be analysed. We therefore conducted a descriptive secondary analysis of CDC National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) reports for 2018-21 and the 2022 NHSN Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Option report.
RESULTS: In 2018-21 adult NHSN data, 11.9% of tested P. aeruginosa isolates from device-associated infections were MDR, compared with 3.9% from surgical-site infections. Among central-line-associated bloodstream infection isolates, MDR proportions were highest in long-term acute-care hospitals (LTACHs, 25.3%), followed by hospital intensive-care units (14.2%), hospital wards (11.9%) and oncology units (8.5%). Among catheter-associated urinary tract infection isolates, MDR phenotype was observed in 20.8% of LTACH isolates. In the 2022 AR Option report, carbapenem non-susceptibility exceeded 10% among community-onset isolates and approached 20% among hospital-onset isolates.
CONCLUSIONS: NNDSS cannot currently quantify the burden of MDR P. aeruginosa, but substantial resistance surveillance is available through NHSN and the CDC AR Laboratory Network. The principal gap is not an absence of surveillance data but fragmentation across systems with different populations, denominators, objectives and reporting mechanisms.

title: Antibiotic-loaded cement spacers: a comprehensive review.
abstract: SUMMARYPeriprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) have become a costly complication of total joint arthroplasty, and the incidence continues to rise, given an increasing elderly population requiring total knee and total hip replacements. Traditionally, two-stage exchange (TSE) is the standard of care to combat chronic PJIs. The first stage of a TSE is defined by the removal of the prosthesis with implantation of an antibiotic-loaded cement spacer. There is a lack of guidance regarding the dosing of antimicrobials in cement spacers and a lack of safety data available in the infectious diseases literature. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of antibiotic-loaded cement spacers (ALCS) by reviewing published literature from peer-reviewed journals dating from 1988 to 2024 and discussing the authors' clinical experience. It was noted that with improvements to ALCS over the years, associated complications also evolved. Not only do mechanical challenges such as increased joint subluxation persist, but also complications of nephrotoxicity and allergic reactions occur due to unknown levels of systemic absorption of antibiotics. A multidisciplinary approach involving orthopedic surgeons, infectious diseases specialists, and pharmacists, in conjunction with patient-specific anti-microbial spacer dosing, would likely lead to improved outcomes in patients with chronic PJIs.

title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Incident Heart Failure from Routine Electronic Health Record Data.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) is largely preventable. Contemporary therapies can reduce incident HF among at-risk individuals, making scalable and accurate identification of high-risk patients a priority. Risk prediction models are traditionally developed from long-term epidemiologic cohorts, but machine learning (ML) can derive interpretable models directly from electronic health record (EHR) data captured in routine care. We developed an interpretable ML model for incident HF from health-system EHR data and compared it with established risk equations.
METHODS: We developed ML-based models for 5-year incident HF using EHR data from the Stanford Healthcare system, incorporating over 2000 predictors including structured data, temporal transformations, and variable interactions. We applied a neural additive model that combines feature selection and nonparametric survival analysis to develop the AIHF-Base model. We removed implausible predictors in an adjusted model (AIHF-Refined) to enhance clinical interpretability. We internally validated the models using a holdout Stanford sample and externally validated them in an independent national Veterans Affairs (VA) cohort with 10-year follow-up. Model discrimination was compared between the AIHF models and two benchmark HF prediction models, PCP-HF and PREVENT-HF.
RESULTS: The AIHF-Base model achieved an AUC of 0.847 in the Stanford cohort and 0.750 in the VA cohort. The AIHF-Refined model had an AUC of 0.840 (Stanford) and 0.741 (VA). Discrimination was comparable to that of PREVENT-HF and PCP-HF in both cohorts; in the VA cohort the AUC was 0.764 for PREVENT-HF and 0.738 for PCP-HF. Of the 14 features in the AIHF-Refined model, representing 13 distinct clinical variables, 7 used longitudinal EHR data. Age and smoking were the only features used by all models. Of 27 total features across models, 8 were used in at least one AIHF and one benchmark model, 19 were used only by AIHF or benchmark models.
CONCLUSIONS: Interpretable ML models built from routine EHR data identified clinically coherent predictors of incident HF and achieved discrimination comparable to established risk equations. By drawing on data already captured in clinical care, including longitudinal trends, this approach offers a scalable, transparent strategy for identifying patients at risk for HF and targeting them for prevention.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Understand Reasons for SGLT2 Nontreatment Among Patients With Heart Failure.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients with heart failure (HF) and a guideline indication for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) do not receive a prescription, but the reasons behind this are unclear. This study optimizes an large language model framework to identify reasons for the lack of SGLT2i prescriptions.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We extracted clinical notes for patients >18 years old with a first HF diagnosis identified by International Classification of Diseases, 10th edition, code seen in cardiology clinics between August 10, 2021, and March 1, 2025. Five annotators labeled reasons for SGLT2i nonprescription (the test set); the remaining unlabeled notes served as the inference set. Using both zero-shot (prompts do not include examples) and few-shot prompting techniques, we compared 2 large language models from OpenAI on their ability to classify the documented reason for nonprescription into 1 of 6 themes and 1 of 14 subthemes. We identified 599 HF patients (with 1123 notes), with an average age of 71 years and predominantly having HF with preserved ejection fraction. We used 313 labeled and 705 unlabeled notes as the test and inference sets, respectively, for a total set of 1018 notes. GPT-o1 outperformed GPT-4o and was 84.7% accurate (95% confidence interval 80.2%-88.5%) in identifying theme reasons for SGLT2i nonprescription. The most frequent theme was physician-attributed factors (n = 292 notes [28.7%]), among the total set. Physician deferral to a future visit (n = 157 notes [15.4%]) and the physician perceiving the patient to be at low risk or unlikely to benefit (n = 75 [7.4%]) were the most prevalent subthemes.
CONCLUSIONS: We optimized a large language model to accurately discriminate reasons for not prescribing SGLT2is from clinical notes. When a reason for SGLT2i nonprescription was documented, delayed initiation of SGLT2i and physician perception of patients as being at low risk were the most common reasons, offering valuable insight to improve guideline-indicated SGLT2i prescription.

title: Assessing the relevance of test of memory malingering (TOMM) trial 2 performance after failure of trial 1 among veterans with self-reported histories of mild traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Objective: Despite empirically established cut scores for Trial 1 of the Test of Memory Malingering (TOMM), the interpretive significance of failing Trial 1 while passing Trial 2 remains equivocal, possibly due to the original manual's emphasis on Trial 2. This study examined whether individuals with a Trial 1 fail/Trial 2 pass pattern demonstrate cognitive profiles more similar to individuals who fail both trials or pass both trials. Method: Participants were 203 Veterans with a history of self-reported mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) who completed a comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation in a multicenter study. Based on TOMM performance, participants were classified into Pass-Pass, Fail-Pass, and Fail-Fail groups. Standardized measures of learning and memory, attention/processing speed, executive functioning, and additional performance validity tests were examined. One-way analyses of variance were conducted to compare cognitive performance across groups. Results: The Fail-Pass group did not differ from the Fail-Fail group and performed significantly worse than the Pass-Pass group across learning and memory, attention/processing speed, executive functioning, and overall performance. Similarly, the Fail-Pass and Fail-Fail groups demonstrated comparable rates of failure on at least one additional independent performance validity test, with both groups exhibiting significantly higher failure rates than the Pass-Pass group. Conclusions: Veterans who fail TOMM Trial 1 but pass Trial 2 demonstrate cognitive and performance validity profiles more consistent with those who fail both trials than those who pass both trials. Consequently, Trial 2 pass status does not negate the clinical significance of Trial 1 failure in those with a history of self-reported mTBI.

title: Using Qualitative Methods to Support Implementation of Video Telehealth Across a National Health System: A Wholistic Process.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Personalized Implementation of Video Telehealth for Rural Veterans Team facilitated adoption of video telehealth for mental health care in rural facilities within the U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs (VA). It adapted several qualitative methods to support a multisited, multiyear telehealth implementation project. This paper details this work, providing guidance on how qualitative methods can be pragmatically used to support implementation of video telehealth.
METHODS: Three main qualitative activities were used to support implementation of video telehealth: interviews, integrated periodic reflections, and Rapid Reviews. The qualitative team consisted of two qualitative methodologists. From 2020 to 2023, needs-assessment interviews were conducted with site partners at 17 different VA medical centers. One-year post interviews were conducted with 15 site partners in 2020-2022. Integrated periodic reflections with the implementation team occurred twice a month from 2020 to 2024. From 2020 to 2024, the qualitative team created quarterly Rapid Reviews for active site partners. The number of periodic reflections created each quarter fluctuated from 5 to 12 during this time.
RESULTS: The qualitative activities and products presented here were used to support the implementation of video telehealth for mental health across multiple VA facilities. Methods were adapted to reduce burden for partners in rural areas. Qualitative activities supported practical use of information, helping all parties to understand how to continuously improve their activities for better mental health access.
CONCLUSIONS: The implementation of other innovative technologies for mental health faces many of the same challenges as video telehealth. Qualitative methods can support communication and increase likelihood of successful implementation.

title: Opioid and Gabapentinoid Prescribing in Older Adults with Dementia Before and After the 2016 CDC Opioid Prescribing Guideline.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In March 2016, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued guidelines advising against opioid use for most chronic pain because of their associated risks. Evaluating how this guideline affected subsequent opioid and non-opioid analgesic prescribing in older adults with dementia is critical, as this population is at heightened risk for both pain undertreatment and adverse medication effects.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the 2016 CDC opioid prescribing guideline was associated with changes in opioid and gabapentinoid prescribing in older adults with dementia.
DESIGN: Interrupted time series analysis of a longitudinal cohort from 2010 to 2022.
PARTICIPANTS: Community-dwelling older adults (≥ 65 years) with dementia enrolled in the Medicare Current Beneficiary Survey (MCBS), a nationally representative survey linked to Medicare claims.
MAIN MEASURES: Quarterly prescribing rates of opioids (typical opioids, tramadol, buprenorphine) and gabapentinoids (gabapentin, pregabalin) before and after CDC guideline release. Interrupted time series models estimated level (immediate) and trend (slope) changes associated with the guideline.
KEY RESULTS: We identified 3246 older adults with dementia (median age [IQR] 80.7 [73.8-86.2] years; 61.4% female). Typical opioid prescribing declined by 26.5% over the study period, but the guideline was not associated with this decline (trend change: 0.09 [95% CI -0.1, 0.3] percentage points [ppts]/quarter; level change -1.5 [95% CI -4.1, 1.0] ppt). The guideline was associated with the 27.1% decrease in tramadol prescribing (trend change: -0.2 ppts/quarter [95% CI, -0.3, -0.1]; level change: -1.8 [95% CI, -3.1, -0.6] ppts). Gabapentinoid prescribing increased from 9.5% to 11.5%, with no change in trend (0.0 ppts/quarter [95% CI, -0.01 to 0.02]) after the guideline release. Buprenorphine prescribing remained near zero.
CONCLUSIONS: We identified analgesic selection shifts rather than uniform opioid reductions following the CDC guideline release, but the impact of these shifts on symptom control remains unknown. More nuanced, evidence-based analgesic prescribing guidance is needed for older adults with dementia.

title: Implementation of Programmatic Mailed Fecal Immunochemical Testing for Colorectal Cancer Screening in the Veterans Health Administration.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted the Veterans Health Administration (VA) to implement programmatic mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) screening for colorectal cancer. This paper describes VA's programmatic mailed FIT development, implementation and initial outcomes.
METHODS: VA adapted mailed FIT processes from a Centers for Disease Control and Prevention-sponsored Mailed FIT Implementation Guide, performed regional pilots, created a national Mailed FIT Implementation Team (MFIT), and issued formal policy. The MFIT then provided training and disseminated tools to support VA mailed FIT programs.
RESULTS: Programmatic mailed FIT has been implemented in 89.5% of eligible facilities. Between December 1, 2022 and September 30, 2025, 643,933 FIT were ordered and 40.2% were returned. Of those, 89.1% were testable and 10.9% were cancelled, primarily due to missing sample collection date (63.2%) or receipt >15 days after collection (31.5%). Of the 230,427 FIT results, 7.4% were abnormal and colonoscopy was completed in 54.4%. Among 5846 VA colonoscopies, adenomas were detected in 68.0%, and adenocarcinoma was found in 2.3%. Linear regression analysis demonstrated a direct correlation between increasing mailed FIT adoption and the proportion of Veterans who are up to date with screening (r=0.65, p=0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: VA has successfully developed and disseminated strong practices for population-level CRC screening outreach with programmatic mailed FIT. This practice is associated with moderate levels of adherence and significant improvements in the overall proportion of Veterans who are up to date with screening. Further dissemination of mailed FIT programs, process improvement, and sharing of best practices is ongoing.

title: Emergence and dissemination of an IncC plasmid co-harbouring bla KPC-2, bla NDM-1 and bla VIM-24 carbapenemase genes across multiple Gram-negative species in Colombia.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CRGNB) pose a public health threat, increasingly driven by plasmid-mediated dissemination of carbapenemase genes. As part of a Colombian genomic monitoring programme, we aimed to characterize CRGNB co-harbouring multiple carbapenemase genes and determine their genetic context.
METHODS: We screened 832 carbapenem-resistant isolates collected during 2011-2023 using carbapenemase-targeted qPCR. Ten isolates co-harbouring bla KPC, bla NDM and bla VIM underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing, long-read whole-genome sequencing, comparative genomics and conjugation assays.
RESULTS: Nine Enterobacterales isolates and one Aeromonas caviae isolate from unrelated patients in geographically distant Colombian hospitals carried closely related IncC plasmids ranging from 160 to 317 kb. These plasmids co-harboured bla KPC-2, bla NDM-1 and bla VIM-24 within three conserved multidrug resistance regions, including a Tn21-associated region carrying bla NDM-1 and bla VIM-24 and a Tn6454-associated bla KPC-2 platform, alongside class 1 integrons, insertion sequences and multiple additional antimicrobial resistance determinants. The ten isolates were resistant to multiple β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations, and five were cefiderocol resistant. Aztreonam/avibactam remained active against all isolates; colistin resistance was confined to intrinsically resistant Providencia rettgeri and Serratia sarumanii. Conjugation assays demonstrated plasmid transfer to Escherichia coli J53, and sequencing confirmed transfer of a 179 kb IncC plasmid with functional conjugation machinery. Comparative genomic analysis showed a highly conserved IncC plasmid backbone across multiple species, supporting broad dissemination of this resistance platform.
CONCLUSIONS: This first report of a single plasmid co-harbouring three carbapenemase genes. This finding highlights a concerning mechanism for interspecies dissemination of MDR Gram-negative pathogens and underscores the importance of long-read genomic surveillance focused on high-risk plasmids.

title: Comparison of an Artificial Intelligence Nutrition Platform With Dietitians in Providing Nutrition Support to Patients With Cancer.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with cancer experience nutrition challenges, but access to registered dietitians (RDs) is limited. The purpose of this study was to determine whether a specialized Artificial Intelligence (AI) Nutrition Platform trained on curated high-quality evidence is equivalent in providing nutrition information to patients with cancer compared with oncology-credentialed RDs.
METHODS: Twenty nutrition queries were developed by an expert panel, encompassing common cancer types, symptoms, and food allergies/preferences. These queries were administered to the AI Platform and to four nationally recruited human dietitians. Three expert reviewers with >10 years of cancer-specific nutrition experience blindly reviewed all query responses using a modified version of the Quality Assessment of Medical AI (mQAMAI) instrument, which assigns a score between 1 and 5 for accuracy, clarity, relevance, completeness, and usefulness (total quality score between 5 and 25). The primary outcome was mQAMAI total score. Equivalence was evaluated a priori using two one-sided tests (TOST). Secondary outcomes included readability and response time.
RESULTS: The AI Nutrition Platform met equivalence criteria with human dietitians at ±3 to ±5 points (mean difference: 0.9 points; 90% CI, -0.27 to 2.15; TOST P < .05), while scoring higher on individual components: clarity (4.2 v 3.9; P = .001), relevance (4.1 v 3.9; P = .04), and usefulness (3.8 v 3.5; P = .02). AI responses were easier to read (Flesch-Kincaid grade level 7.2 v 9.8; P < .001) with faster response time (8.5 v 18.5 minutes per two queries; P < .001).
CONCLUSION: The AI Platform was equivalent to human dietitians for cancer nutrition information, delivering responses with greater clarity, relevance, usefulness, and readability in less time. This tool could broaden access to nutrition support for patients in settings where access to dietitians is limited.

title: Accelerated brain aging with functional and cognitive decline after traumatic brain injury
abstract: Introduction Individuals with a history of traumatic brain injury (TBI) have been shown to have greater brain age compared to their chronological age. However, the trajectory of post-TBI brain aging and its association with long-term functional and cognitive outcomes remain unclear. This report aims to characterize the influence of brain aging on functional outcomes post-TBI. Methods Data were drawn from 157 individuals enrolled in the Magnetic Resonance Imaging of NeuroTrauma Study cohort. Participants completed self-report assessments and underwent structural neuroimaging (T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging at baseline and at 1-, 6-, and 18- months). Brain age was estimated using a neural network trained on T1 scans, and the predicted age difference (PAD) was calculated. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE) and the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Logistic mixed-effects models examined associations between PAD and outcomes. Results The predicted brain age estimates derived from the T1 scans were higher than the post-TBI participants’ chronological ages. Logistic mixed-effects models showed a 16% increase in the odds of unfavorable functional recovery (GOSE ≤ 4) and a 6% increase in the odds of cognitive impairment (MMSE ≤ 28) per unit increase in PAD. Conclusion Individuals with TBI exhibit functional and cognitive declines that correlate with increased brain age. An elevated PAD is associated with poorer outcomes and may serve as a clinically useful biomarker. Incorporating brain age metrics into care may support early detection, guide personalized interventions, and improve outcomes. Future research should explore how brain age interacts with other risk factors to better understand post-TBI decline.

title: Longitudinal associations among eating disorder and posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms in veteran men and women: A latent difference score modeling approach.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cross-sectional studies have established associations between eating disorders (EDs) and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) among both women and men. Although there is evidence that trauma exposure may contribute to the onset of EDs, few longitudinal studies have examined whether there is a reciprocal relationship between ED symptoms and PTSD symptoms resulting from trauma exposure. This issue is particularly relevant for military veterans, who have high rates of PTSD and EDs.
METHOD: We investigated bidirectional associations among PTSD and ED symptoms in a sample of U.S. veteran men and women. Participants were randomly selected from the national population of veterans and invited to complete the time 1 (T1) survey; respondents were invited to complete the time 2 (T2) survey approximately 12 months later. We estimated latent difference score (LDS) models to determine whether T1 PTSD symptoms were associated with T2 ED symptoms and vice versa.
RESULTS: Bivariate LDS model results indicated that only among the female subsample, T1 PTSD symptoms, particularly negative affect and externalizing behaviors, were positively associated with change in ED symptoms from T1 to T2. T1 ED symptoms were not associated with the PTSD LDS.
DISCUSSION: Among veteran women only, negative affect and externalizing behaviors were associated with later ED symptoms, consistent with the theory that ED symptoms may be used to cope with trauma-related symptoms. Further research is needed to investigate longitudinal associations between PTSD and ED symptoms that may be more relevant to veteran men. Findings have the potential to positively impact future treatment efforts.

title: Global Underutilization of Antiviral Therapy and Survival Outcomes in Hepatitis B Virus-Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 78 Studies and 68,243 Patients.
abstract: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is recommended for patients with viremic hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis regardless of levels of viremia or liver enzymes. However, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an antiviral treatment criterion in the U.S. HBV treatment guidelines, though prior studies have reported improved survival with antiviral treatment in HBV-related HCC. To inform guidelines, we estimated antiviral treatment rates and their association with survival and HCC recurrence rates in HBV-related HCC. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects models pooled study estimates. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. The pooled antiviral treatment rate (52 studies, 41,345 patients) was 53.1%. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis. Treated (vs untreated) patients had higher 3- and 5-year OS (80.4% vs. 59.2% and 72.1% vs. 46.8%, both p < 0.01). Five-year OS was 78.0% vs. 56.4% in inactive HCC (p < 0.01) and 48.2% vs. 22.6% in active HCC (p = 0.14). Antiviral therapy remained independently associated with improved 5-year OS in multivariable meta-regression. There was no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.

title: Depression and loneliness differentially predict visual hallucinations in veterans with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Loneliness, social isolation, and depression are risk factors for hallucinations in patients with dementia. However, it is unclear whether relationships between these socioemotional factors and hallucinations differ in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) or Lewy body dementia (LBD) compared to those with neither diagnosis.
METHODS: We used logistic regression models on a large sample of veterans from a memory disorders clinic with varied diagnoses to test whether loneliness, social isolation, and/or depression predicted visual hallucinations (VHs) and interacted with neurocognitive diagnosis.
RESULTS: Depression and loneliness were associated with VHs among patients with diagnoses of AD and/or Lewy body dementia, but not in those with neither diagnosis. Social isolation did not predict hallucinations in any diagnostic group.
DISCUSSION: Depression and loneliness can predict the presence of VHs, depending on the patient's underlying diagnosis. Future studies are needed to tease out causal relationships.

title: Use of nasal epithelium as a minimally invasive surrogate for testing acid sphingomyelinase activity through thermal burn injury-induced microvesicle particle release.
abstract: Skin keratinocyte acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) is critical in the generation of subcellular microvesicle particles (MVP) implicated in skin responses to multiple environmental stressors including ultraviolet B radiation and thermal burn injury (TBI). Additionally, ASM is a pharmacologic target to potentially treat many systemic conditions from metabolic disorders to viral infections. Yet, the ability to confirm ASM inhibition is a therapeutic gap. The current studies sought to test if nasal epithelium could serve as a minimally invasive test for ASM activity by using MVP release. For these studies we obtained nasal epithelial washes from human volunteers and treated them ex vivo with an experimental TBI with MVP quantified to asses ASM activity. Epithelial cells were obtained from 20 healthy adult volunteers using a nasal brush. Histologic characterization and pan-cytokeratin staining revealed approximately equal numbers of epithelial and goblet cells. Treatment of the fresh epithelial cells with an experimental TBI resulted in fairly reproducible increased numbers of MVP blocked by ASM inhibitors imipramine and amitriptyline. These studies provide a simple methodology that could be used to assess ASM inhibitory effects of systemic agents that may possibly be employed to treat ASM-associated pathologic conditions including photosensitivity, acute TBI and viral infections including COVID. Oral treatment with acid sphingomyelinase inhibitors is a potential therapeutic avenue for skin disorders. The ability to directly assess the level of acid sphingomyelinase inhibition is a methodologic gap. The current studies suggest harvesting nasal epithelium to measure microvesicle particle release could provide a needed methodology to address this concern.

title: Wearable sensors and VOC monitoring: data fusion and machine learning for non-invasive disease detection.
abstract: Emerging technologies that detect volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emanating from the body enable rapid and non-invasive detection of diseases. Respiratory illnesses, in particular, can be identified through measurement of VOCs in exhaled breath. However, the low specificity of some methods leaves room for improvement. By combining information from multiple data streams, we can potentially improve on the results obtained from using each data stream individually. Here we evaluate a novel data fusion approach combining a wearable vitals monitor and exhaled breath VOCs for the classification of asthma patients. The wearable vitals monitor or 'e-glove' measures key information such as skin temperature, trans-epidermal water loss, heart rate, and galvanic skin response, while the breath VOC data (measured by gold standard gas chromatography-mass spectrometry) provide insight into the biochemical and metabolic state of the body. Data fusion is a process used in many applications for combining information from disparate sources. We leverage data fusion in this case to achieve superior classification accuracy using the integrated data streams. The low-level data fusion achieved a higher ROC AUC score (0.88) in asthma classification than the breath VOC-only approach (0.72,p< 0.001). These results are promising for future data analysis workflows for non-invasive diagnostic and health monitoring.

title: Investigating AI’s potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
abstract: Abstract Objective We aimed to 1) evaluate whether AI algorithms could identify a very low-risk sub-population Lung-RADS 1/2 cases suitable for a safe switch to biennial screening, and 2) externally validate Sybil, an imaging-based deep learning lung cancer risk prediction tool. Materials and methods We gathered all lung cancer screenings (LCSs) from a tertiary safety-net hospital (n=3120, up to September 2024), manually extracted relevant clinical data, and analyzed Sybil’s performance across various subgroups, with a specific focus on Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases. We simulated LCS interval extension using Sybil and the Brock model risk scores calibrated on a subset of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). Confidence intervals were obtained through bootstrapping. Results The median follow-up was 2.3 years (interquartile range 1.5–3.1), with a total 6-year cancer incidence rate of 2.3% (72/3120). Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases comprised 90.5% of our scans. Sybil’s overall area under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.819 to 0.912; while its 2-year AUC for Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases was 0.746. In the screening interval extension simulation, calibrating for a 30% shift to biennial screening translated into 33.8% of negative screens in our data being safely extended using Sybil, with no delayed cancers. The Brock model demonstrated an AUC of 0.513 on our data, with a sensitivity of 18.2% using the 1.5% threshold. Conclusion Sybil has the potential to safely extend LCS intervals for low-risk individuals, reducing radiology workload and opening spots for life-saving new screenings. Key points We investigated whether AI risk stratification tools could identify the lowest-risk individuals undergoing lung cancer screening suitable for switching to a biennial screening schedule. In our simulations, Sybil reduced follow-up screening load by at least 30% through switching the lowest-risk Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases to biennial screening without delayed cancer diagnoses. Very low-risk individuals, as predicted by AI algorithms, could potentially be placed on biennial screening schedules, reducing radiology department workload and freeing time for new patients.

title: Clinical Outcomes after Deprescribing Thyroid Hormone Therapy: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Background: Levothyroxine (LT4) is widely prescribed, often for subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH), despite limited evidence of clinical benefit in patients without overt hypothyroidism. This updated systematic review synthesizes current evidence on biochemical, symptom, and safety outcomes following thyroid hormone (TH) discontinuation. Methods: In this systematic review, electronic databases were searched from inception to September 25, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating supervised TH discontinuation. Primary outcomes included postdiscontinuation thyroid function, symptom changes, adverse events, and need for therapy reinitiation. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled proportions and mean differences. Results: Twenty-three studies met inclusion criteria (22 observational studies, 1 RCT), most evaluating LT4 monotherapy discontinuation ( n = 20). Twenty-one studies including 2020 participants reported categorical TH status outcomes; 37% of participants (CI, 26%–48%; I 2 = 94.5%) remained euthyroid after discontinuation. Euthyroidism was less frequent among patients with initial overt hypothyroidism (11%, CI, 2%–38%) than among those with SCH (41%, CI, 21%–65%). Eleven studies (1104 participants) reported TH reinitiation, with 60% of patients restarting therapy (CI, 39%–78%; I 2 = 97.1%) in the overall population, increasing to 87% (CI, 66%–96%) among those with overt hypothyroidism. Thyroid autoantibody positivity, heterogeneous thyroid ultrasound findings, and higher baseline TSH levels were associated with therapy reinitiation. Thyroid-related symptoms after discontinuation were generally unchanged, and adverse events were uncommon. Conclusions: Approximately 37% of patients remained euthyroid after TH discontinuation, with higher success rates among those initially treated for SCH. These findings support consideration of deprescribing in selected patients, particularly those without clear indications for treatment initiation, using a structured approach with close biochemical monitoring and predefined criteria for therapy reinitiation.

title: Abstract 7400: Mobility-Informed Environmental Exposures and Cardiovascular Outcomes Across the Life Course
abstract: Background: Environmental exposures such as green spaces are increasingly recognized as determinants of cardiovascular health, yet most studies rely on static, residence-based proxies that fail to capture how people move through and interact with their environment. Cell-phone mobility data offer an opportunity to quantify dynamic, behaviorally grounded exposures at scale, but their relationship to cardiovascular outcomes remains poorly characterized. Research Question: Do dynamic, mobility-based frameworks for assessing environmental cardiovascular exposures better reflect cardiovascular outcomes than static residence-based measures? To evaluate area-level mobility-informed interactions with green space, recreational areas, and movement patterns related to cardiovascular risk, mortality patterns, and geographic clustering of cardiovascular outcomes. Methods: We integrated large-scale anonymized mobility data with mortality data and longitudinal outcomes in nearly 3 million individuals from a regional Ohio cohort, University Hospitals (UH, n =498,759), and a national Veterans Affairs (VA, n =2,534,577) health system cohort (median follow-up: 7.8 and 8.8 years, respectively). Mobility-derived exposures included time spent in green spaces, recreational spaces, and a Community Movement Index (CMI) capturing mobility intensity and diversity. Associations with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality were assessed using survival models with age interactions. Findings were independently validated in meta-analyses and further evaluated in geospatial analyses of cardiovascular and mortality rates at regional and national scales. Results: Among participants in the younger UH cohort (median age 50.8 years), 11.0% experienced MACE and 9.7% died during follow-up. In contrast, the older VA cohort (median age 63.0) exhibited higher event rates, with 15.2% sustaining MACE and 12.8% experiencing death. Across both cohorts, greater engagement with green and recreational environments and higher mobility diversity were consistently associated with lower MACE risk, with age-attenuated benefits (HR=0.289-0.762, p<0.0001). Meta-analysis confirmed robust protective associations for green time and recreation time (HR=0.630-0.816, p<0.001). Ecological analyses further demonstrated inverse spatial correlations between beneficial mobility exposures and MACE rates across Ohio, as well as all-cause mortality rates across the United States. Conclusions: Dynamic population mobility patterns are robustly associated with cardiovascular risk across diverse populations and geographic scales. By moving beyond static residential proxies, mobility-informed exposure metrics provide a scalable, behaviorally grounded framework for linking lived environmental experience to cardiovascular health across the life course.

title: Human Pegivirus Type 1 Coinfections: Epidemiology, Heterogeneity and Clinical Implications.
abstract: This narrative review explores the complex landscape of coinfections involving Human Pegivirus Type 1 (HPgV), a member of the Hepaciviridae family previously known as GB virus type C or hepatitis G virus. Structurally similar to hepatitis C virus (HCV), HPgV is lymphotropic and while viraemia in healthy donors is asymptomatic, it has been associated with the onset of several non-Hodgkin lymphoma subtypes. We begin with an overview of HPgV's genomic features, classification, transmission routes and natural history, including spontaneous clearance and post-infection anti-E2 antibody development. As of 03 February 2026, a PubMed search yielded 346 relevant studies from which data were synthesized, reporting HPgV coinfection across human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), HCV, hepatitis B virus and other viral diseases - highlighting genotype distributions, geographic variability and population-specific patterns. In summary, HPgV shows a reproducible signal in HIV coinfections, suggesting potential therapeutic benefits, while its impact on chronic hepatitis, acute infections and lymphoma risk remains preliminary and requires further investigation. This review highlights the need for rigorous prospective studies with standardized protocols to clarify HPgV's true impact on human health and its potential for therapeutic application.

title: Computational image features of immune architecture reveal molecular patterns associated with outcome and risk of recurrence in microsatellite-stable or MSI-low colon cancers.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) density provides prognostic information in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD), but the additional value of TIL spatial organization remains unclear.
METHODS: We developed CoATIL, a computational pathology framework quantifying TIL spatial architecture from routine H&E-stained whole-slide images. The study included 461 patients with microsatellite-stable or MSI-low COAD. The model was trained using 140 patients from University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, validated internally in 52 patients, and externally in The Cancer Genome Atlas (n = 130), and Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital (n = 139). Prognostic performance was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. CoATIL was compared with a clinical model and eight foundation-model-based multiple-instance learning approaches.
RESULTS: CoATIL was associated with progression-free survival (HR per standard-deviation increase, 1.32; 95% CI 1.13-1.55; p < 0.001; C-index=0.66) and remained prognostic after adjustment for clinicopathologic factors in each validation cohort (adjusted HRs, 2.00-4.40; all p < 0.05). High-versus-low-risk stratification was retained within stage II (HR 3.07; 95% CI 1.83-5.15; p < 0.001) and stage III disease (HR 3.24; 95% CI 1.28-8.19; p = 0.013). The combined clinical-CoATIL model achieved a higher C-index than the clinical model alone (0.69 versus 0.61; paired bootstrap difference, 0.08; 95% CI 0.03-0.14). Exploratory genomic analyses associated AMER1 and FBXW7 mutations with lower and higher CoATIL risk scores, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Spatial immune architecture extracted from routine histology provides complementary prognostic information in COAD. Prospective validation is warranted.

title: GLP-1RA Discontinuation Among Veterans With Type 2 Diabetes and Irritable Bowel Syndrome
abstract: OBJECTIVE To examine whether coexisting irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is associated with an increased risk of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) discontinuation among veterans with type 2 diabetes. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS Using national Veterans Health Administration administrative data (2018–2023), we identified 245,084 veterans with type 2 diabetes initiating a GLP-1RA. Two cohorts were defined: type 2 diabetes only and coexisting type 2 diabetes and IBS. The primary outcome was GLP-1RA discontinuation within 1 year of initiation. Discontinuation risk was compared using χ2 tests and Cox proportional hazards (CPH) regression, adjusting for demographics and clinical variables. RESULTS Among GLP-1RA initiators, 2,178 (0.9%) had coexisting IBS. Overall, 63,335 (24.8%) discontinued GLP-1RA therapy within 1 year. Rates of discontinuation were lower among veterans with IBS (491 of 2,178 [22.5%]) compared with those without IBS (62,844 of 242,906 [25.9%]) (P < 0.001). In an unadjusted CPH model, IBS was associated with a lower risk of discontinuation (hazard ratio [HR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.80–0.96), but the association was not statistically significant after adjustment (adjusted HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.85–1.01). Several covariates, including BMI, concurrent glucose-lowering therapy, depressive disorders, GLP-1RA type, and initiation year, were independently associated with discontinuation. CONCLUSIONS In a large national cohort of veterans with type 2 diabetes, IBS was not associated with higher GLP-1RA discontinuation risk after adjustment for demographic and clinical characteristics. These findings challenge assumptions that gastrointestinal comorbidities universally heighten GLP-1RA intolerance and suggest that IBS symptom experience or self-management may support persistence. Clinical decisions should consider patient comorbidity profiles, treatment burden, and symptom management experiences to optimize GLP-1RA continuation.

title: DUF6383-domain containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.

title: Characterization of sex-dependent skeletal muscle alterations in the 3xTg Alzheimer's disease mouse model.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic condition with effects beyond the central nervous system. Skeletal muscle dysfunction, including sarcopenia and reduced physical performance, is prevalent in AD patients, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized skeletal muscle alterations in male and female 3xTg-AD mice at 3, 6, and 12 months of age and compared them to age- and sex-matched B6129 controls. We measured body composition, muscle function, and skeletal muscle parameters including fiber type distribution, cross-sectional area (CSA), and neural cell adhesion molecule (NCAM) expression. Our findings revealed early-onset and progressive impairments of skeletal muscle mass, morphology, and function in 3xTg-AD mice, with sex-specific differences. Male mice exhibited reduced lean mass, muscle weight, and torque generation as early as 3 months and decreased CSA of type IIB and IIX fibers and increased NCAM expression by 12 months, indicating a potential neuromuscular junction deficiency. Female mice in this study generally exhibited a milder phenotype. Together, these results identify skeletal muscle dysfunction as an early and sex-dependent feature of AD pathology in 3xTg-AD mice. Our study underscores the importance of considering systemic effects in AD and highlights skeletal muscle as a potential target for therapeutic intervention aimed at preserving mobility and quality of life in affected individuals.

title: The Portland SEEQ: A Harmonizable Questionnaire for Environmental Exposome Profiling in Prodromal Synucleinopathy
abstract: Abstract Objective To describe development of the Portland Suspected Environmental Exposures Questionnaire (SEEQ) and its initial application for environmental exposome profiling in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD). Background Environmental exposures may contribute to Parkinson disease and related synucleinopathies, yet existing instruments variably capture specific agents, co-exposures, exposure uncertainty, timing, and mitigating factors. Methods SEEQ was iteratively developed to assess pesticides, solvents/industrial chemicals, welding fumes, heavy metals, residential and occupational exposures, and relevant lifestyle factors. Direct exposures were classified as definite, probable, possible, or uncertain/unlikely, with additional assessment of frequency/duration, life stage, and protective-equipment use. SEEQ was administered to participants with polysomnography-confirmed iRBD. Exposure prevalence, co-exposure patterns, and exploratory associations with clinical phenotypes and longitudinal progression were examined. Results Eighty-three participants completed SEEQ; 81 (97.6%) completed all four direct exposure domains. Definite/probable exposure was reported for pesticides in 38.6%, solvents/industrial chemicals in 43.4%, welding fumes in 21.0%, and heavy metals in 34.1%. Among complete responders, 60.5% reported ≥1 and 42.0% ≥2 direct exposure domains. Forty-five participants identified ≥1 named agent or mixture. Greater exposure burden was cross-sectionally associated most consistently with greater autonomic symptom burden, but was not associated with longitudinal clinical worsening. Conclusion SEEQ provides a practical, multidomain framework for structured environmental exposome profiling in prodromal synucleinopathy. Larger studies with external exposure validation and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

title: Parkinson’s disease genetic risk converges on Lewy body pathology-associated microglial states
abstract: Abstract Parkinson’s disease (PD) and related α-synucleinopathies are defined by the spread of Lewy body (LB) pathology across vulnerable brain regions, yet how substantia nigra (SN) myeloid cells respond remains unresolved. Using SOX10-based oligodendrocyte depletion and CD11b-based myeloid enrichment, we profiled 169,799 brain myeloid cells and nuclei from 96 donors spanning the LB continuum, including 86,427 from the SN, and integrated them with AMP PD for a total of 298,592 profiles. Across eight conserved states, α-synucleinopathy is associated with a bidirectional signature: upregulated glycolytic and proteostatic-stress programs alongside downregulated lysosomal and mitochondrial pathways. Microglia shift from P2RY12-high sensome cells toward an HSP90AA1-high proteostatic stress state, a transition that intensifies at late Braak LB stages. Immunohistochemistry confirmed that HSP60 + proteostatic microglia state proportions increase with SN neuron loss. A rare NUCKS1-high state (∼1% of myeloid cells), more abundant in late-stage disease, carried the strongest PD polygenic-risk loading. The PD-protective rs3732765-A allele, a microglial cis-eQTL that lowers P2RY12 expression, was nominally associated with a higher proportion of P2RY12-high microglia and higher lysosomal program activity. These findings frame microglial involvement as structured and genetically tractable, nominating the P2RY12 genetic axis and NUCKS1-high microglia for mechanistic studies.

title: The Interaction between Race, Ethnicity, Gender, Sexual Orientation, and Age on Internalized HIV-related Stigma in the DC Cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Internalized HIV-related stigma can have a negative impact on health outcomes among people with HIV (PWH). A multilevel model, informed by an intersectional framework, is needed to evaluate the interactions between various aspects of one's identity and their impact on internalized HIV-related stigma. Therefore, we used a Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA) to evaluate internalized stigma among PWH. METHODS: We evaluated a subset of participants in the DC Cohort longitudinal study on PWH who completed a patient reported outcomes (PROs) survey. Participants were sorted into 24 strata of race/ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and age. Stigma was evaluated using a self-reported 4-item instrument. We evaluated the individual and strata level impacts of these variables on internalized stigma using MAIHDA. RESULTS: We evaluated 1,540 DC Cohort participants with complete strata information, most of which were non-Hispanic Black (80.3%), male (73.1%), gay/lesbian/bisexual (52.1%), and had a mean age of 52.3 years old. Based on the null model, the strata explain 6.96% of the total variance in stigma. This variance was reduced to 1.67% after adjusting for the individual effects of race/ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and age. This shows that the main effects of these covariates jointly account for 77.27% of the between-strata stigma variance, while the remaining 22.73% of the between-strata variance is potentially due to the intersectional effects between the covariates. CONCLUSION: Although the individual effects of race/ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and age did not explain a large portion of the variance in stigma, nearly a quarter of the between-strata variance in stigma is potentially attributable to the interaction between these covariates.

title: Validation of research site mentorship as an approach for increasing study site performance (enrollment).
abstract: The identification of strategies that improve participant enrollment in clinical trials remains a key focus of stakeholders in this field, due to its role as a leading indicator of timely trial completion and its contributions to the validity and generalizability of clinical trial results. The VA Cooperative Studies Program (CSP) Network of Dedicated Enrollment Sites (NODES) replicated a previously piloted research site mentorship model in two actively enrolling CSP-funded clinical trials to validate its impact on study participant enrollment (CSP #2005: VA Lung Cancer Surgery vs. Stereotactic Radiotherapy trial (VALOR) and CSP #2008: Pentoxifylline in Diabetic Kidney Disease (VA PTXRx)). The "Total Randomized Participants (#) by Mentee Site" and the "Percentage of Randomized Participants (Actual/Expected) Monthly Average By Site (%)" were evaluated across participating mentee study sites over three time periods: 1) 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP), 2) 5-month intervention period (IP), and 3) 3-month follow-up period (FUP). These data were averaged across months during the respective time periods (PIP, IP, FUP). Our findings demonstrate an association between the NODES site mentorship model and improvements in most mentee sites' "Total Randomized Participants (#)" (4/7; 57%) at the end of the 5-month intervention period (IP), as compared to the 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP) (Table B). Increases in most sites' (5/7; 71%) "Percentage of Randomized Participants (Actual/Expected) Monthly (Average) By Site (%)" at the end of the 5-month intervention period (IP), as compared to the 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP) was also observed (Table C).

title: Simpson’s Paradox, Amyloid Paradox, and Racial Differences
abstract: Importance: The underlying mechanisms for the paradox of higher prevalence of dementia but lower prevalence of amyloid positivity in self-identified Black US residents than White US residents remain unknown and are important for designing and analyzing prevention and treatment trials of Alzheimer disease. Objective: To assess whether the age of mean amyloid onset (AMAO) explains the paradox of the reported racial differences in dementia and amyloid positivity. Design, Setting, and Participants: This was a retrospective, multicenter, longitudinal cohort study with harmonized amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) and clinical data from self-identified Black and White individuals who were middle-aged or older across 5 academic institutes in the US conducting studies of memory and aging. The study was conducted from June 2020 to March 2026. Exposures: Self-identified race, vascular comorbidities, sex, age, educational attainment, and apolipoprotein E ε4 carrier status. Main Outcomes and Measures: Amyloid PET centiloid and cognition measured as a global cognitive composite constructed by averaging z scores across at least 6 cognitive tests in self-identified Black and White participants. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses were conducted to compare racial groups in amyloid burden and cognition. Data were also analyzed using propensity score-matching of 2:1 (White:Black) by main covariates. Results: Of 2653 participants (mean [SD] age, 69.0 [8.8] years; 1574 [59.3%] female), 406 (15.3%) were Black and 2247 (84.7%) were White. Black participants had a delayed AMAO compared with White participants in the unmatched (83.86 [95% CI, 76.55-91.35] years vs 71.38 [95% CI, 67.74-73.17] years; difference, 12.48 [95% CI, 5.03-22.28 years) and covariate-matched (85.17 [95% CI, 80.16-91.38] years vs 72.61 [95% CI, 70.79-74.55] years; difference, 12.57 [95% CI, 7.25-19.54] years) analyses. Although Black participants had a lower overall prevalence of amyloid positivity than White participants (24.1% vs 31.7%, P = .002), they had a higher prevalence of amyloid positivity than White participants in almost every interval of expected years to amyloid onset (EYAO, defined as participants' simple chronological age minus the group-specific AMAO), hence Simpson's paradox, (eg, -15 to -10 years for Black minus White prevalence in the unmatched cohort, 15.30 percentage points [95% Wilson CI, 0.06-0.26]). No significant racial differences were found in the longitudinal rate of amyloid accumulation after adjusting for the covariates either before the AMAO (eg, unmatched cohort Black minus White difference in slope per year, -0.28 [95% CI, -0.64 to 0.08]; P = .13) or after the AMAO (eg, unmatched cohort Black minus White difference in slope, -1.23 [95% CI, -3.05 to 0.60]; P = .17). Black participants had a higher prevalence of vascular comorbidities than White participants (56.9% vs 39.3%; P < .001), and Black but not White participants showed significant cognitive decline before the AMAO (Black minus White difference in slope per year, -0.016 (95% CI, -0.028 to -0.004)]; P = .009). Conclusions and Relevance: This cohort study found that Black participants had delayed AMAO compared with White participants, partially explaining the paradox of the reported racial differences in prevalence of amyloid positivity and dementia. This finding suggests that EYAO may be an important confounder to analyze racial differences and may serve as a better (than age) inclusion or exclusion criterion to improve the representation of Black US residents in clinical trials of Alzheimer disease.

title: Menopausal status, hormonal therapy, and elevated lipoprotein(a): Implications for prevalent coronary artery disease in U.S. Women Veterans
abstract: Aims: To determine whether menopausal status, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), or oral contraceptive (OCP) use modifies the association between elevated Lp(a) and prevalent coronary artery disease (CAD). Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 6,314 U.S. Women Veterans with Lp(a) testing from 1999-2025 to evaluate whether menopausal status, MHT use, or OCP use modify the association between elevated Lp(a) (≥ 125 nmol/L) and prevalent CAD. Logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aOR), with interaction terms evaluated by likelihood ratio tests. Restricted cubic splines were used to model the continuous association between Lp(a) and prevalent CAD. Results: Elevated Lp(a) was present in 31.6% of Women Veterans and was independently associated with increased odds of prevalent CAD (aOR 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.06-1.44, p = 0.0079). We observed a continuous increase in prevalent CAD with rising Lp(a) levels (aOR 1.023 per 25 nmol/L increase, 95% confidence interval 1.010-1.040, p = 0.0033). No effect modification was detected for menopausal status (p-value for interaction = 1.0), MHT use in postmenopausal women (p-value for interaction = 0.20), or OCP use in premenopausal women (p-value for interaction = 0.32). Conclusion: Elevated Lp(a) is common and associated with prevalent CAD in Women Veterans. We did not detect modification of the association between elevated Lp(a) and prevalent CAD based on menopausal status or hormonal therapy. These findings support systematic Lp(a) screening across the full female reproductive spectrum.

title: Training-free generation of 4D CT and other rare acquisitions improves segmentation across modalities
abstract: Abstract Rationale Routine clinical imaging captures anatomy under a limited set of physiologic and acquisition conditions, leaving segmentation models with sparse examples of how lesions and surrounding tissues deform with compression, respiration, or vascular pulsation. Standard image augmentation expands training datasets but does not explicitly model the mechanics underlying these changes. Patient-specific biomechanical simulation offers an approach to generate anatomically consistent images and corresponding segmentation masks under conditions absent from the original scan, without additional imaging or training a generative model. We hypothesized that incorporating this mechanistically grounded variability into training improves segmentation across imaging modalities. Methods We evaluate across three segmentation tasks: breast cancer on 3D digital breast tomosynthesis, lung tumors on chest CT, and carotid plaque on ultrasound. From each routine scan, patient-specific biomechanical models generate acquisitions absent from the original study—a range of breast compressions, the respiratory cycle, and arterial wall distension across the cardiac cycle. The resulting displacement fields deform both images and masks. Segmentation models were trained with and without the generated data across a range of standard image augmentation techniques, evaluated via cross-validation and held-out test sets. Realism was assessed through blinded reader studies, and generated respiratory motion was validated against real 4D CT. Results Training on the generated acquisitions improved segmentation across modalities, increasing Dice scores by 6.6% for breast (p<0.05), 10.1% for lung (p<0.05), and 4.5% for carotid plaque (p>0.05) relative to the routine scans alone. Generated respiratory motion closely matched real gated 4D CT, with Dice of 0.94 ± 0.02 for lung volume overlap. Blinded readers discriminated generated from real images at near chance (AUC: breast 0.61, lung 0.41, carotid 0.46). Conclusions Mechanistic simulation generates imaging acquisitions that clinical systems do not supply, without training data or additional scanning, and improves AI-based disease detection across modalities.

title: Trends and Facility-Level Variation in Minimally Invasive and Sphincter-Preserving Rectal Cancer Surgery in Veterans Health Administration: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: A comprehensive characterization of surgical trends, facility-level variation, and potential health equity gaps among patients undergoing rectal cancer surgery is lacking within Veterans Health Administration - the nation's largest integrated healthcare system serving a population underrepresented in other cancer registries. We characterized national temporal and facility-level trends in rectal cancer surgery and evaluated whether race and ethnicity independently predict treatment.
METHODS: This was a retrospective study of veterans who underwent oncologic resection for rectal cancer in Veterans Health Administration from 2014-2024. Receipt of minimally invasive and surgery sphincter-preserving surgery were measured.
RESULTS: We identified 2,758 veterans who underwent resection for rectal cancer across 91 facilities; the cohort was predominantly male (95.9%) with a mean age of 65.2 years and included 72.4% non-Hispanic White and 16.4% non-Hispanic Black veterans. Open surgery declined from 69.7% to 33.9%, driven by a five-fold increase in robotic-assisted procedures, which rose from 9.0% to 50.0% (p<0.001). Sphincter-preserving surgery rates remained stable, (73.3% to 72.0%, p<0.001). Facility-level heterogeneity was wide - median facility robotics utilization was 4.8% (range 0-67.1%) and sphincter-preserving surgery use was 75.0% (range 25.0%-100%). Veterans in the most deprived neighborhoods experienced reduced odds of minimally invasive surgery (odds ratio 0.60, 95% confidence interval 0.42-0.85). Race and ethnicity were not predictors of outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Robotic-assisted rectal cancer surgery increased five-fold within Veterans Health Administration, while sphincter-preserving surgery remained stable. Race and ethnicity did not independently predict receipt of either procedure. However, lower odds of minimally invasive surgery in deprived neighborhoods and facility-level heterogeneity suggest structural disparities.

title: Factors Associated With Clinical Trial Participation in Adult Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Recipients: A Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Only 3%-5% of patients with cancer nationwide enroll in clinical trials. Although participation among patients with solid tumors has been well studied, data in the hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) setting remain limited. We sought to (1) describe clinical trial participation rates by HSCT type; (2) examine associations between patient, disease, and transplant characteristics and trial participation; and (3) explore the association between trial participation and overall survival (OS).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study using Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) data from US adults aged 18-75 years who underwent autologous or allogeneic HSCT between 2013 and 2019 (N=84,151; autologous: n=51,133; allogeneic: n=33,018). Logistic regression models assessed predictors of participation, while Cox models evaluated associations with OS.
RESULTS: Trial participation was 2.0% among patients undergoing autologous HSCT and 11.1% among those undergoing allogeneic HSCT. Among autologous recipients, greater comorbidity burden was associated with lower odds of participation. Patients with multiple myeloma had higher odds than those with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (odds ratio [OR], 1.25; P=.01). Among allogeneic recipients, older adults had higher odds of participation (eg, OR, 2.19 for age ≥70 vs 18-19 years; P<.0001), as did non-Hispanic Black patients compared with non-Hispanic White patients (OR, 1.35; P=.0002). Participation was higher with cord blood grafts, mismatched unrelated donors, and certain diagnoses (eg, sickle cell disease). Lower participation was observed for severe aplastic anemia and haploidentical or peripheral blood grafts. Trial participation was not associated with OS in either group.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical trial participation remains low, particularly among autologous HSCT recipients, younger adults, and patients with specific diagnoses. Findings highlight the need to broaden trial eligibility, enhance outreach, and ensure equity in trial access to promote generalizable, patient-centered evidence in HSCT.

title: PFAS Exposure During Pregnancy Is Associated with Shorter Gestational Age at Birth and with Growth Trajectories During the First 2 Years of Life
abstract: Introduction: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) may influence birth outcomes and postnatal growth and adiposity, yet prospective evidence is limited. We evaluated sex-specific associations of first trimester maternal PFAS exposure with birth outcomes and children's growth and body composition through age two. Methods: Participants were enrolled in the Glowing prospective cohort study (2010-2014, NCT01131117 ). Levels of six PFAS (PFOS, PFOA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFNA, PFHxA) in maternal serum at 10-12 weeks' gestation were analyzed. Five participants were excluded due to unsuccessful PFAS characterization. We tested associations between PFAS exposure and gestational age, birth weight, birth length, and 11 repeated measures of weight, length, fat mass, and fat-free mass (FFM) during the first two years of life with linear regression, SuperImposition by Translation And Rotation growth curve size and intensity, and quantile g-computation. Results: Among 217 complete-case dyads, higher first trimester PFAS concentrations were associated with shorter gestation (PFOS and PFHxS; e.g., PFOS β = -0.198 weeks per doubling, 95% CI -0.368 to -0.028). PFHxS was associated with lower birth weight (β = -0.048 kg, 95% CI -0.093 to -0.002). Among males only, PFOS, PFHxS, PFOA, and PFNA were associated with shorter gestation and PFNA with shorter birth length. For postnatal growth, PFBS was associated with lower weight and fat-free mass growth intensity. PFHxS was associated with smaller length and fat-free mass among females. The joint six-PFAS mixture was not associated with any outcome. Associations were robust to adjustment for maternal albumin and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Conclusion: In a Central Arkansas birth cohort, first trimester maternal PFAS concentrations, particularly PFHxS, were individually associated with shorter gestation and reduced early growth and fat-free mass accrual, with more sex-specific male associations among birth outcomes and more female associations in longitudinal postnatal growth through age two.

title: Association of complete blood count derived indices of inflammation with psychiatric disorders and mortality.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Psychiatric disorders have been implicated in a bidirectional association with inflammation. Current methods of measuring inflammation in observational data are limited. Complete blood count (CBC)-derived indices of inflammation may address this limitation, though gaps in knowledge on their association with psychiatric disorders and mortality in the presence of these disorders remain. We sought to determine if six psychiatric diagnostic groups - substance, trauma, depressive, psychotic, personality, and bipolar - were associated with increased inflammatory indices, and if presence of these groups moderated the indices' effect on mortality.
METHODS: We identified annualized values of six CBC-derived indices of inflammation - systemic immune response index (SIRI), systemic immune inflammation index (SII), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), neutrophil-to- lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) - in a national cohort of Veterans Affairs healthcare users. To assess the effect of psychiatric disorders on indices, we fit linear mixed effects models on indices with the primary exposure being prior-year psychiatric diagnoses. To assess the effect of inflammatory indices on mortality, we fit Cox proportional hazards models on all-cause mortality and suicide with the primary exposure being a patients' initial inflammatory index.
RESULTS: All disorders, save trauma, were associated with higher index values, with the greatest effect being for substance disorders (SIRI: 20.71% [99.17% CI: 20.27, 21.15]). All six indices were associated with increased all-cause mortality and suicide. Only all-cause mortality was moderated by presence of psychiatric disorders.
CONCLUSION: In the context of limited generalizability, CBC-derived indices of inflammation serve as readily available measures of inflammation that are associated with psychiatric morbidity and mortality.
