title: Amputee motor control during loaded walking with stiffer and powered prostheses
abstract: Abstract Background Individuals with transtibial amputation often rely on prosthetic feet with fixed mechanical properties, which may limit distal limb neuromuscular strategies during demanding tasks such as load carriage. Although stiffer and powered prosthetic feet are purported to aid ambulation under load, their influence on motor control during loaded walking remains unclear. This study investigated whether changing prosthetic foot prescription alters muscle activation, and motor module composition and complexity during load carriage. Methods Twelve individuals with unilateral transtibial amputation walked at their preferred speed while carrying no load and a 13.6-kg (30-lb) load in multiple conditions (front, back, intact-side, and prosthetic-side). Subjects used a clinically prescribed prosthetic foot, the same foot but one category stiffer, and, in a subset ( n = 7), a powered ankle-foot prosthesis. Surface electromyography was collected from eight intact-limb muscles and five residual-limb muscles; module analysis primarily focused on the intact limb. Muscle activation and co-contraction were quantified, and a muscle motor module analysis using non-negative matrix factorization was performed to quantify motor control. Linear mixed-effects models tested differences between feet in muscle activation and module complexity, while module similarity and activation timing were evaluated using cosine similarity and one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping, respectively. Results Prosthetic foot types influenced activation of several intact-limb muscles across load conditions. Compared with the prescribed foot, the powered foot increased medial gastrocnemius activation by 26–29% during unloaded and intact-side load walking and rectus femoris activation by 46% during unloaded walking, while the stiffer foot increased vastus medialis activation by 37% during intact-side load walking. Despite these muscle-level changes, module complexity remained largely unchanged, with only limited task-specific differences. Three modules explained > 90% of electromyographic variance in most subjects, with only modest reductions in first-module variance (≈ 2–3%) for the powered foot during back and intact-side-load conditions. Module composition and activation timing were similar across feet. Exploratory analysis of the residual-limb muscles found no significant between-foot differences in module complexity within any load condition. Conclusions Although prosthetic feet with different mechanics alter specific muscle activation patterns during loaded walking, the underlying module composition and activation timing were largely unchanged, while module complexity showed small, task-specific changes that did not produce consistent changes in the number of modules required. These findings suggest that individuals with transtibial amputation accommodate changes in prosthetic foot mechanics and added load primarily through changes in muscle activation rather than reorganization of motor control strategies. title: Markers of Biological Aging and Survival in Recurrent and Metastatic Head and Neck Cancer Patients Receiving Immunotherapy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Immunotherapy has become a cornerstone in the treatment of recurrent and metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC), but reliable noninvasive biomarkers of prognosis remain limited. We investigated the associations between markers of biological aging and survival outcomes among patients with R/M HNSCC treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs).
METHODS: Peripheral blood samples collected prior to ICI initiation from 100 patients with R/M HNSCC underwent DNA methylation profiling using the Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC array. Four epigenetic age acceleration measures were estimated from DNA methylation levels and evaluated for associations with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).
RESULTS: Greater intrinsic and extrinsic epigenetic age acceleration were each associated with longer PFS (p = 0.025 and p = 0.048, respectively) and OS (p = 0.024 and p = 0.029, respectively). Significant interactions between GrimAge acceleration and chronological age were observed for both PFS (p = 0.010) and OS (p < 0.001). Greater GrimAge acceleration was associated with improved PFS among patients less than 65 years of age but shorter OS among patients 65 years of age or older.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, pretreatment epigenetic aging measures were associated with survival outcomes among patients with R/M HNSCC receiving ICIs. These findings suggest biological aging metrics may have clinical relevance and warrant further investigation as potential noninvasive prognostic biomarkers.

title: A Two-Stage Plasma Biomarker Algorithm Reduces Amyloid PET Use and the p-Tau217 Gray Zone.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Plasma p-Tau217 leaves 30%-50% of patients in an indeterminate "gray zone" often requiring Aβ-PET. We developed GRAD (Gatekeeper-Reflex for Alzheimer's Disease), a two-stage Aβ-positivity prediction model to improve classification while reserving Aβ-PET for residual uncertainty.
METHODS: GRAD was developed in 145 cognitively impaired ADNI participants and externally validated in 1644 cognitively unimpaired A4/LEARN participants. Stage 1 used p-Tau217 alone; probabilities between 0.25 and 0.75 were considered indeterminate. Stage 2 used L2-regularized logistic regression combining plasma-biomarkers, genetic and demographic features. Aβ-PET served as the reference standard (ADNI florbetapir SUVR > 1.11; A4 Centiloid ≥ 20).
RESULTS: Full model AUC was 0.915 (95% CI, 0.859-0.961) internally and 0.879 (95% CI, 0.861-0.895) externally. In the external gray zone (n = 630), Stage 2 improved discrimination over p-Tau217 alone (AUC 0.793 vs. 0.719; p < 0.001), increased correct classification without PET from 41.4% to 56.2%, and reduced PET referral from 35.9% to 24.3%. In the p-Tau181 subset (n = 256), Stage 2 outperformed p-Tau181 (AUC 0.799 vs. 0.597; p < 0.001). Overall, 89.0% of ADNI and 90.7% of A4/LEARN participants were classified without PET; modeled testing costs were 44%-52% lower than p-Tau217 screening with PET confirmation of the gray zone.
INTERPRETATION: Reflex multimarker testing improves indeterminate p-Tau217 classification while retaining Aβ-PET for residual uncertainty. GRAD may reduce PET use and testing costs in memory-clinic triage, prevention-trial enrichment, and disease-modifying therapy workup.

title: Electronic Dementia Assessment Score
abstract: INTRODUCTION: With population aging, ensuring that people living with dementia receive appropriate assessment and services is critical. The objective of this study was to determine whether electronic dementia assessment is associated with increased receipt of home-based and community-based services (HCBS) among Veterans with heart failure and newly diagnosed dementia. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of community-dwelling Veterans with heart failure who received an incident dementia diagnosis between 2010 and 2023. Electronic health record (EHR) data were used to identify completion of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments from 365 days before to 90 days after dementia diagnosis. The primary outcome was receipt of HCBS. Logistic regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and health care utilization. RESULTS: Among 46,157 Veterans with heart failure and incident dementia, 4% had documented cognitive, 82% psychiatric, and 41% functional assessments. Overall, 25% received HCBS. IPTW-adjusted odds of receiving HCBS significantly increased with electronic health record documentation of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments. CONCLUSIONS: Among Veterans with heart failure and newly diagnosed dementia, documentation of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments was associated with greater odds of receiving HCBS. Electronic dementia assessment may support system-level efforts to align dementia care with the goals of aging in place.

title: T cells in type 1 diabetes: mechanisms of β-cell autoimmunity, innate-adaptive immune crosstalk, and translational immunotherapy
abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease in which immune responses drive the destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells, ultimately resulting in lifelong insulin dependence. Although T cells are central mediators of β-cell autoimmunity, growing evidence shows that innate immune cells, including dendritic cells, macrophages, and natural killer (NK) cells, play essential roles in initiating, shaping, and sustaining pathogenic adaptive responses within the islet microenvironment. Both CD4 + helper and CD8 + cytotoxic T lymphocytes contribute to β-cell injury through the production of inflammatory cytokines, direct cytotoxicity, and disruption of self-tolerance. At the same time, regulatory T cells exhibit reduced numbers and/or impaired suppressive function, thereby further accelerating autoimmune progression. Recent advances in animal models, single-cell transcriptomics, spatial immune profiling, and T cell receptor sequencing have refined our understanding of autoreactive repertoires, antigen specificity, and bidirectional crosstalk between innate and adaptive immune compartments. At the translational level, immune signatures are emerging as tools for disease prediction and patient stratification, while therapeutic strategies ranging from anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies to tolerogenic vaccines and adoptive Treg therapies are moving from preclinical development into clinical evaluation. The clinical success of teplizumab as the first disease-modifying therapy for T1D reinforces the value of targeting immune pathways, but durable remission across diverse patient groups remains a major challenge. This review synthesizes recent advances in the immunobiology of T cells in T1D, emphasizing their functional interplay with innate immune cells, tracing the path from mechanistic discovery to clinical translation, and highlighting future directions for precision immunotherapy.

title: Consensus Statement on Traumatic Brain Injury in First Responders: The 1st International Conference on TBI in First Responders.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop the first interdisciplinary consensus recommendations for the recognition, diagnosis, and management of traumatic brain injury (TBI) in first responders (ie, law enforcement/corrections officers, firefighters, emergency medical services [EMS] personnel).
SETTING: The first International Conference on TBI in First Responders, held at The Ohio State University in March 2026.
PARTICIPANTS: An interdisciplinary author group of 52 clinicians, researchers, policy and organizational professionals, and first responders with lived or operational experience.
DESIGN: Six expert workgroups conducted a best-evidence synthesis of first responder-specific literature and relevant evidence from military personnel, athletes, and other populations. Preliminary recommendations were developed over 6 months and refined using a modified Delphi process with 2 rounds of anonymous voting via Microsoft Forms. Consensus was predefined as ≥80% agreement without reservations or with minor reservations.
MAIN MEASURES: Evidence quality and recommendation strength were graded using the Strength of Recommendation Taxonomy (SORT). The primary outcome was the percentage of agreement for each recommendation.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine preliminary statements were evaluated across 6 domains: injury risk, recognition, and reporting challenges; early assessment and diagnosis; return to duty; mental health; prevention; and workplace and policy context. In round 1, 27 of 29 statements reached consensus. After group discussion, review of anonymous comments, wording refinement, and consolidation of related statements, 28 final recommendations were evaluated in round 2; all reached consensus.
CONCLUSION: These recommendations provide the first interdisciplinary framework for TBI in first responders. They emphasize shared organizational responsibility, standardized terminology, nonpunitive reporting and referral pathways, clinician-guided care, occupation-specific RTD progression, mental health screening and treatment, exposure mitigation, and first responder-engaged research. Implementation of these recommendations may improve timely care, operational readiness, and the evidence base for first responders with TBI.

title: Optimal Incidence Threshold for Cost-Effective Hepatocellular Carcinoma Surveillance in Alcohol-Associated Cirrhosis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Current guidelines recommend routine hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance in patients with cirrhosis when annual HCC incidence exceeds 1 per 100 person-years, a threshold derived from older studies and not specific to alcohol-associated cirrhosis. However, contemporary data suggest that HCC incidence in this population is often below 1%, leaving the value of routine surveillance uncertain.
METHODS: We developed a Markov-based state-transition microsimulation model to simulate the natural history of HCC and subsequent treatment pathways in patients with alcohol-associated cirrhosis in the setting of the United States. The model compared biannual surveillance with ultrasound and alpha fetoprotein vs no surveillance separately for 2 distinct cohorts: patients who continued to actively consume alcohol and patients who had achieved sustained abstinence. Inputs included the natural history of alcohol-associated cirrhosis, HCC incidence, test performance, surveillance adherence, and contemporary treatment. Sensitivity analyses examined the robustness of model assumptions and findings.
RESULTS: Biannual surveillance becomes cost-effective when annual HCC incidence reached approximately 0.45 per 100 person-years using a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY). Among active drinkers, surveillance yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of $18,952 per QALY; among abstinent patients, the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $56,000 per QALY. Per 100,000 patients, routine surveillance generated an estimated 2083 additional life-years and 992 QALYs in active drinkers and 3357 life-years and 1700 QALYs in abstinent patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine biannual HCC surveillance with ultrasound and alpha fetoprotein is cost-effective for patients with alcohol-associated cirrhosis in the United States when HCC incidence exceeds 0.45 per 100 person-years, substantially below the historically cited 1 per 100 person-years threshold. Updating clinical guidelines to reflect these contemporary thresholds could improve early HCC detection in this high-risk population.

title: Functional prediction of immune checkpoint inhibitor response in renal cell carcinoma using a zebrafish patient-derived xenograft platform
abstract: To predict individual patient responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), we developed a biologic assay for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in which whole tumor cells (WTCs) isolated from patients are mixed ex vivo with nivolumab or control IgG and injected into zebrafish larvae (zPDX). ICI response is quantified as the percentage reduction in tumor size relative to control treatment. In zPDX treated with nivolumab, tumor shrinkage correlated with upregulated hIL-2 mRNA expression and was completely reversed by co-injection of a CD3-neutralizing antibody, indicating a T cell-mediated effect. Histological examination of whole-body zPDX treated with ICI revealed a significant increase in T cells and a marked decrease in vimentin + tumor cells. The zPDX assays were repeatable and reproducible within accepted precision thresholds. We performed zPDX assays for 21 cases, which clustered into three groups; High-, Low-, and Non-responders. zPDX response showed no significant correlation with immune-response gene signatures or percentage of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs). However, gene-expression analysis comparing High-responders with Low-/Non-responders revealed strong associations between zPDX response and the expression of positive immune regulators. Non-responder WTCs retained the intrinsic ability of T cells to respond to TCR stimulation. In the four patients with available clinical data, zPDX responses were generally consistent with outcomes following ICI therapy, supporting the potential of our novel zPDX platform to predict ICI efficacy in patients with RCC and, potentially, other malignancies.

title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency.
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/- mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II-treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/- mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility-HFpEF interactions.

title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
abstract: Although cerebellum is neuropathologically affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD), the cell type-specific genomic and epigenomic changes remain poorly understood. Here, we present single-nucleus multiome (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both the cerebellum and frontal cortex of diseased individuals and cognitively healthy controls. We identify 431,834 significant peak-to-gene linkages across cell subtypes, revealing cis-regulatory elements linked to cell type-specific and disease-associated transcriptomic and regulatory network changes. Differential trajectory analysis pinpoints disease-associated genes in cerebellar granule cells, such as STMN1 and CLU. Integrating epigenomic, genetic, and three-dimensional genome data, we pinpoint two likely causal variants linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells and KANSL1 in granule cells. Through CRISPR interference in patient-derived cerebellar organoids, we show that silencing the variant-containing regulatory elements suppresses SEZ6L2 and KANSL1 expression, which perturbs neurodegeneration-associated gene programs. This cell type-specific regulatory landscape provides genomic and epigenomic insights into the pathological role of the cerebellum in AD/ADRD. Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type‑specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single‑nucleus multiomics to map disease‑associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.

title: Long-Term Safety and Procedural Performance of an Interatrial Shunt for Heart Failure According to Ejection Fraction.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term device durability and phenotype-specific safety outcomes after interatrial shunting require further characterization.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the procedural success, device durability, and heart failure (HF) phenotype-specific safety outcomes of an interatrial shunt in the RELIEVE-HF trial.
METHODS: Randomized patients were assigned 1:1 to shunt or sham control with prespecified stratification by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) into heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (LVEF ≤40%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (LVEF >40%). Procedural performance, device durability, serious adverse events (SAEs), major adverse cardiovascular or neurological events (MACNE), major bleeding, and renal outcomes were assessed through 2 years.
RESULTS: Among 605 enrolled patients (508 randomized; 97 roll-in), shunt implantation was attempted in 370 and was successful in 369 (99.7%). Among implanted patients with follow-up (n = 348), no device- or procedure-related MACNE occurred through 2 years (0%; 95% CI: 0%-0.9%), and shunt patency was 99.4% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.9%). Prespecified LVEF-stratified analyses demonstrated divergent safety profiles. In HFrEF, shunt therapy was not associated with excess all-cause MACNE, major bleeding, or renal decline and was associated with lower SAE burden. In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline.
CONCLUSIONS: Interatrial shunt implantation was mechanically reliable and durable through 2 years. Safety outcomes differed by HF phenotype, with no evidence of excess clinical safety events in HFrEF but increased adverse events in HFpEF. These findings support phenotype-specific evaluation of interatrial shunt therapy. (REducing Lung congestion symptoms using the v-wavE shunt in adVancEd Heart Failure [RELIEVE-HF]; NCT03499236).

title: A genetically informed investigation into the relationship between childhood maltreatment and adult health
abstract: The underlying mechanisms linking childhood maltreatment (CM) to adverse health outcomes are unclear. Here, we estimated CM pleiotropy across human phenome, also assessing the role of socioeconomic factors. Specifically, we performed a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of CM-associated loci using electronic health records and genetic data from the All of Us Research Program (N = 98,551), FinnGen Project (N = 377,277), and Million Veteran Program (N = 449,042). To characterize CM pleiotropy, we also conducted genetic correlation (rg), latent causal variable analysis (LCV), and bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses. Additionally, multi-trait conditional and joint analysis and multivariate MR (MVMR) were performed to estimate whether genetically inferred CM associations are partially explained by household income (HI, a proxy for socioeconomic factors). PheWAS revealed CM loci associations with 66 medical outcomes (p < 2.76 × 10 −6 ), including psychiatric, musculoskeletal, circulatory, neurologic, and respiratory conditions. Similarly, we observed 285 CM genetic correlations (p < 3.24 × 10 −5 ) with a range of medical domains. Among them, emotional disorders starting during childhood or adolescence showed the highest CM genetic overlap (rg=0.75). LCV analysis revealed CM genetic relationships with musculoskeletal, metabolic, respiratory, and eye-related outcomes. For these, MR analyses highlighted bidirectional and heterogeneous effects possibly due to dynastic confounders, and MVMR showed a reduced effect of CM genetic liability after accounting for HI. In conclusion, different pleiotropic mechanisms likely contribute to CM relationships with several health domains, which appear to be at least partially explained by socioeconomic factors.

title: Sex-specific skeletal muscle fiber atrophy and reduced macrophage inflammation in a rodent transverse aortic constriction model.
abstract: Heart failure is associated with systemic skeletal muscle remodeling, where sex-specific differences suggest differential peripheral involvement in disease progression. Skeletal muscle macrophages regulate angiogenesis and tissue remodeling and may contribute to early alterations in muscle structure and function during cardiac pressure overload. We tested whether chronic pressure-overload induces sex-specific skeletal muscle remodeling and alters macrophage abundance and paracrine signaling in male and female Sprague Dawley rats that underwent transverse aortic constriction (TAC) or sham surgery at 4 weeks of age and were studied after 40 wk. TAC induced 12% greater heart mass (p = 0.049) and 17% greater heart-to-body mass ratio (p = 0.018) in males, while females showed minimal cardiac remodeling. In extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscle, TAC males exhibited ~ 10% smaller fiber perimeter corresponding with higher capillary-to-fiber perimeter exchange (p < 0.05 for both), while female TAC rats had no difference in fiber size and 17% lower capillary-to-fiber ratio than female sham (p = 0.033). In soleus muscle, TAC rats had higher capillarization indices (p < 0.05) regardless of sex. Muscle macrophage abundance was 19% lower in TAC males than sham males (p = 0.005). TAC macrophages secreted less MCP-1 (- 35%, p = 0.0058), IL-1β (- 16%, p = 0.0167), TNF-α (- 16%, p = 0.0337), and VEGF-A (- 16%, p = 0.0120) and produced less complex endothelial networks (18% larger mesh size, p = 0.001). These findings indicate that TAC is associated with skeletal muscle remodeling and macrophage immunosuppression, with some changes occurring in a sex-specific manner. This suggests the potential for immune-microvascular coupling in peripheral adaptations to cardiac pressure overload.

title: Sex Differences in the Prevalence, Medical Therapy, and Outcomes in Heart Failure With Improved Ejection Fraction.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with improved ejection fraction (HFimpEF) is a rapidly growing clinical entity. There is little understanding of how sex relates to the epidemiology, predictors, and trajectory of HFimpEF.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to describe sex-based differences in the epidemiology, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use, and clinical outcomes among patients with HFimpEF within a large, diverse health care system.
METHODS: The authors identified adults with incident heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction ≤40%) between 2013 and 2022. HFimpEF was defined as a subsequent ejection fraction measurement >40% within the following 12 months. Sex was based on self-report. Among patients with HFimpEF, the authors examined GDMT use at the time of incident HFrEF, HFimpEF, and 1 year following HFimpEF, stratified by sex. They examined the incidence of worsening heart failure (WHF) events and all-cause death 1 year postincident HFrEF. We compared event rates between patients with HFimpEF and persistent HFrEF, adjusted for demographic and clinical characteristics.
RESULTS: Among 28,292 patients with incident HFrEF (females: 34.8%), 35.2% experienced HFimpEF. Females were more likely to experience HFimpEF in the 12 months following HFrEF than males (36.5% vs 34.5%, P < 0.0001). Among patients with HFimpEF, GDMT use was similar among females and males and declined after incident HFimpEF in both sexes. Compared with patients with persistent HFrEF, patients with HFimpEF had better WHF outcomes and all-cause death outcomes, which was consistent by sex. However, females with HFimpEF had higher rates of WHF compared with males with HFimpEF, even when adjusted for clinical covariates.
CONCLUSIONS: HFimpEF is associated with improved outcomes for both females and males. However, females with HFimpEF have higher rates of WHF events compared with males.

title: Emergency Department Visits for Falls and First-Time Seizure.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Unrecognized seizures occur in up to 77% of individuals with epilepsy, leading to delays in diagnosis with significant consequences including injury, mortality, impaired psychosocial functioning, and negative socioeconomic impacts. Falls are a common reason to present to the emergency department (ED) and may be a sentinel sign of an unrecognized seizure. Whether falls represent missed opportunities for earlier seizure recognition remains unknown. We therefore evaluated the temporal association between ED visits for falls and first-time seizure.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case-crossover study using the State Inpatient Databases and State Emergency Department Databases from 11 states (Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Massachusetts, Maryland, Nebraska, New York, Utah, Vermont, and Wisconsin) between 2016 and 2021. Adults aged 18 years and older with an acute care visit for a first-time seizure were identified using ICD-10 codes. Using patients as their own controls, we applied conditional logistic regression to compare the odds of an ED visit for a fall during prespecified case periods preceding the seizure (1-7, 8-30, 31-90, and 91-180 days prior) vs corresponding control periods 1 year earlier. Prespecified intervals were selected to assess graded temporal proximity.
RESULTS: There were 57,547 patients with a first-time seizure and 7,307 patients (mean age 49.3 years and 55.2% female) with at least one prior ED visit for a fall during the case or control periods. ED visits for a fall were more common in case compared with control periods, with the highest odds in the 7 days immediately before the acute care visit for first-time seizure (OR = 2.6, 95% CI 2.2-3.2). In a week-by-week analysis, the association persisted up to 22 weeks before seizure, demonstrating temporal attenuation as time from the event increased. These findings were consistent across age and sex strata and after excluding those who had traumatic brain injury. In analyses restricted to first-time status epilepticus, the association in the 7 days preceding seizure was most pronounced (OR = 4.5, 95% CI 2.5-9.0).
DISCUSSION: ED visits for falls are more common immediately preceding first-time seizure, potentially representing missed opportunities for earlier diagnosis, evaluation, and intervention. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.

title: Mutating ubiquitin carboxy terminal hydrolase L1 cysteine 152 ameliorates white matter injury and functional deficits in experimental vascular dementia
abstract: Vascular cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID) is characterized by extensive subcortical white matter injury and progressive sensorimotor and cognitive impairment. Post-translational modification of UCHL1 at cysteine 152 (C152) impairs repair of white matter injury and recovery of function after ischemia. We hypothesized that mutation of UCHL1 C152 would ameliorate white matter injury and cognitive impairment in VCID. VCID was produced using the asymmetric bilateral common carotid artery stenosis (ABCS) model in young and 18-month-old mice bearing a UCHL1 cysteine 152 to alanine mutation (C152A) and wild-type (WT) controls. White matter injury was assessed using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and immunohistochemistry. Sensorimotor function was assessed using adhesive tape removal test. Cognitive function was assessed by Morris water maze, passive avoidance, and novel object recognition tests. C152A mice exhibited reduced white matter injury as detected by DTI and improved performance on both sensorimotor and cognitive tests compared to WT mice in both young and 18-month-old groups. These results suggest that post-translational modification of UCHL1 cysteine 152 is important in the pathogenesis of white matter injury and functional impairment in VCID. Therapeutic strategies aimed at preventing post-translational modification of UCHL1 C152 could reduce white matter injury and improve cognitive function in VCID.

title: Brain structural covariance networks in co-occurring PTSD and alcohol use disorder: An ENIGMA PTSD and ENIGMA addiction working group collaboration.
abstract: High rates of comorbid posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and alcohol use disorder (AUD) may stem from a shared neurobiological basis; however, research exploring this overlap remains limited. We examined whole-brain structural covariance (SC) across PTSD, AUD, comorbid PTSD & AUD, trauma-exposed controls, and trauma-naïve controls to identify shared and unique SC profiles. Structural brain scans were acquired from individuals across 14 sites (N = 1565), and cortical thickness estimates were extracted to compute SC. Group differences in SC between pairs of cortical regions were examined using the Network-Based statistic and quantified using local and global graph theory (GT) measures. Clinical groups showed consistent alterations in SC compared with trauma-naïve controls, characterised by lower SC involving frontal regions, particularly the inferior frontal gyrus and frontal pole, which also demonstrated high centrality in local GT analyses. In contrast, higher SC was observed in temporal regions, with the fusiform gyrus consistently emerging as a central region. Comparisons involving PTSD & AUD also showed increased SC in occipital regions, suggesting a potentially distinct pattern of structural organization in this group. Global GT analyses demonstrated altered network organization in clinical groups, including increased clustering and path length, and reduced global efficiency relative to trauma-naïve controls. Local efficiency was increased in PTSD and PTSD & AUD, but not AUD alone. Together, these findings indicate that alterations in frontal and temporal regions are implicated across PTSD, AUD, and their comorbidity. However, the PTSD & AUD group also exhibited additional occipital lobe alterations, suggesting a broader distribution of structural covariance alterations in the comorbid group.

title: Clinician Experiences With Tele-Emergency Care: Qualitative Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency departments (EDs) face persistent challenges related to overcrowding, boarding, ambulatory care access barriers, and workforce strain, contributing to compromised patient care and high rates of physician burnout. Virtual care has emerged as a potential strategy to alleviate pressure on emergency care systems. In 2020, the Veterans Health Administration (VA) launched the national Tele-Emergency Care (TEC) program, in which patients who call a call center can be connected to an emergency medicine clinician by phone or video. Although virtual care may help address ED capacity and clinician burnout, the perspectives of emergency medicine-trained clinicians remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to examine the experiences of emergency medicine clinicians participating in VA's TEC program.
METHODS: As part of a national mixed methods evaluation of TEC, we conducted semistructured interviews with clinicians delivering emergency care through TEC between February 2025 and June 2025. Participants (n=15) were recruited via multistage purposeful sampling from 4 of 18 regional TEC programs that varied in geography, volume, duration, and operational models. Interviews explored experiences of providing care in a virtual environment, including perceived benefits and challenges. We performed a descriptive qualitative analysis.
RESULTS: We interviewed 14 physicians and 1 nurse practitioner with formal emergency medicine training. Interviewees described four primary themes: (1) clinical decision-making in a virtual environment; (2) development of the provider-patient relationship; (3) clinician job satisfaction and professional well-being; and (4) challenges. Participants reported that TEC provided perceived opportunities to avoid ED referrals, more focused patient interactions, and improved job satisfaction related to flexible virtual shifts. Reported challenges included filling primary care gaps and performing care coordination tasks.
CONCLUSIONS: TEC represents an emerging model of emergency care delivery that clinicians perceive may expand access, prevent avoidable ED visits, and support clinician well-being while also introducing distinct clinical and operational challenges. Our findings can inform the implementation of similar emergency telehealth services in other health systems.

title: Human iPSC-Derived Tissue-Engineered Nigrostriatal Pathway for Chronic Restoration of Dopaminergic Axon Tracts in a Rat Parkinson's Model.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by loss of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra, causing motor symptoms. Current surgical interventions fail to restore the native nigrostriatal pathway essential for dopamine regulation. We have developed tissue-engineered nigrostriatal pathways (TE-NSPs) using hyaluronic acid hydrogel microcolumns with a collagen/laminin core encasing aggregated dopaminergic neurons and long-projecting axon tracts. TE-NSPs fabricated using human iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons extended bundled axon tracts at a rate of 1 mm/day-twice that of neuronal aggregates on planar surfaces. Fully grown engineered microtissue exhibited nigrostriatal-like cytoarchitecture, appropriate dopaminergic phenotypes, evoked dopamine release, and innervation of striatal neurons in vitro. TE-NSPs were then evaluated in a rat 6-OHDA PD model via histology and voltammetry at 3- and 6 months post-implantation. TE-NSPs showed dopaminergic neuronal survival in the substantia nigra, preserved axon tracts within the microcolumn, and outgrowth into host striatum. Voltammetry on ex vivo brain slices containing the implanted microtissue revealed evoked dopamine release at both 3- and 6-months post-implant. This study shows engineered microtissue fabricated using human cells with an anatomically-inspired architecture and subsequently used for chronic replacement of a long-distance brain pathway in a preclinical model, potentially offering a promising future treatment for pathway reconstruction in PD.

title: Inhibition of ROR1 signaling with zilovertamab plus ibrutinib in chronic lymphocytic leukemia: safety, mechanistic insights, and an exploratory signal in del(17p) disease
abstract: The receptor tyrosine kinase‑like orphan receptor (ROR1) is aberrantly expressed on chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) cells and promotes survival signaling through NF‑κB, ERK1/2, and mTORC1. Zilovertamab is a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting ROR1. We conducted a multicenter phase 1b/2 study of zilovertamab plus ibrutinib (Z + I) in relapsed/refractory CLL. Phase 1b/2a (N = 34) established a recommended zilovertamab dose based on safety, pharmacokinetics, and ROR1 occupancy. In phase 2b, patients were randomized to zilovertamab plus ibrutinib (N = 18) or ibrutinib alone (I; N = 10); the primary endpoint was complete response (CR) per iwCLL, with progression‑free survival (PFS) and safety as secondary endpoints. Z + I was well tolerated, with no dose‑limiting toxicities and safety profile consistent with BTK inhibition. CR rates, overall response, and PFS were similar between randomized arms. In a post hoc subset of 10 patients with del(17p), Z + I was associated with prolonged disease control relative to historical BTK inhibitor experience; this hypothesis-generating observation requires prospective confirmation. Zilovertamab achieved ROR1 occupancy and attenuated NF‑κB, ERK1/2, and mTORC1 signaling in CLL cells, supporting further exploration of ROR1‑targeted strategies in biologically high‑risk CLL. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03088878).

title: TNFα promotes brain-predominant EAE independent of IFNγ and IL-17A in HLA-DR3 transgenic mice.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is thought to be mediated by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class II-restricted autoreactive CD4 T cells producing interleukin (IL)-17A and/or interferon γ (IFNγ), but the necessity of these cytokines for disease pathogenesis is unclear. Utilizing HLA-DR3 (DRβ1*0301) transgenic mice lacking IFNγ or IL-17A in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a model of MS, we found that neither cytokine is essential for disease induction, although both have distinct roles. The absence of IFNγ caused atypical, brain-predominant EAE characterized by high levels of IL-17A, while the absence of IL-17A resulted in classical EAE, targeting the spinal cord. To assess whether IL-17A drives atypical EAE in the absence of IFNγ, we generated HLA-DR3.IFNγ-/-.IL-17A-/- double knockout (DKO) mice. DKO mice developed atypical EAE with brain infiltration and inflammation of the brainstem and cerebellum, indicating that IL-17A is dispensable for brain-predominant disease in the absence of IFNγ. DKO mice exhibited significant CD4 T cell infiltration and increased expression of CD4 T cell-associated genes at peak disease. Prior to central nervous system infiltration, CD4 T cell accumulated in the spleen and inguinal lymph nodes of DKO mice, where they exhibited an altered cytokine milieu and upregulated genes involved in recruitment, activation, and migration to the brain. DKO mice exhibited elevated expression of tumor necrosis factor α (TNFα), granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, and IL-17F; however, only TNFα inhibition ameliorated atypical disease. Together, our findings indicate TNFα promotes brain-predominant inflammatory pathology in the absence of IFNγ and IL-17A.

title: Sleeve Gastrectomy Improves Metabolic Health, Cognition, and Alzheimer's Disease Pathology in 3xTG Mice.
abstract: Obesity and diabetes are well-established risk factors for Alzheimer's disease (AD), implicating metabolic dysfunction in AD pathogenesis. Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) is among the most effective metabolic interventions available, yet its impact on AD progression remains poorly understood. We hypothesized that SG performed early in life would improve metabolic health, attenuate AD pathology, and preserve cognition in a transgenic AD mouse model. Five-week-old female 3xTg-AD mice were preconditioned on a Western diet (WD) to induce obesity and glucose intolerance, then randomized to SG or sham surgery and maintained on either Control or continued WD for 12 months. Metabolic phenotyping, body composition, and cognitive assessments (Novel Object Recognition, Barnes Maze, Fear Conditioning) were performed longitudinally, with histological and molecular brain analysis at endpoint. Under Control-fed conditions, SG reduced fat mass and improved peripheral insulin sensitivity independent of food intake. These changes were accompanied by reduced cortical Aβ plaque burden and attenuated astrocytic (GFAP) and microglial (IBA1) activation, specifically in the cortex. Mechanistically, SG altered the insulin signaling-autophagy axis in a region-specific manner, with increased pAKT and suppressed ATG5/ATG7/ATG16L1 in the cortex. Under persistent WD, SG improved glucose homeostasis, reduced fat mass, lowered frailty, and rescued short- and long-term spatial memory deficits in the Barnes maze, accompanied by reduced cortical Aβ burden. Collectively, these findings provide the first preclinical evidence that SG attenuates AD progression through a brain insulin signaling-autophagy axis, supporting metabolic surgery as a promising disease-modifying intervention for AD prevention in individuals with obesity.

title: Full Spectrum Raman Spectroscopy Combined With Deep Learning for Prediction of Tensile Mechanical Properties of Human Cortical Bone.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) alters bone quality at the matrix level in ways that current methods do not fully capture. Raman spectroscopy provides molecular information on bone composition and is well suited to probing such alterations. Full-spectrum Raman data were acquired from cortical bone of fresh-frozen cadaveric femurs from 60 non-diabetic and 60 T2DM donors (equal numbers of men and women, aged 50-97 years), followed by uniaxial tensile testing. Machine learning (ML) models (random forest [RF], gradient boosting machine [GBM], adaptive boosting [AdaBoost], stacking) and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) were trained on the full spectrum to predict tensile properties. A combined 1D CNN and multilayer perceptron (MLP) model that added clinical variables (age, sex, group) reached the highest performance, with R2 values from 0.83 to 0.89, while spectral-only models also performed well. These findings show that full-spectrum Raman analysis with deep learning (DL) predicts tensile mechanical behavior of human cortical bone. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further showed that collagen associated spectral regions, rather than mineral-related regions, were the primary contributors to the model predictions.

title: Insights Into the Role of Platelet Factor 4 in Neurodegenerative Diseases.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: As population aging accelerates worldwide, the prevalence and burden of neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) continue to rise, underscoring the urgent need to identify key molecular mechanisms driving disease progression and novel therapeutic targets. Chronic neuroinflammation is a hallmark of multiple NDs, including Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Platelet factor 4 (PF4) is a chemokine primarily released by activated platelets and has traditionally been investigated for its roles in hemostasis, thrombosis, and peripheral inflammation.
RESULTS: Growing evidence has implicated PF4 in the pathogenesis of NDs. Altered PF4 expression has been observed across multiple NDs. As a central player at the intersection of the nervous, immune, and vascular systems, PF4 modulates inflammation, vascular homeostasis, and neuronal survival, all of which are critical in the pathogenesis of NDs. Dissecting the cell-type specific and temporally dynamic roles of PF4 across diverse disease contexts is essential for elucidating its contribution to neurodegenerative processes and disease progression.
CONCLUSION: This review highlights PF4 as a potential mechanistic mediator in NDs and discusses its promise as both a biomarker and a therapeutic target. Further elucidation of PF4 signaling pathways may provide new insights into disease mechanisms and uncover novel opportunities for targeted interventions in NDs.

title: Leadership Perspectives on Hospital at Home and Equity: Broadening Access, Removing Enrollment Barriers, and Adding Value by Addressing Disparities.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital at home (HaH) delivers safe and high-quality acute hospital-level care in patients' homes as an alternative to traditional hospital care. As HaH expands across the USA, there remains uncertainty in how HaH program leaders conceptualize equity and how they approach operational challenges affecting equitable delivery of HaH. Our objective was to explore how equity is defined, as well as barriers and strategies to achieving equity in HaH.
METHODS: We purposively sampled HaH programs diverse in size, geography, and safety-net status. We conducted semi-structured interviews and used rapid analysis with debrief templates and summaries, and applied targeted coding to develop themes, organized into a frame analysis.
RESULTS: We conducted 18 interviews with 28 leaders representing 15 hospital-based and three commercial HaH programs; approximately half represented safety-net hospitals. Participants articulated three distinct frames to conceptualize HaH equity, with associated themes incorporating challenges, and strategies to overcome them. Frame 1, Broaden HaH Access, focuses on factors limiting and enabling program establishment (e.g., in rural areas) to reach the broadest population. Frame 2, Remove Barriers to HaH Enrollment, focuses on socio-demographic factors (payer, geography, home safety, patient/caregiver preferences) affecting program enrolment. Leaders described specific strategies to overcome each factor (e.g., expanding payer mix). Frame 3, Add Value by Addressing Disparities, describes how HaH actively seeks to mitigate pre-existing health and social challenges and improve longer-term outcomes.
DISCUSSION: These three complementary and non-mutually exclusive frames reveal different HaH equity-related foci. Within each frame, HaH program leaders demonstrated an understanding of equity-related issues, barriers, and targeted strategies enhancing the equitable provision of HaH care and, in turn, HaH's value to health system goals.
CONCLUSION: Clarifying and aligning HaH equity frames and matching targeted improvements within and across frames can enhance the ability to deliver comprehensive, equitable care as the model continues to grow.

title: Implementing systematic distress screening in veteran oncology care: a quality improvement initiative
abstract: Distress is common among patients with cancer and is associated with worse outcomes yet routine distress screening remains inconsistently implemented in outpatient oncology clinics, particularly for Veterans. We conducted a quality improvement project (QIP) in the surgical oncology clinic at a large Veterans Affairs medical centre to improve distress screening among Veterans with newly diagnosed cancer.A multidisciplinary team designed and implemented a comprehensive psychosocial distress screening programme using the validated NCCN Distress Thermometer. Key drivers of screening reliability were identified through stakeholder interviews and used to guide intervention design. The intervention incorporated standardised screening, evaluation of positive screens, predefined referral pathways, timely follow-up with embedded mental health services and structured electronic record documentation. The programme was iteratively refined through Plan–Do–Study–Act cycles.A total of 178 veterans were included over a 6-month baseline period and 12 months of intervention. During the baseline phase, only 5% of eligible veterans had documented distress screening. Following implementation, screening rates increased from 5% at baseline to 87% by the end of the intervention period. 27 of 117 veterans (23.1%) screened positive for distress during the intervention period. 18 accepted referrals to mental health services, four were already established with mental healthcare and five declined referral. Veterans requiring urgent evaluation were seen by mental health services the same day or the following day, while all remaining veterans accepting referral were scheduled within 2–3 weeks.This project demonstrates that systematic distress screening for veterans with cancer can be successfully embedded into routine outpatient oncology care. Pairing standardised workflows with integrated referral pathways, timely follow-up and electronic health record documentation provides a scalable and sustainable model for comprehensive psychosocial distress screening in veteran oncology care.

title: Effects of semaglutide and dapagliflozin on natriuretic peptides in type 2 diabetes: a randomized comparative study
abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is associated with a substantially increased risk of heart failure, partly mediated by myocardial stress and neurohormonal activation. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) both improve cardiovascular outcomes in T2D, but their comparative effects on heart failure and cardiac stress pathways remain incompletely understood. Purpose To compare the longitudinal effects of the GLP-1 RA semaglutide and the SGLT2i dapagliflozin on plasma N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations in patients with T2D. NT-proBNP is a well-established biomarker of myocardial wall stress and prognostic risk. Methods Post hoc analysis of a prospective, open-label randomised clinical trial that recruited participants between 2020 and 2022 and followed them for 6 months. NT-proBNP was measured in blood samples collected at baseline and after 6 months. Participants with type 2 diabetes on metformin monotherapy, recruited at a single centre, were randomised in a 1:1 ratio to treatment with semaglutide or dapagliflozin. Changes over time in NT-proBNP were analysed using Tobit regression to account for left-censoring. Between-group differences were assessed using mixed-effects models adjusted for relevant covariates. Results A total of 75 participants received semaglutide and 92 received dapagliflozin (mean age 66 years; 31% women; mean HbA1c 53 mmol/mol). Baseline NT-proBNP levels were overall low (median 77 ng/L, interquartile range 55–138) and below the limit of quantification in 25% of participants. During the 6-month follow-up, NT-proBNP declined significantly by 7% in the semaglutide group (p=0.01), whereas it increased by 20% in the dapagliflozin group (p=0.07). A significant time-by-treatment interaction was observed, indicating that the magnitude of change in NT-proBNP differed between the treatment groups. Conclusions In patients with T2D without heart failure, treatment with semaglutide but not dapagliflozin was associated with a reduction in NT-proBNP over 6 months, independent of renal function, body mass index, and other known determinants of NT-proBNP. These findings suggest that glucose-lowering therapies may exert distinct influences on myocardial stress pathways, with potential implications for heart failure risk modulation.NT-proBNP levels at baseline and follow-up.Longitudinal trajectories by treatment group.

title: Genetic evidence supports a cortical neuroprotective role of GLP‐1 receptor activation in Alzheimer's disease: A drug‐target Mendelian randomization study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Whether glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor (GLP-1R) activation lowers Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk via peripheral metabolic improvement or direct neuroprotection remains unclear. METHODS: Using blood and brain-cortex cis-acting expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTLs) for GLP-1R as instruments, we performed cis-Mendelian randomization (cis-MR) for AD and seven biomarkers. Mendelian randomization Bayesian model averaging (MR-BMA), cis-multivariable Mendelian randomization (cis-MVMR), and two-step cis-MR assessed 11 metabolic and inflammatory mediators, and tissue-specific cis-MVMR identified the causal tissue. RESULTS: GLP-1R expression was associated with lower AD risk and cerebrospinal fluid phosphorylated tau (p-tau) levels. The cis-MVMR identified systolic blood pressure as the only independent mediator, whereas GLP-1R retained a direct protective effect on AD. Tissue-specific cis-MVMR attributed the effect predominantly to cortical (posterior inclusion probability [PIP] = 0.998) rather than blood GLP-1R expression (PIP = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Genetic evidence supports GLP-1R as a potential target in AD, with a protective effect not fully explained by peripheral metabolic improvement and possibly involving cortical neuroprotection, supporting further investigation of brain-penetrant agents at preclinical or prodromal stages.

title: Dietary intake of methyl-donor nutrients is associated with frailty and partially mediated by oxidative stress in U.S. middle-aged and older adults.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty reflects declining physiological reserve and is a major barrier to healthy longevity. Methyl-donor nutrients, which serve as substrates and cofactors in one-carbon metabolism, are involved in several biological processes relevant to aging, including the regulation of oxidative stress. However, their association with frailty and the potential role of oxidative stress in this relationship remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between a composite Methyl-Donor Nutrient Quality Index (MNQI) and frailty and to evaluate whether oxidative stress may contribute to this association in middle-aged and older adults.
METHODS: Cross-sectional data from NHANES 2005-2018 were analyzed among 13,528 adults aged ≥40 years. Frailty was assessed using a 53-item deficit accumulation frailty index categorized as robust, prefrail, or frail. The MNQI was calculated from seven methyl-donor and cofactor nutrients. The oxidative stress index (OSI) was derived from gamma-glutamyl transferase, uric acid, albumin, and bilirubin. Survey-weighted multinomial logistic regression examined MNQI and OSI associations with frailty, and exploratory mediation analyses evaluated the indirect effect through OSI.
RESULTS: Higher MNQI was associated with 33% lower odds of frailty (OR=0.67; 95% CI: 0.52-0.88; P=0.004), with a significant dose-response relationship. Higher OSI was associated with 113% greater odds of frailty (OR=2.13; 95% CI: 1.92-2.36; P<0.001). Exploratory mediation analyses indicated a significant indirect effect through oxidative stress, accounting for approximately 29% of the MNQI-frailty association.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher dietary intake of methyl-donor nutrients was associated with lower odds of frailty and may support physiological processes relevant to healthy longevity, with oxidative stress potentially representing one pathway underlying this association. Longitudinal studies and randomized trials are needed to confirm these relationships and clarify the underlying mechanisms.

title: Time to untether transitional care from hospital quality: Healthcare utilization following discharge from a Department of Veterans Affairs hospital among community-dwelling older persons.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thirty-day performance measures (e.g., unplanned readmissions), designed to evaluate inpatient care, were neither designed to reflect the experience of patients transitioning from hospital to home, nor the impact of transitional programs to improve postdischarge outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To identify transitional care outcomes by examining a range of postdischarge encounters and mortality.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort (October 2022-September 2023) included community-dwelling patients ≥65-years-old, discharged from 120 Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals to home after medical or neurological admissions. The outcomes, assessed 30- and 90-days postdischarge were: mortality; planned and unplanned readmissions; observation stays; Emergency Department (ED) visits at VA or non-VA hospitals; and number of days in acute care.
RESULTS: Among 99,778 patients, 71.1% had no acute care utilization within 30 days postdischarge; 49.9% in 90 days. Unplanned readmissions occurred in 14.4% (N = 14,400) at 30 days; 27.5% (N = 27,386) at 90 days. Mortality occurred in 1.8% (N = 1750) within 30 days; 5.6% (N = 5624) within 90 days. Mortality was highest among patients with unplanned readmissions: 30 days, 6.1% (882/14,400); 90 days, 13.1% (3599/27,386). Planned readmission mortality rates were 30 days, 5.8% (59/1017); 90 days, 9.6% (258/2692). Half of patients who died within 30 days postdischarge did so after an unplanned readmission (50.4% [882/1750]); 35.0% (613/1750) had no acute care utilization. Among N = 94,154 patients who survived 90-day postdischarge, 11.2% spent ≥10 days in acute care settings.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings support using the number of days in acute care within 90 days postdischarge as a transitional outcome. Thirty-day readmissions do not capture the full scope of postdischarge healthcare utilization and mortality among community-dwelling older adults.

title: Outcomes After Curative-intent Resection of Synchronous Primary Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): Two is Worse than One.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Outcomes following curative-intent resection of synchronous primary lung cancer (SPLC) remain incompletely defined. We compared recurrence and survival in SPLC versus solitary primary tumors among patients with clinical stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of Veterans undergoing curative-intent resection for clinical stage I NSCLC in the Veterans Health Administration (2006-2020). SPLC was defined as two distinct clinical stage I NSCLC tumors diagnosed within six weeks, with curative-intent treatment of both tumors within one year. Propensity score matching (PSM) (1:1) was used to compare patients with SPLC to those with solitary tumors. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR); secondary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Additional analyses examined the role of adjuvant treatment and drivers of recurrence in SPLC patients.
RESULTS: Of 12,606 Veterans with resected clinical stage I NSCLC, 337 (2.7%) had SPLC. SPLC presented with larger tumors and more advanced pathologic stage. Histology was discordant between the two tumors in 44.2% of SPLC cases. In the propensity-matched cohort (281 pairs), SPLC was associated with higher CIR (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.10-2.07), worse DFS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.03-1.50), and worse OS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45). Within SPLC, wedge resection of both tumors was independently associated with recurrence.
CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment, SPLC was associated with higher recurrence and worse survival than solitary tumors, supporting recognition of SPLC as a higher-risk phenotype within clinical stage I NSCLC.

title: The Nuances of Cost-Related Medication Non-Adherence in Patients Receiving Immunosuppression Compared to Patients with Chronic Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background: Medication adherence rates across diseases that require immunosuppression, including autoimmune diseases, are low. While cost barriers affect medication adherence, it is unknown whether adherence rates related to cost barriers differ between medically immunosuppressed patients and similar patients with other chronic diseases. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the influence of immunosuppression on cost-related medication non-adherence (CRMNA). Methods: We performed a cross-sectional study utilizing the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between immunosuppression and CRMNA, accounting for sex, age, education, race, income, life satisfaction, insurance status and marital status. Predicted probabilities of CRMNA were estimated by age group, and a subgroup analysis was performed among people who described as having poor health. Results: In our unweighted sample of 17,394 adults, 54.3% were female, 12.8% self-identified as Black, 35.2% were publicly insured (Medicare and/or Medicaid), and 11.1% were below the federal poverty level. The prevalence of reporting CRMNA was 11% for patients with chronic diseases and no immunosuppression, 12.5% for patients with immunosuppression but no chronic disease, and 19.1% for patients with chronic disease and immunosuppression. In the multivariable model, participants with medical immunosuppression and chronic diseases were more likely to report CRMNA than participants with chronic diseases but no immunosuppression (OR 1.55, 95% CI [1.24, 1.94], p = 0.001). Participants with medical immunosuppression but no chronic disease did not differ significantly from the group with chronic diseases and no immunosuppression (OR 0.87, 95% CI [0.60, 1.29], p = 0.49). The predicted probability of CRMNA was highest for 30-49-year-old immunosuppressed individuals with one or more chronic diseases at 23%. CRMNA was similarly associated with immunosuppression status in patients with poor health. Conclusions: Medically immunosuppressed individuals with chronic disease experience greater CRMNA than individuals with chronic disease who are not immunosuppressed, particularly among individuals 30-49 years of age. Future studies aimed at reducing CRMNA in immunosuppressed individuals may consider interventions that target the role of chronic health conditions in non-adherence.

title: Clonal haematopoiesis subtypes confer dose-dependent risk of serious bacterial infection
abstract: Clonal haematopoiesis (CH) arises from somatic mutations in haematopoietic stem cells that drive clonal expansion and increase haematological malignancy risk. Here we show that CH confers mutation- and dose-dependent risk of serious bacterial infection (SBI). Using a multi-parameter somatic variant calling and filtering approach, we identified 19,822 mutations across 43 CH genes in 40,560 of 590,537 individuals from three population cohorts (6.87%), validated in a combined analysis of 889,215 individuals. CH was associated with SBI development (HR = 1.22, P = 4.66 × 10⁻²⁹) and 28-day post-infection mortality (RR = 1.84, P = 0.0012), independent of malignancy and robust to adjustment for inflammatory comorbidities and ancestry. Recurrent mutations in SRSF2, DNMT3A, SF3B1, IDH2, and NRAS (n = 2143) conferred substantial absolute risks: 22–25% of individuals with expanded SRSF2 P95 clones developed SBI within 10 years. These associations were consistent across diverse populations and largely independent of bacterial strain. Fewings et al. show that clonal haematopoiesis confers subtype- and dose-dependent risk of serious bacterial infection, with splicing-factor mutations carrying the greatest hazard, validated across five biobank cohorts totalling 889,215 individuals.

title: Coordination of Specialty Care Within and Across Health Systems: Patient Experience in the Veterans Health Administration.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare patients' experience of specialty care coordination within a single health system to that across organizational boundaries, and whether coordination varies by illness burden and across coordination domains.
STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: National cross-sectional survey of patients referred from Veterans Health Administration (VA) primary care to VA specialty care ("within-system") or VA-paid community specialty care ("cross-system"). The primary outcome was patient-reported overall coordination. Illness burden was assessed using the Veterans RAND 12-item Health Survey. Secondary outcomes included 10 different domains of coordination.
DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: Data were collected between September 2022 and March 2025 using the Coordination of Specialty Care-Patient Survey and linked to VA administrative data. Eligible participants were Veterans with a recent first visit to cardiology, endocrinology, or pulmonary medicine and no prior visit to the same specialty within 18 months. The analytic sample included 1388 respondents (40% response rate). We used mixed-effects logistic regression models with primary care facility as a random effect.
PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: In adjusted analyses, within-system patients were 5.3 percentage points more likely than cross-system patients to report well-coordinated care [average marginal effect (AME) 0.053, 95% CI: 0.052, 0.053]. Higher illness burden was associated with worse coordination (AME -0.145, 95% CI: -0.147, -0.144), and this did not differ by care setting. Among 10 coordination domains, only Specialist Knowledge of Patient History differed consistently, favoring within-system care.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients receiving within-system specialty care reported better overall coordination than those receiving cross-system care despite similar scores across most domains. Coordination was worse among those with higher illness burden, identifying a higher-risk group in both settings. The divergence between overall coordination and individual domains highlights a challenge in cross-system comparisons: differences in patient experience may arise from processes not represented in available data.

title: Assessment of Ototoxicity in Patients With Heart Failure Receiving High-Dose IV Loop Diuretics
abstract: Importance: Concern for ototoxicity hinders loop diuretic (LD) dosing in heart failure (HF); given the mechanism by which LDs affect the ear, high-dose LDs should produce transient, not permanent, hearing changes. Objective: To measure the association of LD dose with permanent and temporary ototoxicity. Design, Setting, and Participants: Cohort 1 received a randomized sequence of LD doses (bumetanide, 1.25-10 mg) across study visits with serial audiometry assessments. Cohort 2 received serial LD up to furosemide 500-mg doses during a HF hospitalization with audiometry at baseline and prior to discharge. Cohort 3 retrospectively characterized clinically diagnosed ototoxicity in HF hospitalizations was defined using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. Cohorts 1 and 2 were single center, while cohort 3 was multicenter. Cohort 1 studied outpatient participants with stable HF, while cohort 2 (n = 40) and cohort 3 studied hospitalized patients with acute HF. Exposure: Intravenous LD. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcomes were clinically diagnosed ototoxicity and hearing changes via audiometry. Results: Cohort 1 contained 50 participants, cohort 2 contained 40 participants, and cohort 3 contained 22 656 participants. In cohort 1, mean (SD) participant age was 63.2 (10.4) years, and 21 of 50 participants (42%) were women. In cohorts 1 and 2, clinically diagnosed ototoxicity was not observed. In cohort 1, at peak diuretic concentration, worsening hearing shifts were infrequent (24 ears of 400 doses [6%]) but were more common with higher doses (odds ratio [OR], 1.99; 95% CI, 1.21-3.28 per doubling dose; P = .007). Within hours, hearing shifts largely resolved and were absent in 98% of measurements (393 ears of 400 doses). No significant association between LD dose and hearing shifts was present at any time aside from peak LD concentration. In cohort 2, hearing shifts were not different across groups divided by the median daily LD dose and were not associated with LD dose (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.71-1.98 per doubling dose; P = .52). In cohort 3, 608 HF hospitalizations (2.7%) had clinically diagnosed ototoxicity. In multivariable analyses, peak dose of 160 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.52-1.31; P = .43) and 400 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.71-2.31; P = .41) were not associated with greater clinically diagnosed ototoxicity risk relative to less than 160 mg. Conclusions and Relevance: In this analysis of 2 small HF cohorts, short-term exposure to high-dose LD was not associated with permanent ototoxicity, although concomitant ototoxin use was excluded. Future studies are needed to understand the risk of ototoxicity with repeated LD exposure and in broader HF populations. title: Military Occupation and Incident Cancer in Canadian Armed Forces Personnel and Veterans: A Sex-Stratified Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) includes a large workforce with a diverse spectrum of military occupations and potentially related exposures. The objective was to examine associations between service in distinct military occupations and the subsequent development of cancer.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used CAF administrative data linked to national cancer registry data. Personnel and Veterans with at least 2 years of CAF service between 1990 and 2017 were identified (N = 19,660 females and 129,840 males). Service in common military occupations was categorized using military occupation codes. Associations with incident primary cancer diagnoses (all cancers combined and specific cancer types) between 1990 and 2017 were analyzed using sex-stratified Cox proportional hazards models with age as the timeline for analysis, adjusted for enrollment era.
RESULTS: For most military occupations, no significant associations with all cancers combined or specific cancer types were observed in females or males. Exceptions included occupation as an aviation systems technician, which in females was associated with an increased likelihood of breast cancer, and in males with all cancers combined as well as oral, colorectal, Hodgkin lymphoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and kidney/renal cancers. Positive associations were also observed in females for colorectal cancer in supply technicians, and in males for non-Hodgkin lymphoma in gunners, pancreatic cancer in infanteers, and lung/bronchus cancer in supply technicians.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings can inform health protection measures, benefits and services for military personnel and Veterans. Future research should examine specific factors linked to the increased risks observed.

title: Ambient AI scribes are here: What every PA needs to know before clicking "Sign".
abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes, which record patient encounters and automatically draft clinical notes, are rapidly entering frontline practice. They rely on large language models to convert recorded conversations into structured documentation and are marketed as a way to reduce the documentation burden that contributes to clinician burnout. Early evidence from multicenter studies, randomized trials, systematic reviews, and international research suggests that ambient AI scribes may reduce documentation time and improve clinician well-being. However, most available studies are observational, reliant on small samples, and limited to short-term follow-up. At the same time, studies consistently raise concerns about new risks, including AI-generated "hallucinations" (fabricated content that appears confident), errors in draft notes (with omissions being the most common error type), documentation drift toward generic language, racial disparities in speech recognition accuracy, the use of unauthorized "shadow" AI tools with HIPAA and security implications, and unresolved questions about clinical safety outcomes. For physician associates (PAs), who are high-volume users of electronic health records and whose notes frequently serve as the primary communication channel with collaborating physicians, these risks carry particular weight. This review explains how ambient AI scribes work in accessible terms, synthesizes the current evidence base, and offers concrete strategies that PAs can use to ensure that these tools support safe, efficient, patient-centered practice.

title: Neuronal intranuclear inclusions: Case report of an unusual cause of rapidly progressive dementia.
abstract: Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS) and neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) are caused by CGG repeat expansions in the FMR1 and NOTCH2NLC genes, respectively. They have similar clinical, radiological, and pathological features. Neither typically presents as rapidly progressive dementia (RPD). Here we report a case that highlights that FXTAS and NIID should be considered in the differential for RPD. A 62-year-old Caucasian man with diabetes and obstructive sleep apnea presented to our movement disorders clinic with a chief complaint of cognitive impairment and falls. His family confirmed he worked full time until late 2022 as a closing agent without any concern for his work performance. In late 2022, he developed decreased stamina, tremors, and urinary incontinence. In early 2023, he started falling and was referred to physical therapy. By summer of 2023, he had clear cognitive impairment with an incident of getting lost while driving in his own neighborhood. His family reported fluctuating cognition but unchanged personality. He was now having trouble keeping up at work. Before he could be seen in neurology clinic, he was hospitalized in October 2023 with COVID-19, at which time he was also started on levodopa, which improved his tremor. In November 2023, he went on medical leave from work due to his rapid cognitive decline. He required round-the-clock assistance from his family to complete activities of daily living. There was no history of REM behavior disorder or hallucinations.

title: Direct and Indirect Links Between Peer Relationships, Father Involvement and Self-Harm Among Rural Chinese Adolescents.
abstract: Objectives: Epidemiological surveys in rural China have reported comparatively high adolescent self-harm rates. Evidence on how peer relationships and father involvement jointly relate to this risk and on whether depression or anxiety helps to explain those links is more limited. This study investigated peer relationships and father involvement as two potential protective correlates of self-harm and assessed whether associations with self-harm were linked via depression and anxiety in a cross-sectional model. Methods: This study analysed publicly available data from the China Rural Children Mental Health Database. Data were collected in 16 rural primary schools across seven provinces. A sample of 588 adolescents aged 12-16 years with complete key variables was included. Structural equation modelling examined indirect associations between peer relationships, father involvement and self-harm through depression and anxiety. Results: Depression was positively and significantly associated with self-harm (β = 0.37, p < 0.001), while anxiety demonstrated only a marginally significant association with self-harm (β = 0.12, p = 0.06). Both peer relationships and father involvement were significantly associated with lower depression levels. The total associations for peer relationships (-0.23) exceeded those for father involvement (-0.16). The indirect associations of both variables with self-harm were linked primarily via depression. Conclusions: In this cross-sectional model, depression was the main pathway linking peer relationships and father involvement with self-harm, and the association for peer relationships was stronger than that for father involvement. Our results can guide assessment, prevention and intervention among adolescents in rural Chinese schools, including peer support and screening for depressive symptoms.
