title: Association between Trust and Patient-Reported Outcomes and Experience in Prostate Cancer Patients.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between patient-physician trust, treatment choice, patient-reported outcomes, and patient-reported experiences among patients with localized prostate cancer.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of data from a multicenter randomized controlled trial among patients with localized prostate cancer. Trust was measured at baseline, prior to treatment, using the Patient Trust-Wake Forest Physician Trust Scale (PTWF). Outcomes were assessed at baseline and at 3, 6, 12, and 24 mo. Treatments were robotic-assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy, radiation therapy, and active surveillance. The primary treatment outcome was receipt of active treatment (surgery or radiation therapy) versus active surveillance. Multivariable logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were adjusted for age, race/ethnicity, marital status, education, employment, insurance, prostate cancer risk group, intervention assignment, and study site. Sensitivity analyses modeling trust as a continuous variable yielded findings that were materially consistent with the primary analyses.
RESULTS: The high-trust group had higher odds of receiving active treatment than the low-trust group did (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 1.80, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.14-2.87; P = 0.013). Higher baseline trust was also consistently associated with better physical and mental health-related quality of life and higher satisfaction with care and treatment decision making across follow-up assessments through 24 mo. Sensitivity analyses using trust as a continuous measure produced similar findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher patient-physician trust was independently associated with treatment choice, patient-reported outcomes, and patient-reported experience. These findings underscore the importance of patient-physician trust as a component of patient-centered cancer care and shared decision making. Future studies should evaluate interventions designed to strengthen trust and improve patient-centered outcomes across diverse clinical settings.

title: Comprehensive or Wasteful? Clinical AI and the Up-front Workup
abstract: AbstractClinical AI is being adopted faster than it is being evaluated, on the promise that it will improve health and reduce waste. Aran and colleagues show that large language models recommend more up-front testing, referrals, and treatment than the physicians who actually saw the patients and at more than three times cost, at least in the short-term. But practicing differently is not the same as practicing worse: whether this reflects wasteful excess or appropriate thoroughness is unknown, as are the consequences for long-run health and spending. On one hand, more up-front care could reduce diagnostic errors, catch disease earlier, deliver guideline-concordant treatment that clinicians overlook, and avert costly late-stage care. On the other hand, it could surface incidental findings that spark anxiety and follow-up cascades, add treatments of marginal benefit, and raise spending through added visits and more intensive billing and diagnosis coding. Neither vignettes nor single-visit studies can settle this. Clinical AI deserves the standard we would demand of any new therapy: trials that randomize practices to these tools and measure long-run effects on patients' health and spending.

title: Impact of a dietary and exercise intervention on health-related quality of life of prostate cancer patients on active surveillance with overweight/obesity: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Quality of life (QOL) is important for men on active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer (PCa). To improve QOL, interventions such as those focused on diet and exercise have been proposed. However, their effectiveness remains unclear, especially in individuals with overweight/obesity.
METHODS: We previously conducted and published a randomized controlled trial of a lifestyle intervention for PCa patients on AS with overweight/obesity. Men were randomized to as follows: (1) 6-month diet and exercise intervention with a 7% weight loss goal vs (2) provided US Dietary and Physical Activity Guidelines. Herein, we report the secondary QOL findings from the trial. QOL was assessed at baseline and conclusion of the intervention via four validated questionnaires. Linear regression and two-sided t-tests evaluated mean differences. Subset analyses of the questionnaires were performed using cut-points correlating with clinical assessments.
RESULTS: Between 2016 and 2020, 100 men completed the trial. The intervention group had a mean weight loss of 7.1% vs 1.8% in controls. Despite this, no significant difference was observed between groups in general QOL (EQ-5D-5L), urinary QOL (IPSS), PCa-related QOL (EPIC-26), or PCa specific anxiety (MAX-PC). However, exploratory subgroup analyses demonstrated that participants with poor "bowel function," low "sexual bother," and good "sexual function" had clinically significant improvements of 12 (95% CI 0.1-24.0), 22 (95% CI 4.2-39.0), and 19 points (95% CI 4.4-34.0) on the EPIC-26.
CONCLUSION: In this secondary analysis of a previously published randomized trial, a 6-month diet and exercise intervention did not improve overall QOL among men with overweight/obesity on AS for PCa. While diet and exercise interventions may not universally improve QOL in this population, they remain important for broader health benefits and may offer targeted value for certain patients.

title: Glyceryl tribenzoate, a flavoring agent, stimulates hippocampal plasticity and protects memory via PPARα.
abstract: Glyceryl tribenzoate (GTB) or tribenzoin is a flavoring agent with characteristic anti-microbial property. We have already delineated GTB's immunomodulatory role via the enrichment of regulatory T cells in mouse models of multiple sclerosis and anti-neuroinflammatory role via the reduction of glial activation in a monkey model of Parkinson's disease and a mouse model of Huntington's disease. However, its role has never been explored in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common neurodegenerative disorder in human. This study underlines the importance of GTB in promoting the growth and function of hippocampal neurons via upregulation of plasticity-associated genes, enrichment of dendritic spines and stimulation of inotropic calcium influx. Accordingly, oral GTB improved hippocampal plasticity and protected memory and learning in 5xFAD mice. Similarly, GTB treatment also reduced cerebral plaque load and increased the life span of aged 5xFAD mice. Interestingly, we observed that peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα), a nuclear hormone receptor, served as a receptor of GTB. Consequently, GTB was shown to improve hippocampal plasticity and increase cognitive functions in 5xFAD, but not 5xFAD/Ppara-null, mice, indicating an important role of PPARα in GTB-mediated neuroprotection. These results suggest that oral GTB may have therapeutic importance for improving hippocampal functions in AD patients.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Clinical Decision Support for Postoperative Delirium Prevention: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium affects up to 50% of older adults with cognitive impairment, yet preoperative identification of at-risk patients remains limited. Artificial intelligence methods, such as natural language processing, can extract cognitive impairment signals from electronic health records and enable targeted clinical decision support interventions to promote adherence to perioperative best practices and reduce postoperative delirium. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of an artificial intelligence-driven non-interruptive clinical decision support intervention in reducing postoperative delirium by promoting adherence to best practices among anesthesia teams caring for surgical patients with cognitive impairment.
METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic randomized controlled trial embedded within routine clinical care at The Mount Sinai Hospital in New York City from June 20, 2023, to August 31, 2024, including patients with preoperative cognitive impairment identified immediately before surgery using a validated natural language processing algorithm, Mini-Mental State Examination scores, or diagnostic codes. Patients were randomized to an artificial intelligence-driven non-interruptive clinical decision support intervention within the electronic health record to promote adherence to best practices among anesthesia teams or routine perioperative care. The primary outcome was postoperative delirium, assessed with the 4 A's Test within seven days postoperatively. Secondary outcomes were adherence to 12 perioperative best practices. We used chi-square tests for primary and secondary outcome analyses.
RESULTS: Overall, 7294 patients were identified as having cognitive impairment immediately before surgery and were randomized to the intervention (n = 3624) or control (n = 3670) group. In total, 1255/7294 (17.2%) patients had documented postoperative delirium assessments, of whom 426/1255 (34%) developed this condition. Between intervention and control groups, there were no statistically significant differences in POD incidence (225/641, 35.1% vs 201/614, 32.7%, P = .37) or best practice adherence (all P > .05).
CONCLUSIONS: In this pragmatic randomized controlled trial, less than 20% of the sample had documented delirium assessments due to variability in routine POD screening practices, limiting our ability to conclude that artificial intelligence-driven clinical decision support was not effective in preventing postoperative delirium. However, based on our secondary outcome analyses, the intervention did not significantly change best practice adherence. Further work is needed to determine the best way to use these tools effectively.

title: Pilot Study of Cannabis Use Reduction and Associated Functional Outcomes.
abstract:
AIMS: Interventions for cannabis use disorder often reduce the frequency and quantity of use, but rarely achieve sustained abstinence. It remains unclear whether reductions in use (rather than sustained abstinence) result in meaningful improvements in functioning. This study evaluated whether cannabis reductions among individuals with heavy use were associated with improvements in functional outcomes.
DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial with ecological momentary assessment (EMA) and repeated daily biological verification of cannabis use.
METHODS: Fifty-nine individuals were randomized to a mobile contingency management (mCM) intervention or a yoked control condition. Participants completed 2 weeks of EMA during a baseline ad lib cannabis use period, followed by a 6-week reduction period. Participants completed EMA assessments multiple times per day and were prompted to complete videotaped saliva cannabis testing 2-3 times daily.
RESULTS: Group × time interactions indicated that participants randomly assigned to the mCM condition demonstrated significant functional improvements in drugged driving and working memory. The results for positive and negative affect and pain were less clear, and there was no detected change in physical activity.
CONCLUSION: These results suggest that among individuals with heavy cannabis use, significantly reducing, but not abstaining from, cannabis was associated with decreased drugged driving and improved working memory; however, more research is needed, as the relatively short duration of the study may have limited our ability to detect longer-term functional changes. This study is among the first to demonstrate that significant reductions in cannabis use can result in significant short-term improvements in drugged driving and working memory.

title: Novel [67Cu]Cu-Labeled 4- p -(Tolyl)butyric Acid-Conjugated Lactam-Cyclized Alpha-Melanocyte-Stimulating Hormone Peptides with Glycine and Polyethylene Glycol Linkers for Melanoma Targeting
abstract: This study managed to examine how the 4-p-(tolyl)butyric acid (p-TBA) albumin binder and the aspartic acid linker affect the tumor targeting and biodistribution properties of [67Cu]Cu-labeled p-TBA-conjugated alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) peptides. p-TBA was attached to 1,4,7-triazacyclononane-1,4,7-triacetic acid (NOTA)-Lys-Gly-Gly-Nle-c[Asp-His-DPhe-Arg-Trp-Lys]-CONH2 (NOTA-Lys-GGNle-CycMSHhex) and NOTA-Lys-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex with or without the Asp linker to generate NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-GGNle-CycMSHhex and NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex. The melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) binding affinities of the designed peptides were determined on B16/F10 melanoma cells. The biodistribution properties of [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-GGNle-CycMSHhex and [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex were evaluated on B16/F10 melanoma-bearing C57BL/6 mice at 2 h post-injection to select a lead peptide. Then, the melanoma targeting and imaging properties of [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex were determined on B16/F10 melanoma-bearing C57BL/6 mice. The IC50 values of NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-GGNle-CycMSHhex and NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex were 0.26 ± 0.04, 0.54 ± 0.03, 0.46 ± 0.08, and 0.32 ± 0.04 nM, respectively. [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex was selected as a lead peptide due to its highest tumor/kidney and tumor/liver uptake ratios among the [67Cu]Cu-peptides at 2 h post-injection. The B16/F10 melanoma uptake of [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex was 29.31 ± 3.22, 39.05 ± 1.38, 25.07 ± 2.03, and 11.77 ± 1.61% ID/g at 0.5, 2, 4, and 24 h post-injection, respectively. The B16/F10 melanoma lesions were clearly visualized by SPECT/CT using [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex as an imaging probe at 2 h post-injection. The utilization of p-TBA as an albumin binder prolonged the blood circulation and enhanced the tumor uptake of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG as compared to [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex without an albumin-binding moiety. The Asp linker expedited the blood clearance of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG as compared to [67Cu]Cu-p-TBA-PEG. The combination of p-TBA, Asp, and PEG linkers resulted in the highest tumor/blood, tumor/kidney, and tumor/liver uptake ratios of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG among the designed [67Cu]Cu-labeled p-TBA-conjugated CycMSHhex peptides. The favorable tumor targeting and blood clearance properties of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG underscore its potential for future melanoma therapy.

title: Abstract 14715: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonism in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Target Trial Emulation; PRAISE-HFmrEF
abstract: Introduction: While Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) improve outcomes in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), their safety and efficacy in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) has not been established. The increased cyclic AMP signaling effect of GLP-1RA is a possible safety concern in patients with HFrEF, with prior trials suggesting potential increased risk for HF hospitalization (HFH). Given the closer biological alignment of HFmrEF with HFrEF than HFpEF, evaluating the safety of GLP-1RAs in this group is critical. Research Questions: Among patients with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and overtly symptomatic HFmrEF, are GLP-1RA associated with differences in HFH or all-cause mortality? Methods: PRAISE-HFmrEF is a nationwide multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals. Using centralized electronic health records (2000-2022), we identified patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m 2 ), and HFmrEF (LVEF 40-49%) using a validated algorithm. Patients were required to have loop diuretic prescriptions or elevated natriuretic peptides ( Figure 1 ). Using a target trial emulation framework with an active-comparator, new-user design, GLP-1RA initiators were compared to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor or sulfonylurea (DPP4i/SU) initiators between 2015-2021. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on the propensity score balanced 31 covariates including demographics, comorbidities, HF severity indices, and baseline pharmacotherapy. The primary outcome was time to composite of HFH or all-cause mortality, assessed using doubly robust IPTW-Cox models. HFH was additionally evaluated using Fine-Grey competing risk models. Results: A total of 2,262 patients met the inclusion criteria (GLP-1RA: n=957; DPP4i/SU: n=1,305) ( Figure 1 ). Mean age was 68.7 ± 8.4 years, median BMI 36.6 kg/m 2 [IQR 33.5-41.4], 97.6% were male. After IPTW, all 31 covariates were well balanced (absolute standardized mean differences <10%) ( Figure 2 ). Over a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 1131 patients (50.5%) experienced the primary outcome. Crude incidence rates were 16.7 and 15.0 events per 100 person-years in the GLP-1RA and DPP4i/SU groups respectively. After adjustment, GLP-1RA was not associated with an increased risk of the primary outcome (IPTW HR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.73-1.05; p=0.16) ( Figure 3A ). Competing risk analysis showed no differences in HFH (subdistribution HR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.76-1.32). There was no heterogeneity across all tested subgroups ( Figure 3B ). Conclusions: In this nationwide cohort with obesity, diabetes, and rigorously phenotyped HFmrEF, GLP-1RA at diabetes management doses appear to be safe without evidence of adverse HF outcomes. However, the efficacy and safety at weight loses doses warrants further randomized evidence.

title: Tirzepatide Versus Semaglutide in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction and Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation Study
abstract: OBJECTIVE To evaluate the comparative effectiveness of semaglutide and tirzepatide in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS This target trial emulation study included adults with HFpEF and T2D who were initiating once-weekly tirzepatide or semaglutide (June 2022 to June 2025). The data were from two U.S.-based commercial claims databases. The coprimary outcomes were heart failure (HF) hospitalization and all-cause mortality. Between-group characteristics were balanced through propensity score–based fine stratification. Adjusted incidence rates (IRs) per 1,000 person-years and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated. RESULTS After fine stratification weighting, the final cohort consisted of 37,183 patients (age, mean ± SD, 67 ± 10 years; 54% women) with HFpEF and T2D newly initiating either tirzepatide (n = 11,780) or semaglutide (n = 25,387). Over a median follow-up of 5.1 months, tirzepatide initiators experienced a lower rate of HF hospitalization when compared with semaglutide initiators (IR 19.7 vs. 25.5, respectively; HR 0.80 [95% CI 0.66–0.96]). No evidence of heterogeneity was observed across key subgroups defined by age, sex, BMI, and baseline use of medications for HF or other cardiovascular conditions. Rates of all-cause mortality between the exposure groups were similar (IR 20.5 vs. 19.5, respectively; HR 0.99 [95% CI 0.81–1.21]). Sensitivity analyses mimicking on-treatment and intention-to-treat approaches revealed similar findings for both coprimary outcomes. CONCLUSIONS Tirzepatide was associated with a lower rate of HF hospitalization but not all-cause mortality when compared with semaglutide in adults with HFpEF and T2D in routine care. These findings may inform treatment selection for individuals with HFpEF and T2D.

title: Patient-reported and caregiver-reported outcomes in refractory ascites secondary to cirrhosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Refractory ascites (RA) secondary to advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) results in poor health-related quality of life (HRQL), high symptom burden, and caregiver workload. Patient/caregiver-reported outcomes (PROs) remain uncharacterized in this cohort. This review summarises the available evidence on this topic. METHODS: MEDLINE/Embase/Cochrane/PsycINFO/Web of Science/CINAHL were searched for articles that included PROs in RA secondary to ACLD. A structured narrative synthesis and a meta-analysis were undertaken. RESULTS: Sixteen articles were included, comprising 1040 patients and 47 caregivers. Fourteen PRO measures were used, most commonly the Short Form-36 (SF-36) and the Chronic Liver Disease Questionnaire (CLDQ). Domain scores were pooled from 4 SF-36 and 3 CLDQ studies. Pooled domain scores were lower than those reported in stable outpatients with cirrhosis in 3/8 SF-36 domains: Social functioning (mean difference -18.8 [95% CI: -30.2 to -7.3]), Mental health (-17.9 [-33.5 to -2.3]), and Physical functioning (-13.6 [-24.5 to -2.7]); and 4/6 CLDQ domains: Abdominal symptoms (-1.5 [-2.3 to -0.7]), Activity (-0.9 [-1.4 to -0.5]), Worry (-1.2 [-2.1 to -0.3]), and Emotional function (-0.7 [-1.3 to -0.1]). Disease-specific tools had broader domain coverage and were more sensitive at picking up impairments in HRQL compared with generic ones. One symptom tool (the Ascites Questionnaire) had been validated in RA. The Short-Form Liver Disease Quality of Life questionnaire (SFLDQoL), the only HRQL measure validated in decompensated ACLD, was used once. Only 2 studies assessed informal caregivers. CONCLUSIONS: RA in ACLD detrimentally impacts HRQL across multiple domains. However, the lack of validated tools remains a barrier to assessing PROs and conducting well-designed RCTs in this cohort. This review highlights potential domains for the future development of such tools, which could drive equitable, patient-centered care in ACLD.

title: A randomized controlled trial of an intravenous SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibitor PF-07304814 for hospitalized COVID-19 patients
abstract: Abstract Background Antiviral treatment options for hospitalized COVID-19 patients are limited. Methods We conducted a phase 2/3, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial of PF-07304814, an intravenous SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibitor. From September-December 2021, adults hospitalized for COVID-19 were randomized to continuous intravenous infusion of PF-07304814 (250 mg/24 hours) or placebo for 120-hours (or hospital discharge). The primary outcome was time to sustained recovery through day 90. The primary safety outcome through day 28 was a composite of death, serious adverse events, organ failure, thromboembolic events (pre-specified as events of special interest), serious infections, and grade 3/4 adverse events. Results We randomized 58 participants (32 PF-07304814; 26 placebo). After three participants experienced serious adverse events (SAEs), two related to thromboembolic events and one to acute abdominal pain, the trial was put on hold by regulators and thereafter administratively closed. The composite safety outcome through day 28 occurred in 17/32 (53%) participants assigned PF-07304814 and 11/26 (42%) participants assigned placebo (hazard ratio (HR) 1.20, 95% CI 0.56–2.57; p = 0.64). The estimated cumulative incidence of sustained recovery at day 90 was 75% for PF-07304814 and 50% for placebo participants (sHR 1.41; 95% CI: 0.71–2.80). In the PF-07304814 arm, 4 (12.5%) experienced a thromboembolic event; all died by day 90. In the placebo arm, 2 (7.7%) experienced a thromboembolic event (HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.27–7.95); both survived to the end of follow-up. Conclusion The risk/benefit of PF-07304814 could not be established due to early termination of enrollment. Rates of thromboembolic events with PF-07304814 were not statistically different than placebo. Trial Registration TICO ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04501978, Registration date: August 6, 2020. Keypoints The safety and efficacy of an intravenous SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibitor PF-07304814 could not be established in this randomized controlled trial of 58 participants. These results provide preliminary data for testing other protease inhibitors and antiviral medications in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

title: Histotripsy therapy elicits distinct anti-tumor immune responses unique from radiotherapy
abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) is a non-invasive approach that uses high-dose radiation to damage tumor cell DNA, leading to cell death. Histotripsy (HT) is the first non-invasive, non-thermal therapy that uses ultrasound pulses to destroy tumor tissue. It is unknown how RT and HT may differentially modulate the tumor immune microenvironment to enable tumor control. Therefore, we directly compared the immune responses following RT and HT in a murine model of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. While both RT and HT treatments induced local tumor control, single-cell RNA sequencing of CD45 + tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes revealed that RT and HT induce distinct immune responses. Within the myeloid compartment, only RT promoted a type I IFN response, while both RT and HT induced a TNF response. Within the T cell compartment, RT promoted the proliferation and type I IFN response of CD8 + T cells, while HT promoted expansion of immunosuppressed CD8 + and CD4 + T cells. Combination of RT or HT with anti-PD-L1 therapy enhanced local tumor control and delayed abscopal tumor growth through distinct mechanisms. Addition of anti-PD-L1 during HT treatment enhanced myeloid antigen presentation and TNF response pathway in myeloid, CD4 + , and CD8 + T cells compared to RT + anti-PD-L1. Furthermore, while RT + anti-PD-L1 promoted the expansion of proliferative CD8 + T cells, HT + anti-PD-L1 promoted the expansion of central memory and early effector CD8 + T cells with an enhanced T cell activation signature. Therefore, this study shows that combination of HT with anti-PD-L1 enhances anti-tumor immune mechanisms unique from RT.

title: Demonstrating the False-Positive Paradox in Radiology with Artificial Intelligence: Estimating Clinically Anticipated PPV, FDR, NPV, and FOR of FDA-Cleared Devices Using Performance Metrics from 510(k) Summaries and Prevalences from Local and Published Data.
abstract: The false-positive paradox (FPP) describes the counterintuitive phenomenon whereby a test can achieve high sensitivity and specificity yet still produce mostly false-positive results when applied to low-prevalence populations. This phenomenon is particularly relevant to radiology artificial intelligence (AI), where devices are typically marketed and cleared using diagnostic accuracy metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). However, these metrics do not indicate the proportion of false-positive and false-negative outputs clinicians should expect in local practice. This study estimated the positive predictive value (PPV), false discovery rate (FDR), negative predictive value (NPV), and false omission rate (FOR) for recent Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared radiology AI devices by combining publicly reported 510(k) sensitivity and specificity with local or literature-derived prevalence estimates. Public FDA summaries for 38 radiology AI devices authorized in 2024 or 2025 were reviewed, yielding 57 target pathology entries. Median reported sensitivity, specificity, and ROC-AUC exceeded 90%; nevertheless, clinically anticipated FDRs were often high. For example, a large vessel occlusion detector with 90.6% sensitivity and 88.8% specificity was estimated to have a PPV of 29.3% and an FDR of 70.7% at a prevalence of 4.87%, meaning most positive AI alerts would be false positives. These findings do not evaluate device performance but instead illustrate the FPP in radiology AI. Public 510(k) summaries should consistently report sensitivity, specificity, and test set prevalence so that radiologists and other stakeholders can estimate PPV, FDR, NPV, and FOR for their own patient populations before implementation.

title: Effectiveness of the 2025-2026 Covid-19 vaccine against Covid-19-associated emergency department visits and hospitalizations among U.S. veterans: An observational study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 continues to cause clinically important morbidity, but Covid-19 vaccine effectiveness can vary across seasons as circulating variants, vaccine antigen composition, population immunity, and immunization policy change. During 2025-2026, peak Covid-19 hospitalization rates were lower than in the preceding season, making the absolute benefit of vaccination especially important for clinical and policy decisions. We estimated the effectiveness of the 2025-2026 Covid-19 vaccine against Covid-19-associated emergency department visits and hospitalizations among US veterans.
METHODS: We emulated a target trial using electronic health records from the US Department of Veterans Affairs. Adults aged 18 years or older who received a 2025-2026 seasonal influenza vaccine between Sept 21, 2025, and Jan 31, 2026, were eligible. Same-day coadministration of the 2025-2026 Covid-19 and influenza vaccines was compared with influenza vaccination alone; recipients of influenza vaccine alone were censored if they subsequently received a 2025-2026 Covid-19 vaccine. Outcomes were Covid-19-associated emergency department visit, Covid-19-associated hospitalization, and their composite. Per-protocol vaccine effectiveness and risk differences per 10,000 persons at 180 days were estimated with inverse-probability-of-treatment-weighted and inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted discrete-time survival models.
FINDINGS: Among 931,943 participants, 114,911 received same-day Covid-19 and influenza vaccines and 817,032 received influenza vaccine alone. Over 180 days, Covid-19 vaccination was associated with lower risks of Covid-19-associated emergency department visits (vaccine effectiveness 31.72%, 95% CI 17.58 to 43.03; risk difference - 7.04 per 10,000 persons, 95% CI -10.34 to -3.63), Covid-19-associated hospitalizations (vaccine effectiveness 43.57%, 95% CI 16.12 to 62.10; risk difference - 2.63 per 10,000 persons, 95% CI -4.52 to -0.83), and the composite outcome (vaccine effectiveness 32.72%, 95% CI 18.94 to 43.82; risk difference - 7.41 per 10,000 persons, 95% CI -10.75 to -3.99).
INTERPRETATION: In this national cohort of US veterans presenting for seasonal influenza vaccination, receipt of the 2025-2026 Covid-19 vaccine was associated with lower risks of Covid-19-associated emergency department visits and hospitalizations. Absolute risk reductions were modest, but they quantify the benefit of vaccination in a lower-incidence season and can inform shared clinical decision making and seasonal vaccine policy.

title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND
abstract: Importance: It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy. Objective: To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease. Design, Setting, and Participants: In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle. Intervention: ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy. Main Outcomes and Measures: All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time. Results: Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]). Conclusions and Relevance: In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management. title: Effect of Electronic Behavioral Nudges on Low-Value Preoperative Testing
abstract: Importance: Robust randomized trials have demonstrated that routine testing before cataract surgery does not improve outcomes; however, despite this evidence and long-standing professional society recommendations discouraging routine testing, preoperative testing remains frequent in real-world practice, with most patients undergoing cataract surgery receiving at least 1 preoperative test. Objective: To measure whether electronic health record (EHR)-embedded, behavioral science-informed nudges reduce preoperative testing. Design, Setting, and Participants: This pragmatic randomized clinical trial was conducted at a large academic health system (UCLA Health) in Los Angeles, California. Physicians performing preoperative evaluations were randomized to 1 of 3 EHR nudge alerts or usual care. All encounters with patients undergoing a preoperative visit with a randomized physician within 30 days of cataract surgery were silently enrolled. Patients were enrolled from June 24, 2021, to April 11, 2023. Data were analyzed from June 2020 (1 year prior to first enrollment) to April 2024 (1 year after last enrollment). Interventions: The EHR interruptive alerts cited professional society recommendations against routine testing; each emphasized a different potential patient harm, including lack of safety benefit, financial burden, or psychological stress. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was the change in the proportion of preoperative cataract surgery encounters with any signed testing order(s) between the 12-month period before the physicians' first encounter (enrollment) and the 12-month postencounter period. Secondary outcomes included order cancellation rates among clinicians exposed to the intervention, separate comparisons of each nudge, and analyses comparing orders for specific categories of tests. Results: During the enrollment period, 229 of 776 randomized physicians had 1 or more eligible encounter during which a patient was enrolled. Together, these clinicians had 1045 preoperative encounters during the intervention period with 967 unique patients. Mean (SD) patient age was 72.1 (9.1) years, and 595 encounters (56.9%) were with female patients. Mean (SD) signed preoperative testing rates decreased from 83% (29%) to 79% (31%) in the combined intervention arms vs 84% (30%) to 82% (31%) in the control arm. In mixed-effects models, exposure to any nudge was not associated with a reduction in overall testing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.68; 95% CI, 0.34-1.34). In prespecified secondary analyses, 16% of orders were cancelled following exposure to a nudge, and the psychological stress nudge was associated with decreases in rates of complete blood cell count (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.75; P = .01) and electrocardiogram orders (aOR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.21-0.83; P = .01) vs control. Conclusions and Relevance: This randomized clinical trial of EHR nudges did not reach statistical significance on the primary outcome of overall preoperative testing. Secondary outcomes suggest future studies might consider the role of a psychological stress nudge in combination with other behavioral, workflow, and/or payment changes. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04104256.

title: Global, regional, and national burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gallbladder and biliary diseases-including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, and other non-malignant biliary tract disorders-are important contributors to the global digestive disease burden, but a global, comprehensive, and systematic estimation of their burden is absent. We aimed to quantify long-term trends and current patterns in prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with gallbladder and biliary diseases across geographies, sexes, and ages.
METHODS: We used estimates from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 to assess the burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Mortality was modelled with the Cause of Death Ensemble model and prevalence with the Disease Modelling Meta-Regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Years of life lost (YLLs) were calculated as the number of deaths for each age-sex-location-year multiplied by the standard life expectancy at each age. Severity-specific prevalence values were multiplied by their respective disability weights (with asymptomatic cases assigned zero disability) to estimate years lived with disability (YLDs). Disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were computed by summing YLDs and YLLs. We report prevalence, mortality, YLDs, YLLs, and DALYs as counts and age-standardised and age-specific rates per 100 000 population with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), stratified by sex, GBD region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI).
FINDINGS: In 1990 and 2023, the global counts for prevalence attributable to gallbladder and biliary diseases were 157·4 million (95% UI 134·0 to 183·3) and 264·4 million (226·0 to 309·9), for deaths were 65 800 (95% UI 53 000 to 78 800) and 146 700 (121 800 to 171 300), and for DALYs were 4·8 million (95% UI 3·5 to 6·2) and 8·2 million (6·3 to 10·6), representing substantial increases. However, age-standardised rates declined over the same period, from 3573·2 (95% UI 3045·5 to 4159·1) per 100 000 population to 2990·1 (2561·5 to 3492·5) per 100 000 population for prevalence, from 1·95 (1·58 to 2·31) per 100 000 population to 1·67 (1·39 to 1·95) per 100 000 population for mortality, and from 111·5 (84·1 to 143·3) per 100 000 population to 92·3 (70·9 to 119·6) per 100 000 population for DALYs. Over the past three decades, females had higher age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates than males, while sex differences in mortality rates were smaller. In 2023, age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates were lowest in south Asia and highest in central and western Europe, central Asia, and many regions in Latin America. By contrast, several regions in sub-Saharan Africa had relatively low prevalence and DALY rates but comparatively high mortality rates. National patterns broadly mirrored these regional profiles. In 2023, prevalence and DALY counts peaked in middle to early-older adulthood (ages 55-69 years), but age-specific rates continued to rise into the oldest age groups, with DALYs dominated by YLDs in midlife and early-older adulthood and by YLLs at older ages (≥80 years). The number of deaths peaked in the ninth decade of life, but age-specific rates also peaked in the oldest age groups. Across GBD regions, the association between SDI and age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates generally followed a reversed U-shaped pattern, with the lowest rates at low SDI, peak rates at intermediate SDI, and declining rates at the highest SDI levels. The association between SDI and mortality rate was less clear.
INTERPRETATION: The global burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases is rising in absolute terms despite declining age-standardised rates, underscoring the importance of population growth and ageing. Health systems, particularly in settings with rapidly ageing populations and intermediate SDI levels, will need to expand diagnostic, elective, and emergency surgical capacity while investing in prevention of obesity and metabolic risk factors. Marked regional and national heterogeneity, as well as differences in risk factors, might reflect variance in health-system capacity and access to care, including timely diagnosis, availability of surgical services, and perioperative care. The predominance of non-fatal disability in midlife and rising mortality in older age groups indicates that integrated strategies spanning risk-factor control, early diagnosis, elective management, and robust acute care for older adults are essential to reduce both YLDs and YLLs.

title: Attitudinal and behavioral factors affecting willingness to engage in Alzheimer's disease biomarker testing
abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION Ethnoracialized individuals, for example, Black/African American (AA), American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN), and Hispanic/Latinx (H/L), are underrepresented in Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarker studies. We investigated whether and how ethnoracialized groups differ in their willingness to engage in preclinical AD biomarker studies. METHODS We administered an online questionnaire to 1825 adults (725 non‐Hispanic White, 599 AA, 352 AI/AN, and 149 H/L). We examined factors hypothesized to be associated with AD biomarker testing willingness: gender, family history of dementia, education level, attitudes toward research, attitudes toward genetic testing, and preventive and proactive health behavior engagement using structural equation modeling. RESULTS The unconstrained (configural) model demonstrated good overall fit to the data. However, the constrained model and nested chi‐square difference test indicated a lack of structural invariance, that is, relationships between the variables and testing willingness differed by group. DISCUSSION The findings provide impetus for tailoring engagement strategies based on contextual factors such as ethnoracialized group membership.

title: Single-cell transcriptome-wide association analysis reveals epithelial cell-specific genetic susceptibility to colorectal cancer
abstract: Bulk-tissue transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) have identified colorectal cancer (CRC) susceptibility genes, but cell-type-specific regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell TWAS integrating matched germline genotypes and single-cell transcriptomes from normal colorectal mucosa (381 donors) and polyps (84 donors), cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility, and GWAS from 132,261 cases and 1,752,398 controls. We identified 546 gene-cell-type associations implicating 347 candidate susceptibility genes across seven normal and nine polyp epithelial populations, including 213 previously unreported genes, with 74% exhibiting cell-type-specific associations. Integrated co-expression and ChIP-seq analyses revealed distinct TF-risk gene networks, highlighting GATA6, MAX and RAD21 in normal mucosa, and TFAP4- and CEBPB-associated networks in premalignant polyp populations. Further multi-omics analyses supported dysregulation of 233 genes (67%), while drug-target analyses identified 63 potentially druggable genes. DepMap and CRISPR-Cas9 analyses implicated 35 genes in CRC cell viability. These findings reveal cell-type-specific susceptibility mechanisms and prioritize candidate therapeutic targets for CRC prevention.

title: Acute nociceptive stimulation induces long-lasting constitutive activity of spinal μ-opioid receptors that masks pain sensitization
abstract: Acute nociceptive stimuli evoke transient pain sensitization that normally resolves after the stimulus has ceased. However, whether this apparent recovery reflects restoration of the nociceptive system to its basal state or active suppression of persistent sensitization remains unclear. Here, we show that mechanical hypersensitivity induced by acute chemical or electrical stimulation of primary afferent C-fibers was transient in wild-type mice but persisted for 1-2 weeks in mice lacking spinal μ-opioid receptors (MORs). Furthermore, intrathecal pretreatment with naloxone, naltrexone, or CTOP, all of which act as MOR inverse agonists, prevented recovery from C-fiber-induced mechanical hypersensitivity, whereas the neutral antagonist 6β-naltrexol had no effect. The naltrexone-induced reinstatement of mechanical hypersensitivity was prevented by 6β-naltrexol, consistent with induction of constitutively active spinal MORs. C-fiber stimulation also increased phosphorylation of spinal MORs, a biochemical marker of receptor activation, and this increase was abolished by naltrexone but not by 6β-naltrexol. Although mice had fully recovered behaviorally by 3, 6, and 24 hr after C-fiber stimulation, pharmacological inhibition of constitutively active MORs at each time-point consistently reinstated mechanical hypersensitivity. Together, these findings support a model in which acute nociceptive stimulation induces two parallel forms of long-term spinal plasticity: persistent pain sensitization and constitutive activation of MORs, the latter continuously masking the former to maintain an apparently resolved pain state. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized homeostatic mechanism underlying pain resolution after acute nociceptive stimulation, and the C-fiber-mediated mechanisms for inducing MOR constitutive activity may provide a clue to develop a therapeutic strategy for sustained analgesia.

title: Cannabinoid receptor type 1 availability in individuals with a history of childhood trauma: a positron emission tomography study.
abstract: Early life adversity has a lasting impact on the endocannabinoid (eCB) system based on animal models. However, the impact of early life adversity, such as childhood trauma (CT), on the eCB system has not been thoroughly studied. We assessed the availability of cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1R) in individuals with CT compared to healthy controls without CT (HCs). Cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1R) availability was compared in adults with CT (N = 22) and age- and sex-matched HCs (n = 22), using positron emission tomography (PET) imaging with the CB1R-specific radiotracer [11C]OMAR. Using linear models, the effect of the group was assessed on global and trauma-relevant brain regions (amygdala, hippocampus, and frontal cortex). Compared to HCs, lower CB1R availability was observed in CT globally (difference = -11.36%, F(1,42) = 4.35, p = 0.04), in amygdala (-13.70%, F(1,84) = 6.66, p = 0.01), and in hippocampus (-14.50%, F(1,84) = 6.59, p = 0.01), but not in frontal cortex (-8.08%, F(1,84) = 2.17, p = 0.14). There were no effects of a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), major depressive disorder (MDD), nicotine dependence, or the use of antidepressant medication. This preliminary result of lower CB1R availability in adults with CT compared with HCs suggests eCB dysregulation associated with CT. Future studies should replicate and extend this finding and examine the potential effects of various trauma features on the eCB system.

title: Long-Term Daily Chlorhexidine Foot Cleansing Reduces Staphylococcal Burden on the Feet of People with Prior Diabetic Foot Complications
abstract: Abstract Background Individuals with diabetes remain at high risk for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) even after ulcer healing. Dysbiosis of the skin microbiome has been associated with ulcer formation. Topical chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) is a broad-spectrum antiseptic commonly used to reduce microbial burden. In a prior randomized clinical trial comparing daily CHG foot treatment with soap-and-water treatment, no statistically significant reduction in new DFUs was observed, prompting evaluation of whether CHG produced durable changes in the skin microbiota. Objective To compare changes in foot skin microbiota (including bacterial bioburden, diversity, and community composition) associated with daily CHG versus soap-and-water use over one year in people with diabetes and prior foot complications. Methods In a single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial, 87 participants were randomized to daily CHG wipes or soap-and-water wipes for 12 months. Foot swabs were collected at baseline, 3 and 12 months, and 4 weeks post-treatment. Bacterial bioburden was quantified. Microbiota composition was assessed using 16S rRNA and ITS amplicon sequencing. Key Results CHG treatment significantly reduced bacterial bioburden, increased microbial diversity, and altered community composition, including sustained reductions in Staphylococcus abundance. Several microbiota changes persisted more than 4 weeks after treatment cessation. Soap-and-water treatment showed similar but smaller and largely nonsignificant trends. Conclusions Daily CHG use durably modifies foot skin microbiota in high-risk individuals with diabetes. However, this alone does not prevent new foot complications, highlighting the need for additional interventions. These findings have implications for long-term CHG use in populations at risk for staphylococcal infections.

title: Greater lifetime alcohol consumption is associated with smaller hippocampal volumes in adults with low-level alcohol intake.
abstract: For decades, low-level alcohol consumption, operationalized as no more than two standard drink equivalents/day for males and one standard drink equivalent/day for females, was indicated to carry minimal systemic health risks. However, the neurobiological correlates of low-level drinking in healthy adults are not well characterized. To date, no study has concurrently assessed the associations of lifetime low-level alcohol consumption, modeled as a continuous rather than categorical or ordinal variables, with hippocampal volumes in healthy adults. This study examined the associations between recent and lifetime alcohol consumption and magnetic resonance-derived measures of bilateral hippocampal volumes in healthy non-smoking adults (22-70 years of age) with no history of alcohol use disorder or other conditions known to affect brain structure. All participants consumed ≤ 60 standard drink equivalents/month over the 1 year preceding study and median lifetime average drinks/month were 21. Greater lifetime average drinks/month were significantly related to smaller right and average of left and right hippocampal volumes. Findings indicated that lifetime alcohol consumption considered "low risk" for adults may have implications for the integrity of the hippocampi. Increased rate of hippocampal atrophy in cognitively normal middle-aged to older adults is clinically relevant as it may serve as surrogate biomarker for future cognitive decline or progression to mild cognitive impairment. These results may have implications for current harm reduction strategies and alcohol consumption public health guidelines.

title: Tamoxifen targets Wisp2 to impair subcutaneous adipocyte progenitor self-renewal and adipogenic differentiation
abstract: Breast cancer endocrine therapy, including tamoxifen, systemically disrupts estrogen receptor signaling and increases type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk in women. Hyperplastic adipose tissue expansion, especially in subcutaneous depots, facilitates nutrient storage and attenuates inflammation during a chronic positive energy balance and is impaired in the absence of estrogen. Adipocyte progenitors are renewed through Wnt signaling pathway activation, however the the mechanisms that explain the depletion of these cells during endocrine therapy are not defined. Here we show the direct impact of tamoxifen on proliferation, renewal, and differentiation in subcutaneous adipose stromal cells from humans and adult mice. In obesity, the Wnt1 inducible signaling pathway protein 2 (Wisp2) was lost in adipocyte progenitors following endocrine therapy. Wisp2 gain and loss of function studies defined the link between estrogen signaling and adipocyte progenitor maintenance. We found that tamoxifen treatment disrupts the protection of adipocyte progenitors by estrogen, mediated through suppression of Wisp2. These studies reveal effects of tamoxifen therapy that precede and could influence T2D development in breast cancer survivors.

title: Home-based transfusions in hospice patients with hematologic malignancies: a pilot study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospice care (HC) for patients with hematologic malignancies (HM) is underutilized due to concerns about cessation of blood transfusions. Home-based transfusion (HBT) programs have proven to be safe, but little research exists for HM patients in HC. We hypothesized that HBT protocol could be safely implemented to reduce symptoms burden, lengthen life expectancy and improve quality of life in HC.
METHODS: In a non-randomized pilot study between 8/2020 and 7/2023, adult transfusion-dependent HM patients were offered weekly transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells (PRBC) and/or one unit of platelets based on symptoms criteria, not lab values. Exclusion criteria included prior transfusion reactions, extended blood typing, or residence outside 50 miles from the transfusion center. Hospice agencies provided management and support, while Our Blood Institute (OBI) provided palliative HBT. Symptom scores and complete blood counts (CBC) were collected weekly, and EORTC QLQ-C30 quality of life (QOL) questionnaire was completed before and after transfusions. The primary feasibility and safety outcomes were recruitment, ability to administer indicated transfusions, and transfusion reactions. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04454723) on 6/30/2020.
FINDINGS: We enrolled 21 patients (mean age in years = 67.1 (standard deviation (SD) = 14.4); 100% enrollment, one withdrew consent). Participants received an average of 3.4 units (SD = 3.4) of platelets or PRBCs. No transfusion reactions reported. Mean cost was $571 per week (SD = $939). The EORTC Composite Score least squares-mean difference (post-pre- transfusion) increased 0.18 (SE = 1.88) (p-value = 0.92) but not significantly. Median hospice duration was 11 days, IQR = 8-40 days, 95% CI: 9-33 days. All patients died at home, with no hospitalizations or intensive care unit (ICU) admissions.
INTERPRETATION: HBT, in the setting of hospice represents a feasible and safe option for further study to avoid costly hospitalizations and ICU admissions, with limited cost. This trial demonstrates proof of concept for an economical, patient-centered HBT protocol in HM patients receiving HC.

title: FedMann: A Manually Coordinated Federated Learning Framework Applied to Multiple Myeloma—A Feasibility Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Federated learning (FL) enables multi-institutional model development in oncology without sharing patient-level data, but automated FL infrastructures typically require dedicated servers, firewall modifications, and substantial IT support to deploy. These requirements may be prohibitive for smaller institutions or consortia with limited IT resources or stringent information security requirements. We developed FedMann, a manually coordinated FL framework, and demonstrated its feasibility by applying it to prediction of suboptimal multiple myeloma (MM) treatment across two clinical sites with substantially different patient populations. Methods: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health record data from patients newly diagnosed with MM at the Veterans Affairs (VA) Healthcare System or Boston Medical Center (BMC) between 2012 and 2022. Demographic, clinical, and geographic predictors were used to predict non-receipt of guideline-concordant primary therapy, defined as not receiving a frontline triplet or quadruplet regimen or autologous stem cell transplant when eligible. FedMann was implemented as a four-stage cycle of local training, parameter sharing through an access-controlled repository, sample-size-weighted parameter averaging at a coordinating site, and federated model redistribution. Models were evaluated on site-specific held-out test sets using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with bootstrap-resampled 95% confidence intervals. Results: VA and BMC contributed 4887 and 261 cases, respectively, with substantial demographic differences across all measured characteristics including sex distribution (96.3% male at VA vs. 58.6% at BMC; p < 0.001). The BMC-only model achieved an AUC of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.56–0.81) on the BMC test set. The federated model achieved 0.68 (95% CI, 0.55–0.80) on the BMC test set and 0.70 (95% CI, 0.67–0.72) on the VA test set. Conclusions: A manually coordinated FL framework can support multi-institutional model fitting in oncology without exchanging patient-level data and without requiring dedicated FL infrastructure. In a two-site MM application, performance was comparable between the federated model and each site’s own local model, and the VA only model showed no apparent loss of discrimination when externally validated at BMC, with no statistically significant differences in AUC on the BMC test set. Although absolute AUCs were modest, reflecting limited cohort size and a small predictor set, this application demonstrates the feasibility of the framework as an alternative when automated FL deployment is impractical.

title: Drug use equipment and skin colonization facilitate Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection and reinfection
abstract: It is unknown if Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) in people who inject drugs is a result of concomitant skin colonization or re-use of contaminated drug use equipment. Further, it remains unclear whether repeat instances of SAB among people who inject drugs are related to relapse of infections with the same S. aureus strain or reinfection by unrelated S. aureus strains. We prospectively recruited 101 patients with SAB, including 50 patients who inject drugs. We used hybrid assembly of short- and long-read whole genome sequencing (WGS) data to compare whole genome single nucleotide polymorphism (wgSNP) differences between blood culture, colonization, drug use equipment, and community syringe S. aureus isolates to assess for clonality (≤20 wgSNP). Plasmidic contigs from WGS of isolates that shared ≥ 99.9% average nucleotide identity with other plasmids were identified as instances of potential plasmid transmission. Hospitalized individuals with SAB and no reported drug use were analyzed as a comparator. Clinical data and hospitalization history were abstracted from the electronic medical record. Bloodstream isolates from people who inject drugs with two or more admissions for SAB between 2016 and 2024 with available isolates of sufficient quality ( n = 47) were sequenced and assessed for clonality. We identified that 22% of SAB isolates from people who inject drugs in the prospective colonization study were related to colonization isolates and 11% to isolates recovered from drug use equipment or discarded syringes. Network analysis revealed that potential plasmid transmission events were primarily driven by injection drug use related isolates (61.2%), MRSA status (72.6%), and sequence type (ST) group 8/1181 isolates (62.4%). Among patients hospitalized with multiple admissions for recurrent SAB, 63.8% were attributed to relapse with related isolates. SAB may result from nonsterile injection practices that facilitate infection with colonizing organisms, as well as shared fomites or common environments. These practices and factors may also contribute to local spread of S. aureus strains among people who inject drugs.

title: Cav1.3-C-terminus Restores Electrical and Contractile Functions in hiPSC-derived Cardiomyocytes Model of Heart Failure.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Heart failure (HF) is a major global health concern characterized by impaired excitation-contraction coupling and extensive structural remodeling of the myocardium, often modeled using a potent vasoactive and neurohumoral mediator, endothelin-1 (ET-1). This study investigates whether AAV6-mediated delivery of the Cav1.3-C-terminus, acting as an auto-trans-regulator of gene transcription, can restore electrophysiological and contractile functions in an ET-1-induced HF model using hiPSC-CMs.
METHODS: hiPSC-CM monolayers were treated with 10 nM ET-1 for 48 hours to induce HF-like phenotype and then co-treated with an AAV6-Cav1.3-C-terminus. We subsequently evaluated gene expression via RT-qPCR, single-cell electrophysiological properties via patch-clamp, and contractile function using custom video analysis software.
RESULTS: ET-1 treatment induced a HF-associated remodeling phenotype, characterized by significant upregulation of hypertrophic (NPPA, NPPB, and ACTA1) and extracellular matrix-associated (COL1A1) genes, along with increased cell membrane capacitance. This structural remodeling was accompanied by marked electrophysiological alterations, including downregulation of KCNH2, CACNA1D, CACNA1C, and SCN5A, reduced potassium, calcium, and sodium current densities, and prolonged action potential duration. ET-1 impaired both the spontaneous beating rate and contraction amplitude of the monolayers. Co-treatment with the Cav1.3-C-terminus successfully restored CACNA1D and KCNH2 gene expression to baseline levels, accompanied by normalized L-type calcium and potassium current densities, normalized APD prolongation, and completely restored the chronotropic and inotropic functions to control levels.
CONCLUSIONS: ET-1-treated hiPSC-CMs model effectively recapitulates the electrophysiological and contractile dysregulations of HF. Gene therapy by Cav1.3-C-terminus provides robust functional rescue myocardial contractility, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic strategy for HF.

title: Treatment patterns and healthcare utilization for patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) in the Veterans Health Administration (MCLOVA) who were prescribed their first Bruton Tyrosine Kinase inhibitor (BTKi): A national retrospective cohort study
abstract: IntroductionMantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is a rare subtype (5%) of Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL), with 5-year survival of about 50%. Bruton Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors (BTKis) may improve health outcomes for patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) MCL.Study objectiveThe objective of this study was to compare treatment patterns and healthcare utilization for patients with R/R MCL prescribed their first BTKi therapy using data from the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA).MethodsThis was a retrospective cohort study of adult patients (18 + years) prescribed BTKis for MCL in all VHA medical facilities in the United States from 1/1/20 to 12/31/23. Data were statistically analyzed using chi-square, Wilcoxon Rank-Sum test, Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves, multivariable negative binomial regression, and Cox Proportional Hazards regression, and a p-value <0.05.ResultsThere were 494 patients included. Of those included, 177 received ibrutinib, 189 received acalabrutinib, and 128 received zanubrutinib. More patients on ibrutinib switched to other BTKis (27%) compared to patients on acalabrutinib (10%, p < 0.01) or zanubrutinib (9%, p < 0.01). Median (interquartile range [IQR]) laboratory visits at 12 months were higher for ibrutinib (5, 0-12) than acalabrutinib (1, 0-8, p < 0.01) or zanubrutinib (0, 0-6, p < 0.01). Finally, overall survival (OS) was higher for patients on zanubrutinib than those on ibrutinib (p < 0.01) or acalabrutinib (p < 0.01).ConclusionsPatients prescribed acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib experienced fewer laboratory and hematology/oncology visits at 12 months than patients who received ibrutinib. Patients who received zanubrutinib experienced a survival advantage when compared to those treated with ibrutinib.

title: Gastric resection and restriction yield distinct neuroendocrine and metabolic outcomes in obese mice
abstract: Abstract Whether the metabolic benefits of sleeve gastrectomy arise from gastric restriction alone or also depend on tissue resection remains unclear. We compared sleeve gastrectomy (SG) with a surgical clip-based sleeve gastroplasty (GP) model that restricts the stomach without removing tissue. Diet-induced obese male C57BL/6J mice were randomized to SG, GP, or sham surgery and evaluated over six weeks for energy balance, glucose regulation, hepatic lipid accumulation, circulating hormones and branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), and hypothalamic neuropeptide expression. SG and GP produced comparable weight loss of 12% and 11%, respectively, without significant differences in energy expenditure. However, the procedures differed in the timing of reduced food intake, and only SG produced smaller, more frequent meals. Both procedures improved glucose handling, with greater improvement after SG. SG also selectively reduced hepatic triglyceride content and circulating BCAAs. Hypothalamic POMC expression decreased after both procedures, whereas NPY and AgRP expression decreased only after SG. SG further produced a distinct hormonal profile, including higher fasting GLP-1 and PYY, lower ghrelin, and greater glucose-stimulated increases in several gut and pancreatic hormones. Thus, comparable short-term weight loss after gastric resection and non-resection restriction was accompanied by distinct metabolic and neuroendocrine responses. These findings support a contribution of gastric resection beyond restriction alone and identify candidate gut–brain and metabolic pathways for developing less invasive interventions that reproduce the broader benefits of sleeve gastrectomy.

title: Precision Perioperative Treatment for Resectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Current Status and Perspectives
abstract: The treatment paradigm for resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) continues to evolve toward precision perioperative strategies. Despite curative-intent surgery, disease recurrence remains common. Adjuvant tyrosine kinase inhibitors have substantially improved disease-free survival and, in selected populations, overall survival, particularly for patients with sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK rearrangements. Targeted therapies for other actionable genomic alterations (AGAs), including RET fusions, remain investigational. Adequate tissue acquisition and comprehensive molecular profiling before treatment initiation are therefore essential for optimal treatment selection. For patients without sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK rearrangements, neoadjuvant or perioperative PD-(L)1 blockade combined with platinum-based chemotherapy has become a standard of care for eligible patients with resectable stage II–III NSCLC, improving pathological response, event-free survival, and, in select trials, overall survival. Multidisciplinary reassessment of resectability following neoadjuvant treatment is particularly important for borderline-resectable disease. Patients subsequently deemed unresectable require individualized management, potentially including definitive chemoradiotherapy followed by consolidation immunotherapy. Although cross-trial comparisons suggest advantages of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy over adjuvant-only immunotherapy, direct randomized comparisons are lacking. The incremental benefit of postoperative immunotherapy after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy remains uncertain for selected patients. Future priorities include optimizing treatment sequencing, improving pathological complete response rates, refining radiographic and molecular response assessment, investigating resistance mechanisms, and integrating circulating tumor DNA-based minimal residual disease detection into individualized postoperative treatment. Whether surgery can be safely omitted in exceptional responders also warrants prospective investigation. Together, these advances support a biomarker-driven, response-adapted approach to precision perioperative NSCLC management.

title: Delivery of Behavioral Insomnia Care in VA Primary Care Mental Health Integration Clinics: Sustainment Outcomes of a Hybrid Type 3 Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is a common disorder associated with significant negative health and functional consequences. Behavioral interventions, such as cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), are recommended and supported by training efforts, but access to care remains challenging for many.
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate change in the delivery of a brief behavioral treatment for insomnia (BBTI) following the withdrawal of implementation strategy support in Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Primary Care Mental Health Integration (PCMHI) clinics.
DESIGN: A pre-post analysis of the withdrawal of implementation strategy support during the sustainment phase of a stepped wedge hybrid type 3 trial.
PARTICIPANTS: Veterans in Primary Care and PCMHI clinics at four VA Medical Centers.
INTERVENTIONS: Implementation, and withdrawal, of strategies and support to improve BBTI delivery in VA PCMHI clinics.
MAIN MEASURES: Delivery of BBTI, CBT-I, and total behavioral insomnia care in PCMHI clinics and prescriptions for sleep medications in Primary Care clinics.
KEY RESULTS: Across all four study sites, from phase 3 (implementation) to phase 4 (sustainment), delivery of BBTI in PCMHI increased 12.5% among Veterans with insomnia (20.2-32.7%, OR 1.9, p < 0.001) when implementation strategy support was withdrawn. Total behavioral insomnia care (BBTI + CBT-I) also increased (25.5-37.9%, OR 1.8, p < 0.001), although CBT-I delivery was stable during this time period (p = 0.8). Prescription sleep medications in Primary Care also reduced by 0.8% (n = 2158; OR 0.9, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Across four VAMCs, BBTI training plus implementation strategy support increased the delivery of BBTI, and total behavioral insomnia care (BBTI + CBT-I), including the sustainment phase when implementation support was withdrawn. Increased access to behavioral insomnia care, notably through BBTI implementation, was also associated with decreased prescriptions of sleep medications. BBTI training and implementation support in PCMHI clinics help increase access to behavioral insomnia care and support the VA/DOD Clinical Practice Guidelines for insomnia disorder.

title: Discordance between actual care and recommendations by a reinforcement learning model for sepsis
abstract: Fluid and vasopressor management of sepsis requires a complex set of sequential treatment decisions tailored to individual responses. We examined the frequency and implications of disagreement between reinforcement-learning (RL), using the AI Clinician as a test example, and actual clinical decisions. A novel discordance score was defined as the Euclidean distance between clinical team actions and RL-recommended treatments (range 0 to 5.66), across 25 treatment options of vasopressors and intravenous (IV) fluids. Among 30,678 ICU patients with sepsis cared for across 309,415 time-epochs, discordance was more common among epochs of patients with SOFA > 6 than those with SOFA < 6, and for intravenous fluid choices than for vasopressors. After multivariable adjustment, greater discordance was associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 1.11, 95%CI: 1.05,1.18) in the SOFA strata > =6 but not for SOFA < = 4 (adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.02, 95%CI: 0.97,1.08).

title: PROSTHETIC KNEE PRESCRIPTION IN THE US DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT ANALYSIS
abstract: In U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals and clinics, amputee clinic teams work closely with Veterans to ensure they receive the best care possible. As part of this best-care approach, VA physicians and prosthetists quickly adopt technologies that have been shown to benefit users. As microprocessor-controlled prosthetic knees (MPKs) have been shown to provide a multitude of functional, cognitive, and safety benefits to those with limb loss, this study aimed to determine how frequently these and other types of prosthetic knees are prescribed to Veterans, in an environment free from restrictive reimbursement limitations. Within VA, prosthetic knees were prescribed primarily for the Medicare Functional Classification Level (K) 3 (variable cadence community ambulators), followed by K2 (household ambulators), K1 (transfer and therapeutic users), and finally K4 (high activity and bilateral) users. Mechanical knees were the most frequently prescribed due to their use for K1 and K2 users, making up 95.2% and 65.8%, respectively, and 55.9% overall. MPKs were prescribed more frequently for Veterans at the K3 and K4 levels, making up 62.1% and 60.8% respectively. Activity‑specific knees made up 3.6% of all knee prescriptions. Comparative data showed that overall, VA prescribed MPKs at a rate 69.9% higher than what is provided outside of VA and saw a higher frequency of K1 functional level patients. Veterans with above‑knee limb loss, especially those K2 and above, benefit from considerably greater prescription of MPKs. Provider education is recommended to expand this benefit and bolster Veteran access to MPKs and activity-specific devices.

title: Nationwide Survey of Antimicrobial Stewardship in Korean Hospitals: Insights From the Early Stage of the 2024 National Pilot Implementation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial stewardship programmes (ASPs) are essential for optimising antibiotic use and mitigating antimicrobial resistance. In Korea, antimicrobial consumption exceeds the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development average, and ASP activities remain fragmented, particularly in smaller hospitals. In November 2024, the National Health Insurance Service introduced a pilot reimbursement scheme to support ASPs in hospitals with ≥ 300 beds. This study aimed to provide baseline data to evaluate its impact.
METHODS: A nationwide web-based survey was conducted between January and February 2025 among 297 hospitals with ≥ 300 beds. The questionnaire was designed to allow comparison with the 2020 national survey and to assess the ASP infrastructure, resources, and practices.
RESULTS: Of 153 responding hospitals, 71 participated in the pilot programme. Participating hospitals were typically large, university-affiliated, and metropolitan-based; non-participants were smaller, non-teaching, and regional. Participating hospitals employed more infectious disease specialists (2.96 vs. 0.63) and paediatric infectious disease specialists (0.66 vs. 0.12) and allocated more full-time equivalent staff to ASP activities. Participants had stronger institutional support, including financial (46.5% vs. 1.2%) and workforce (52.1% vs. 2.4%) support. Guidelines, interventions, monitoring, and information technology-based decision support systems were more common in participating hospitals, which were all registered with the Korea National Antimicrobial Use Analysis System. Non-participating hospitals frequently lacked guidelines (62%) and interventions (48%). Both groups reported workforce shortages and insufficient incentives as major barriers.
CONCLUSION: The Korean ASP pilot programme strengthened the stewardship infrastructure in participating hospitals, even early on. However, substantial disparities with non-participating hospitals persist, underscoring the need for tailored support for resource-limited institutions.

title: Written exposure therapy augmented with transcranial direct current stimulation for posttraumatic stress disorder: A pilot randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Written exposure therapy (WET) is an evidence-based, trauma-focused psychotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) that has been tested with several trauma-exposed samples. Although many individuals who receive WET and other trauma-focused psychotherapies experience a significant reduction in PTSD symptoms, there remains room for improvement given that a meaningful proportion of individuals continue to meet the diagnostic criteria following treatment. Adjunctive interventions that can be easily combined with trauma-focused psychotherapies for PTSD may improve treatment outcomes. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a noninvasive neurostimulation intervention that has demonstrated preliminary evidence of reducing PTSD symptoms. In this study, we combined WET with tDCS to treat PTSD in a pilot randomized clinical trial. Participants (N = 25) received five WET sessions and were randomized to active or sham tDCS targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Results showed no statistically significant group differences in PTSD symptom reductions at 1-month follow-up, as assessed using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 or PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5), ps = .573-.619, and both treatment groups demonstrated significant PTSD improvements, ps < .001, at the final assessment point. However, there was a significant two-way interaction for the PCL-5, p = .010. Deconstruction of this interaction showed that WET with tDCS had an accelerated effect, with larger PTSD symptom reductions occurring earlier in treatment relative to WET with sham tDCS. The findings highlight the potential of tDCS to accelerate PTSD outcomes when combined with WET and support conducting larger randomized clinical trials.
