title: Comparative evaluation of time-to-event analysis methods for mobility limitation in older adults: A multi-cohort benchmarking study
abstract: Time-to-event models are central to aging research, quantifying both whether and when an event occurs. However, guidance on selecting among traditional statistical and machine learning (ML) methods for prediction modeling remains limited, particularly for epidemiologic aging cohorts with wide assessment intervals. Mobility limitation, as a clinically important aging outcome with such complexities, provides a relevant test case for methodological benchmarking. We conducted a systematic benchmark comparison of 14 statistical and ML time-to-event methods using harmonized data from four longitudinal U.S. aging cohorts (N = 14,821). The outcome was time to incident mobility limitation, defined by self-reported walking difficulty or gait speed < 0.8 m/s. Models were evaluated using 4-fold cross-validation repeated 100 times within cohorts. Performance metrics captured complementary dimensions of predictive quality: discrimination (C-index), accuracy and calibration (Brier score, integrated log loss, calibration index), and computational efficiency (model training time). Prespecified decision rules synthesize results across metrics to identify preferable methods. Across pooled analyses, multiple methods demonstrated comparable discrimination, including penalized Cox models, tree-based ensembles, and boosting approaches. Oblique random survival forest achieved the most favorable overall trade-off, combining high discrimination (C-index 0.673), good calibration (Brier score 0.147), and moderate training time (9.2 min). When computational efficiency was prioritized, penalized regression methods may be preferable, with good discrimination and Brier score. These findings support random forest and penalized regression as strong defaults for time-to-event prediction modeling in gerontologic research and highlight the importance of joint evaluation of discrimination, calibration, and feasibility.

title: TM6SF2 acts at ER membrane contact sites to enable RAB7-dependent endolysosomal VLDL secretion and maintain Golgi structure.
abstract: Although a loss-of-function variant of TM6SF2 is a highly penetrant risk factor for steatotic liver disease, including progression to cirrhosis and cancer, its normal function is largely unknown. Here we show that endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized TM6SF2 forms membrane contact sites (MCSs) with late endosomes/lysosomes, where it activates the small GTPase RAB7 to enable an endolysosomal route for selective secretion of lipid-rich very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) particles. In accord, TM6SF2 and RAB7 deficiency similarly cause endolysosomal VLDL retention and accumulation of enlarged late endosomes/lysosomes. TM6SF2 further binds to VAMP-associated protein (VAP) ER-anchor proteins to maintain MCSs between the ER, endosomes, and the trans-Golgi network, with TM6SF2 deficiency causing Golgi fragmentation and disruption of cGAS-STING signaling known to prevent cirrhosis and cancer by clearing senescent hepatocytes. Our findings establish TM6SF2 as an ER-MCS component that enables endolysosomal VLDL secretion and maintains Golgi structure, which suggests that TM6SF2 loss of function causes liver disease through steatosis-dependent and independent mechanisms.

title: Who is eligible for lung cancer screening, and where are they? National subpopulation estimates of people eligible for lung cancer screening.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The utilization of lung cancer screening services is less than 20%. There are a myriad of barriers at the patient, provider, and health care system levels that account for such low uptake. One reason lung cancer screening rates remain low is that identifying who is eligible is challenging at the patient and at the population level because a quantitative estimate of smoking history (i.e., 20 pack-years of cigarette smoking exposure) is required to determine eligibility. This pack-year determination is often missing from clinical documentation and is also absent in large health survey data.
METHODS: The Smoking History Generator was integrated into national cross-sectional surveys to estimate smoking exposure intensity and duration for older US adults who have smoked. National estimates, at the substate level, for the number of individuals eligible for lung cancer screening are presented.
RESULTS: A publicly available dataset that enables researchers to estimate the population eligible for lung cancer screening at the census tract level was developed. Additionally, this approach permits exploration and description of the eligible population by age, sex, racial/ethnic groups, and current or former smoking status.
CONCLUSION: The dataset can be aggregated by geographic location (e.g., county, state) and filtered by age range, sex, race/ethnicity, and smoking status to estimate specific subpopulations eligible for lung cancer screening. This dataset will greatly enhance future programmatic efforts to identify and direct resources to individuals eligible for lung cancer screening.

title: Historical Baseline Electrocardiogram Ascertainment Prior to Cancer Diagnosis and Cardiovascular Diagnosis Patterns in Cancer Survivors: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among cancer survivors. Contemporary cardio-oncology frameworks emphasize baseline cardiovascular risk assessment before potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapies. Historical real world implementation of baseline electrocardiography (ECG), however, remains incompletely characterized. The objective of this study was to characterize historical baseline ECG ascertainment before cancer diagnosis and examine its association with documented cardiovascular diagnosis patterns in cancer survivors.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 4592 adult cancer survivors within the Froedtert & Medical College of Wisconsin health system from 2000 to 2020. The analytic cohort was derived from a previously established longitudinal cancer survivor resource integrating demographic and cardiovascular clinical data, cancer treatment exposures, multimodality cardiac function ascertainment, and linked clinical, radiation oncology, and cancer registry information. Cardiac function ascertainment from an available cardiovascular imaging modality within three years before cancer diagnosis was one component of the analytic cohort definition. Patients were stratified by ascertainment of a 12-lead ECG within the same pre-diagnostic interval. Cardiovascular diagnoses documented before and after cancer diagnosis were characterized separately. For the newly documented diagnosis analyses, each cardiovascular outcome was evaluated among participants without a prior diagnosis of that same condition before cancer diagnosis. A multivariable logistic regression model evaluated the association between baseline ECG ascertainment and newly documented overall CVD diagnosis (including HF, AFIB, CAD, and stroke) while adjusting for age, sex, race, comorbidity count, and treatment count.
RESULTS: Among 4592 individuals, 3726 (81%) had a baseline ECG. ECG ascertainment was associated with older age and greater pre-existing cardiovascular and cardiometabolic burden. The available follow up distributions were similar between patients without and with baseline ECG ascertainment (748 [Q1 258, Q3 1781] vs. 767 [Q1 219, Q3 1822] days; p > 0.9). In multivariable analysis, baseline ECG ascertainment was associated with lower odds of a newly documented overall CVD diagnosis (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.31-0.46); this odds ratio represents an association rather than a time-specific risk or protective effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline ECGs were commonly ascertainable within this longitudinal cancer survivor cohort and identified groups with different pre-existing cardiovascular burden and subsequent cardiovascular diagnosis patterns. These findings provide a historical benchmark for cardiovascular assessment in cancer care and support prospective patient-level studies integrating ECG findings with clinical and oncologic risk factors to refine cardiovascular surveillance strategies across cancer survivorship.

title: "Once they learn here…they can work pretty much anywhere": Perspectives on clinical education in rural veterans affairs hospitals.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: One of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)'s greatest contributions to US Healthcare is its commitment to education. Rural VAs are tasked with increasing the number of health professions trainees they teach, but little is known about the current experience of teaching in rural VA hospitals.
OBJECTIVES: This evaluation explores the experiences of rural VA hospitalists and identifies and describes barriers and facilitators to engagement in clinical teaching.
METHODS: Using qualitative descriptive evaluation, we conducted six focus groups and one interview with hospitalists and others invested in the VA educational mission (n = 27) across six hospitalist divisions at rural VAs (VA systems caring for a population that is approximately 50% rural or greater). Focus group and interview questions were developed based on literature, a hospitalist needs assessment, and clinical experience. We used rapid qualitative analysis to report findings on the domains of VA Educational Mission-Rural Perspective, VA Rural Medicine, Rural VA Work/Life Balance, and Burnout among rural VA hospitalists.
RESULTS: VA educational mission contributed to rural hospitalists' decisions to work at VA, yet how teaching impacted burnout and work/life balance varied. Rurality impacted topics taught and trainee recruitment. Rural VA teaching barriers included administrative challenges, generational differences, and lack of specialty resources. Facilitators included professional growth, amplified personal and institutional impact, and serving rural Veterans.
CONCLUSIONS: This evaluation identified several actionable areas to target in faculty development programs that can support rural hospitalists, including how to leverage the additive curriculum of rural medicine as an asset.

title: Body Mass Index, Valsartan, and Myocardial Remodeling in Early-Stage Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Secondary Analysis of the Randomized VANISH Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is associated with adverse outcomes in overt hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but the prevalence and impact of elevated body mass index (BMI) in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is uncertain.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the randomized VANISH (Valsartan for Attenuating Disease Evolution in Early Sarcomeric Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy) trial, participants were categorized according to baseline BMI (nonelevated or elevated [≥85th percentile if age <18 years; ≥25 kg/m2 if age ≥18 years]). Exercise capacity (peak oxygen uptake [milliliters per kilogram per minute]) and cardiac imaging parameters were evaluated by baseline BMI and 2-year change in BMI.
RESULTS: Among 171 (96%) participants (mean age, 23±10 years; 39% female sex; 97% White), 82 (48%) had nonelevated BMI and 89 (52%) had an elevated BMI. After covariate adjustment, higher baseline BMI was associated with lower peak oxygen uptake; lower left ventricular systolic and diastolic function; higher left ventricular mass; and higher atrial, ventricular, and extracellular volumes. Similarly, greater 2-year increases in BMI were associated with greater declines in peak oxygen uptake and greater increases in left ventricular mass. Participants with elevated BMI were more likely to develop late gadolinium enhancement over 2 years (adjusted odds ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-11.9]; P=0.033). Valsartan appeared to modestly attenuate 2-year increases in body weight versus placebo (adjusted mean difference, -3.1% [95% CI, -6.2 to -0.1%]; P=0.042). Baseline BMI did not appear to modify the effect of valsartan on cardiac remodeling (Pinteraction=0.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated BMI was common and associated with greater hypertrophic, eccentric, and fibrotic remodeling in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Two-year increases in BMI were associated with greater phenotypic progression. These findings suggest prevention and treatment of elevated BMI may attenuate hypertrophic cardiomyopathy progression.

title: Mood Disturbances Following Traumatic Brain Injury: A Case Report and Treatment Review.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with a substantial and persistent risk of depression, often complicated by cognitive, behavioral, and functional changes. We present a 59-year-old woman who developed progressive depressive symptoms, irritability, and short-term memory difficulties following a moderate TBI. Her presentation required careful consideration of multiple potential contributors to her mood symptoms, including a remote history of substance use, psychosocial stressors, and neurologic injury. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of depression after TBI and reviews the available evidence for treatment approaches in this population.

title: Addressing non-communicable diseases and injuries through an equity lens: insights from the Cameroon non-communicable disease and injury (NCDI) Poverty Commission.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-communicable diseases and injuries (NCDIs) constitute a leading cause of premature mortality globally, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). To curb the rising burden of NCDIs in Cameroon, the Ministry of Public Health established the National NCDI Poverty Commission to assess the burden of NCDIs, evaluate investments and expenditures related to NCDI services, and generate evidence to guide national policy formulation and resource prioritisation.
METHODS: We synthesised data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2019 database and conducted a comprehensive literature review of peer-reviewed and grey literature (2005-2022) to characterise the burden and risk factors of NCDIs in Cameroon. Investments and expenditures related to NCDIs were extracted from the World Health Organization Global Health Expenditure Database and national planning documents. A two-phase priority-setting process was applied to rank NCDI conditions and identify cost-effective, context-appropriate interventions through quantitative scoring and expert consensus.
RESULTS: NCDIs accounted for 43% of all deaths in 2019, with nearly 29% occurring among individuals aged <40 years. Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) from NCDIs have risen steadily since 1990, with almost two-thirds (61%) attributable to conditions beyond the 'big four' disease categories of diabetes, neoplasms, chronic respiratory diseases, and cardiovascular diseases. Over half (51%) of NCDI-related DALYs in Cameroon were not attributable to quantified behavioural or metabolic risk factors in the GBD framework. Despite this high burden, only 6% of disease prevention funding was directed to NCDIs between 2016 and 2020. The Commission identified 49 priority NCDI conditions and 123 interventions for phased implementation across community, primary, and hospital platforms.
CONCLUSIONS: NCDIs are a major public health burden in Cameroon, heavily impacting the 'economically productive' age group. Rebalancing financing and integrating a prioritised package of NCDI services into Universal Health Coverage (UHC) would be essential to reduce premature mortality and financial hardship.

title: Low-barrier tobacco screening and cessation outreach: A multisite veterans affairs quality improvement initiative.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe implementation of a multi-site, equity-informed tobacco screening and cessation outreach initiative across three Veterans Affairs healthcare systems.
METHODS: This quality improvement initiative was implemented in fiscal year 2025 in San Francisco, California, Danville, Illinois, and Orlando, Florida. The intervention combined dashboard-informed targeting with in-person outreach events offering tobacco use screening, brief education, medications for tobacco use disorder, referral to cessation resources, and selected lung cancer screening education and referral. Outcomes included reach, service delivery outputs, tobacco use screening trends, and implementation barriers and facilitators, summarized descriptively using dashboard and event-level data.
RESULTS: Implementation varied across sites. San Francisco completed four outreach events with 417 total participant encounters, including 212 Veterans, and documented 19 tobacco use screenings, 18 lung cancer screenings, medication linkage, quitline/provider referrals, and research linkage. Danville completed three outreach events reaching 120 Veterans and documented 6 tobacco use screenings and 12 medication prescriptions. Orlando did not complete events because of staffing and operational barriers. Key determinants included staffing capacity, workflow fit, event approvals, procurement, outreach availability, and lung cancer screening infrastructure.
CONCLUSIONS: Dashboard-informed outreach may extend tobacco-related preventive care beyond routine clinic encounters, but implementation depends on local infrastructure, staffing, referral pathways, and interdisciplinary partnerships.

title: Autoimmune gastritides: A critical review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune gastritis (AIG) has long been considered a host-related autoimmune disease that results in oxyntic atrophy, leading to Pernicious Anemia and increasing neoplastic risk. Current evidence discloses that gastric autoimmunity includes a spectrum of inflammatory diseases (i.e., Autoimmune Gastritides) with distinct etiologies, comorbidities, clinical presentations, histological phenotypes, and outcomes.
AIM: To distinguish the clinical-pathological subtypes of immunomediated gastric disorders.
RESULTS: Gastric autoimmune diseases comprise Type-1 and Type-2 variants. Type-1 atrophic AIG may lead to vitamin B12 malabsorption, resulting in pernicious anemia, and carries a high risk of Type-1 neuroendocrine gastric neoplasia. Type-1a AIG includes two subtypes. Type-1a is the canonical oxyntic-restricted AIG subtype with no history of exposure to H. pylori infection. In this subtype, a T-cell-rich, cytolytic infiltrate targets the corpus/fundus mucosa, resulting in oxyntic-restricted atrophic changes. Type-1b combines autoimmune etiology with prior or current exposure to H. pylori infection. The dual etiology of Type-1b AIG combines autoimmune oxyntic damage with H. pylori-related antral lesions. This condition may lead to extensive (antral and oxyntic) atrophy, necessitating cancer prevention strategies tailored to the histological stage of gastritis. Type-2 AIG is far less frequent than Type-1, presents with mucus-secreting (antral-pyloric) and oxyntic (corpus/fundus) erosive mucosal high-grade pangastritis, and involves symptomatic multiorgan immune-mediated comorbidities, irrespective of H. pylori status. Type-2 combines Type-1-like serology with a wide, variable spectrum of circulating organ-specific and non-organ-specific autoantibodies and requires targeted treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: The nosology of autoimmune gastritides should reflect their diverse etio-pathogenesis, clinicopathological presentations, and outcomes.

title: Scaling Caregiver Health and Wellbeing Coaching: a mixed-methods evaluation of implementation and sustainment in the Veterans Health Administration.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Effective and sustainable support for family caregivers is a growing priority, yet practical guidance for scaling promising coaching interventions into routine practice is limited. The objective of this evaluation was to identify organizational determinants, barriers, facilitators, and adaptations affecting national implementation of the Caregiver Health and Wellbeing Coaching (CHWC) program in the Veterans Health Administration.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: An explanatory, sequential mixed‑methods design included surveys of CHWC staff (n = 53) and qualitative interviews (n = 14), guided by the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, its Outcomes Addendum, and the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications‑Enhanced.
RESULTS: Successful implementation-defined as program launch and delivery to at least 1 caregiver at each site-and successful sustainment-defined as ongoing or expanding delivery to new and returning caregivers-were associated with thorough planning, leadership engagement, and flexible delivery. Barriers included staff turnover, complex documentation, and challenges recruiting caregivers. Facilitators and process improvements were rapidly integrated into program operations.
DISCUSSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Findings can inform strategies to scale caregiver support programs that underpin sustainable aging and long-term care systems.

title: Nicotine replacement therapy sampling for cigarette cessation in dental care: A National Dental Practice‐Based Research Network cluster randomized clinical trial
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cigarette smoking is detrimental to oral health. Oral health professionals rarely prescribe smoking cessation medications. Nicotine replacement therapy sampling (NRTS), providing brief starter courses of NRT, could improve provision of NRT and promote cessation. The aim of the Free Samples for Health (FreSH) study was to test the effectiveness of NRTS compared with enhanced usual care on long-term abstinence from combustible tobacco. DESIGN: Two-group, pragmatic, cluster (dental practice) randomized clinical trial. SETTING: The study was conducted in the Midwest and Northeast nodes of the United States' National Dental Practice-Based Research Network in 59 dental practices. Practices were randomized to intervention condition. PARTICIPANTS: Participants (recruited June 2023-June 2025) were adult patients of network practices who smoke cigarettes daily [n = 1196; NRTS n = 486, comparison group (ET) n = 710; 59% female; 71% White]. INTERVENTION AND COMPARATOR: All participants received Ask-Advise-Refer: oral health practitioners asked smoking status, advised quitting and referred to state tobacco quitlines. Participants in the NRTS group were given a 2-week supply of 14 mg nicotine patches and 4 mg nicotine lozenges; participants in the ET group were given an electric toothbrush. MEASUREMENTS: Participants were surveyed after their visit and at 1, 3 and 6 months post enrollment. The primary outcome was 7-day point-prevalence abstinence measured 6 months post enrollment confirmed via expired breath carbon monoxide (CO) < 6 p.p.m. Secondary outcomes included quit attempts, short-term abstinence, NRT and quitline use. Covariates included stage of change, confidence, readiness and cigarettes per day. RESULTS: While there was no condition effect on CO-confirmed abstinence at 6 months post intervention [NRTS: 8.4%, ET: 8.0%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.04, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.65-2.09], the NRTS intervention statistically significantly increased NRT use across all timepoints (NRTS: 50%, ET: 13%; aOR = 7.39, 95% CI = 5.29-10.31) and quit attempts at all timepoints (NRTS: 58%, ET: 49%; aOR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.06-2.02). There was a statistically significant effect of NRTS on self-reported 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 1 month post enrollment (NRTS: 12.8%, ET: 9.0%; aOR = 1.72, 95% CI = 1.03-2.88). There was no difference in quitline use. Practices assigned to the NRTS condition recruited notably fewer participants (t = 2.11, P = 0.04). SUMMARY: Free nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) samples are not sufficient to improve long-term smoking abstinence in dental patients; however, NRT samples increase engagement with quitting behaviors and may serve as a starting point toward quitting. Low recruitment in the NRT sampling group demonstrates discomfort by oral health practitioners in discussing smoking among those not voicing readiness to quit.

title: Genomic inbreeding and selection signatures analyses in the Doberman Pinscher breed
abstract: The Doberman Pinscher population has undergone strong artificial selection for morphology and behavior, which can reduce genomic diversity and increase autozygosity. Here, we characterized the genome structure and identified selection signatures in Doberman Pinschers using complementary within- and between-population approaches. Genotypes from 3,226 Dobermans Dogs (Illumina CanineHD; 216,184 SNPs) provided by the Doberman Diversity Project were analyzed after purpose-specific quality control. Genomic inbreeding was quantified using four allele-frequency-based metrics and the runs of homozygosity (FROH) approach. Selection signatures were detected using intrapopulation (i.e., Runs of Homozygosity-ROH; Integrated Haplotype Score-iHS; and Number of Segregating Sites by Length-nSL) and interpopulation methods (i.e., Fixation Index-FST; Cross-Population Extended Haplotype Homozygosity-XP-EHH; and Cross-Population Number of Segregating Sites by Length-XP-nSL) comparing the Doberman Pinscher breed to Labrador Retriever (n=237). Dobermans showed high overall inbreeding, with a mean FROH of 0.42 (range 0.22-0.68), whereas the allele-frequency-based inbreeding estimators had similar means (~0.04). The partitioning of the ROH indicated high contributions from medium-to-long ROHs, consistent with recent inbreeding. The ROH scans identified 39,512 SNPs in ROH islands (≥50% frequency across individuals), with notable concentrations on CFA2, CFA3, and CFA31. Haplotype-based scans identified 2,820 candidate iHS SNPs and 2,173 candidate nSL SNPs (|score|>2). A common set of 310 SNPs was shared among ROH, iHS, and nSL, mapping near 279 genes that were mostly enriched for developmental pathways, particularly neurodevelopment and neuron-related cellular components. Between breeds, 349 highly differentiated SNPs were detected by FST, while XP-EHH and XP-nSL highlighted more than 1,000 haplotype-based signals differentiating Doberman Pinschers from the Labrador Retriever reference population. A total of nine SNPs overlapped across FST, XP-EHH, and XP-nSL, which were located mainly on CFA8 (~59.48-60.61 Mb) near the KCNK10, SPATA7, PTPN21, NEGR1, and BTG1 genes. Functional annotations for some candidate genes, including BTG1 and KCNK10, suggest possible links to cellular regulatory and cardiac-related biological processes; however, direct associations with Doberman disease phenotypes remain to be validated. Overall, the Doberman Pinscher breed exhibits high genome-wide autozygosity and levels of inbreeding. In addition, our results showed consistent, multi-method evidence of selection at loci associated with neurodevelopmental and regulatory pathways. These findings provide prioritized candidate regions for follow-up studies that integrate phenotypes relevant to breed health and performance.

title: Myeloid cell reprogramming drives enhanced defense against Streptococcus pneumoniae lung infection following exposure to commensal Prevotella.
abstract: Clinical data link the prevalent respiratory tract anaerobe Prevotella with reduced pneumonia mortality, but the mechanisms directing Prevotella regulation of lung immune homeostasis are unclear. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to define the transcriptional immune signatures underlying improved clearance of Streptococcus pneumoniae following lung exposure to Prevotella melaninogenica. Overall, we observed a substantial shift in myeloid cell transcriptional programming from interferon-dominant to a more antibacterial profile in S. pneumoniae-infected mice after pre-exposure to P. melaninogenica, correlating with increased macrophage and neutrophil phagocytosis of S. pneumoniae and improved pathogen clearance. In neutrophils, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling through TNFR2 was essential for increased antimicrobial function. Moreover, improved defense required CCR2-dependent monocyte-derived macrophages, with selective enrichment of more a mature Cxcl3+ population which was distinct from the hallmark S. pneumoniae-associated C1qa+ population enriched in the absence of effective clearance. Together, these findings inform the myeloid cell transcriptional changes associated with natural infection resistance mediated by pulmonary microbial exposures.

title: Understanding regional variations in the veterans health administration’s clinical resource hub program using hierarchical agglomerative clustering
abstract: Abstract Background Large healthcare systems such as the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) have potential to optimize resource allocation and improve efficiency through regionalization. VHA’s Clinical Resource Hubs (CRH) is a regionally based program with one “hub” based in each of the 18 VHA administrative regions; hubs fill temporary staffing gaps across each region’s “spoke” ambulatory care sites. Understanding clusters of pre-existing regional characteristics in relationship to observed program outcomes could inform program design and evaluation. Existing clustering approaches, however, are difficult to interpret and apply. We aimed to test, as a proof-of-concept, whether unsupervised hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) can (a) reveal interpretable regional typologies and (b) show face validity for learning about variations in CRH program outcomes. Methods We first developed a set of characteristics with hypothesized links to regional CRH variations. Based on these, we created regional variables based on Veteran characteristics by aggregating their relevant data. We also included relevant pre-existing regionally defined VHA data variables. We used principal component analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction and for developing interpretive feature loadings. We applied HAC to identify regional clusters among the retained variables and iteratively tested cluster face validity. We compared access pre-CRH and post-CRH (FY19 and FY23) and utilization (FY23) across HAC-based clusters. Results HAC identified four clusters, or regional profiles (e.g., older/sicker/rural vs. younger/growing/more female). Analysis of access and utilization outcome variations showed apparent differences by cluster; e.g., one cluster with the lowest variation in access scores also had the lowest access score, suggesting regional access challenges. Conclusions PCA-informed HAC produced interpretable regional typologies that aligned with operational leadership insights and corresponded with illustrative variations in CRH program access and utilization results. Future work, however, is needed to confirm the usefulness of this method more generally as an approach for understanding outcome variations across regionally based programs.

title: B-cell activating factor contributes to CAR-T cell-associated cytokine release syndrome
abstract: Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is the most common and potentially life-threatening toxicity associated with CAR-T cell therapy and is related to a heightened immune effector state. In this work, we identified a novel role of the pro-tumorigenic cytokine B-cell activating factor (BAFF) in its pathophysiology. First, we observed that patients who experienced CAR-T cell-related CRS have elevated serum BAFF levels that coincide with elevated IL-6. Mechanistically, we show that IFN-γ, produced by activated CAR-T cells, stimulates monocytes to release BAFF, which induces the expression of CRS-related cytokines from monocytes. Monocytes derived from CRS patients express BCMA, which is further induced by IFN-γ stimulation. Neutralization of BAFF with belimumab significantly reduces production of various CRS and Immune Effector Cell-Associated Neurotoxicity Syndrome (ICANS)-related cytokines without impairing CAR-T cell activation or killing. Overall, we demonstrate that BAFF contributes to CAR-T-cell-related CRS, and its neutralization may be a novel strategy for treating both CRS and ICANS.

title: CfDNA methylation profiling in blood following moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury using brain cell type-enriched signatures: A pilot study.
abstract: The human brain consists of diverse cell types that collaboratively perform complex functions and form intricate neuronal networks. When traumatic brain injury (TBI) occurs, multiple molecular pathways involving diverse cell types are activated in response to injury. Understanding how brain cell composition is altered during TBI may help improve patient outcomes. Upon brain trauma, neurovascular disruption leads to the release of brain-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) into peripheral blood. The tissue-specific DNA methylation patterns in this cfDNA have the potential to serve as candidate markers for studying brain injury. To characterize brain cell type-enriched methylation features, we analyzed the methylomes of five major brain cell types-neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, and vascular endothelial cells (VECs)-using whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS). Cellular enrichment analysis showed that differentially methylated genes (DMGs) exhibited reference-defined cell type-enriched patterns. Gene Ontology pathway analysis further supported the biological plausibility of these methylation features. To demonstrate the feasibility of applying cfDNA methylation profiling in TBI, we analyzed a limited pilot dataset comprising healthy controls and samples collected at acute (1 day), subacute (1 month), and chronic (6 months) post-injury time points from patients with moderate-to-severe TBI (msTBI). These analyses identified candidate brain cell type-enriched cfDNA methylation features that differed across post-injury sampling groups. Together, our findings highlight that brain cell type-enriched methylation signatures may provide a powerful tool for characterizing distinct cell populations and nominating candidate brain cell-associated cfDNA methylation biomarkers in TBI.

title: Psychedelics Restructure the Global Workspace of Consciousness
abstract: ABSTRACT Psychoactive drugs profoundly alter consciousness, but the neural mechanisms by which they do so remain poorly understood. Global workspace theory may provide a framework for investigating these mechanisms. The global workspace, a candidate neural substrate of consciousness, is a set of brain regions that integrate and disseminate information to the rest of the brain. According to a recent model, the integrators, or “gateways,” are characterized by synergistic interactions with other brain regions, while the disseminators, or “broadcasters,” exhibit redundant interactions. Here, we measured the effects of various psychoactive drugs, including “classic” psychedelics like LSD, mescaline, and psilocybin, “atypical” psychedelics (entactogens) like MDMA, and the stimulant D-amphetamine, on the global workspace. In a secondary analysis of resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data on all these drugs, we found that classic psychedelics are associated with significant increases in the number of gateways in the frontoparietal control and dorsal attention networks. Meanwhile, MDMA and amphetamine reduced the number of gateways in the visual and somatomotor networks. The regional topographies of both synergy and redundancy distinguished classic psychedelics from other drugs. Finally, drugs producing similar changes in synergy and redundancy also produced similar profiles of subjective effects. Overall, our findings provide the first direct evidence that psychedelics may alter the synergistic and redundant interactions that characterize the global workspace of consciousness.

title: Does Intensive Therapy Targeting Modifiable Risk Factors Prevent Diabetic Neuropathy in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes? A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a serious complication of type 2 diabetes (T2DM). Guidelines recommend targeting modifiable risk factors for primary prevention, but their effectiveness is unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the efficacy of interventions targeting modifiable risk factors to prevent DPN in adults with T2D.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov databases for RCTs published since 1980 investigating glycemia, lipids, blood pressure (BP), smoking cessation, lifestyle, and multifactorial interventions. Two reviewers independently screened articles; a third reviewer resolved disagreements. Meta-analysis used a random-effects model. Results are reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence and prediction intervals.
RESULTS: From 1287 identified articles, 863 underwent title/abstract screening, with 41 full-text review, yielding nine studies with extractable data. Eight had low risk of bias (Cochrane RoB 1); one had unclear risk. The glycemic control meta-analysis (n = 5) yielded OR = 0.89 (95% CI 0.66-1.19; prediction interval 0.37-2.15; I2 = 77.8%). Sensitivity analysis identified BARI-2D as the dominant heterogeneity source; its removal reduced I2 to 23% and narrowed the prediction interval (0.80-1.08). This is clinically explainable: BARI-2D compared insulin-sensitizing versus insulin-providing drug strategies rather than glycemic intensity targets, in patients with coronary artery disease. The four-study analysis showed glycemic control may result in little to no difference in DPN risk (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.85-1.02). In BARI-2D, an insulin-sensitizing strategy may reduce incident DPN independently of achieved HbA1c (0.84 (95% CI 0.71-0.99)) (low certainty). Single-study evidence suggests that BP-lowering and multifactorial interventions may reduce incident DPN (low certainty).
DISCUSSION: Glycemic intensity interventions may result in little to no difference in incident DPN risk. The BARI-2D drug class-specific finding and single-study evidence suggesting benefit from BP-lowering and multifactorial interventions warrant further rigorous research on incident DPN.

title: Reliability and accuracy of medication-based performance measures for assessment of outpatient cardiology clinicians.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple performance measures are used to assess the management of common cardiovascular conditions, such as coronary artery disease (CAD), heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), and atrial fibrillation (AF). These measures are sometimes used to assess individual clinicians, despite lack of evidence of reliability and accuracy. We used national Veteran Affairs (VA) data to test medication-based performance measures for assessment of clinician performance in outpatient cardiology care.
METHODS: This retrospective study examined VA cardiology clinician/Veteran dyads from 2017-2023 to evaluate 10 medication-based performance measures for CAD, HFrEF, or AF with elevated stroke risk. Achievement of each performance measure was defined as an active prescription of an indicated medication for each eligible patient encounter, summarized at the clinician level. Reliability was calculated using the beta-binomial method. A Bayesian causal model was used to assess the impact of case complexity on performance measure achievement. Finally, we performed peer review of a subset of cases (n = 952) to assess the accuracy of three representative performance measures.
RESULTS: Of 456,071 unique cardiology encounters included in this study, 312,331 included CAD, 224,599 included HFrEF, and 178,678 included AF. These patients were treated by 1,043 cardiology clinicians. Median performance measure achievement ranged from 0.23 (SGLT2i for HFrEF) to 0.99 (beta blocker for HFrEF). Measure reliability varied from 0.63 to 0.90. Case complexity did not significantly affect performance measure achievement. Using peer review as the gold standard, accuracy was poor to moderate (balanced accuracy 0.51-0.73), and measures underestimated performance relative to peer review.
CONCLUSIONS: Ten medication-based performance measures for CAD, HFrEF, and AF can be efficiently measured using electronic health record data, and most have sufficient reliability to support clinician benchmarking and the identification of potential care gaps without need for risk adjustment. However, suboptimal accuracy compared with a peer review gold standard indicates that these measures may be insufficient as a standalone assessment of clinician quality.

title: Sotagliflozin Reprograms Hepatic Lipid Metabolism and Attenuates Atherosclerosis Beyond Empagliflozin in CKM Mice.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce cardiovascular mortality and chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, but this benefit derives primarily from reductions in heart failure and cardiovascular mortality rather than in atherothrombotic events. Sotagliflozin, which inhibits both intestinal SGLT1 and renal SGLT2, is the only drug in this class shown to lower rates of myocardial infarction and stroke in CKD. However, its mechanism remains unclear, and its effectiveness in non-diabetic CKD has not been studied. We hypothesized that dual SGLT1/2 inhibition reprograms systemic substrate utilization toward fatty acid oxidation, which may partially account for this protective effect.
METHODS: CKD was induced in male low-density lipoprotein receptor-deficient mice by 5/6 nephrectomy. Sham and CKD mice received a high-fat diet and drinking water containing sotagliflozin, empagliflozin, or vehicle for 16 weeks, at doses that produced equivalent fractional excretion of glucose. We quantified atherosclerosis en face and in the aortic sinus. Indirect calorimetry, echocardiography, hepatic RNA sequencing, plasma acylcarnitine profiling, and in vivo deuterium labeling of palmitate were performed.
RESULTS: At matched levels of glucosuria and plasma total cholesterol, sotagliflozin decreased body mass, atherosclerosis burden, triglycerides, and TNF-α more than empagliflozin, and raised postprandial total GLP-1 approximately 3-fold, while both drugs similarly improved albuminuria and diastolic function. Sotagliflozin increased energy expenditure independent of body mass and lowered respiratory exchange ratio despite compensatory hyperphagia. Sotagliflozin reduced hepatic lipogenic genes and de novo lipogenic flux, while increasing β-oxidation and ketogenesis; empagliflozin only activated the oxidative pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: In experimental CKM syndrome, dual SGLT1/2 inhibition reduces atherosclerosis and metabolic syndrome more effectively than selective SGLT2 inhibition and is associated with reprogramming of hepatic lipid metabolism. These results suggest that sotagliflozin could be an attractive candidate for mitigating atherosclerotic risk in non-diabetic CKD.

title: Comprehensive Aortic Stenosis Characterization Using Multiview Deep Learning.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of aortic stenosis (AS) requires integration of both structural and functional information characterized by visual traits as well as quantitation of gradients. Existing artificial intelligence models use solely either structural or functional information.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to develop and validate an automated multiview deep learning framework to assess AS severity.
METHODS: The authors developed EchoNet-AS, an open-source end-to-end integrated approach combining video-based convolutional neural networks to assess valve motion with segmentation models to automate measurement of aortic valve peak velocity and classify AS severity.
RESULTS: EchoNet-AS was trained on 210,193 images from 16,076 studies from KPNC (Kaiser Permanente Northern California) and validated on 1,588 held-out test studies and a temporally distinct cohort of 19,202 studies. The final model was also externally validated on 2,415 studies from SHC (Stanford Healthcare) and 9,038 studies from CSMC (Cedars-Sinai Medical Center). Combining assessments from multiple echocardiographic videos and Doppler measurements, EchoNet-AS achieved excellent discrimination of severe AS with an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.964 (95% CI: 0.952-0.973) in the KPNC held-out cohort and 0.986 (0.983-0.989) in the temporally distinct cohort, which was superior to models using single views or only Doppler measurements. The performance was consistently robust in distinct external cohorts with an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.985 (0.975-0.992) at SHC and 0.989 (0.986-0.992) at CSMC.
CONCLUSIONS: EchoNet-AS synthesizes information from both B-mode videos and Doppler images to accurately assess AS severity. Its strong performance generalizes robustly to external validation cohorts and shows potential as an automated clinical decision support tool.

title: AI Trustworthiness in the Perioperative Period for Patients with Serious Illness: Scoping Narrative Review
abstract: Background: Despite the promising potential of AI in the perioperative context, the rapid pace of development and diverse implementation warrant a thorough review to consolidate existing knowledge, identify gaps, and assess the use of trustworthiness principles in AI integration into the perioperative period for patients with serious illness. Objective: The purpose of this study was to address deficiencies in the perioperative AI literature by elucidating the extent to which discussions of equity, ethics, and safety are incorporated, thereby establishing a foundation for the development of robust ethical guidelines for the safe and effective integration of AI in health care. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials), and Scopus for studies published from 2010 to July 2024. We included studies that reported patient functional outcomes, occurred in the perioperative period (30 d before and up to 90 d after surgery), incorporated AI integration, and included patients with serious illness (defined as malignancy, advanced organ failure, frailty, dementia or neurodegenerative disease, or stroke). To ensure reliability and minimize bias, 2 independent reviewers screened all studies at the title or abstract and full-text stages; conflicts were resolved through team consensus. The abstraction form was developed iteratively and was tested through pilot abstractions. Any discrepancies identified during data extraction were resolved through discussion and consensus among the reviewers. The ROBINS-I (Risk of Bias Tool in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions) tool was used to assess quality. Abstraction and risk assessment were conducted through a blinded, independent dual-review process. A narrative review was compiled from the identified studies. Results: Of the 10,980 papers identified through the database searches, this review yielded 81 papers that met the inclusion criteria. Analysis of AI implementation strategies revealed foundational efforts toward equitable access, with 6 studies providing open-access tools and several more designing models with simple inputs suitable for low-resource settings (17 studies). Seven studies mentioned their commitment to transparency (eg, publishing code) to enhance safety and trust. However, significant ethical deficiencies persist, particularly regarding input data, as only 2 studies explicitly addressed racial or ethnic disparities, and concerns about lack of sample diversity (16 studies) and the omission of socially relevant features (5 studies) were frequently noted as limitations. Conclusions: Machine learning for predictive analytics and other types of AI tools for surgical outcomes offer significant potential but require adherence to trustworthiness and safety principles to be clinically viable. Future research should prioritize adherence to guidelines for equity, ethics, and safety, conduct prospective studies, incorporate more external validation of AI models, and facilitate transparent monitoring and reporting of model performance to build clinician and patient trust and encourage broader health care system adoption.

title: Pathological Uromodulin Retention in Altered Thick Ascending Limb Cells Drives Kidney Disease Progression
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is increasingly prevalent and is a leading cause of mortality. Recent transcriptomic studies have identified the persistence of injury-induced renal tubular epithelial cell states, yet the cell populations that drive CKD remain unresolved. Uromodulin (UMOD) is the most abundant urinary secreted protein expressed exclusively in thick ascending limb (TAL) epithelial cells in the kidney. UMOD is strongly associated with CKD risk in genome-wide association studies, suggesting a broader, yet unexplored role of UMOD and TAL cells in CKD pathogenesis. Here, using spatial proteomics, we identified an injury-induced TAL cell state marked by intracellular UMOD accumulation. Spatially resolved multimodal integration revealed that UMOD accumulation occurred without transcriptional upregulation. Impaired urinary UMOD secretion further supported pathological intracellular retention. These altered TAL cells with UMOD retention exhibited inflammatory signaling, formed profibrotic niches enriched with M2-like macrophages across renal compartments, and were associated with CKD progression in multiple experimental models. Reducing the burden of UMOD retention diminished altered TAL cells and their profibrotic microenvironments, and attenuated CKD development. A similar altered TAL state was identified in human kidney disease and was associated with worse kidney function. Together, we identify pathological UMOD retention and altered TAL cells as key drivers of CKD development and potential therapeutic targets. This study also highlights that protein-level alterations can redefine disease-associated cell states beyond transcript profiling.

title: Improving palliative care integration for veterans with metastatic lung cancer at Orlando VA Medical Center (OVAMC).
abstract: 310 Background: Early palliative care (PC) improves quality of life and end-of-life outcomes in advanced cancer and is recommended by ASCO. Despite this, timely outpatient integration remains inconsistent in VA settings, where fragmented workflows and competing clinical demands may delay referral. At OVAMC, only 31% of veterans with metastatic lung cancer (13/41) completed at least one outpatient PC visit between March and June 2025. Root cause analysis identified inconsistent oncology-PC communication and nonstandard referral processes as key drivers. This initiative aimed to increase the proportion of veterans completing at least one outpatient PC visit to ≥61% by March 2026. Methods: This quality improvement initiative was conducted in the OVAMC hematology/oncology outpatient clinic using Model for Improvement methodology and iterative PDSA cycles. Interventions focused on embedding PC referral identification into routine oncology workflow. Initial efforts included clinician education with monthly run chart feedback. Biweekly oncology-PC huddles were implemented to proactively identify eligible patients in real time. A navigator-led pathway prioritizing PC referrals for newly diagnosed metastatic disease was later introduced, followed by standardized referral workflows and communication across teams. The primary outcome measure was the proportion of eligible veterans completing at least one outpatient PC visit, monitored monthly using run charts. The process measure was monthly PC consult orders. Data were collected through chart review and analyzed using run charts. Results: Monthly PC consult volume demonstrated a sustained shift of six or more consecutive points above the baseline median, consistent with special-cause variation. The proportion of veterans completing at least one outpatient PC visit increased from 31% (13/41) to 79% (38/48), representing an absolute increase of 48 percentage points and exceeding the project aim by 18 percentage points. Temporal analysis suggested that implementation of multidisciplinary huddles coincided with the greatest increase in consult generation, while navigator-led prioritization appeared to facilitate more timely visit completion. No balancing measure concerns were identified, and oncology scheduling remained stable throughout the intervention period. Conclusions: Embedding proactive identification of palliative care needs through multidisciplinary workflow redesign substantially improved early PC integration for veterans with metastatic lung cancer. Sustained run chart shifts suggest successful integration into routine practice. Limitations include lack of assessment of downstream outcomes such as hospice utilization, goals-of-care documentation, and acute care utilization. Future work will expand this model to other tumor types and evaluate patient-centered and utilization outcomes.

title: Potential utilization and projected cost savings of Baveno VII–guided selective endoscopy prior to systemic therapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: A real-world Veterans Health Administration experience.
abstract: 15 Background: Patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are at risk for gastroesophageal varices and bleeding. First-line atezolizumab–bevacizumab therapy, established by the IMBrave 150 trial, requires baseline esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) to exclude high-risk varices, which may delay treatment and increase procedural burden, particularly in resource-limited settings. We hypothesized that Baveno VII criteria could risk-stratify unresectable HCC patients for baseline EGD urgency, estimated potential utilization, and implicated cost savings with a selective screening strategy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with unresectable HCC treated at a single Veterans Health Administration center from 2020–2026. Data was sourced from the electronic health record. Portal hypertension severity was stratified using Baveno VII criteria as low-risk for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH), probable CSPH, or definite CSPH. The primary endpoint was variceal bleeding requiring hospitalization. Associations were analyzed using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. A proposed selective screening strategy was used to model projected procedural cost savings. EGD for variceal screening and hospitalization costs for variceal bleeding were estimated at $1,500 and $25,000, respectively. Results: One hundred patients were included. The primary endpoint occurred in three patients, all with probable CSPH (n = 1) or definite CSPH (n = 2). No variceal bleeding occurred among patients without cirrhosis or those classified as low risk for CSPH. Of the thirty-five patients (35%) who did not undergo baseline EGD, seven experienced a bleeding event from a source other than portal hypertension. Under the proposed Baveno VII–guided selective EGD strategy, 30 of 100 baseline EGDs were avoided, with no variceal bleeding events observed in the low-risk group. In the base-case analysis, selective EGD was projected to save $45,000 per 100 patients, or $450 per patient, compared with universal EGD. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort, variceal bleeding requiring hospitalization during systemic therapy was uncommon and limited to patients with probable and definite CSPH by Baveno VII criteria. No bleeding occurred in patients without cirrhosis or those classified as low risk. Selective baseline EGD guided by Baveno VII criteria demonstrated projected cost savings without observed loss of effectiveness or safety, suggesting a potentially cost-effective approach for risk stratification to avoid treatment delays. title: A measurement-based care strategy for buprenorphine-naloxone treatment (Bup-MBC): Development of an EHR-integrated intervention.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Risk of recurrent opioid use during buprenorphine-naloxone (bup-nx) treatment is dynamic and remains elevated after initiation, with vulnerability shaped in part by treatment intensity and gaps between visits, yet routine outpatient care relies on episodic encounters and retrospective data. This mismatch can delay recognition of emerging instability and limit timely treatment adjustments. This paper reports the development and specification of an intervention strategy to address this mismatch.
METHODS: We used a structured, multi-phase design process to specify and configure a measurement-based care (MBC) strategy for bup-nx treatment (Bup-MBC) in outpatient addiction clinics through three phases: (1) a systematic review of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) for substance use treatment; (2) a qualitative needs assessment using the Theoretical Domains Framework and COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior) model to identify gaps in risk monitoring, agency, and trust; and (3) iterative co-design with multidisciplinary clinicians to refine workflow fit and trust-preserving use of data. Patients informed item and feedback content during the needs assessment but did not participate in the co-design cycles.
RESULTS: Bup-MBC integrates (1) brief between-visit PROMs (e.g., withdrawal, craving, adherence); (2) immediate non-punitive patient feedback; (3) clinician-facing summaries and non-directive prompts in the electronic health record (EHR); and (4) an opt-in between-visit outreach pathway with predefined safety triggers, all configured within existing EHR and patient portal infrastructure. It targets patient and clinician capability to recognize changes in risk, opportunity for action through structured monitoring and visit preparation, and trust and agency through non-punitive communication, without adding substantial burden. The full measure set, severity bands, and question-to-action map are provided as supplementary material. Key trade-offs included prioritizing single-item measures for feasibility, balancing opt-in outreach with safety overrides, and assuming routine clinician use of summaries.
CONCLUSION: This development study specifies an EHR-integrated MBC strategy for outpatient bup-nx treatment. As single-center design work with co-design limited to clinicians and delivery contingent on portal or text-message access, its outputs are hypotheses about mechanism and fit rather than demonstrated effects. Feasibility studies are needed to evaluate uptake, acceptability, workflow fit, and effects on treatment.

title: Provider-Level and Specialty Variation in ARNI and SGLT2i Use After Heart Failure Hospitalization
abstract: Background: Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are incompletely utilized in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The degree to which use varies at the individual level and within specialties is unknown. We aimed to characterize provider-level and specialty-level variation in ARNI and SGLT2i prescribing after HF hospitalization. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included Veterans Affairs (VA) providers seeing patients within 6 months of HFrEF hospitalization 2017-2023. We used descriptive statistics and site-adjusted multilevel logistic regression to examine prescribing by medical specialty, provider type, and provider sex. Adjusted median odds ratios (mOR) and empirical (unadjusted) provider-level rate ratios (RRs) by percentile were used to describe provider-level variation. Clinical pharmacy visits were assessed as an independent factor and as an interaction with specialty. Results: Among 7,946 providers caring for 76,795 patients across 211,267 outpatient encounters, provider-level variation remained substantial after adjustment for patient characteristics and site-level clustering (mOR 1.45 for ARNI; 1.46 for SGLT2i). Within every specialty, providers ranged from near-zero to near-100% use. Relative to the median provider in the same specialty, RRs ranged from 0-0.31 (5th percentile), 0.37-0.71 (25th), 1.38-1.66 (75th), to 1.8-3.2 (95th). Cardiology visits carried the highest adjusted odds of ARNI (OR 2.30, 95% CI 2.18-2.44) and SGLT2i use (OR 1.99, 95% CI 1.88-2.11) and most new starts. Pharmacist visits were independently associated with greater use of ARNI (OR 1.14, 1.06-1.23) and SGLT2i (OR 1.15, 1.06-1.24), with no effect modification by specialty. In early 2023, 58.4% (ARNI) and 40.2% (SGLT2i) of post-hospitalization HF visits had untreated patients. Conclusions: Provider-level variation in ARNI and SGLT2i use after guideline incorporation was large within every specialty and independent of site effects. Though specific specialties have higher use, individual providers, not specialty alone, may be an important target for efforts to close gaps in therapy.

title: Evaluating Novel Healthcare Approaches to Nurturing and Caring for Hospitalised Elders (ENHANCE): protocol for a stepped wedge, cluster randomised clinical trial for delirium prevention in older adults.
abstract: Introduction The objective of this trial is to test whether a family-augmented version of the Hospital Elder Life Program (FAM-HELP) is superior to conventional HELP for prevention of delirium in older patients during hospital admission. Methods and analysis This is a multicentre, stepped-wedge, cluster randomised clinical trial comparing HELP to FAM-HELP. The trial will employ an effectiveness-implementation design (hybrid type I), simultaneously evaluating FAM-HELP effectiveness compared with conventional HELP, while also measuring implementation barriers and facilitators. The primary outcomes are delirium incidence (via long-form Confusion Assessment Method, CAM) and delirium severity (CAM-S Severity Score). Secondary outcomes related to delirium will also be collected, including patient-reported and caregiver-reported delirium burden, delirium duration, length of hospital stay and discharge disposition. Outcome assessors are masked to intervention arm, and intervention teams are masked to delirium status and other study outcomes. The primary statistical analysis will be based on generalised estimating equations with an intention-to-treatment principle and secondary analyses will include strategies for incorporating protocol fidelity and adherence into models. The planned sample size is 1900 patients, which will provide ≥80% power based on estimated parameters. Prespecified subgroup analyses are also planned for exploring heterogeneity of treatment effects. Ethics and dissemination The trial was approved by the University of Michigan Institutional Review Board (IRBMED, HUM00227397), which serves as the single IRB with ceded review from all performance sites. Recruitment began in December 2023 and is expected to continue until summer 2027. Comprehensive verbal informed consent is obtained from all patient and family care partner participants. An independent safety officer has been commissioned to oversee trial operations and provide guidance to the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute. Results will be disseminated via medical journals, academic conferences, dissemination stakeholder partner organisations and news media. Trial registration number NCT05929703.

title: Sex differences in the preoperative diagnosis of heart failure: a mixed methods study
abstract: Heart failure poses significant perioperative risk, and optimal management begins with an accurate preoperative diagnosis. There is significant diagnostic variation in HF, and one component of such variation may include sex-based differences, potentially arising from biological differences in disease progression versus underrecognized biases in healthcare pertaining to diagnosis and disease course. The authors performed an explanatory sequential mixed methods study with three phases. First, electronic health records of adult patients undergoing surgical procedures at an academic institution from 2015 to 2019 were manually reviewed by a multispecialty panel of physicians involved in heart failure care (cardiologists, cardiac anesthesiologists, intensivists). Preoperative clinical HF diagnoses documented in the medical record were compared to adjudicated HF diagnoses rendered by the multispecialty panel. Characteristics associated with inaccurate diagnoses among female versus male patients were analyzed. Second, survey data were obtained from attending anesthesiologists, nurse anesthetists, and preoperative clinic physician assistants. Survey content included sex-based differences in the perceived importance of HF diagnostic factors, barriers to obtaining diagnostic data, and methods to overcome barriers. In the third phase, clinicians participated in semi-structured interviews, exploring thought processes related to survey results. In the first phase, 1,018 patients were panel-reviewed. A small difference in overall rates of missed diagnoses of heart failure were found for female patients (51.9%) compared to male patients (41.0%); standardized difference = 0.31. Compared to male patients with missed diagnoses, female patients more commonly were older and presented with pulmonary edema, pleural effusions, and hepatomegaly. Conversely, male patients with missed diagnoses were more commonly American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status class 1 or 2 and underwent general surgery. In the second phase, among 64 survey respondents, small sex-based differences in perceived barriers to diagnosis existed, including a lack of knowledge in how female patients present with heart failure due to previous underrepresentation in clinical trials, generally sex-neutral diagnostic guidelines, and lower prevalence of female patients with heart failure presenting for surgery. Respondents indicated that knowledge gaps regarding sex-based differences in diagnosis might be best addressed by electronic flagging of patients likely to have heart failure and educational presentations. In the third phase, barriers to diagnoses with a perceived differential impact on female versus male patients included symptom disclosure, clinician training, and underrecognized biases. Sex-based differences in heart failure diagnostic processes emanate from a variety of sources. Clinicians may be receptive to a variety of training and process workflow interventions addressing this issue. Not applicable.

title: Long-Term Survival of Liver Transplantation in Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Insights From National Claims Data.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading indication for liver transplantation (LT) in the United States. While post-transplant outcomes are well established, the relative survival benefit of LT compared to non-LT remains underdefined.
METHODS: Using Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database, we identified adults with ALD between 2017 and 2024. We used logistic regression to evaluate factors associated with LT, and Cox regression to compare survival between LT recipients and non-recipients.
RESULTS: Among 373,025 patients with ALD, 3453 underwent LT. Female sex (adjusted OR = 0.805; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.750-0.866), African-American race (adjusted OR = 0.542; 95% CI: 0.462-0.636), older age, and non-liver comorbidities, and all types of metastatic cancer were associated with lower odds of LT; non-metastatic liver cancer, however, was associated with increased odds of LT (adjusted OR = 4.147; 95% CI: 3.659-4.699). The 8-year restricted mean survival time was 2600 days (~7.12 years) for LT recipients and 1799 days (~4.93 years) for nonrecipients. The median survival among deceased patients was 1000 days with LT vs. 355 days without LT. LT was associated with a lower adjusted mortality risk (HR, 0.365; 95% CI: 0.333-0.401).
CONCLUSION: LT confers a substantial survival advantage for patients with ALD, beyond what is achieved without transplantation. However, significant sex and race-based disparities persist, underscoring the need for policy interventions to promote equitable access and optimized candidate selection.

title: Persistent Opioid Exposure in Older Adults With Rheumatic Disease: National Patterns, Disparities, and Cross-Specialty Prescribing.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate national prevalence of opioid use, including chronic and high-risk use, among older adults with rheumatic diseases (RDs); to identify sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with chronic opioid use; and to characterize prescribing patterns by clinician specialty in a contemporary Medicare-linked national registry cohort.
METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of the Rheumatology Informatics System for Effectiveness (RISE) registry linked to Medicare Part D (2016-2021). Patients were aged ≥ 65 years with qualifying RDs and continuous Medicare enrollment in 2021. Opioid use was identified from Part D claims. Chronic use was defined as ≥ 90-day supply in 2021. High-risk use was assessed using Office of Inspector General indicators. Generalized estimating equations modeled factors associated with chronic opioid use.
RESULTS: Among 45,455 patients (mean age 75.8 years; 76.88% women), 43.13% filled ≥ 1 opioid prescription and 17.93% met criteria for chronic use in 2021. Very high-risk prescribing was rare (< 1%). Chronic use was most prevalent in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA; 26.19%) and least prevalent in polymyalgia rheumatica (11.58%). In adjusted analyses, axSpA (odds ratio [OR] 1.63, 95% CI 1.35-1.98), fibromyalgia (OR 2.68, 95% CI 2.39-3.00), mood disorder (OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.31-1.52), anxiety disorder (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.35-1.57), higher comorbidity burden (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.62-2.06), American Indian/Alaska Native race (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.09-2.45), and greater socioeconomic deprivation (OR 1.91, 95% CI 1.71-2.13) were independently associated with chronic use. Nonrheumatology clinicians wrote most opioid prescriptions (62.60%) and more high-dose prescriptions (≥ 50 morphine mg equivalents/day).
CONCLUSION: Opioid exposure remains common among Medicare-insured older adults with RDs, although very high-risk prescribing is rare. Coordinated, guideline-concordant pain management across specialties may help preserve appropriate opioid use for patients who may benefit while reducing avoidable long-term exposure.

title: Baroreflex Failure After Surgical Resection of Bilateral Carotid Body Tumors: A Systematic Review
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Surgery remains the definitive treatment for carotid body tumors (CBTs); however, concern persists regarding the risk of baroreflex failure (BRF) following bilateral CBT resection. The true incidence and long-term clinical course of BRF remain poorly defined. We performed a systematic review to examine the risk and clinical course of BRF after surgical resection of bilateral CBTs. DATA SOURCES: PubMed/Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane. REVIEW METHODS: A systematic review was performed based on a population, intervention, comparison, and outcome search (PICOTS) of reports on BRF in surgical resection of bilateral CBTs. Additional articles were added by citation searching. The study was reported per the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. RESULTS: This systematic review included 15 single case reports and 8 case series of BRF in surgical resection of bilateral CBTs. No higher quality studies of clinical trials or cohort studies were available. Results from this systematic review showed that BRF symptoms most commonly occurred immediately after the second surgery in bilateral CBT resections, and that many reported cases demonstrated improvement over time, although long-term outcomes were inconsistently reported. Commonly used treatments of BRF included clonidine and benzodiazepines. CONCLUSION: Despite the commonly perceived high risk and debilitating clinical outcomes, the reported clinical course of BRF following bilateral CBT resection appears more variable and, in many cases, less severe than historically perceived. The optimal management of CBTs remains unclear, though surgical resection of bilateral CBTs warrants individualized consideration based on age, tumor characteristics, genetic risk, and treatment goals.

title: Focal therapy vs radical prostatectomy for localized prostate cancer: a systematic review, meta-analysis, bayesian network, and trial sequential analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer is a prevalent malignancy with procedural treatment strategies. These treatments are associated with significant quality of life impact, including erectile dysfunction and urinary incontinence. Focal therapy (FT) has emerged as an option that may minimize treatment-related side effects. Its efficacy in cancer control compared to standard strategies, such as radical prostatectomy (RP), remains controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis sought to compare the oncologic and functional outcomes of focal therapy versus radical prostatectomy (RP) for localized prostate cancer.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive systematic search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Google Scholar in October 2025. The study followed PRISMA guidelines and included prospective and retrospective observational studies comparing RP with FT. Eleven studies met inclusion criteria providing a total of 8399 patients of which 4498 underwent RP and 3901 underwent FT. The coprimary endpoints were salvage treatment-free survival and failure-free survival, with secondary endpoints including continence, erectile function, and complication rate.
RESULTS: Oncologic outcomes revealed a statistically significant overall difference in salvage treatment-free survival and failure-free survival between FT and RP, with a HR of 2.05 (95% Cl 1.29-3.26, p=0.002) and 2.68 (95% CI 1.04-6.93, p=0.04), respectively. Differences in overall survival were not statistically significant HR 1.71 (95% CI 0.75-3.90, p = 0.20). Subgroup analyses showed varied results across different focal therapy approaches, with cryotherapy and combined approaches demonstrating higher treatment failure rates. Functional outcomes strongly favored FT, with significantly higher rates of continence and erectile function across all measured time intervals. At 12 months post-treatment, FT patients demonstrated substantially better continence (OR 3.45, p<0.00001) and erectile function preservation (OR 6.43, p<0.00001) compared to RP.
CONCLUSION: FT offers substantial quality of life benefits, particularly within the first 12 postoperative months, compared to RARP, however, at the cost of decreased oncologic treatment effectiveness. Differences in oncologic outcomes become attenuated in propensity-matched studies and trial sequential analysis yielded inconclusive results. Careful patient selection is paramount, and patients should be thoroughly counseled about potentially reduced oncologic control effectiveness and increased post-ablation monitoring.

title: Gaps in Etiologic Classification of Chronic Kidney Disease in US Veterans: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Many patients living with chronic kidney disease (CKD) may not have a clearly identified cause, which can be a barrier to targeted therapies. We assessed the assignment of CKD etiologies in the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) electronic health record data, overall and by demographics. We identified regular VHA users aged 18 - 100 years with new-onset CKD based on persistent eGFR <60 ml/min/1.73m 2 occurring 2005-2015. CKD etiologies were identified by administrative codes over 3 years before and after the incident CKD date. Etiologies were categorized as diabetic, hypertensive/vascular, obstructive/urologic, glomerular, cystic/congenital, and tubulointerstitial. CKD was considered recognized, but without etiology, if only a general CKD code was present. Logistic regression models assessed disparities by sex and race/ethnicity after adjustment for age, US Census region, and calendar year of incident CKD. Among 452,851 Veterans with CKD, 42.5% were assigned at least one etiology. Hypertensive/vascular (24.5%) was the most common. After adjustment, non-Hispanic Black Veterans and Hispanic Veterans were more likely to be assigned an etiologically-specific diagnosis than non-Hispanic White Veterans (OR 1.61 and 1.23, respectively, each p<0.001). Differences were greater at younger ages. Non-Hispanic Black Veterans were much more likely to be assigned a hypertensive/vascular etiology (OR 2.17; p<0.001), but both non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic Veterans were more likely than White veterans to be assigned diabetic and glomerular etiologies as well (each p<0.001). Women were much less likely to be assigned an etiology overall, and in all categories, compared to men (each p<0.001). Women were less likely to have CKD recognized even if etiology was not assigned. Overall, the assignment of an etiology for CKD is low among U.S. Veterans, particularly among women, possibly due to poor CKD recognition. Types of etiologies assigned differ by race/ethnicity, which may represent true etiologic difference or biased assignment.

title: Re-Evaluating Predictive Performance in the Clinical Risk Analysis Index of Frailty.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether the Risk Analysis Index (RAI), last calibrated in 2010-2014, requires scoring system changes to remain an effective measure of surgical frailty.
SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: The RAI is among the most validated and widely used measures of surgical frailty. However, like any clinical prediction model, the RAI's scoring system might be prone to algorithmic drift that could invalidate continued use.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of patients evaluated in outpatient surgery clinics at Veterans Health Administration (VHA) or University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC). All-cause mortality was measured 180 days after frailty assessment using the RAI-clinical questionnaire (RAI-C).
RESULTS: In 410,715 patients from UPMC and 190,044 patients from VHA, the existing RAI-C scoring system demonstrated strong discrimination (c = 0.868 95% CI [0.864-0.872] for UPMC, 0.827 [0.822-0.832] for VHA) which improved modestly after recalibrating parameter weights (c = 0.872 95% CI [0.868-0.876], for UPMC, 0.839 [0.834-0.845] for VHA). Calibration improved slightly, especially at the extremes where the model tends to underpredict mortality, but little change was observed in the range around the threshold of frailty. Of note, the scoring weights associated with a cancer diagnosis demonstrated some multicollinearity-driven instability, but cancer remained the largest contributor to total score. Decision curve analysis demonstrated that reclassification of just a single additional patient as frail would require screening 1400-6000 patients with the recalibrated system, depending on the threshold score defining frailty, and after accounting for the harms of false-positive classification, weighted proportional to the odds at each threshold probability.
CONCLUSIONS: The RAI scoring system remains robust after a decade of widespread use without evidence of meaningful algorithmic drift. The minimal incremental improvement associated with recalibration does not justify the resources required to disseminate and implement a revised scoring system.
