title: TMEM106B C-Terminal fragment aggregation exacerbates α-synuclein and TDP-43 proteinopathy phenotypes.
abstract: Genetic variation in the human gene encoding the lysosomal transmembrane protein 106B (TMEM106B) drives risk of neurodegenerative dementia. A C-terminal fragment of TMEM106B (TMEM CT) accumulates in lesions across neurodegenerative disease, potentially contributing to neurotoxicity and hampering efficacy of therapeutic interventions. Previously, we developed the first transgenic organism model of TMEM CT neuronal aggregation in Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans). We demonstrated that TMEM CT neuronal aggregation drives severe neuronal dysfunction and neuronal loss. To investigate the potential synergistic interaction of TMEM CT aggregation with other types of aggregated neurotoxic proteinopathies occurring in dementia, we assessed neuronal degeneration and pathogenic protein accumulation in bigenic C. elegans expressing TMEM CT and other key proteinopathies of neurodegeneration including a-synuclein, tau, and TAR DNA binding protein 43 (TDP-43). Our results showed strong neurotoxic synergy of TMEM106B with TDP-43 or α-synuclein. However, we detected only mild synergy between TMEM106B and tau. This work provides evidence in support of TMEM CT aggregation as a significant participant in the neurodegenerative process attributed to other toxic protein aggregates. The work also highlights the importance of considering secondary proteinopathy contributions including TMEM CT aggregation when developing interventions against primary TDP-43 or α-synuclein proteinopathies.

title: Prediction of First and Recurrent Falls in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally validate prediction models for next-year falls in Parkinson's disease (PD), and to evaluate the incremental value of imaging and fluid biomarkers.
METHODS: We developed models in Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) to predict next-year falls with external validation in University of Pennsylvania (UPenn) cohorts. We evaluated incident falls among visits without current or prior falls and recurrent falls among visits with current falls. We calculated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and development-derived risk strata.
RESULTS: The incident model, comprising Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale Part III, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, and Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS), was developed in 773 visit-pairs and validated in 589 visit-pairs. AUROC was 0.704 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.653-0.750) in PPMI and 0.630 (95% CI = 0.564-0.687) in UPenn. Incident fall risk increased from 7.1 to 18.5% across low- to high-risk groups in UPenn. The recurrent model, comprising Hoehn and Yahr (H&Y), GDS, and Symbol Digit Modalities Test, was developed in 302 visit-pairs and validated in 137 visit-pairs. AUROC was 0.683 (95% CI = 0.623-0.753) in PPMI and 0.641 (95% CI = 0.538-0.732) in UPenn. Recurrent fall rates increased from 22.2 to 65.0% across low- to high-risk groups in UPenn. Exploratory biomarker augmentation modestly improved discrimination beyond clinical models in PPMI, but not in external validation, where estimates were imprecise.
INTERPRETATION: Clinical measures may identify next-year fall risk in PD with moderate discrimination, although performance attenuated in external validation. Exploratory biomarkers provided modest incremental value in development but not in external validation. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: Community health worker intervention to prevent incident type 2 diabetes: A cluster randomized trial
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) affects millions of Americans, and prediabetes significantly increases progression to T2DM. Community Health Workers (CHWs) may help prevent diabetes through behavioral interventions, but their effectiveness in real-world settings remains uncertain. We evaluated whether a CHW intervention prevents incident T2DM among adults with prediabetes. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Pragmatic, cluster-randomized controlled trial in primary care clinics at the Veterans Affairs NY Harbor Healthcare System (Manhattan) and Bellevue Hospital, New York City. The study included adults aged 18-75 years with HbA1c 5.7-6.4% and no prior diabetes or use of diabetes medications other than metformin. Primary care teams were cluster-randomized to a 12-month CHW program-health action plans, motivational interviewing, health education, and community referrals-versus usual care. The primary outcome was incident diabetes during up to 6 months' follow-up after the 12-month intervention. Secondary outcomes were changes in HbA1c, weight, blood pressure, lipids, and health care utilization. RESULTS: Incident diabetes occurred in 5.9% of intervention patients versus 4.3% of controls (risk difference 1.6%; 95% CI -3.68% to 4.10%). No significant differences were observed in HbA1c, weight, blood pressure, or lipids. The intervention group had more primary care encounters (77.6% vs 62.5%) and emergency department encounters (35.0% vs 29.1%). CONCLUSIONS: In this pragmatic trial, a 12-month CHW program did not reduce incident diabetes among adults with prediabetes but was associated with greater health care engagement (more primary care visits). More intensive or standardized CHW models should be tested to determine whether increased engagement translates into long-term metabolic benefit. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03006666, 12/27/2016). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03006666.

title: Evaluating the Diagnostic Utility of PRAME and CD34 Dual Staining in Fibrosarcomatous Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans
abstract: Abstract Preferentially expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) is a melanoma-associated antigen that has shown its utility in distinguishing melanoma from benign melanocytic nevi. However, it is reported to express in various other malignancies. Fibrosarcomatous dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (FS-DFSP) is a high-grade variant of conventional dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (C-DFSP), characterized by increased cellularity, mitotic activity, and nuclear atypia, with a higher risk of metastasis. Distinguishing FS-DFSP from C-DFSP can be challenging, particularly in cases with ambiguous morphological features. Immunohistochemically, most cases of C-DFSP show diffuse and strong cytoplasmic expression of CD34. Nonetheless, there may be diminished or absent CD34 expressions in FS-DFSP. We present a case of a 49-year-old man with FS-DFSP confirmed by COL1A1:PDGFB fusion, demonstrating a loss of CD34 and positive PRAME expression. This case signifies the potential utility of the CD34-PRAME dual-marker approach in diagnosing FS-DFSP, particularly in morphologically challenging cases. PRAME-positive cases of FS-DFSP can also be considered as a potential therapeutic target with PRAME-specific immunotherapy.

title: Neural shape models enable cohort-scale simulation of knee cartilage mechanics
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis affects over 350 million people worldwide, is a leading cause of disability, and carries substantial costs. Cartilage mechanical load is believed to play a critical role in osteoarthritis pathophysiology, yet clinical biomechanics research uses external measures of joint loading that do not capture tissue-level load. We developed a fully-automated pipeline that builds biomechanical knee models from a single MRI using deep learning-based segmentation and neural shape models, and elastic foundation contact to simulate gait. Applied to 756 knees from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, each simulated under the same 10 standardized gaits, the pipeline converged in 99.6% of 7,560 simulations. Medial tibial pressure decreased from healthy to incident to mild osteoarthritis as disease-related shape changes enlarged contact area, an effect reproduced in simulations of synthetic knees. Yet within knees, medial cartilage thinned fastest over six years in regions of highest pressure, with stronger relationships in incident and mild osteoarthritis knees. Automated simulations provided cohort-scale, tissue-level support for mechanical theories of osteoarthritis progression and a framework for prospectively quantifying cartilage load to guide mechanical interventions.

title: Standardizing ototoxicity monitoring for children treated with cisplatin: an urgent call to action.
abstract: Over the past 25 years, considerable progress has been made in identifying the prevalence, risk factors, functional impacts, and protective strategies for cisplatin-induced ototoxicity. Despite these advances, ototoxicity monitoring and audiologic management of children undergoing cisplatin treatment remains inconsistent across clinical settings. This position paper from the German-Indonesian Society for Medicine (DIGM) Ototoxicity Working Group reflects a consensus process based on expert opinion, supported by a narrative review of the scientific literature and recently published recommendations regarding audiologic management of children receiving cisplatin chemotherapy. We advocate that ototoxicity monitoring be recognized as standard of care for every child receiving cisplatin and incorporated into pediatric cancer treatment protocols. This paper proposes a minimum benchmark for the audiologic management of children undergoing cisplatin chemotherapy; a standard that can be readily implemented in most clinical settings worldwide.

title: Integrating Functional Cognitive Rehabilitation With Activity-Based Stroke Telerehabilitation: Intervention Design and Development Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many stroke survivors experience chronic cognitive deficits that, together with motor impairments, negatively impact well-being and daily function. Critically, poststroke cognitive deficits can interfere with successful engagement in rehabilitation programs aimed at improving participation in home and community activities. To address this issue, we developed a new telehealth intervention that integrates brief, functional cognitive rehabilitation (COG) into an existing upper extremity-focused, activity-based occupational therapy (OT) telerehabilitation program.
OBJECTIVE: To describe the development and specification of a telehealth intervention (COG+OT) that integrates functional cognitive rehabilitation into activity-based stroke telerehabilitation.
METHODS: COG+OT was developed using a multi-disciplinary, theory-informed process guided by principles of functional cognitive rehabilitation. It is reported according to the Template for Intervention Description and Replication checklist for rehabilitation (TIDieR-Rehab). The intervention was developed by a team with expertise in stroke rehabilitation from the fields of OT, neuropsychology, clinical psychology, and speech-language pathology. Cognitive rehabilitation content was adapted from an evidence-based compensatory strategy program and condensed into a brief "primer" format. The COG component was iteratively integrated into an existing upper-extremity, activity-based OT telerehabilitation program to support engagement and transfer of strategies to real-world functional tasks. In this paper, we describe the intervention structure, content, delivery, and tailoring procedures.
RESULTS: COG+OT is an 8-week, 13-session telehealth intervention delivered in three phases: (1) cognitive strategy training ("primer"; sessions 1-4), (2) review and guided application of strategies within OT activities (sessions 5-10), and (3) integration of strategies to support generalization to everyday contexts (sessions 11-13). The intervention combines individualized, strategy-based cognitive rehabilitation with goal-oriented OT using a titrated approach. Patient-facing materials, structured session workflows, and therapist-guided metacognitive strategies support tailoring and real-world application.
CONCLUSIONS: COG+OT is a theory-informed, user-centered intervention that provides a structured approach for integrating functional cognitive rehabilitation into stroke telerehabilitation. This work establishes a well-specified, replicable intervention model and supports future feasibility, effectiveness, and implementation studies.

title: Functional Deficits and Diffusion Tensor Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Olfactory and Vision Systems in the Alzheimer’s Disease Model of Aging GluN3A Knockout Mice
abstract: Sensory dysfunction, such as olfactory and visual deficits, is a notorious symptom during the progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related dementia (ADRD). The causal factor/s and structural disruptions underlying the sensory dysfunction in the AD/ADRD brain are not well understood. The NMDA receptor subunit GluN3A (NR3A) negatively regulates the receptor activity to uphold cellular Ca2+ homeostasis. In GluN3A knockout (KO) mice, animals spontaneously develop chronic neurodegenerative excitotoxicity, cognitive decline, and AD-like pathology. Using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), we examined neuronal network destruction together with sensory dysfunction in the GluN3A KO mouse. Specific attention was given to the selective vulnerability of the olfactory and visual nuclei, white matter injury in regional connections between subcortical centers and the cortex and hippocampus. Compared to age-matched wild-type (WT) controls (male), consistent with our early reports in younger ages, 18-month-old aging/aged GluN3A KO mice (male) suffered significant olfactory, visual and social deficits, accompanied by marked Aβ42 deposition in the brain. Ex vivo MR images of the GluN3A KO and control brains were acquired on the 7T MRI system, using a four-channel mouse array RF coil. High-resolution 3D T2-weighted RARE anatomical and DTI scans were performed. The DTI analysis revealed that GluN3A KO mice developed brain atrophy, involving significant damage in the white and gray matter of the olfactory and visual systems and impaired pathways among the superior colliculus, lateral geniculate nucleus, and the hippocampus and/or the cortex. This investigation disclosed a receptor-mediated neurodegeneration that explains sensory syndromes featured in a sporadic AD mouse model.

title: Low-fat diet reduces fatigue and alters serum metabolomic pathways in people with multiple sclerosis: a sub-study of a randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fatigue is one of the most common and disabling symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS). Dietary interventions have shown promise for fatigue reduction, but the metabolic mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated the effects of a low-fat diet on fatigue and serum metabolomic pathways in people with MS, focusing on lipid and amino-acid metabolism.
METHODS: This exploratory analysis used data from a 16-week, two-arm, randomized controlled trial in people with MS comparing a low-fat diet (intervention) with a waitlist (control) group that continued their usual diet. Serum metabolites and fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale, MFIS) were measured at baseline and week 16. Additional outcomes included dietary composition, adherence, body composition, and cardiometabolic biomarkers. Spearman rank correlations were used to examine associations between MFIS scores and individual metabolites. Metabolites were then grouped into biochemical super-pathways and sub-pathways for pathway-level summary. Group-level percentage changes in metabolites were also calculated.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven participants (16 intervention, 11 control) with complete data were included. Of the 986 metabolites detected, changes in MFIS scores were correlated to shifts in fatty acid (e.g., octadecenedioylcarnitine, cis-4-decenoate) and amino acid (e.g., phenol sulfate, phenylpyruvate) pathways. Over the 16-week study, several lipids decreased in the intervention group but increased in controls, consistent with modulation of mitochondrial fatty acid β-oxidation.
CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first study to explore the impact of a low-fat diet on serum metabolomic pathways in people with MS. These preliminary exploratory findings suggest that diet-induced modulation of lipid and amino acid metabolism may contribute to fatigue changes. The small sample size and inter-individual variability warrant cautious interpretation; replication in larger, adequately powered trials is needed.

title: CBFB-MYH11 directly activates TGFβ and PD-L1 to drive immune evasion in acute myeloid leukemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Core binding factor acute myeloid leukemia (CBF-AML) driven by the CBFB-MYH11 fusion oncogene is associated with high initial remission rates, yet 30%–50% of patients ultimately relapse. While immune evasion is a recognized hallmark of leukemia progression, the precise mechanisms orchestrated by the CBFB-MYH11 oncogene remain poorly understood. Furthermore, the role of transforming growth factor-beta (TGFβ) in hematological malignancies is highly controversial, often viewed as a tumor suppressor in early hematopoiesis rather than a driver of immune evasion.
METHODS: We used an inducible Cbfb-MYH11 knock-in mouse model and primary AML cell transplantation to profile the immune microenvironment during leukemogenesis. We integrated flow cytometry, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), CUT&RUN, luciferase reporter assay, ChIP-qPCR, and ChIP-Seq. Functional in vitro T-cell suppression assays and in vivo engraftment using Pdcd1 knockout (PD-1 KO) mice, and treatments with the anti-PD-L1 antibody, TGFβ receptor inhibitor galunisertib, and cytarabine were performed to evaluate immunotherapeutic vulnerabilities.
RESULTS: Leukemogenesis in the Cbfb-MYH11 model was accompanied by profound T-cell suppression and exhaustion, and the AML cells effectively inhibited T-cell proliferation in co-culture. Transcriptomic profiling identified marked upregulation of Cd274 (PD-L1) and Tgfb1 in AML cells. Mechanistically, CUT&RUN and ChIP-Seq demonstrated that the CBFβ-SMMHC fusion oncoprotein and its co-factor RUNX1 directly bind to the promoter regions of CD274 and TGFB1 to transcriptionally activate their expression in both murine and human AML models. While genetic ablation of PD-1 in host mice provided only limited survival benefits, pharmacological blockade of TGFβ effectively restored T cell function and delayed AML progression. Importantly, combining cytarabine with galunisertib provided superior disease control, reversed T cell exhaustion, and significantly prolonged survival compared with chemotherapy alone, which can be further enhanced by targeting PD-L1/PD-1.
CONCLUSIONS: The CBFB-MYH11 oncogene directly orchestrates an immunosuppressive microenvironment by transcriptionally activating PD-L1 and TGFβ. These findings provide more insight into the role of TGFβ in CBF-AML, establishing it as a primary, tumor-derived immunosuppressor directly driven by the fusion oncogene. This provides a strong mechanistic rationale for incorporating TGFβ blockade into standard chemotherapy and immune checkpoint blockade regimens to restore anti-leukemic immunity and prevent relapse.

title: Large-scale integrated single-cell analysis reveals molecular subtypes and microenvironmental remodeling in cutaneous T cell lymphoma
abstract: Cutaneous T cell lymphoma (CTCL) comprises a clinically and molecularly heterogeneous group of skin-homing non-Hodgkin lymphomas for which robust biomarkers remain limited. Prior single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies have provided important insights into CTCL biology, but many of these prior studies have been limited by small sample sizes and focused on niche questions of interest. Additionally, many studies have suffered from pseudoreplication, resulting in inflated test statistics and reduced external validity. Here, we assembled and integrated scRNA-seq data spanning 244 unique samples and 132 patients across CTCL, healthy control (HC), and benign inflammatory dermatoses (BID) conditions, generating the most diverse atlas of CTCL to date. Following identification of malignant cell populations and heterogeneous, within-sample gene expression alterations, we applied pseudobulk aggregation and robust linear mixed-effects modeling to nominate recurrent changes across this highly heterogeneous patient cohort. Interrogation of the skin microenvironment identified significant compositional and cell type-specific expression changes in CTCL lesions as compared to control lesions and across clinical stages of disease. Finally, we used unbiased clustering to identify stable, molecularly defined subtypes of disease that were predictive of outcome in an independent dataset. Together, this study provides a rigorous analysis of the most diverse scRNA-seq dataset of CTCL ever compiled, nominating specific alterations in cell type composition and gene expression across malignant cell and microenvironmental populations with significant clinical implications.

title: Finerenone-Empagliflozin Combination Therapy in Apparent Resistant Hypertension: A CONFIDENCE Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (aTRH) is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with type 2 diabetes and predicts worse outcomes. Spironolactone, the established fourth-line agent, is limited by hyperkalemia in CKD.
OBJECTIVES: This analysis assessed whether finerenone plus empagliflozin lowers blood pressure (BP) meaningfully in aTRH, and whether aTRH modifies these agents' efficacy and safety.
METHODS: Post hoc analysis of CONFIDENCE (NCT05254002), a double-blind randomized trial of finerenone, empagliflozin, or both in CKD with albuminuria and type 2 diabetes. aTRH was BP ≥130/80 mm Hg on 3 antihypertensive drugs, or ≥4 drugs regardless of BP. Mixed models and logistic regression identified predictors of BP response.
RESULTS: Of the 796 participants, 307 (39%) had aTRH; they were older, more obese, and had more atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, higher albuminuria, and higher systolic BP (140.9 vs 131.5 mm Hg) but similar estimated glomerular filtration rate (53 vs 55 mL/min/1.73 m2). Combination therapy lowered systolic BP more than either monotherapy. Independent predictors of a ≥10 mm Hg systolic BP fall were aTRH (OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.08-2.25) and higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR: 1.15 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: 1.05-1.26); diuretic use and albuminuria were not. The aTRH effect was treatment-independent (interaction P = 0.21). Adverse events were more frequent with aTRH (63.8% vs 51.1%), yet on combination therapy hyperkalemia was less frequent (11.2% vs 17.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: aTRH affected approximately 40% of participants and marked a higher-risk phenotype responsive to finerenone-empagliflozin, with BP reductions comparable to spironolactone but without the excess hyperkalemia that limits its use in CKD.

title: NOTIFY-DISCUSS: Patient and clinician perspectives on opportunistic screening for coronary artery calcification using artificial intelligence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: NOTIFY-1 was a quality improvement study that utilized a validated deep learning algorithm to perform opportunistic coronary artery calcification (CAC) screening on previously acquired non-gated chest CT scans, significantly increasing statin prescribing and coronary artery disease testing. NOTIFY-DISCUSS explored patient and clinician perceptions of this real-world clinical application of an artificial intelligence (AI) tool.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews and focus groups were conducted with n = 20 NOTIFY-1 participants (n = 11 patients, n = 9 clinicians). All patients had received their incidental CAC results prior to interviews. Topics included attitudes toward AI use in medicine, experiences with this AI-assisted tool, preferences for communicating incidental findings, and perceived barriers to guideline-directed statin prescribing. Transcripts were coded by a qualitative researcher in NVivo and reviewed by a qualitative expert; analysis of transcripts utilized thematic analysis and consensus approaches.
RESULTS: Most participants appreciated the notification tool for providing compelling personalized data to support shared decision-making and behavior change around statin initiation. Participants also noted its potential to improve identification of incidental findings and improve health equity. However, several themes indicated concerns: consent to the use of AI tools; data rights, usage, and security; the time-burden of discussing and contextualizing incidental CAC findings; potential for unintended harm; and need for timely notifications.
CONCLUSIONS: NOTIFY-DISCUSS offered a unique opportunity to assess perceptions of an implemented AI-driven opportunistic cardiovascular screening tool. Concerns around consent, security, burden and unintended harms will be essential to address when designing and deploying future AI tools, and patient perspectives should be included in ongoing monitoring efforts.

title: Pentoxifylline for chronic kidney disease in people with diabetes: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Pentoxifylline is an inexpensive anti-inflammatory agent tested in diabetic kidney disease for four decades; prior meta-analyses report reduced albuminuria. Whether it is secure, extends to kidney function, or reaches hard outcomes is unclear; we hypothesized the surrogate evidence might be conclusive and the hard-outcome evidence not.
METHODS: We reviewed randomized trials of oral pentoxifylline in diabetic kidney disease to June 2026, without language restriction. Co-primary surrogate outcomes were albuminuria (ratio of means) and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) change (mean difference); the primary hard outcome was end-stage kidney disease or death (risk ratio). We pooled with random-effects models, assessed risk of bias with RoB 2, and report a prediction interval and trial sequential analysis with every estimate.
RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included, 32 contributing data. Albuminuria fell by about a third (ratio of means 0.69, 95% CI 0.50-0.94; 22 studies contributing 23 comparisons), but heterogeneity was extreme (I2 97%), the prediction interval 0.15-3.10, and only 53% of the required information had accrued, with no boundary crossed. Over ≥ 12 months, GFR changed 4.49 mL/min/1.73 m2 more favorably with pentoxifylline than with control (0.84-8.14; 5 studies contributing 5 comparisons); in two trials at low or some-concerns risk of bias it was 2.96 (-15.34 to 21.26), with 11% of the required information accrued. For end-stage kidney disease or death, 29 events in 6 studies contributing 7 comparisons gave a risk ratio of 0.90 (0.46-1.77), 3% of that required. Gastrointestinal adverse events were three times as common (3.00, 1.94-4.64); serious ones were not (0.83, 0.56-1.22).
CONCLUSIONS: Pentoxifylline reduces albuminuria, but the effect is heterogeneous, depends on which trials are counted, and may not reappear in a new trial. Kidney failure and death have scarcely been tested. The priority is an adequately powered, long-term trial reporting hard endpoints; gastrointestinal intolerance should be anticipated.

title: Movement-specific effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation over premotor and parietal cortices after stroke
abstract: Abstract Background Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has been proposed to support post-stroke motor recovery, but the response may depend on the task and motor-network status. We aimed to compare how premotor and parietal stimulation affects performance across reach directions with different movement demands, in preparation for therapeutic application of TMS. Methods 16 participants with chronic subcortical stroke performed planar reaches with the KINARM exoskeleton toward distal and proximal targets. Before movement, a 10-Hz triple-pulse TMS train was delivered over bilateral dorsal or ventral premotor cortex (PMd, PMv) or dorsomedial posterior parietal cortex (PPC) at subthreshold and suprathreshold intensities. The parietal midline was used as the control target. Participant-level bootstrap confidence intervals assessed changes in trajectory straightness and smoothness relative to the control target and differences between reach directions. We compared motor-network activity and connectivity using task-based and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from participants with stroke and neurologically intact controls. To explore response variability, we tested associations between TMS response and motor impairment, resting-state connectivity, and the change in task-evoked activity at the stimulated region from planning to movement. Results Suprathreshold PMd and PPC stimulation in both hemispheres improved trajectory straightness or smoothness during distal reaches relative to the control target. Suprathreshold contralesional PMd stimulation increased trajectory deviation and reduced smoothness during proximal reaches. Baseline performance during distal reaches was more closely related to motor impairment, and contralesional PMd effects were more favorable during distal than proximal reaches across all kinematic measures. Participants with stroke showed lower bilateral PMv activation during movement and stronger interhemispheric PPC connectivity. Only the change in task-evoked activity at the stimulated region from planning to movement was related to TMS response. Smaller changes relative to controls were associated with more favorable kinematic effects during distal reaches. Conclusions Movements more affected after stroke were the most responsive to this type of stimulation. The response to TMS was also associated with task-evoked activity differences at the stimulated region between movement planning and execution. Neuromodulation may therefore be most effective when designed around both the pathophysiology of the cortical target and the type of movement. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04286516 . Registered 21 January 2020.

title: Hydroxychloroquine Cardiotoxicity Mimicking Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis in a Patient With HFpEF.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is an immunomodulatory drug used in systemic lupus erythematosus and other rheumatologic disorders, with rare but potentially severe cardiotoxic effects.
CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction presented with subacute worsening chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, and neuropathy. Electrocardiogram showed low voltage; echocardiogram revealed moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with reduced global longitudinal strain without apical sparing. Coronary angiography was normal. Technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy showed focal grade 2 uptake. Endomyocardial biopsy revealed widespread myocyte hypertrophy and lysosomal curvilinear bodies consistent with HCQ cardiotoxicity.
DISCUSSION: HCQ is a long-term medication used in connective tissue diseases. Patients with rheumatologic conditions are at increased risk for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of HCQ use. Recognition of insidious organ toxicity can be challenging. HCQ toxicity can cause infiltrative pathology and mimic transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Endomyocardial biopsy is key for definitive diagnosis.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In patients with an equivocally positive technetium-99m pyrophosphate scan and chronic HCQ use, endomyocardial biopsy should be considered to differentiate drug toxicity from transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.

title: Obesity and Pathologic Response to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in Head and Neck Cancer: Preliminary Results From a Pilot Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations between obesity and pathologic response to neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted at a single tertiary academic center. We identified 42 patients with HNSCC treated with neoadjuvant ICI with or without chemotherapy. Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m2. The primary outcome was any pathologic response (partial, major, or complete response). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess associations between obesity and response, adjusting for smoking status and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status. BMI was also analyzed as a continuous variable. Adjusted predicted probabilities of response were estimated across BMI.
RESULTS: Seven patients (17%) were obese. Obese patients had lower rates of pathologic response compared to non-obese patients (29% vs. 69%). On multivariable analysis, obesity was associated with decreased odds of response (OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02-0.72; p = 0.021). Increasing BMI was independently associated with lower odds of response, with a 15% decrease per 1 kg/m2 increase [OR 0.85 (0.72-0.99), p = 0.039]. Adjusted predicted probability of response declined from ~85% at BMI 18 to 25% at BMI 40. In a subset of patients receiving immunotherapy alone, increasing BMI remained associated with decreased response [OR 0.66 (0.44-0.99), p = 0.045].
CONCLUSION: In a small pilot cohort, obesity was associated with decreased pathologic response to neoadjuvant ICI in HNSCC. These findings contrast with the "obesity paradox" observed in recurrent/metastatic settings and suggest the relationship between metabolic state and immunotherapy response may be context-dependent. Further validation in larger cohorts is needed.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

title: Implementation of a self-care intervention for patients with heart failure discharged from the emergency department: implementation findings from a multicenter hybrid type 2 implementation study
abstract: Patients with acute heart failure (AHF) discharged directly from emergency departments (EDs) are at high risk for 30-day revisits, readmissions, and mortality. Most transitional care interventions have focused on inpatient settings, thereby excluding this vulnerable population. Our team developed a self-care coaching intervention called Get with the Guidelines in Emergency Department Patients with Heart Failure (GUIDED-HF) to address care transitions for patients with AHF discharged from EDs, aiming to improve patient self-management and clinical outcomes. We describe the implementation outcomes of a large hybrid type 2 study conducted across six EDs in two geographically diverse healthcare systems, guided by Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance (RE-AIM) and Care Transitions Intervention frameworks. We employed a multifaceted implementation strategy that included a best practice alert in the electronic health record, identification of local champions, educational meetings, and implementation of audit and feedback mechanisms. Data was collected through ED staff surveys, electronic health records, and monthly tracking sheets to assess implementation outcomes of reach, adoption, implementation, and maintenance. Clinical effectiveness is reported elsewhere. The study reached 37% of eligible patients (67% in one healthcare system, 14% in the other), with 47.5% of ED encounters resulting in adoption of GUIDED-HF. Reported median scores for implementation climate and staff involvement were higher at 24 months when compared with baseline scores. Feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness ratings were consistently high over the 24-month study period. Lessons learned include matching implementation strategies to specific contextual factors; we found this critical for overcoming barriers and enhancing implementation success. Variability in implementation outcomes across the examined healthcare systems underscores the importance of tailoring implementation approaches to local contexts and involving stakeholders in strategy development to maximize intervention adoption and effectiveness. Our hybrid design implementation study demonstrated an evidence-based approach to implementing a self-care intervention for patients with AHF in ED settings, contributing to the limited knowledge base in this area. Future research should focus on scaling GUIDED-HF across diverse healthcare settings, addressing specific implementation barriers, and refining implementation strategies. n/a.

title: PRKCZ missense variant rs202071893 as a potential genetic marker for prostate cancer
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a multifocal and heterogeneous disease. Genetic predisposition accounts for more than 50% of PCa risk. Missense single-nucleotide polymorphisms can influence disease susceptibility by altering protein structure, function, and regulatory interactions. Protein kinase C Zeta (PRKCZ) regulates various cellular pathways, and its aberrant expression is associated with cancer metastasis and chemoresistance. Genetic variations in PRKCZ may lead to cancer onset and progression. Moreover, current PCa testing modalities are limited in their ability to predict tumor heterogeneity and patient outcomes. Therefore, the current study aimed to determine the genetic association of the PRKCZ missense variant rs202071893 with PCa risk and progression. DNA was extracted from blood samples of PCa patients and healthy control individuals using the phenol-chloroform protocol. Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium (HWE) was evaluated in the control group to assess genetic stability in the studied population. QUANTO was used to calculate the power of the current study. Genotyping was performed via mutation-specific Tetra-ARMS PCR. Multiple genetic models (allele, codominant, dominant, recessive, overdominant) were applied to comprehensively assess the association between rs202071893 and PCa risk and development. Statistical analyses, such as the chi-square and Fisher’s exact tests, were performed to assess the association of rs202071893 with PCa risk and clinical parameters, including tumor stage, metastasis, and family history. The raw p-values were adjusted using a Bonferroni correction to reduce Type 1 error from multiple comparisons. The genotype distribution in the control group conformed to HWE ( p = 0.4323). rs202071893 was significantly associated with increased PCa risk and development under the recessive (OR = 5.108, RR = 2.167, p < 0.0005) allele (OR = 2.652, RR = 1.666, p = 0.0075) and codominant models (OR = 3.654, RR = 2.754, p = 0.0025), indicating variant homozygous GG and variant allele G as risk genetic variations. However, heterozygous AG showed a significant protective effect under the overdominant genetic model (OR = 0.2404, RR = 0.4454, p < 0.0005). Moreover, a non-significant association in subgroup analysis may represent a type II error due to a small subgroup sample size following stratification. The study findings highlighted that rs202071893 could serve as a non-invasive genetic marker for PCa, offering novel insights into tumor biology and informing future therapeutic strategies against PCa.

title: Surgical bypasses to arteries of the foot
abstract: Author’s revised review of surgical technique. Pedal bypass remains an important option for limb salvage in selected patients with severe peripheral artery disease, particularly when an adequate pedal target and autogenous vein conduit are available. Durable outcomes depend on careful target selection, high-quality angiography and attention to the technical details of distal bypass construction. This chapter reviews published outcomes of dorsalis pedis and pedal-branch bypasses, then emphasizes practical strategies for identifying pedal targets with angiography and Doppler ultrasonography. Operative planning, vein assessment, exposure of pedal arteries, graft tunnelling, construction of the distal anastomosis and completion assessment are discussed in detail. Post-operative care and the prevention and management of wound complications are also reviewed. This revised version includes an explicit disclosure of generative AI assistance in document preparation and illustrative image editing. Generative AI was not used to modify any angiograms or intraoperative anatomy images. Material from an earlier version was presented at the 46th Annual Northwestern Vascular Symposium in December 2022 and published in the accompanying course textbook; this deposit is the author’s revised version.

title: Retrospective Lung-RADS v2022 Characterization of Fatal Lung Cancer Cases in the National Lung Screening Trial.
abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Persistent lung cancer mortality despite screening is multifactorial. Characterizing computed tomography (CT) findings preceding fatal lung cancer may identify imaging features and screening challenges that warrant further study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, outcome-enriched case series nested within the 26,722-participant low-dose computed tomography arm of the National Lung Screening Trial. Among 359 participants who died of lung cancer within the prespecified interval, exclusions for positive baseline screening (n = 186), incomplete screening (n = 28), withdrawal/declined screening (n = 19), unavailable CTs (n = 6), or three negative screens followed by death 2+ years after the final screen (n = 29) yielded 91 participants. Screening CTs were retrospectively assessed using the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) v2022. Four thoracic radiologists independently reviewed visible-in-retrospect nodules and adjudicated whether they met criteria for suspicion.
RESULTS: Of 91 participants, 22 (24%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 17%-34%) had visible-in-retrospect nodules considered suspicious under Lung-RADS v2022 ("missed"), 16 (18%; 95% CI, 11%-27%) had visible nodules not meeting suspicion criteria ("not callable"), 50 (55%; 95% CI, 45%-65%) had no visible-in-retrospect nodule, and 3 (3.3%) were inconclusive. Missed nodules were frequently juxtapleural (41%), obscured (50%), or irregularly bordered (68%); not-callable nodules were frequently <6 mm (75%), juxtapleural (56%), or irregularly bordered (56%).
CONCLUSION: In this selected fatal-case series, small and juxtapleural nodules were common among visible nodules not meeting Lung-RADS v2022 suspicion criteria. These findings warrant evaluation in representative screening populations and should not be interpreted as estimates of population-level Lung-RADS performance.

title: Two dimensions of pain acceptance: divergent links to opioid misuse and readiness to change
abstract: More than 13 million Americans remain on long-term opioid therapy for chronic pain (CP) despite well-established risks and no quality evidence of long-term benefits. Pain acceptance, defined as willingness to experience pain and engage in valued life activities despite pain, has been consistently linked to improved pain outcomes and more recently identified as a protective factor against opioid misuse. This study examined the relationship between both factors of pain acceptance and opioid misuse behaviors and readiness to change opioid use among opioid-using individuals with CP. A community sample of adults with a variety of CP conditions using opioid medications ( N = 157) were recruited through ResearchMatch.org. Participants completed self-report questionnaires, including the Chronic Pain Acceptance Questionnaire (CPAQ), Prescription Opioid Misuse Index (POMI), Brief Pain Inventory (BPI), and single-item Visual Analog Scale (VAS) measures of readiness and confidence to discontinue opioid use. Two CPAQ subscales (activity engagement and pain willingness) and pain severity were entered into a logistic regression predicting POMI score and multiple linear regression models predicting readiness and confidence to reduce opioid use. All three models were significant ( p < 0.05). Activity engagement was associated with greater odds of opioid misuse, whereas pain willingness was associated with lower odds of misuse. In contrast, higher activity engagement and lower pain willingness predicted higher readiness and confidence to taper opioid use. Findings demonstrate nuances in the dimensions of pain acceptance and support the value of further exploring activity engagement and pain willingness in efforts to reduce opioid-related risks.

title: Six-Month Trajectories of Symptoms, Perceived Recovery, and Functional Health in Ecuadorian Adults with COVID-19.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Most longitudinal evidence on post-acute COVID-19 comes from hospitalized patients in high-income countries and less is known about community samples in low- and middle-income settings. This study examined changes in perceived recovery, symptom burden, general health perception, and functional difficulties over six months in Ecuadorian adults with confirmed COVID-19. Methods: In a prospective observational cohort in Quito, Ecuador, 120 adults with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 were assessed at baseline (within four weeks of diagnosis) and again three and six months after the baseline assessment; 91 completed all three assessments. The Spanish-language ISARIC follow-up survey covered 39 symptoms, perceived recovery, the EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS, and six Washington Group functioning items rated retrospectively for the pre-COVID period and currently. Analyses were exploratory and descriptive, and all p-values are nominal and unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Results: Participants' perceived complete recovery improved (χ2 = 15.24, p < 0.001), as did perceived general health (F(2, 178) = 5.80, p = 0.004). Chest pain, palpitations, muscle weakness, confusion, tinnitus, and diarrhea declined over follow-up. At six months, 37.4% still reported headaches, 35.2% fatigue, 35.2% confusion or inattention, and 25.3% sleep disturbance. Among EQ-5D-5L domains, only pain/discomfort improved (p = 0.012). Vision, walking, memory, and communication declined from pre-COVID to baseline and improved between baseline and six months; pre-COVID and six-month levels were not compared directly. Conclusions: Recovery over six months was gradual but incomplete, with a substantial minority reporting ongoing or recurrent symptoms at six months. These findings describe post-acute symptom burden following confirmed COVID-19 rather than formally diagnosed post-COVID-19 condition.

title: A New Application of 64 CuCl 2 PET / CT : Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma
abstract: ABSTRACT Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour‐bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64 CuCl 2 and underwent whole‐body PET/CT imaging. Semi‐quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour‐to‐muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64 Cu‐avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour‐to‐muscle ratios across tumour‐bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

title: Levodopa Preferentially Reorganizes Dorsal Subthalamic Activity in Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: Abstract Background Dopamine replacement reshapes subthalamic activity in Parkinson’s disease, but whether this response reflects anatomically organized network reconfiguration remains unclear. Objectives To determine whether levodopa preferentially reorganizes dorsal subthalamic spectral activity and cortico-subthalamic directionality. Methods Twelve participants undergoing bilateral subthalamic deep brain stimulation contributed 30 contacts (14 dorsal, 16 ventral). Recordings obtained OFF and ON medication underwent spectral parameterization and multiband state-space analysis. Simultaneous electroencephalography in six participants enabled assessment of directional cortico-subthalamic coupling using the phase slope index. Results Levodopa suppressed beta power more strongly dorsally than ventrally (−2.473 versus −0.120 dB; p=0.0438). Dorsal theta power increased, with a trend toward an increase after baseline normalization (p=0.07). Dorsal contacts exhibited greater theta–beta (+5.904 versus +1.610 dB; p=0.006) and gamma–beta (+2.516 versus +0.384 dB; p=0.0188) state-space shifts, principally driven by beta suppression. Gamma changes did not differ regionally. Concurrently, dorsal low-beta and beta interactions shifted toward cortical leading at selected electrodes, whereas ventral responses were less consistent. Conclusions Levodopa produces a topographically organized subthalamic response, combining preferential dorsal beta suppression with altered cortico-subthalamic directionality. These findings position contact anatomy as a key consideration in characterizing dopaminergic network responses and motivate clinical validation of spatially informed multiband biomarkers for adaptive stimulation.

title: Thyroid Involvement in Laryngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma-Should it be Spared?
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence and predictors of thyroid gland invasion in Hispanic patients with laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma undergoing total laryngectomy and to assess thyroidectomy-associated comorbidities.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cross-sectional review.
SETTING: University District Hospital, Puerto Rico Medical Center, San Juan, PR.
METHODS: Records of adults with laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma who underwent total laryngectomy from 2009 to 2022 were reviewed. Tumor characteristics were correlated with histopathologic thyroid gland invasion, and postoperative hypocalcemia was documented. Categorical variables were compared using Fisher's exact or Pearson's chi-square tests, with effect size reported by Cramér's V; continuous variables were analyzed with the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test.
RESULTS: Of 105 patients, 8 (7.6%) had thyroid gland invasion. Tumors with invasion were larger (5.0 ± 1.3 vs 3.3 ± 1.4 cm; P = .003) and were associated with thyroid cartilage invasion (100% vs 54.6%; P = .020). Patients with invasion underwent total thyroidectomy more often (75.0% vs 28.9%; P = .013). Postoperative hypocalcemia occurred in 41.9% (44/105) of patients overall and was more frequent after total than after partial thyroidectomy (79.4% vs 23.9%; P < .001). Intravenous calcium replacement was required in 19.0% (20/105) of patients, more often after total thyroidectomy (47.1% vs 5.6%; P < .001).
CONCLUSION: Thyroid gland invasion was uncommon but associated with larger tumors and thyroid cartilage invasion. Total thyroidectomy carried a higher risk and greater severity of hypocalcemia. These findings support selective thyroid management during total laryngectomy and provide evidence from an underrepresented Hispanic population.

title: Preliminary accuracy, inter- and intra-rater reliability of a 4-point cervical artery dissection diagnostic decision support tool in an ambulatory setting using real and simulated cases: a quality improvement project.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical artery dissection (CeAD) is a rare but life-threatening condition that commonly presents with non-specific symptoms such as neck and head pain, complicating early recognition in ambulatory care settings. The CeAD diagnostic decision support tool (DDST) is a 4-item assessment designed to identify patients that should be referred for advanced diagnostic work-up to rule out CeAD; however, its utility in ambulatory settings has not been established.
METHODS: This quality improvement project aimed to evaluate the accuracy, inter-rater reliability, and intra-rater reliability of chiropractors applying the CeAD DDST using clinical vignettes simulating a typical ambulatory encounter before deploying the DDST broadly as part of the clinical workflow. Five experienced chiropractors assessed 40 standardized clinical vignettes. CeAD-positive cases (n = 10) were derived from published imaging-confirmed ambulatory care case reports. CeAD-negative cases (n = 30) were developed using generative artificial intelligence and refined by senior authors to reflect common conditions encountered in chiropractic practice. Raters independently assessed cases with the DDST (score 0-4), with a cutoff score of ≥ 3 recommending referral for advanced diagnostic work-up in two rounds, beginning November 11, 2025 and January 07, 2026, with a two-week capture period. Accuracy, inter-rater reliability, and intra-rater reliability were assessed.
RESULTS: Accuracy in identification ranged from 72.5% to 95.0% across raters and rounds. False positives and negatives were present across raters in both rounds, with false positives being more prevalent. Inter-rater reliability was moderate to substantial in both rounds (Round 1: κ = 0.609, 95% CI 0.432-0.806, Round 2: κ = 0.540, 95% CI 0.365-0.735). Intra-rater reliability ranged from moderate to almost perfect agreement (range 0.457-0.931).
CONCLUSIONS: The CeAD DDST demonstrated moderate to good accuracy and reliability among chiropractors in a simulated ambulatory setting. The presence of false negatives and inter-rater reliability falling below recommended benchmarks preclude recommendation for implementation at this time. Iterative refinement informed by end-user input and prospective ambulatory testing is warranted prior to clinical adoption of the CeAD DDST. Future evaluations should include prospective studies using real clinical data to better represent real-world settings.

title: Screening for Geriatric Problems in Older Adults Receiving Hemodialysis Using a Self-Administered Battery.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Older adults receiving hemodialysis experience geriatric problems that affect quality of life and contribute to high healthcare utilization but are often underrecognized in dialysis care. Scalable approaches to identifying these problems are needed. This study evaluated the agreement between a self-administered screening battery and a geriatrician telehealth evaluation and assessed the feasibility of implementing the screening battery in dialysis clinics.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Participants aged ≥55 receiving hemodialysis completed the Geriatric screen for Older adults receiving Dialysis (GOLD), a screening battery assessing seven geriatric problems: depression, anxiety, functional impairment, cognitive impairment, falls risk, limited social support, and low nutritional status, followed by a blinded geriatrician telehealth evaluation. Intra-problem agreement between the GOLD and geriatrician evaluation was assessed using Cohen's κ, and analyses evaluated alternative screening thresholds. Acceptability and feasibility of the GOLD were evaluated through participant and staff surveys.
RESULTS: The cohort included 50 participants [76% (n=38) Black race, 62% (n=31) male, 16% (n=8) Hispanic/Latino ethnicity] with a mean (SD) age of 68 (7.8) years and a median dialysis vintage of 3.5 [IQR (1, 12.5)] years. Geriatric problems were common, including fall risk (78% geriatrician; 90% GOLD), functional impairment (58% geriatrician; 44% GOLD), and low nutritional status (50% geriatrician; 40% GOLD). Agreement between the GOLD and geriatrician evaluation was substantial for anxiety (κ=0.74), functional impairment (κ=0.65), low nutritional status (κ=0.64), and limited social support (κ=0.65), but not for cognitive impairment, falls risk, or depression. Most participants (37 of 45) reported the GOLD was easy to complete, and a minority (16 of 50) required assistance.
CONCLUSION: The GOLD demonstrated agreement with geriatrician evaluation for many geriatric problems and was feasible to implement in dialysis clinics. These findings suggest potential utility for scalable geriatric screening in dialysis care, although further work is needed to confirm these findings in larger cohorts and to refine screening for cognitive impairment and other domains.

title: Subjective Cognitive Concerns and Cognitive Trajectories in Parkinson's Disease: Biomarker Impact
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the relationship of subjective cognitive concerns (SCC) with biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease (AD), neurodegeneration, and Parkinson's disease (PD) and domain-specific cognitive trajectories among cognitively unimpaired persons with de novo PD. METHOD: Cognitively unimpaired participants with SCC (n = 294) and without SCC (n = 857) from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative underwent neuropsychological testing, lumbar puncture, and dopamine transporter (DaT) single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT). Multiple regression analyses examined SCC associations with biomarkers of AD (CSF phosphorylated-tau181/amyloid-beta42 [p-tau181/Aβ42]), neurodegeneration (CSF neurofilament light [NfL]), and PD (DaT-SPECT in contralateral putamen). Linear mixed effects models examined 5-year cognitive trajectories (working memory, category fluency, learning and memory, visuospatial functioning, processing speed) by SCC status and the extent to which biomarkers of AD, neurodegeneration, and PD moderated these associations. RESULT: At baseline, the SCC group had higher p-tau181/Aβ42 (FDR-adjusted p = 0.004) than the No SCC group, while NfL and DaT-SPECT did not differ. Relative to the No SCC group, the SCC group exhibited faster decline in learning (FDR-adjusted p = 0.016), delayed recall (FDR-adjusted p = 0.016) and working memory (FDR-adjusted p = 0.016). AD and PD-related biomarkers moderated cognitive trajectories: SCC in combination with (1) higher CSF p-tau181/Aβ42 was related to steeper declines in working memory (FDR-adjusted p = 0.032); and (2) lower DaT-SPECT was related to steeper declines in delayed recall (FDR-adjusted p = 0.032). INTERPRETATION: SCC is related to AD biomarkers and accelerated cognitive decline in the earliest stages of PD. SCC may serve as an early marker of cognitive risk, especially among persons with greater AD- or PD-related burden.

title: A Small-Molecule TrkB Agonist Promotes Synaptic Resilience Against Aβ and Tau Oligomers and Mitigates Alterations in TrkB-Akt and Fyn Signaling.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathogenic amyloid-beta and tau oligomers (oAβ, oTau) drive synaptic degeneration and cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), expressed in neurons and glia, supports synaptic integrity in AD-affected regions. We tested whether PTX-BD4-3, a small-molecule TrkB partial agonist, promotes neuroprotective signaling, reduces degenerative signaling, and prevents synaptic loss in an AD mouse model and hippocampal neurons exposed to oAβ or oTau.
METHODS: Cultured hippocampal neurons were treated with oAβ or oTau ± PTX-BD4-3. Effects on synaptic proteins (±TrkB-blocking antibody), spine density, and Fyn, NR2B, and tau phosphorylation as well as tau oligomerization were assessed. Two cohorts of APPL/S mice, 5 and 12 months of age, received intraperitoneal PTX-BD4-3 or vehicle for 3 months, followed by assessment of synaptic proteins, dendritic spines, TrkB signaling, and Y-maze analysis.
RESULTS: In vitro, PTX-BD4-3 prevented oAβ-induced synaptic marker loss in a TrkB-dependent manner, reduced phosphorylation of Fyn, NR2B, and tau, suppressed oligomeric tau formation, and attenuated oTau-induced spine loss. In APPL/S mice, PTX-BD4-3 mitigated deficient TrkB/Akt signaling, reduced phosphorylation of Fyn and tau, preserved synaptic markers and dendritic spines, and improved Y-maze performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Small-molecule TrkB partial agonists may normalize TrkB signaling and promote synaptic resilience, supporting their potential as AD therapeutics.

title: Role of remimazolam in gastrointestinal endoscopy: American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy clinical practice update.
abstract: This clinical practice update provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, for procedural sedation during GI endoscopy. Remimazolam was approved by the Food and Drug Administration in July 2020 for use in procedural sedation. It offers rapid onset, short duration of action, and organ-independent metabolism, making it an alternative to traditional sedatives such as midazolam and propofol. This update synthesizes data from randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, and real-world studies, addressing efficacy, safety, dosing, and patient selection. It aims to assist clinicians in optimizing sedation while minimizing risks, particularly in high-risk populations. Previous guidelines, such as the 2018 American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy guidelines on sedation and anesthesia in GI endoscopy, focused on midazolam and propofol but did not include remimazolam. This update incorporates emerging evidence to guide the integration of remimazolam into practice.

title: A randomized, controlled experimental medicine study of the novel Kv7 channel opener azetukalner in individuals with major depressive disorder and anhedonia
abstract: Abstract Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a common and debilitating disease. Kv7 potassium channels are relevant to reward processing and represent a novel target for depression and anhedonia. Azetukalner is a positive allosteric modulator of Kv7 channels. This phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial assessed changes in brain reward function, clinical outcomes, and safety following treatment with azetukalner or placebo in individuals with MDD and anhedonia. The study included 60 participants with MDD and anhedonia in a current major depressive episode. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive azetukalner (20 mg orally once daily with food) or placebo for 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was change in bilateral ventral striatum (VS) activity assessed by functional MRI (fMRI) during a reward task from baseline to week 8. Secondary endpoints included changes in depression severity and anhedonia measured by the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) and Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (SHAPS). Of 60 participants, 29 were randomized to azetukalner and 31 to placebo. There was no significant difference in VS response to reward anticipation between groups. Compared to placebo, azetukalner was associated with numerical benefit on the MADRS and SHAPS that did not reach statistical significance. Most exploratory endpoints numerically favored azetukalner over placebo. Discontinuation rates due to adverse events were low and did not differ across groups. Despite not meeting the primary neuroimaging endpoint, secondary and exploratory outcomes suggested potential improvement in depressive symptoms and anhedonia. Trial Registration: Clinicaltrials.gov ID NCT04827901.

title: Infrared Thermal Imaging Combined with Machine Learning for Detecting Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: Abstract Standard rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flare assessment relies on components that are either subjective (patient global assessment) or non-specific (ESR, CRP), motivating interest in objective, non-invasive adjuncts. This proof-of-concept study evaluated infrared thermal imaging combined with machine learning for detecting RA flare and classifying disease activity. Eleven seropositive RA patients and nine seronegative controls underwent standardized thermal imaging alongside clinical assessment across 2–3 visits. Whole-hand maximum temperature (Tmax) was compared between RA flare visits and controls. Per-joint thermal zone data were used to train logistic regression and random forest classifiers predicting disease activity, using leave-one-patient-out cross-validation to prevent data leakage. RA patients showed significant clinical improvement with treatment (DAS28-ESR 5.23 to 3.32, p = 0.0007). Whole-hand Tmax did not significantly distinguish flare from controls (p = 0.53). A leakage-free analysis (n = 26 visits) found no model exceeded baseline for 3-class severity classification. Reclassifying activity using a binary treat-to-target threshold yielded a non-significant trend toward improved classification with random forest (73.1% vs. 57.7% baseline, p = 0.08). A single whole-hand temperature value does not reliably distinguish flare from non-flare states. Fine-grained classification was not achievable at this sample size once leakage was corrected. A coarser threshold showed a promising but inconclusive trend, warranting validation in a larger cohort.

title: A meta-analysis of pain intensity changes after placebo interventions in facial pain.
abstract: Interpreting pain improvements after interventions in clinical settings is challenging because placebo effects can influence patient-reported outcomes. In clinical practice, pain intensity reductions of 30% or greater are commonly considered indicative of meaningful analgesic benefit. However, the likelihood of achieving such reductions after placebo interventions is not known. We conducted a comprehensive meta-analysis to quantify pain intensity changes reported after placebo interventions in clinical trials of facial pain (FP). We systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and uncontrolled case series of FP treatments that included placebo or sham arms. The primary outcome was percentage change in pain intensity. The primary analysis focused on RCTs, with pooled effect sizes estimated using random-effects meta-analysis. Data from 115 studies (n = 3,208) were analyzed, including 71 RCTs (n = 2,128) and 44 uncontrolled case series (n = 1,080). Sham interventions yielded an average pain reduction of 29.73% (95% CI 24.09%-35.36%), with a prediction interval (-14.51% to 73.96%) among RCTs. Placebo responses varied by diagnosis (P < 0.001), with larger effects in temporomandibular disorders and classical trigeminal neuralgia. Cumulative probability analyses showed that ≥50% pain relief occurred in ∼25% of placebo-treated patients, whereas ≥75% improvement was reported in ∼2.5%. In FP, placebo interventions often produce mild to moderate relief but rarely yield dramatic improvements of ≥75%. These results can guide the interpretation of reported pain relief in clinical settings and inform clinical trial design in chronic pain conditions, suggesting that ≥75% pain intensity reductions after analgesic interventions are unlikely to be primarily driven by placebo effects.

title: Nasal Tuft Cell Markers Are Predictive of Overall Survival in Sinonasal Neuroendocrine and Sinonasal Undifferentiated Carcinomas.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal neuroendocrine carcinoma (SNEC) and sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma (SNUC) are rare aggressive malignancies with no established prognostic markers. Because features of POU2F3+ small cell lung carcinomas have been identified in both tumors, we evaluated immunostaining for POU2F3, a tuft cell transcription factor, and KIT, a tuft-progenitor marker, to determine whether SNECs/SNUCs exhibit a tuft cell lineage.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied patients with rare sinonasal malignancies treated between 2010 and 2025 at the University of Pennsylvania. Archived specimens underwent immunohistochemistry for KIT, POU2F3, SOX9, TRPM5, ASCL1, and IDH2 R172 mutations. Clinical, radiological, and treatment data were collected. Associations with overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: KIT was expressed in 90.2% of SNECs (N = 11) and 54.6% of SNUCs (N = 11), with the KIT+POU2F3+ phenotype in 72.7% and 18.2%, respectively. KIT/POU2F3 expression correlated with SOX9 and TRPM5, and KIT/POU2F3 phenotypes correlated with IDH2 R172 mutation status (p = 0.015). KIT+POU2F3+ tumors had significantly improved OS (p = 0.004) and DFS (p = 0.001). Univariable analysis showed that lack of double positive KIT/POU2F3 phenotype predicted decreased OS (HR: 12.24; 95% CI: 2.29-226.78; p = 0.001) and DFS (p < 0.001). In multivariable analyses, this association persisted for OS in models including histologic subtype or IDH2 mutation status.
CONCLUSIONS: Results indicate that a subgroup of SNECs and SNUCs expresses a tuft cell-associated marker profile. KIT+POU2F3+ SNECS and SNUCs have markedly improved OS and DFS suggesting these markers have diagnostic, prognostic and potentially therapeutic utility.

title: Cardiac adaptation in a murine iliac arteriovenous fistula model and the impact of sex and N-acetylcysteine supplementation
abstract: This murine iliac AVF model with concurrent renal insufficiency replicates compensated cardiac hypertrophy without heart failure, matching the predominant clinical phenotype in humans unlike existing preclinical models designed to induce high-output heart failure. Cardiomyocyte mitochondrial function was studied for the first time after AVF creation. Female sex was associated with increased respiratory capacity and preserved cardiac function. NAC supplementation showed a trend toward improved mitochondrial function in females.

title: Family history of alcohol and other substance use disorders integrated with associated phenotypic characteristics reveal brain structural differences in non-abusing young adults
abstract: ABSTRACT Early adulthood is a critical developmental period for the emergence of alcohol and substance use disorders (A/SUD). Young adults with family histories of A/SUD (FH+) have a higher risk for developing A/SUD themselves compared to individuals without such family histories (FH−). FH+ individuals often exhibit behavioral and cognitive alterations similar to those observed in A/SUD populations; however, A/SUD-related structural brain alterations have not been consistently observed in FH+ neuroimaging studies, which may reflect underlying heterogeneity in FH+ individuals. We compared n=79 FH+ and 128 FH− young adults (ages 18-25) on brain volume differences in five regions of interest identified from prior A/SUD neuroimaging mega-analyses. Additionally, we compared study participants who scored low and high on a novel family history integrated phenotype (FHIP) score that combined family history with key phenotypic variables related to FH+ status. FH+ participants displayed trend-level reductions in corpus callosum volumes compared to FH− participants. However, participants with high FHIP scores had significantly decreased whole corpus callosum and increased amygdala volumes compared to participants with low FHIP scores. Post hoc testing of corpus callosum subregions found that participants with high FHIP scores had significantly reduced mid-anterior corpus callosum volume. There were no differences in hippocampus, thalamus, or putamen volumes between FH or FHIP score-based groupings. FHIP scores were more sensitive than family history status alone in identifying structural brain differences in non-abusing healthy young adults. These findings suggest that corpus callosum and amygdala volumes differences could be related to a possible overarching A/SUD-relevant endophenotype rather than simply be consequences of problem alcohol and other substance use.

title: A Knowledge Graph Framework for Longitudinal Congenital Heart Disease Modeling
abstract: BACKGROUND: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is characterized by evolving clinical trajectories; staged interventions; and complex relationships among diagnoses, procedures, and encounters. Conventional machine learning applied to electronic health record (EHR) data often rely on static feature representations that do not preserve the natural longitudinal disease progression or clinical context. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to develop a knowledge graph-based framework for trajectory-aware representation and analysis of longitudinal CHD EHR data. METHODS: We constructed a longitudinal knowledge graph that integrates patients, encounters, diagnoses, and procedures while preserving temporal ordering across the care continuum. Term frequency-inverse document frequency and Word2Vec approaches were applied to encounter contexts extracted from the graph to generate longitudinal patient representations that supported phenotyping, patient similarity analysis, and retrospective classification. RESULTS: Using accumulated longitudinal EHR from a cardiovascular magnetic resonance cohort, we demonstrate that the framework captured clinically meaningful patterns and supported retrospective identification of single ventricle physiology as a representative use case. CONCLUSIONS: This knowledge graph framework provides a scalable approach for preserving temporal and relational clinical context and enable trajectory-aware modeling of longitudinal cardiovascular EHR data in patients with CHD.

title: Interaction Between Exercise Intensity and Sedentary Behavior on VO2max Change in Patients with De Novo Parkinson Disease: The Study in Parkinson Disease of Exercise (SPARX) Phase 2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parkinson disease (PD) is associated with increased sedentary time and reduced cardiorespiratory fitness, making exercise an important component of disease management. Although exercise improves cardiorespiratory fitness, individuals with PD vary substantially in their response to exercise. Sedentary time may contribute to this variability, yet whether sedentary time modifies the response to intervention and varying exercise intensities within an intervention is unknown. We examined whether sedentary time interacted with 6 months of moderate-intensity or high-intensity aerobic exercise on maximal oxygen consumption (VO2max) in individuals with PD.
METHODS: This secondary analysis used data from the SPARX phase 2 randomized clinical trial including 128 de novo PD patients assigned to high- or moderate-intensity treadmill exercise, or usual care for 6 months. Interactions between randomized group and post-randomization 6-months average sedentary time were assessed for associations with 6-month change in VO2max by using linear regression models corresponding to Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) models with interaction.
RESULTS: The interaction between exercise intensity and sedentary behavior on 6-month change in VO2max in the moderate-intensity group compared with usual care was not significant (β: -1.78, 95% CI: -3.76 to 0.20, p-value: 0.08), although the sensitivity analysis restricted to complete cases showed a significant interaction where each 10% increase in 6-months average sedentary time was associated with a 2.51 mL/kg/min decrease in VO2max change in the moderate-intensity group compared with usual care (β: -2.51, 95% CI: -4.53 to -0.48, p-value: 0.02). There was no significant interaction between exercise intensity and sedentary behavior on 6-month change in VO2max in the high-intensity group compared with usual care (β: -1.46, 95% CI: -4.74 to 1.83, p-value: 0.38). The sensitivity analysis showed similar results.
CONCLUSIONS: These hypothesis-generating, preliminary findings suggest that sedentary time may modify the response to exercise among individuals participating in moderate-intensity aerobic exercise. Future adequately powered randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings and determine whether sedentary behavior should be considered when prescribing exercise for individuals with PD.

title: Predicting treatment recovery and adherence in alcohol behavioral couple therapy using natural language processing.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol Behavioral Couple Therapy (ABCT) is an efficacious treatment for Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD). Research increasingly focuses on identifying predictors of treatment outcomes to guide the continued refinement of ABCT for diverse AUD populations and relationship typologies, with language spoken by couples emerging as a promising behavioral domain for understanding treatment success. Leveraging natural language processing (NLP) methods and a prospective design, the present study examined a broad range of linguistic features exhibited by couples as predictors and moderators of treatment outcomes.
METHOD: Participants represent a subset (n = 84, 42 couples) of individuals enrolled in a larger parent study examining ABCT intervention efficacy. Patients' drinking behaviors were tracked throughout treatment and at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. Using NLP tools, linguistic features of patients' and partners' speech during session 1 of ABCT were extracted, respectively.
RESULTS: Partners' behaviors moderated patients' drinking trajectories, with patients whose partners more frequently referenced alcohol, β = -0.0015, SE = 0.0006, p = 0.0075, and paired alcohol-related statements with positive sentiment, β = -0.0717, SE = 0.0183, p < 0.001, reporting more pronounced declines in drinking quantity over time. After accounting for patients' effects, patients whose partners used more collective pronouns showed more pronounced declines in drinking frequency over time, β = -0.0140, SE = 0.0060, p = 0.0204. In contrast, patients' behaviors predicted treatment adherence, with more frequent use of positively-valenced overall, OR = 0.984, 95% CI = [0.971, 0.998], and alcohol-specific statements, OR = 0.924, 95% CI = [0.858, 0.994], associated with lower likelihood of treatment completion.
CONCLUSIONS: Both AUD patients and their partners' language - particularly how couples discuss alcohol - may shape patients' treatment outcomes in different ways, with partners' language influencing drinking trajectories and patients' language influencing treatment adherence. Findings point to both what is said (alcohol-related language) and who said it (treatment role) as key predictors of ABCT treatment success.
