title: Low-Dose Buprenorphine Initiation Strategies for Pain
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this review is to describe the common benefits and pitfalls of various low-dose buprenorphine initiation strategies for patients experiencing long-term pain without opioid use disorder (OUD). DATA SOURCES: A search of the primary literature was performed in PubMed using the following keywords: "Buprenorphine OR Buprenorphine-naloxone OR Belbuca OR Suboxone, Primary care OR Outpatient, Pain OR Pain management," from January 1980 to August 2, 2026. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Case reports involving the use of sublingual/buccal buprenorphine in outpatients for pain without OUD were included. DATA SYNTHESIS: Three low-dose buprenorphine initiation methods were evaluated, titrating buprenorphine from once to thrice-daily up to a total of 7 days. Two studies abruptly discontinued full μ-agonists prior to initiating buprenorphine, whereas 1 study tapered full μ-agonists by 25% weekly after day 7. Tapering full-agonist opioids after attainment of target buprenorphine dosing was well tolerated and potentially unneeded after steady-state levels were achieved; bridging analgesia with sufficient pharmacokinetic overlap between buprenorphine and full μ-agonist opioids appears tantamount to mitigating withdrawal symptoms. RELEVANCE TO PATIENT CARE AND CLINICAL PRACTICE: The ideal buprenorphine initiation method considers desired duration, whether to perform cross-titration, product pharmacokinetics, patient-specific factors, and goals of care. CONCLUSIONS: No data exist to support one low-dose buprenorphine initiation method over another. All methods discussed were highly successful at rotating patients to buprenorphine, that is, with equivalent or improved pain control with minimal to no withdrawal symptoms and may be used to build a methodology for starting buprenorphine in outpatients with sub-optimal pain regimens.

title: Impact of Simple Vascular Quality Initiative Frailty Score on Outcomes of Venous Leg Ulcer Healing and Recurrence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Up to 1% of patients with chronic venous disease will present with a primary venous leg ulcer (VLU). This study aimed to analyze the impact of frailty as measured by the Simple Vascular Quality Initiative-Frailty Score (sVQI-FS) on the outcomes of patients undergoing treatment for a VLU.
METHODS: Between 2012 and 2024, all patients presenting with a VLU were analyzed. Inclusion criteria were an active VLU, in the presence of superficial truncal venous incompetence, and without total deep venous incompetence (classified as involving all 18 named venous segments) on duplex imaging. Frailty was assessed by the sVQI-FS (congestive heart failure, renal impairment, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, not living at home, not ambulatory, anemia, and underweight status with a body mass index of less than 18.5). An sVQI-FS score of 0.3 or greater was considered frail. Demographics and interventions to effect healing were recorded. The primary outcomes were ulcer healing at 24 weeks and VLU recurrence within 1 year.
RESULTS: A total of 534 patients (61% female, age 67 ± 9 years, mean ± SD) presented with an active VLU. However, 43% of patients were classified as frail by the sVQI-FS, and 31% had their ulcer for ≥12 months. Frail patients were more likely to have suffered a longer ulcer duration (7.1 ± 0.9 vs. 4.7 ± 1.1 months; frail vs. non-frail; mean ± SD; P = 0.001) and have had a longer interval before referral compared to non-frail patients (5.6 ± 1.2 vs. 3.9 ± 1.1 months, mean ± SD; P = 0.001). Frailty was associated with more severe ulcers as measured by wound bed scores (11 ± 3 vs. 15 ± 5; nonfrail vs. frail; mean ± SD; frail vs. nonfrail; P = 0.001). The intensity of therapy, as measured by the sum of scheduled and unscheduled clinic visits and all interventions, was 1.8 times higher in the frail group than in the non-frail group (P = 0.001). Initial VLU healing was 26 ± 2% and 16 ± 2% at 12 weeks for non-frail and frail, respectively (mean ± SEM; P = 0.001). By 24 weeks, initial VLU healing was 67 ± 4% and 38 ± 4%, for non-frail and frail, respectively (P = 0.003). Freedom from VLU recurrence was 59 ± 4% and 36 ± 5% at 1 year (mean ± SEM; P = 0.002). and 30 ± 6%, and 18 ± 7% at 3 years for non-frail and frail, respectively (P = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: Frailty significantly affects early referral for VLU care, is associated with more severe ulcers, and impacts both VLU healing rates and recurrence rates. Intervening to identify and ameliorate frailty is necessary to enhance VLU care.

title: Prescription Stimulant Use and Misuse Among Nursing Students: A Survey Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Substance use disorder (SUD) continues to be a serious public health burden associated with increased morbidity and mortality. The prevalence of prescription stimulant misuse ranges from 8% to 10.4% in the nursing student population.
OBJECTIVE: This study had multiple aims: (a) to identify the use and misuse of prescription stimulants; (b) to investigate if relations exist between particular variables and stimulant use; and (c) to determine motives for stimulant use.
METHODS: An anonymous internet survey was emailed to members of a nursing student organization inquiring about the use of prescription stimulants.
RESULTS: Of the 88 respondents, 55.7% reported no use, 13.6% reported appropriate use of prescribed stimulants, 11.4% reported misuse of prescribed stimulants, and 19.3% reported nonmedical prescription use. There was a statistically significant difference in grade point averages (F(3, 87) = 2.93, p = .038); membership in PanHellenic society (χ2(1, n = 29) = 4.93, p =.026); and employment status (χ2(1, n = 29) = 5.15, p = .023) between groups with appropriate use and nonmedical prescription use. Nursing students had similar motivations to findings in other studies, such as to increase energy following a late night of activities, study longer, and increase their academic edge against the competition.
CONCLUSION: This study contributes unique knowledge to the evolving literature regarding substance use and abuse in the nursing student population. The education of nursing students might include awareness of their vulnerabilities, recognition, and actions for individuals suspected of stimulant misuse.

title: No strain, no gain: within-host bacterial microdiversity and human health.
abstract: It is well established that within a bacterial species, genotypic and phenotypic variation leads to differences in virulence, antibiotic susceptibility, and metabolism. However, there is also increasing evidence that often multiple variants of the same species co-inhabit the same site in the human body, both during health and disease. This within-host microdiversity can develop over time for pathogens in chronic infections and has been observed for many members of the microbiota, for instance in the gut and on the skin. Research is just beginning to uncover how this within-host intra-species diversity develops and why it matters. Intra-species diversity is largely stable over time, with occasional selective sweeps of new genotypes, and the overall level of diversity is modulated by both microbe-microbe and microbe-host interactions. Furthermore, data indicate that within-host microdiversity can impact the stability of bacterial communities, their antimicrobial resistance, and the efficacy of probiotics and microbiota transplants. Here, we describe the evolutionary and ecological processes that promote high or low within-host microdiversity and the extent of this diversity in the human microbiota and in infections. In addition, we consider how microdiversity within individuals shapes the functional role of the human microbiota and the progression of disease. Together, within-host microdiversity is a newly developing way to think about the diversity of human-associated microbes, with implications in how we treat chronic infections and manipulate our microbiota to promote health.

title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI.
METHODS: Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified.
RESULTS: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P < 0.0001). In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA, 45.4% of whom died in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Notably, although risk-adjusted IPCA increased (0.79% to 0.95%; P = 0.042), slight declines in risk-adjusted mortality (45.1% to 43.6%; P = 0.027) were observed over time. PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, non-ST-segment acute coronary syndromes, increasing age, ventricular arrhythmias, severe aortic stenosis, vasopressors or inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, coronary perforation, coronary dissection, cardiac tamponade, intraprocedural heart failure or myocardial infarction, and temporary cardiac pacemaker implantation were associated with increased adjusted odds of IPCA.
CONCLUSIONS: IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

title: Left Ventricular Functional Improvement is Associated With Lower Morbidity and Mortality During Long-Term Mechanical Circulatory Support: An STS Intermacs Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: A subset of patients with advanced heart failure (HF) supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) demonstrate significant improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). However, the impact of such functional improvement on clinical outcomes is unclear.
METHODS: We analyzed adults in the STS-Intermacs registry who underwent continuous-flow LVAD implantation (2006-2017) and had echocardiographic data ≥6 months post-implant. Post-LVAD myocardial function was defined by the maximum LVEF after ≥6 months of support and categorized as <40% versus ≥40% and into finer strata. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, clinically significant sustained cardiac arrhythmia, hepatic and renal dysfunction, cerebrovascular accident/transient ischemic attack, right HF during follow-up, and HF hospitalization. Incidence rates and incidence rate ratios were calculated during 6-month landmarked follow-up through 5 years, and associations were assessed using landmarked multivariable Cox models.
RESULTS: Among 9518 eligible patients (age 56.6 ± 13.2 years, 21.4% female), 1131 (12%) achieved LVEF ≥40% over a median 27.0 months of follow-up. Compared with LVEF <40%, LVEF ≥40% was associated with lower adjusted incidence rates of death (adjusted incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.73-0.98), arrhythmia (IRR 0.59, 95% CI 0.48-0.72), hepatic dysfunction (IRR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35-0.97), and HF hospitalization (IRR 0.65, 95% CI 0.51-0.82), whereas adjusted differences in right HF and renal dysfunction were not significant. In adjusted time-to-event analyses, LVEF ≥40% was independently associated with lower hazards of all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.82, 95% CI 0.71-0.96), HF hospitalization (aHR 0.63, 95% CI 0.50-0.80), cardiac arrhythmia (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.58-0.83), and hepatic dysfunction (aHR 0.57, 95% CI 0.37-0.88). Across ordered LVEF strata, higher LVEF was associated with progressively lower risks of death and HF-related events.
CONCLUSIONS: In a large multicenter LVAD cohort, LV functional response to durable support spanned a spectrum, with ∼1 in 8 (12%) durable LVAD recipients achieving a maximum post-implant LVEF ≥40% after ≥6 months of support. Higher post-implant LVEF was independently associated with improved survival and fewer HF-related events. These findings support viewing myocardial improvement during LVAD support as a clinically meaningful target that affects positively the outcomes of patients while being on mechanical support.

title: Facilitating best practices in practicum training in clinical neuropsychology: introducing the North American Association of Practicum Sites in Neuropsychology (NAPSN) organizational training guidelines.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The North American Association of Practicum Sites in Neuropsychology (NAPSN) was established in 2023 to support external practicum programs in urban, suburban, and rural areas in the United States and Canada by providing resources for member practicum programs and supporting prospective and current neuropsychology practicum students in collaboration with doctoral training programs. This article describes the development of and documents the current NAPSN organizational training guidelines for member programs.
METHOD: A NAPSN training guidelines subcommittee was formed, consisting of six practicing clinical neuropsychologists who supervise practicum students across a variety of patient populations (i.e. adult, pediatric, lifespan), practice settings (e.g. academic medical center, Department of Veterans Affairs, hospital-based, private practice) and types (e.g. clinical, mixed clinical and forensic, mixed clinical and research), and geographic regions (e.g. urban, suburban, rural) to ensure sufficiently broad perspectives were incorporated.
RESULTS: Incorporating best practices for supervision in neuropsychology, existing position statements on practicum training in neuropsychology, and recently revised, profession-wide training guidelines, four core content areas were established through consensus discussion: 1) Supervised experience of clinical practice activities; 2) Didactics/educational programming; 3) Professionalization; 4) Research. Guidelines were drafted for each respective content area. Following multiple internal rounds of revision among the subcommittee, these guidelines were presented to the NAPSN Board of Directors and Elected Officers and underwent additional rounds of revision to arrive at the final guidelines.
CONCLUSION: The NAPSN training guidelines were established not as prescriptive rules/standards but rather are designed to function as supportive guidelines for NAPSN member programs to facilitate high-quality and effective training at the practicum level by allowing for maximum flexibility to account for the range of existing practicum training settings and experiences.

title: TLR7-mediated autoimmunity targets Robo3 to drive astrogliosis in frontotemporal dementia.
abstract: Mutations in GRN and C9orf72 are common causes of frontotemporal dementia (FTD). While it is well-recognized that GRN or C9orf72 mutations also increase the risk of autoimmune diseases, the intersection of innate and adaptive immunity, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration in FTD remains unclear. Here we show that concurrent loss of Grn and C9orf72 breaks immune tolerance by activating the pattern recognition receptor, TLR7, leading to clonal expansion of age-associated B cells and activated B cells. Grn -/- ;C9orf72 -/- B cells exhibited heightened responses upon TLR7 activation and produced autoantibodies that target the axon guidance receptor Robo3 to promote astroglial pathology. Interestingly, immunization with Robo3 extracellular domain in young Grn -/- ;C9orf72 -/- mice accelerated astrogliosis. Conversely, TLR7 antagonist M5049 treatment rescued B cell defects, reduced anti-Robo3 autoantibodies, and mitigated astrogliosis and synaptic loss in Grn -/- ;C9orf72 -/- mice. Together, these results offer critical insights into how TLR7-mediated autoimmune dysfunction targets Robo3 to drive neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in FTD.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors Versus Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitors in Chronic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) receiving background renin-angiotensin system inhibitor (RASi) therapy. We compared the effectiveness of SGLT2is versus RASis on the risks of heart failure (HF) development, kidney disease progression, and mortality in patients with CKD. We conducted a retrospective, active-comparator, new-user cohort study using the global electronic health record database. Adults with CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] 15 to <60 ml/min/1.73 m²), without previous HF, who initiated SGLT2is or either angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor blockers between 2020 and 2023 were included. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, new-onset HF, hemodialysis, or decline in eGFR to <15 ml/min/1.73 m² within 2 years. Propensity score (PS) matching was used to balance baseline characteristics. After PS matching, 18,075 matched pairs were analyzed. SGLT2i initiation was associated with a lower incidence of the primary composite outcome compared with RASi initiation (15.6% vs 19.9%, hazard ratio 0.76, 95% confidence interval 0.72 to 0.80, p <0.001). SGLT2i was also associated with lower risks of the composite of all-cause death or new-onset HF and the composite of all-cause death, hemodialysis, or eGFR decline to <15 ml/min/1.73 m². In subgroup analyses of the PS-matched cohorts, these findings were consistent across diabetes status, CKD severity, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, SGLT2i type, and RASi class. In conclusion, initiation of SGLT2i was associated with lower risks of HF and kidney disease progression compared with RASi in patients with CKD.

title: Effect of AI-assisted radiographic fracture detection on paediatric emergency department length of stay through fracture exclusion: A before-after cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-assisted radiographic fracture detection tools (AI-RFDT) have the potential to support confident fracture exclusion by physicians in the paediatric emergency department (ED), where presentations for suspected fractures substantially outnumber confirmed fractures. This study aimed to evaluate whether implementation of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED is associated with reduced length of stay (LOS) among patients presenting with suspected fractures, and to determine whether any observed effect is specifically mediated through the fracture-exclusion pathway.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective before-after cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary paediatric ED. AI-RFDT (BoneView, Gleamer, Paris, France) was deployed on 1 October 2023 as a passive, second-read decision-support tool. The study population comprised 4172 paediatric patients with rule-out fracture diagnoses (fracture-excluded; F-E) during standard working hours (08:00-15:59; pre-AI n = 2514; post-AI n = 1658). Fracture-confirmed (F-C) patients served as a pre-specified internal control (n = 1155). The primary outcome was ED LOS; secondary outcomes were orthopaedic consultation rate, LOS by consultation status, anatomical subgroup LOS, and 30-day re-admission.
RESULTS: Orthopaedic consultation rates in the paediatric ED decreased from 73% to 68.3% (Δ -4.7 %age points, p = 0.002). The greatest reduction was observed in patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation (2.25→1.78 h, Δ -28 min, p < 0.001), while those with confirmed fractures demonstrated no significant change in LOS (Δ+3 min, p = 0.51). 30-day re-admission rates remained unchanged (6.9% vs 6.9%, p = 1.00). Wrist and forearm injuries demonstrated the greatest LOS reduction (Δ -24 min, p = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Deployment of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED was associated with a reduction in LOS that was concentrated among patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation. The absence of LOS change in confirmed-fracture controls supports a mechanism specific to fracture exclusion rather than generalised care acceleration.

title: Supraclavicular artery island flap for head and neck reconstruction: Our experience and exploratory analysis of risk factors.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The supraclavicular artery island flap (SCAIF) is being increasingly used for reconstruction of complex head and neck defects as an alternative to the traditional free flap or pedicled pectoralis flap. Here, we describe our experience with SCAIF for oncologic head and neck reconstruction and aim to identify patient factors associated with flap complications.
METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who underwent SCAIF reconstruction at a tertiary academic center was conducted between 2015 and 2023 (n=23). Collected variables included patient characteristics, operative parameters, and postoperative outcomes.
RESULTS: The mean patient age was 70.2 years. Six patients had a history of prior radiation, and 6 underwent ipsilateral neck dissection. Twelve patients received adjuvant radiation following flap transfer. Minor flap-related complications included delayed wound healing (n = 3) and partial flap necrosis (n = 6). One patient experienced total flap necrosis. Systemic complications included myocardial infarction (n = 2), pulmonary embolism (n = 1), atrial fibrillation (n = 1), and deep vein thrombosis (n = 1). Advanced age was associated with recipient-site complications (p = 0.018). Elevated body mass index was associated with systemic complications, longer ICU stays, and increased total hospital length of stay (p=0.036, p = 0.008, and p = 0.001, respectively). History of vascular disease and diabetes mellitus were associated with flap necrosis and delayed wound healing, respectively (p=0.025 and p=0.004). Longer operative time was associated with flap dehiscence (p=0.002).
CONCLUSION: SCAIF is a reliable and versatile reconstructive option for oncologic head and neck defects, including in previously operated or irradiated necks. Caution is warranted particularly in patients with diabetes or vascular disease, as vascular comorbidities appear to be more clinically precise risk factors than chronological age alone. Elevated body mass index also warrants consideration.

title: Bilateral conjunctival granulation tissue formation after EGFR inhibitor therapy for non-small cell lung carcinoma.
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors are increasingly used to treat malignancies such as non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We report a rare case of bilateral conjunctival granulation tissue formation associated with amivantamab-lazertinib therapy in a 75-year-old woman with stage IV NSCLC with an EGFR L858R mutation. The patient presented with progressively enlarging bilateral conjunctival lesions emanating from both the upper and lower eyelid fornices resulting in diminished peripheral vision. Surgical excision was performed, and histopathological examination revealed granulation tissue without evidence of malignancy. Clinicians should be aware of the spectrum of ocular manifestations associated with EGFR inhibitor therapy.

title: Foundation Model-Based Computational Pathology Predicts Breast Cancer Biomarker Status from Intraoperative Frozen Sections.
abstract: Prediction of breast cancer biomarkers from routine formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images has been explored previously, but whether biomarker-associated morphologic signals can be reliably captured from artifact-prone intraoperative frozen-section (FS) specimens remains insufficiently studied. This retrospective proof-of-concept study developed a foundation model-based multiple-instance learning framework to predict estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), and Ki-67 status directly from H&E-stained intraoperative FS whole slide images of 248 patients with breast cancer, using postoperative immunohistochemistry and fluorescence in situ hybridization as ground truth. Exploratory feature evaluation identified UNI2-h as a suitable encoder for downstream modeling. In fivefold cross-validation, areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.847 for ER, 0.906 for PR, 0.893 for HER2, and 0.799 for Ki-67, with moderate agreement for ER, PR, and HER2 and fair agreement for Ki-67. An exploratory within-cohort cross-preparation analysis showed limited FFPE-to-FS transferability, whereas the FS-trained model retained relatively favorable performance on FFPE images. Attention heat maps highlighted tumor regions with biologically plausible biomarker-associated morphologic patterns. These findings provide proof of concept that intraoperative FS H&E images retain learnable biomarker-associated morphologic signals despite preparation-related alterations.

title: Predicting Recurrence and Progression in Contemporary Patients with NMIBC Undergoing Blue Light Cystoscopy-Aided Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumor.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although blue light cystoscopy (BLC) is recommended by clinical practice guidelines to improve cancer detection, predictive models for patients undergoing BLC are lacking. We therefore evaluated the associations of clinicopathologic features with recurrence and progression in a contemporary cohort of patients treated with BLC to develop a risk prediction model.
METHODS: We identified patients aged 18-89 years in the multi-institutional Blue Light Cystoscopy with Cysview Registry who underwent BLC-aided TURBT between 2014-2023. Associations of baseline characteristics with recurrence and progression were evaluated using Cox regression, and predictive models were developed using lasso regression.
RESULTS: 1040 patients underwent BLC-TURBT. Tumor stage was Ta in 578 (56%), T1 in 166 (16%), and pure CIS in 190 (18%) patients. On multivariable analysis, HGTa (HR 1.60, 95%CI 1.10-2.35) and HGT1 (HR 1.94, 95%CI 1.25-3.02) tumors were associated with increased risk of recurrence. HGT1 (HR 12.4, 95%CI 4.52-34.0), HGTa (HR 3.08, 95% CI 1.03-9.18), pure CIS (HR 4.51, 95% CI 1.44-14.1), Ta+CIS (HR 4.98, 95%CI 1.17-21.1), and T1+CIS (HR 7.65, 95%CI 1.97-29.7) tumors, as well as lymphovascular invasion (HR 3.27, 95%CI 1.22-8.83) were associated with increased risk of progression. In contrast, adjuvant BCG was associated with decreased risk of progression (HR 0.40, 95%CI 0.22-0.72). Model discrimination was 0.64 for RFS and 0.73 for PFS.
CONCLUSIONS: Using a multi-institutional cohort, we developed predictive models for recurrence and progression in patients undergoing BLC-TURBT. Although they require external validation, these models reflect to contemporary treatment paradigms and can inform personalized, risk-adapted management of NMIBC.

title: Neurophysiological affective reactivity classification and its stability in individuals with cannabis use disorder.
abstract: The increasing prevalence of Cannabis Use Disorder (CUD) necessitates measures that reliably predict outcomes. Based in the incentive sensitization model of addiction, the late positive potential (LPP) has been used to predict choice of drug versus affective cues and classify individuals into clinically-relevant neuroaffective reactivity profiles derived from viewing affective and drug-related pictures in individuals who use substances. However, this approach has not been conducted on a sample of individuals who use cannabis nor has its retest reliability been assessed. This study replicated and extended the neuroaffective reactivity profile findings in individuals with CUD and tested the one-week profile reliability. At two lab visits one week apart, 44 participants completed a probabilistic choice task and viewed cannabis and affective pictures with EEG recording. k-means cluster analyses were applied to the resulting LPPs to create neuroaffective reactivity profiles. Consistent with past literature, at both lab visits, participants were organized into two clusters characterized by differences in the cannabis and pleasant LPP amplitudes (one with greater cannabis than pleasant LPPs and one with greater pleasant than cannabis LPPs), but LPP clusters did not differ in choice behavior or other indicators of problematic use. Despite this reliable classification at the group level, individual level retest reliability for the profiles was low, outperformed by residualized LPP scores and raw LPPs. These findings add to literature suggesting a common pattern of neuroaffective reactivity profiles across addiction populations but caution their clinical utility considering the unresolved reliability and lack of convergent validity across units of analysis.

title: Making Obesity Care Affordable: Patient Views on Deprescribing GLP-1 RAs.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the acceptability of deprescribing injectable incretin mimetics for weight management (IMWMs) among self-identified individuals with obesity in the US.
STUDY DESIGN: An online survey was conducted in November 2024.
METHODS: Respondents (N = 704) watched 2 videos summarizing IMWM risks and benefits. The primary quantitative outcome was agreement with insurers paying for IMWMs during active weight loss and encouraging lower-cost alternatives during maintenance. Descriptive statistics and χ 2 tests were conducted to analyze the data. Qualitative analysis centered on inductive content analysis of respondents' responses to a free-text question about concerns with transitioning from IMWMs to an alternative weight management strategy.
RESULTS: Most respondents agreed with encouraging the strategy (n = 582; 82.7%) and would support their friends or family members switching to low-cost alternatives to expand access to IMWMs (89.8%). Broad coverage of effective, lower-cost treatment options was identified as a critical component of such programs. Common response themes included attitudes toward weight loss medications (44.4%), such as adverse events (26.9%) and the fear of worsening health if the IMWM is stopped (30.2%), primarily related to gaining weight back or maintaining weight loss (25.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: IMWM deprescribing programs are, in principle, acceptable to individuals with obesity. Additional research is needed to determine the feasibility and real-world outcomes of adults with obesity switching to lower-cost alternatives during weight maintenance.

title: Taking Into Account the Susceptible Window for Exposures in Cox Proportional Hazards Model: A Way Using Splines to Model the Lag-Risk Relationship.
abstract: External exposures take time to accumulate and affect human health, leading to a time lag between initial exposure and the manifestation of clinical signs. Susceptible time window analysis aims to describe the relationship between the time since exposure and its effects. To obtain unbiased estimates in susceptible time window analysis, researchers may need to adjust for exposures measured at different times simultaneously. Conventional Cox proportional hazards models often fail in this regard due to the strong multicollinearity between lagged exposure terms. In addition to estimation challenges, missing data in historical exposures present another obstacle for long-term analysis. To address these challenges, we first impose flexible parametric models on the effects across historical exposures by assuming that they follow restricted cubic splines. Based on our proposed restricted cubic spline model, we develop two model selection algorithms to help researchers determine the optimal knot locations in the splines. Additionally, we propose using multiple imputations to handle the missing exposure data. We conducted simulation studies to evaluate the performance of the restricted cubic spline models and the imputation algorithms in various realistic settings. The results show that our model demonstrates strong performance, offering great flexibility and robustness to misspecified maximum length of effect. Compared to the complete-person-time analysis, our multiple imputation algorithm exhibits significantly lower variance, with only a slight increase in bias. Finally, as an illustrative example, we apply our proposed models to analyze the effect of folate consumption on colorectal cancer incidence in the Nurses' Health Study from 1976 to 2016.

title: Proteostasis (in)action: the role of co-pathologies in neurodegenerative disease.
abstract: Clinically distinct neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), share in common progressive neuronal dysfunction and cell death associated with the accumulation of misfolded proteins. Central to these processes are the cellular and organismal proteostasis networks responsible for maintaining protein homeostasis through coordinated actions of molecular chaperones, the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy-lysosomal pathways. As a consequence of ageing, genetic modifications and other disease-specific conditions, the proteostatic network becomes compromised, leading to the accumulation of toxic protein aggregates that disrupt neuronal function and lead to neurodegeneration. Specific misfolded proteins are associated with each neurodegenerative disease (i.e. α-synuclein in PD, amyloid-β/tau in AD and TAR DNA-binding protein 43/SOD in ALS). However, increasing evidence implicates more complex interactions of co-pathologies across these disorders, as Lewy bodies are common in AD brains and Alzheimer pathology is present in the majority of PD autopsy cases. These observations are consistent with the idea that disruption of proteostasis networks by one aggregation-prone protein could result in misfolding and aggregation of other neurodegeneration-related species. This review will examine the characteristics and consequences of co-pathologies in neurodegenerative disorders. Additionally, the review will outline emerging therapeutic strategies targeted at restoring proteostasis and mitigating the effects of co-pathological processes associated with neurodegenerative diseases. This article is part of the Theo Murphy meeting issue 'ProteostaSys: a systems view of proteostasis'.

title: Cognitive Outcomes After Reperfusion Therapy for Acute Ischaemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis and the PRECISE-ACTION Framework for Transdisciplinary Cognitive Management.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is disabling after acute ischaemic stroke (AIS), but cognitive outcomes after reperfusion therapy remain uncertain because studies differ in treatment pathways, cognitive tools, follow-up timing, and ascertainment.
OBJECTIVES: To estimate PSCI prevalence after AIS reperfusion therapy and evaluate comparative cognitive, safety, and functional outcomes.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from 1 January 2000 to 31 May 2024, with an updated search on 16 June 2026. Random-effects models were used. Risk ratios (RRs) were the primary comparative binary measure; odds ratios (ORs) were sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight distinct study records comprising 18,322 participants were included in this meta-analysis. Pooled PSCI prevalence was 33% in treatment-arm analyses (95% CI 14-54%; I2 = 99.48%) and 39% in overall or single-arm cohorts (95% CI 24-56%; I2 = 99.60%). Extreme between-study heterogeneity (I2 ≈ 99%) limited the precision and generalisability of the pooled prevalence estimates. Reperfusion therapy was not associated with PSCI risk (RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.94-1.29; p = 0.241); OR sensitivity analysis was consistent (OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.91-1.75; p = 0.169). Continuous cognitive outcomes showed a pooled standardised mean difference of 0.67 (95% CI 0.16-1.18; p = 0.010), with substantial heterogeneity.
CONCLUSIONS: Post-stroke cognitive impairment remains frequent after AIS reperfusion therapy, affecting approximately one-third of reperfusion-treated patients and two-fifths of overall or single-arm cohorts. Comparative RR and OR analyses did not show a robust overall association between reperfusion exposure and PSCI risk, while cognitive score differences were significant but heterogeneous. These findings support routine cognitive assessment, harmonised endpoints, and prospective therapy-specific follow-up. PRECISE-ACTION is proposed as a preliminary, hypothesis-generating transdisciplinary framework for structured cognitive assessment, longitudinal tracking, integrated care, and future research.

title: International spinal cord injury vocational rehabilitation basic data set
abstract: Abstract Study design: International expert working group consensus. Objective: To develop an International Spinal Cord Injury (SCI) Vocational Rehabilitation Basic Data Set presenting a standardised format for collection and reporting of a minimal amount of information on vocational rehabilitation in daily practice or research in SCI. Setting: Representation from six countries and four world regions. Methods: An iterative decision-making and consensus process was applied, integrating evidence and expert opinion related to SCI and vocational rehabilitation. A Rapid Review of key literature was conducted to identify key concepts, models or frameworks, relevant domains/categories, specific items, and outcomes or predictors in vocational rehabilitation. Following this, a Data Mapping Exercise matched data fields/items from multiple sources and existing International Spinal Cord Society (ISCoS) Data Sets. Further mapping was performed for alignment of fields against the conceptual framework using a consensus approach , identifying gaps and anchoring decisions on key elements and agreement on common terms/definitions. The ISCoS Data Set Advisory Committee provided feedback and assisted with key decision-making throughout the consultative and consensus process. Consumer perspectives were integrated into the data set development. Suggested revisions were considered, and a final version of the data set was disseminated again for final approval and adoption. Results: The Basic Data Set was developed, consisting of nine items. Conclusion: The International SCI Vocational Rehabilitation Basic Data Set provides a standard and consistent way to capture the lived experience of work functioning of people with SCI and support the integration of vocational rehabilitation in clinical practice and comparative research. title: Repair-Dependent Competition Between Direct Driver Founding and Stochastic Tunneling Before Clonal Establishment
abstract: Abstract DNA repair may change not only whether damaged cells survive but also which mutational route produces successful progression. We compare direct two-driver founding in a single division with sequential stochastic tunneling through a transient one-driver lineage. Founders arise from an endogenous homeostatic mutation–repair equilibrium and initiate branching processes stopped by extinction, an irreversible commitment event, or a finite clone-size bound- ary; only commitment before the other outcomes counts as success. At each fixed size boundary, both routes contribute at order V^2 in a rare independent- driver mutation expansion, with V held unchanged across repair comparisons. Exact finite-state coefficients establish a repair-induced reversal of the dominant route after averaging over the homeostatic founder mixture. An opportunity–turnover–establishment identity shows why improved cellular demography need not increase divisions eligible for a second hit. With lesion-dependent post-hit outcomes, a sharp criterion describes overshoot in the unbounded subcritical model, while certified finite-clone examples demonstrate re-entrant dominance. The resulting biological observable is a repair-dependent mixture of successful routes, distinct from clinical cancer incidence. MSC Classification: 92D15 , 60J80 , 60J35

title: Chronic Neuroimmune and Neurovascular Remodeling After Ischemic Stroke in Humans: From the Subacute Phase to the Chronic Infarct
abstract: Ischemic stroke initiates a prolonged sequence of neurovascular and neuroimmune remodeling processes that persist for months to years beyond the acute event and contribute to progressive neurodegeneration, white matter loss, and vascular cognitive impairment. Despite this substantial long-term burden, the biological processes characterizing the chronic post-stroke brain remain incompletely defined. In this review, we integrate human histopathological evidence with mechanistic insights from experimental stroke models to develop a conceptual framework for chronic post-stroke neuroimmune and neurovascular pathology in humans organized around six inter-related biological domains: the cerebrovasculature, the myeloid cell response, adaptive immune infiltration, glial scar formation, glymphatic function, and white matter pathology. Each domain originates as an adaptive response to ischemic injury but progressively evolves into a chronically active state that sustains, rather than resolves, the post-stroke neuroimmune environment. These domains are mechanistically coupled and collectively constitute a self-reinforcing chronic neuroimmune niche whose reparative and maladaptive dimensions coexist and shift with time, infarct context, and individual biological variation. Together, these observations support a paradigm in which the chronic infarct is not simply the residual consequence of ischemic injury but a dynamic neuroimmune microenvironment that continues to shape brain degeneration, vascular remodeling, and functional recovery months to years after stroke, making it one of the most promising therapeutic targets for promoting long-term recovery. The Chronic Infarct: A Self-Sustaining Neuroimmune Niche : Ischemic stroke triggers six interlinked processes: vascular remodeling, myeloid activation, adaptive immune infiltration, glial scarring, glymphatic dysfunction, and white matter injury, which persist for months to years, forming a self-reinforcing niche that drives chronic neurodegeneration. title: Intravenous midazolam alters short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses differently in younger and older adults.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aging is associated with changes in cortical excitability and altered responsiveness to benzodiazepines, but the effects of benzodiazepine challenge on motor cortical paired-pulse physiology in older adults remain incompletely understood. We examined whether intravenous midazolam differentially modulates corticospinal excitability and short-interval paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) responses in younger and older adults.
METHODS: Sixteen younger adults (18-35 years) and sixteen older adults (50-69 years) underwent single-pulse and paired-pulse (conditioning stimulus: 110% motor threshold; test stimulus: 143% motor threshold) TMS of the left primary motor cortex at baseline and during intravenous midazolam administration. Single-pulse motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude was used to assess corticospinal excitability. Short-interval paired-pulse responses were quantified as the ratio of conditioned to unconditioned MEP amplitude.
RESULTS: At baseline, younger adults showed greater corticospinal excitability than older adults, reflected by larger single-pulse MEP amplitudes (adjusted p = 0.04). Younger adults demonstrated paired-pulse inhibition at baseline, reflected by a conditioned/unconditioned MEP ratio below 1.0 (ratio = 0.73; adjusted p < 0.01), whereas older adults did not show inhibition and instead had a mean ratio above 1.0 (ratio = 1.25). Midazolam reduced single-pulse MEP amplitudes in both groups. During midazolam administration, paired-pulse inhibition was no longer observed in younger adults, and older adults continued to show no evidence of inhibition.
CONCLUSIONS: Younger and older adults differed in baseline corticospinal excitability and in short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses. Intravenous midazolam reduced corticospinal excitability and altered paired-pulse response patterns, eliminating baseline paired-pulse inhibition in younger adults while producing little measurable change in older adults. These findings suggest that aging may modify the net motor cortical response to benzodiazepine challenge. The results should be interpreted in relation to the paired-pulse stimulation parameters used and support further studies using complementary approaches to characterize age-related differences in inhibitory and facilitatory motor cortical circuits.

title: Large Language Model–Enhanced Electronic Frailty Assessment and Prognostic Performance in Hospitalized Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Electronic frailty indices (eFIs) derived from structured electronic health record (EHR) data may incompletely capture functional deficits. Large language models (LLMs) can extract frailty-related information from clinical notes, but whether improved frailty ascertainment improves prognostic performance is uncertain. Objective To compare frailty ascertainment and prognostic performance between standard and LLM-enhanced eFIs among hospitalized adults. Design Retrospective cohort study Participants Adults aged ≥50 years enrolled in two studies at an academic medical center and affiliated community hospital between February 2022 and April 2024. Main Measures A validated 35-deficit diagnosis-based eFI and an LLM-enhanced eFI incorporating deficits extracted from physical therapy (PT) documentation using GPT-4o. Frailty was defined using an index threshold of ≥0.20. The primary outcome was a composite of discharge to a facility, readmission, or death within 90 days. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations with the outcome, and discrimination was compared using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Secondary analyses examined threshold-based classification and PT-documentation availability; prespecified sensitivity analyses evaluated population and outcome restrictions. Results Among 616 hospitalizations, mean (SD) age was 70.9 (10.2) years, 329 (53.4%) had PT documentation, and 320 (51.9%) experienced the composite outcome. Standard and LLM-enhanced eFIs classified 216 (35.1%) and 362 (58.8%) hospitalizations as frail, respectively. Both were independently associated with the outcome (standard eFI: adjusted OR, 1.98 [95% CI, 1.39–2.83]; LLM-enhanced eFI: adjusted OR, 2.46 [95% CI, 1.75–3.47]). Discrimination did not differ significantly (AUROC, 0.636 vs 0.660; difference, 0.024 [95% CI, −0.006 to 0.053]; p =0.12). LLM enhancement increased sensitivity (42.5% to 69.4%) but decreased specificity (73.0% to 52.7%). Conclusions LLM enhancement substantially increased frailty ascertainment and sensitivity for adverse outcomes but did not significantly improve prognostic discrimination. Thus, LLM-enhanced frailty assessment may depend on whether the intended use prioritizes broad identification of functional vulnerability or prediction of adverse post-hospital outcomes.

title: Utilization of Laparoscopic Common Bile Duct Exploration: A Veterans Health Admin. Needs Assessment.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Laparoscopic common bile duct exploration (LCBDE) is a safe and cost-effective option for management of choledocholithiasis compared to endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP); however, the procedure remains underutilized nationwide.
METHODS: A national cross-sectional needs assessment survey of Veterans Health Administration (VHA) surgeons was conducted over 15 mo to evaluate current practice patterns related to gallstone-related pathologies as well as provider preferences, training history, knowledge, and utilization of LCBDE. The survey additionally examined ERCP availability, facility transfer requirements, and perceived barriers to LCBDE use. Differences between groups were examined using Pearson's chi-squared test or Kruskal-Wallis test.
RESULTS: 108 surgeon responses were included, representing all 18 Veteran Integrated Service Networks. Respondents predominantly preferred ERCP with laparoscopic cholecystectomy (n = 93, 86%) compared to only 12 (11%) who preferred laparoscopic cholecystectomy + LCBDE. Despite this, 41% (n = 44) have significantly limited ERCP access with only 24% (n = 26) reporting daily access. 78% (n = 84) responded that patients always or sometimes require interhospital transfer for ERCP. Only 35 surgeons (32%) reported using LCBDE with 19% (n = 21) frequently or always utilizing intraoperative cholangiogram. Lack of procedural knowledge (n = 47) and equipment access (n = 32) were the most noted barriers to LCBDE implementation.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite limited ERCP access and high transfer rates for those who require endoscopic intervention, LCBDE utilization within the VHA remains limited with notable perceived barriers to implementation including training, exposure, and equipment access. The VHA currently exists as a powerful opportunity to increase LCBDE utilization, improving and expediting patient care in resource limited environments.

title: SafeLens: A Statistically Controlled Nonlinear Machine Learning Framework for Characterizing Hidden Dynamics in Event-Locked Neural Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT Machine learning has advanced rapidly over the past decade, yet event-locked neural activity is still analyzed predominantly with traditional statistics and linear models. While traditional linear methods provide computationally tractable statistical control for pre-selected features or trial-averaged waveforms, they miss subtle nonlinear and trial-varying neural dynamics. Nonlinear models can capture these complex patterns, but their feature reliance is opaque and notoriously difficult to threshold statistically. We introduce SafeLens (Searchlight Analysis of Fluctuation Events, Leveraging Extensive Null Sampling) to combine the power of nonlinear machine learning with the rigorous false-positive control of traditional statistical inference. At each position of a sliding window, a random forest learns to discriminate event-locked activity from interleaved resting-state neural activity using multiscale temporal derivatives. Randomized feature ablation inverts slope polarity in held-out trials to map the random forest models’ reliance on specific rising versus falling excursions across the time-frequency space. SafeLens then establishes an empirical null by running the same pipeline on separate resting-state recordings, training forests to discriminate rest from rest. This empirical null translates each channel’s complex nonlinear resting dynamics into a model-matched noise floor on the map’s linear reliance scale, allowing a single threshold to control the family-wise error rate against the channel’s own background structure rather than a summary statistic of its baseline. When we injected simulated cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) into resting intracranial EEG recordings, SafeLens recovered ~2.5 times as many polarity-resolved deflections as trial-average thresholding and the closest data-driven method, maintaining its advantage under trial-to-trial variability while yielding ~5–11 times fewer false components, ~2–5 times lower mean boundary error, and superior single-trial latency tracking as a timing prior. In eight patients, CCEPs remained detectable above chance until 1,040 ms after stimulation, compared with 570 and 455 ms for those benchmarks. Together, these findings establish SafeLens as a novel solution for enabling nonlinear models to uncover subtle, trial-varying neural dynamics under strict statistical control. Author Summary Much of what we know about brain function comes from measuring how neural activity responds to specific events, from sensory stimuli and cognitive demands to targeted pulses of brain stimulation. Tracking these responses is fundamental for mapping how brain networks communicate in health and disease and for guiding interventions that modulate neural circuits. Because each response is buried in ongoing background activity and changes across repetitions, isolating it is difficult. Existing methods average repetitions inside short, hand-picked time windows, restricting researchers to seeing only the earliest, most stereotyped part of a response while leaving later, fluctuating activity invisible. Here, we introduce a new approach that combines the pattern-finding sensitivity of modern machine learning with the strict false-positive control of traditional statistics. Our method searches the period after each event without a preset window, using recordings of the brain at rest both to learn how a response differs from normal background activity and to measure what the model detects by chance alone. Using this tool, we show that human brain responses to electrical stimulation last over twice as long as previously recognized, revealing that brief perturbations trigger a longer cascade of neural activity than previously thought.

title: Serologic and clinical correlates of within-host SARS-CoV-2 genetic diversity in a large acute-infection cohort
abstract: Within-host evolution of SARS-CoV-2 has been described primarily in the setting of prolonged infection among immunocompromised individuals, but the determinants of viral genetic diversity during acute infection remain incompletely understood. In particular, the relationships among prior immune exposure, vaccination, viral burden, and intra-host viral populations early in infection remain unclear. We examined whether serologic markers of prior immune exposure or vaccination were associated with within-host SARS-CoV-2 genetic diversity during acute infection. We analyzed SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome deep sequencing data from nasal swabs collected at the time of diagnosis from 4200 acutely infected individuals enrolled across a geographically diverse cohort. Intra-host viral genetic diversity was quantified as the number of intra-host single nucleotide variants (iSNVs) detected per sample. Host immune and clinical factors evaluated included receptor-binding domain (RBD)-neutralizing antibody positivity, nucleocapsid antibody positivity, Spike IgG antibody positivity, vaccination status, and immunosuppressed status. Associations between these factors and viral diversity were assessed using multivariable Poisson generalized linear models with a log link, adjustment for overdispersion, an offset for callable genome size, and covariates retained in the base model. At least two iSNVs were detected in viruses from 1977 (47%) participants, indicating measurable within-host genetic diversity during acute infection. RBD-neutralizing antibodies were detected in plasma from 1,598 (38%) participants. In multivariable analyses, RBD-neutralizing antibody positivity was independently associated with higher iSNV counts ( p < 0.001; incidence rate ratio [IRR]=1.24, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10–1.41). Similar associations were observed for nucleocapsid antibody positivity ( p < 0.001; IRR = 1.27, 95% CI 1.12–1.44). In contrast, vaccination status, defined as receipt of at least one dose, was associated with lower iSNV counts ( p = 0.043; IRR = 0.86, 95% CI 0.74–1.00), while immunosuppressed status was not significantly associated with iSNV counts ( p = 0.23). Additional factors associated with higher iSNV counts included lower viral loads in nasal mucosa, lower plasma N antigen levels, and longer duration of symptoms prior to diagnosis. Because samples were collected at a single timepoint, these associations do not establish whether antibody positivity contributes to within-host diversity or instead reflects infection timing or prior immune exposure. Serologic markers of prior immune exposure and any-dose vaccination status were associated with measurable differences in intra-host SARS-CoV-2 genetic diversity during acute infection in this large cohort. These findings provide a large descriptive baseline for future longitudinal studies of within-host viral dynamics. Four studies from which we obtained the samples have been registered in ClinicalTrials.gov: ITAC, ID: NCT04546581, Date: 2020–09–08; TICO, ID: NCT04501978, Date: 2020–08–03; TESICO, ID: NCT04843761, Date: 2021–04–09 and ICOS, ID: NCT04385251, Date: 2020–05–08.

title: Cumulative multi-threshold intraoperative blood pressure exposure patterns and postoperative mortality.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypotension is commonly defined as MAP <65 mmHg. We evaluated whether cumulative exposure across multiple MAP thresholds provides additional mortality-associated information beyond this single threshold.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults having non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery using perioperative electronic health record data. Pressure-time burden and proportion of operative time were calculated across MAP thresholds from 50 to 150 mmHg. Decision-tree analysis using recursive partitioning sequentially grouped patients according to MAP exposure patterns associated with 30-day mortality. Discrimination of the multi-threshold blood-pressure-only model was compared with that of a model restricted to exposure below MAP 65 mmHg. Medication associations were exploratory.
RESULTS: Among 388,407 patients, 30-day mortality was 1.49%. The multi-threshold model had greater validation discrimination than the MAP 65 mmHg model (AUROC, 0.619 vs. 0.591; ΔAUROC, 0.028; 95% CI, 0.025-0.037; p < 0.001), although the improvement was modest. Terminal exposure groups defined by complete combinations of MAP level and cumulative exposure had different observed mortality rates. Medication associations varied across groups. Observed 30-day mortality was generally higher with deeper hypotension and a greater proportion of operative time spent below MAP thresholds, although the relationship was not uniformly monotonic.
CONCLUSIONS: Multi-threshold MAP exposure captured mortality-associated information not represented by exposure below MAP 65 mmHg alone, complementing this clinical threshold. The multi-threshold analysis identified groups with distinct pressure-time exposure patterns, providing a basis for hemodynamic profiling and investigation of hypotension-related outcomes. External validation is needed to assess the reproducibility and discrimination of these groups in other populations, followed by prospective studies to determine whether management informed by these patterns improves outcomes.

title: Reassessing burnout definitions and interventions: a qualitative study of mental health care providers’ responses to individual-focused approaches to burnout
abstract: Abstract Background Mental health care providers (MHPs) in the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) report high levels of burnout, and the VHA named burnout as an organizational priority at the time this study was conducted. However, a lack of consensus persists regarding burnout’s definition, and although organizational causes of burnout are well-understood, most burnout interventions target individuals through wellness and training programs, which may result in a gap between available interventions and the needs of MHPs. This study sought to contribute to efforts to clarify the definition of burnout and determine what interventions are most appropriate based on MHPs’ experiences of burnout. Methods We conducted an exploratory qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 54 MHPs (social workers [ N = 19], psychologists [ N = 20], psychiatrists [ N = 12] and behavioral health leadership [ N = 3]) across nine VHA sites with varying levels of facility-wide burnout and MHP staffing levels. We used content analysis to analyze interview data. Results According to participants’ definitions and experiences, burnout is a relational phenomenon between individuals and the workplace that emerges when employees continually encounter problems with who has power in deciding allocation of resources, who gets held responsible for burnout, who has influence over workplace conditions, who has power and autonomy in how they do their work, the relative importance of worker well-being, structural limitations on employees’ ability to carry out the purpose of their job, and work cultures that normalize “do more with less.” Participants described individual-targeted burnout interventions as “victim-blaming” and overlooking systemic causes of burnout. Participants not experiencing burnout reported using individualized tactics such as seeking positions with caseload caps and setting “hard boundaries” regarding workload. Participants suggested organization-targeted burnout interventions. Conclusion Our findings problematize framing burnout as a phenomenon that exists within individuals and the predominance of individual-targeted burnout interventions. Burnout may be conceptualized as a distinct form of distress produced by detrimental dynamics within organizational contexts for which individual-targeted interventions alone do not work. Processes of medicalization may explain the persistence of defining and addressing burnout on an individual level rather than an organizational level. To implement systemic changes, healthcare systems may need to confront social, political, and economic limitations on those changes. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Volumetric Quantification of Urinary Stone Burden and Hydronephrosis From CT Images
abstract: Abstract Purpose Given the limitations of conventional stone burden assessment based on maximum diameter or ellipsoid-derived volume estimates, we aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)–based method for automated quantification of stone and hydronephrosis volumes from CT images. Materials and Methods A 2-step algorithm was developed. First, a U-Net incorporating residual blocks, dense blocks, a morphology-aware block, and attention gates (RDAM U-Net) segmented the kidneys; hyperparameters were optimized using Complex System Response (CSR) experimental design with 5-fold cross-validation. Second, within the segmented kidney, hydronephrosis was identified from low–Hounsfield unit (HU) regions, and renal stones from high-HU regions using morphological processing and 3-dimensional (3D) connected-component analysis. AI-derived stone volumes were compared with ellipsoid-based estimates using Pearson and Spearman correlation, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Bland–Altman analysis. Results Eighty-two kidney CT cases were used for model development. RDAM U-Net achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.9432 and Dice coefficient of 0.9681, with fewer parameters and a 32.58% shorter parameter-update time than reference attention-based U-Nets. In 39 paired stone measurements, AI-derived and ellipsoid-estimated volumes showed a near-perfect correlation (Pearson r = 0.977; Spearman ρ = 0.966; R² = 0.954; all p < 0.001) and high agreement (Lin's CCC = 0.959; ICC = 0.960). AI volumes were systematically lower than ellipsoid estimates (mean difference, − 51.21 mm³; p = 0.001), with the difference increasing with stone volume. HU-based composition analysis agreed with the clinical record in 12 of 13 classifiable stones (92.3%). Conclusions AI-based CT segmentation enabled automated volumetric quantification of both urinary stone burden and hydronephrosis, providing direct 3D assessment without reliance on geometric assumptions. Integrating stone volume, hydronephrosis volume, and stone composition into a single automated workflow may support more individualized surgical and metabolic management of urolithiasis. Further validation in larger external cohorts is warranted.

title: Estimating GFR: what it is, what it is not, and why prediction cannot settle the question.
abstract: Schultheiss et al. show that replacing Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration with European Kidney Function Consortium cystatin C-based equations reclassifies women, but not men, into milder chronic kidney disease stages, while outcome prediction is unchanged. We argue that prediction of kidney failure cannot validate a glomerular filtration rate equation: dialysis initiation is a clinical decision, not a filtration measurement. The analysis is cross-sectional, leaving longitudinal performance untested. Equations are population tools; at the bedside, non-glomerular filtration rate determinants of both creatinine and cystatin C can mislead.

title: Optic Disc Features in Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: Spatial Organization and Structure-Function Associations.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether funduscopic features in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) are spatially organized and associated with structural and functional measures at presentation and outcome.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional and longitudinal secondary analysis of the multicenter, QRK207 NAION treatment trial (NCT02341560).
PARTICIPANTS: Trial participants with symptomatic NAION and gradable color fundus photographs at enrollment (n=728) and Month 6 (M6; n=547).
METHODS: We quantified hemorrhage, hyperemia, axoplasmic stasis (cotton wool spots/micro-opacities), pallid edema, and chronic changes via manual annotation. Each feature was analyzed both as presence versus absence (prespecified primary) and as burden standardized to disc area (secondary). Peripapillary swelling was graded 0-4 by degree of vessel obscuration. Spatial distribution was mapped using modified Garway-Heath sectors. We assessed associations with VF, OCT-derived swelling, and symptom duration.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Global and sectoral VF sensitivity (average total deviation; avgTD) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at enrollment and M6; OCT-derived peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, peripapillary optic nerve head volume, and rate of ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thinning.
RESULTS: At enrollment, hyperemic swelling (88.9%) and hemorrhage (79.5%) predominated, and pallid edema was common (27.9%). Acute hyperemia clustered nasally. Hyperemic swelling area correlated with shorter symptom duration (rs = -0.12, p = 0.004). The presence of pallid edema was associated with faster GCIPL thinning (-1.12 vs -0.37 µm/day, p < 0.001), worse enrollment acuity in multivariable models (β = -6.69 letters; p = 0.002), and modestly longer symptom duration (median 11 vs 10 days; p = 0.03). Enrollment features weakly associated with VF but did not predict M6 avgTD. Inferior peripapillary swelling mildly correlated with worse enrollment superior field deviation (rs = -0.27, p < 0.001). At M6, pallor was most prevalent (86.7%), clustered temporally, and was independently associated with worse avgTD (Inferior ONH to superior VF: β=-2.07 dB; p= 0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: Funduscopic features in NAION exhibit distinct, topographically organized spatial and temporal patterns reflecting evolving tissue injury, but have limited standalone prognostic value for long-term visual outcomes. Notably, acute pallid edema is relatively common in NAION.

title: Human genetic investigation of TMPRSS6 as a therapeutic target for liver disease: efficacy and safety liabilities
abstract: Abstract Background & Aims Disease-modifying therapies for steatohepatitis and fibrosis remain limited. Matriptase-2 (TMPRSS6), a serine protease suppressing hepcidin to regulate iron homeostasis, is under clinical investigation for iron overload, and preclinical evidence suggests its inhibition may attenuate metabolic liver disease. Whether these effects translate to humans remains unknown. Methods We proxied TMPRSS6 inhibition using the missense variant rs855791, weighted on circulating hepcidin. Using Mendelian randomization (MR), we assessed effects on (1) magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver phenotypes, including corrected T1 (cT1) and proton density fat fraction (PDFF), liver enzymes and clinical liver outcomes; (2) cardiometabolic endpoints; (3) 2,940 plasma proteins; (4) clinical biomarkers; and (5) 2,272 disease endpoints. Colocalization and mediation analyses were used to characterize mechanisms. Results Genetically proxied TMPRSS6 inhibition was associated with lower liver iron content (β = −2.50, P<0.001) and higher cT1 (β = 1.59, P<0.001), with colocalization indicating a shared causal signal. No association was observed with PDFF, liver volume, NAFLD, cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma. Genetically proxied TMPRSS6 inhibition was also associated with lower C-reactive protein (β = −0.17, P<0.001), higher LDL cholesterol (β = 0.22, P<0.001) and higher coronary artery disease (CAD) risk (OR = 1.59, P<0.001), with weak colocalization of CAD with hepcidin (PP.H4 = 0.56) and LDL cholesterol (PP.H4 = 0.48). Mediation analysis suggested LDL cholesterol may account for approximately 21% (95% CI 9% to 34%) of the CAD association. Conclusions Human genetic evidence supports hepatic iron lowering by TMPRSS6 inhibition, but not an effect on steatosis. Higher cT1, without concordant associations with clinical liver outcomes, may reflect reduced hepatic iron rather than worsening fibroinflammation. The CAD signal, partly mediated by LDL cholesterol, warrants careful consideration in trial design. Impact and implications Preclinical studies have identified TMPRSS6 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy for metabolic liver disease, but its effects in humans and potential safety consequences remain uncertain. Using human genetic evidence, we show that genetically proxied TMPRSS6 inhibition is associated with lower hepatic iron content but not hepatic steatosis, while identifying increased coronary artery disease risk as a potential cardiovascular safety liability. These findings are relevant to researchers and drug developers pursuing TMPRSS6-directed therapies, as they suggest that clinical benefit may be more likely in patients with excess hepatic iron and highlight the importance of cardiovascular risk assessment and lipid monitoring during clinical development. As genetic proxies reflect lifelong perturbation rather than pharmacological treatment, prospective clinical studies are required to determine whether these hepatic and cardiovascular effects are reproduced with therapeutic TMPRSS6 inhibition. Highlights Genetically predicted TMPRSS6 inhibition was associated with lower hepatic iron content. No associations were observed with hepatic steatosis or liver volume. Genetically predicted TMPRSS6 inhibition was associated with increased CAD risk. LDL-C mediated around one fifth of the CAD association.

title: Long-term outcomes of ultrasound-detected hepatic steatosis in primary care: a record linkage study
abstract: Objectives To determine the long-term outcomes of patients with and without ultrasound-detected liver steatosis in primary care to inform guidelines for management of the common finding of steatosis in primary care. Design A record-linkage cohort study with 15-year follow-up. Setting 11 English primary care practices that previously participated in the Birmingham and Lambeth Liver Evaluation Testing Strategies (BALLETS) study. Participants A total of 1215 adults with abnormal liver function tests who underwent an intensive set of diagnostic studies, including ultrasound. Primary and secondary outcome measures The primary liver outcome was death due to liver disease and/or hospital admission with a primary diagnosis of liver disease. Secondary outcomes were hospital admission where liver disease was recorded as a secondary diagnosis, and outpatient attendance under the care of a liver specialist consultant. Results We followed up 760 patients with no steatosis and 455 with steatosis. The unadjusted HR for the primary outcome over 15 years was 1.97 (95% CI 1.23 to 3.01). After making adjustment for age, sex, alcohol intake and Body Mass Index, the probability of the primary liver outcome was 7.7 with no steatosis, vs 14.0 with steatosis—a difference of 6.3% (95% CI 3.2 to 11.2). This relative risk difference was stable over 5, 10 and 15 years. The presence of high Body Mass Index only slightly increased the association between steatosis and liver disease, but the association was more strongly influenced by drinking over the recommended alcohol level. Conclusion Over a 15-year follow-up period, the risk of liver disease is approximately doubled (14% vs 7.7%) if steatosis is present.

title: c-Jun N-Terminal Kinase-2 Mediates Alcohol and Corticosterone-Induced Tissue Injury at the Gut-Liver Axis.
abstract: Chronic stress and the stress hormone corticosterone are exacerbating factors in alcohol-induced gut and liver injury; however, the underlying mechanisms are poorly defined. This study investigates the potential role of c-Jun N-terminal kinase 2 (JNK2) in alcohol- and corticosterone-mediated gut and liver injury. The effects of chronic ethanol feeding and corticosterone administration on gut and liver injury were evaluated in JNK2 knockout (JNK2-KO) and wild-type mice. We measured gut permeability to FITC-inulin in vivo; epithelial tight junction (TJ) integrity by immunofluorescence confocal microscopy; microbiota dysbiosis by 16S rRNA sequencing; mucosal inflammatory responses by cytokine mRNA assay; endotoxemia by plasma lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels; systemic inflammation by cytokine ELISA; and liver damage by multiple assays. Data show that chronic ethanol feeding-induced gut barrier dysfunction, epithelial TJ disruption, and colonic mucosal inflammatory responses were potentiated by corticosterone in the wild-type mice, but not in JNK2-KO mice. Microbiota analyses indicated that the gut microbiota composition in pair-fed and ethanol-fed JNK2-KO mice is distinctly different from that of wild-type mice. The effects of ethanol and its potentiation by corticosterone on Paneth cell-specific genes were absent in JNK2-KO mice. Ethanol-induced intestinal mucosal inflammatory responses, endotoxemia, and systemic inflammation, and their potentiation by corticosterone, were absent in JNK2-KO mice. Ethanol-induced liver injury and its potentiation by corticosterone, as assessed by plasma AST/ALT, liver triglyceride, histopathology, and cytokine expression, were also absent in JNK2-KO mice. These data demonstrate that JNK2 plays a pivotal role in ethanol-induced tissue injury at the Gut-Liver axis and that this effect is potentiated by corticosterone.

title: Sleep and Cognitive Performance: Exploring Benzodiazepine Receptor Agonist Use, Insomnia Symptoms, and Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that benzodiazepine/z-drug (BZRA) dose, insomnia symptoms, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) risk are associated with cognitive performance above and beyond other modifiable dementia risk factors.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we used baseline data from recruited patients without dementia from one VA site and one academic site to analyze regression models based on previously published risk factors for cognitive impairment, adapted to include sleep and benzodiazepine usage interactions. Changes in R2 and model fit (F-tests) were examined for four nested regression models predicting Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Trail Making Test (TMT)-A, TMT-B, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST). Base Models included common dementia risk factors. Model-2 = Base + Insomnia Severity Index; Model-3 = Model-2 + dose; Model-4 = Model-3 + OSA risk; and Model-5 = Model-4 + OSA-BZRA.
RESULTS: R2 for the base model predicting MMSE was 0.139 (n = 313), 0.241 for TMT-A (n = 298), 0.229 for TMT-B (n = 287), and 0.189 for DSST (n = 285). Model-5 R2 was 0.142 for MMSE, 0.246 for TMT-A, 0.238 for TMT-B, and 0.190 for DSST, with all F-test p-values >.145.
CONCLUSIONS: Sleep disorder variables did not significantly explain additional variation in cognition performance. Studies with a wider range of cognitive performance are needed.

title: Peripheral intravenous waveform analysis - a novel tool to confirm intravascular catheter placement.
abstract: Peripheral intravenous (IV) catheter infiltration is a common complication which can cause harmful extravasation of fluid and medications. Significant injury can occur before standard infusion pumps detect a threshold pressure. Peripheral IV waveform analysis (PIVA) uses fast Fourier transform (FFT) to measure the amplitude of the venous waveform. This study aims to evaluate if PIVA can differentiate between IV catheter positions, primarily intravenous versus subcutaneous, in a rat model. Surgical cutdown was performed on the right proximal saphenous vein. Pressure and waveforms were recorded from a 22G IV catheter open-to-air, in the vein, and in the adjacent subcutaneous (SC) tissue. Measurements were performed at baseline and after injection of 1 mL Plasmalyte and are reported as median (interquartile range). The peak amplitude corresponding to the heart rate frequency labeled as f1. Pre-flush intravascular f1, 0.0824 mmHg (IQR 0.0256, 0.1480), differed significantly from both SC, 0.0001 mmHg (0.0000, 0.0004), and open-to-air, 0.0001 mmHg (0.0000, 0.0008), conditions, ANOVA p = 0.03, pairwise p = 0.049 and 0.049, respectively. These significant differences remained after flush. Post-flush pressures between IV, 7.9 mmHg (6.6, 8.9) and SC, 20.5 mmHg (11.3, 28.8) were significantly different, p = 0.0001. There was no significant difference in pre-flush and post-flush pressure within IV, SC, and open-air groups, p = 0.687, p = 0.110 and p = 0.219, respectively. PIVA was superior to absolute pressure measurement for detecting intravascular versus extravascular placement of an IV catheter. This study demonstrates utility of PIVA as a novel method for confirming proper IV placement.
