title: Quantifying the unique needs of women with lower limb loss: A national, cross-sectional, survey-based needs assessment.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite the increasing population of women with limb loss, data to sufficiently characterize potential gender-based differences are lacking, as scientific literature on this topic is often not specifically designed to assess the unique needs of women. Fragmentary information has indicated that women experience a variety of physical and psychological challenges that differ from those experienced by men, but this information has yet to be fully explored. This is the first exploratory needs assessment to combine population-specific physical and psychosocial assessments, as well as gap items that current measures do not capture.
METHODS: In this national, cross-sectional, survey-based needs assessment, individuals with lower limb loss recruited across the Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Defense, and civilian settings completed an online survey. Responses to the survey generated a subset of quantitative scores across several physical and psychosocial domains to compare outcomes between women and men with lower limb loss. Ordered beta regression and multiple linear regression models were used to test the association of gender with scale outcomes, while controlling for additional covariates.
RESULTS: A total of 229 individuals (130 women, 99 men) completed the needs assessment. Results highlighted decreased levels of aesthetic and functional satisfaction, body image, and social adjustment, as well as higher levels of anxiety, in women with limb loss compared with men. There were no differences in depression, activity restriction, or healthcare needs between women and men.
CONCLUSIONS: An important contribution of this exploratory needs assessment was its ability to identify candidate constructs that may serve as building blocks for developing a clinically relevant patient-reported outcome measure for women with lower limb loss. Future research should build on these findings to develop and validate women-specific outcome measures, ultimately supporting limb loss care teams in providing optimal, individualized care for this underserved population.

title: Prognostication in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Narrative Review of Pre-Diagnosis and Functional Outcomes
abstract: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a very heterogeneous disease, yet some of the most common questions received by physicians in the ALS clinic are "how much time do I have?" and "what can I expect to happen next?" This line of inquiry is not strictly limited to patients; clinicians also need an idea of prognosis to appropriately plan for treatment decisions and prepare the patient and caregiver for future care needs. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on prognostic indicators in ALS, organized across three temporal phases: factors preceding diagnosis, factors present at diagnosis, and factors emerging after diagnosis. Pre-diagnosis predictors include age at onset, sex, socioeconomic status, genetic background, premorbid Body Mass Index (BMI) and nutritional status, and comorbid disease. At diagnosis, clinical phenotype and site of onset, diagnostic delay, baseline Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Functional Rating Score-Revised (ALSFRS-R) and forced vital capacity, cognitive involvement, fluid biomarkers, and electrophysiologic measures carry prognostic weight. Post-diagnosis, the trajectory is refined by the rate of ALSFRS-R decline, serial respiratory measures, and weight loss, and is actively modified by clinical interventions including noninvasive ventilation, enteral nutrition, disease-modifying therapy, and multidisciplinary care. Notably, quality of life does not track with physical decline, consistent with the disability paradox described in other severe neurological conditions. For neurorehabilitation, these indicators support a shift from reactive to anticipatory practice: timing equipment provision, communication support, respiratory intervention, and goals-of-care discussions to the predicted trajectory rather than to established deficit. Refinement of prognostic models may also improve stratification in ALS clinical trials.

title: Hepatocyte serine palmitoyltransferase 3 is essential for mitochondrial ceramide homeostasis and electron transport chain function.
abstract: Sphingolipids (SLs) constitute essential membrane lipids that also function as signaling molecules mediating fundamental cellular processes. Disruption of constitutive SL metabolism contributes to a range of metabolic diseases. SL biosynthesis is initiated by serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT), a heteromeric enzyme composed of Sptlc1 and either Sptlc2 or the less-characterized subunit Sptlc3. While the canonical Sptlc1/Sptlc2 complex generates most SLs, Sptlc1/Sptlc3 produces noncanonical SLs that remain poorly understood. Sptlc3 expression increases in liver disease in both mouse models and humans, yet its biological role remains unclear. To address this, we generated a liver-specific SPTLC3 knockout mouse model. Loss of SPTLC3 resulted in severe mitochondrial dysfunction in hepatocytes, characterized by reduced oxygen consumption, decreased ATP production, and elevated NADH/NAD+ ratios with a concomitant increase in glycolytic activity. Mechanistically, we found a defect in the electron transport chain (ETC) which stemmed not from intrinsic impairment of the ETC complexes but rather from hindered electron flow between complex I and complex III likely due to reduced availability of Coenzyme Q. While atypical ceramides constituted (∼4% of total ceramides) when measured in liver homogenates, there measurements in mitochondria-enriched fractions revealed enrichment in this cell compartment. Together, our findings identify SPTLC3 as a critical modulator of mitochondrial ceramide composition and ETC function, revealing a specialized role for noncanonical SLs in hepatocyte energy metabolism.

title: Impaired value estimation over space explains turn-induced freezing of gait in Parkinson’s disease: A cortico-basal ganglia-inspired reinforcement learning model
abstract: ABSTRACT Parkinson’s disease (PD) gait is characterized by reduced walking speed, short shuffling steps, increased double stance time, and increased step time variability. The most debilitating symptom in PD is freezing of gait (FOG), a context-dependent locomotion arrest, mostly occurring while encountering turns, obstacles, and narrow pathways. FOG is more pronounced during turning, a complex task that challenges motor planning and execution. Here, we simulate this phenomenon using a computational model inspired by the cortico-basal ganglia circuitry, based on reinforcement learning (RL) principles. In the model, the agent was trained to learn a value profile while navigating a path that involved turning. To simulate PD conditions, we clamped the temporal difference (TD) error, typically associated with dopaminergic signaling. Our model results show that compared to healthy controls (HC), PD non-freezers and PD freezers exhibit a reduction in turning velocity and step length, alongside an attenuated compensatory step-width widening at the sharpest turn, more pronounced in PD freezers, who additionally show increased step time variability. These kinematic impairments worsen during tighter turns. Ultimately, this model implicates FOG as a problem of impaired estimation of value over space and could potentially represent a generalized deficit in gait impairments in PD.

title: Top Ten Tips Palliative Care Clinicians Should Know About Caring for People Receiving Critical Care for Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide and is a major driver of critical illness, resulting in admission to cardiac intensive care units (CICUs). Patients with acute, life-threatening CVD often experience episodes of acute decompensation characterized by high symptom burden that may portend progressive loss of function, significantly impair quality of life (QOL), and involve high-intensity, technologically advanced therapies to sustain life. Despite these advances, up to 30% of patients die during CICU hospitalizations, and those who survive may subsequently face persistent functional impairment and psychosocial distress. During critical CVD (CCVD), patients often endure prognostic uncertainty and face complex decisions regarding life-sustaining therapies alongside refractory symptoms. Thus, care that focuses exclusively on disease-directed or life-prolonging therapies is often insufficient to address the full spectrum of patient and caregiver needs. When integrated alongside intensive cardiovascular care, palliative care (PC) offers a complementary and essential approach to the management of CCVD to inform therapeutic decisions, improve QOL, and address psychosocial and spiritual well-being. In this article, a multidisciplinary team featuring PC clinicians (physicians, nurse practitioners, social worker, psychologist, and chaplain), cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, cardiothoracic anesthesiologists, and intensivists present evidence-based guidance in a "Top Ten Tips" format to support PC clinicians caring for CICU patients and their caregivers.

title: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Reclassifies Mortality Risk Beyond Traditional Risk Factors: The ETHOS Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) is a powerful predictor of mortality, but its incremental value for improving clinical risk classification beyond traditional cardiovascular risk factors remains incompletely defined. We evaluated whether the addition of CRF improves 10-year mortality risk prediction using contemporary reclassification metrics.
METHODS: We analyzed 562,234 adults from a clinical exercise testing cohort with complete covariate data. CRF was assessed by peak metabolic equivalents (METs) achieved during treadmill testing and dichotomized as fit versus unfit, with unfit defined as the least fit quintile (<5.0 METs). Cox proportional hazards models were constructed to estimate 10-year all-cause mortality risk using traditional risk factors (age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and smoking), with and without CRF. Incremental prognostic value of CRF was assessed using categorical and continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and Harrell's C-statistic.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 10.2±5.1 years, CRF was independently associated with mortality, with each 1-MET higher CRF associated with a 16% lower hazard of death (hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI 0.838-0.842; p<0.001). The addition of CRF significantly improved risk prediction, yielding a categorical NRI of 0.06 and a continuous NRI of 0.37 (both p<0.001), with significant improvement in IDI. Model discrimination increased from 0.662 to 0.682 after addition of CRF (ΔC=0.020; p<0.001). Adjusted 10-year mortality risk was substantially higher among unfit versus fit individuals (32.9% vs 13.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: CRF significantly improves 10-year mortality risk prediction beyond traditional cardiovascular risk factors and meaningfully enhances individual-level risk stratification. Incorporation of CRF into routine clinical risk assessment frameworks should be considered.

title: Demonstration of a methodology for long-term tracking of intracortical microstimulation-evoked perception thresholds in rat somatosensory cortex.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) offers a promising approach for enabling sensory feedback by directly activating neurons within the somatosensory cortex to more fully realize closed-loop neuroprosthetic systems. Despite this potential, questions persist regarding how stable ICMS-evoked responses remain over extended implantation periods.
NEW METHOD: Given the paucity of preclinical tools for examining these temporal patterns, we extended a previously developed rodent nose-poke go/no-go behavioral framework to assess the reliability of ICMS perception thresholds across a 30-week implantation window. Rats implanted with microwire arrays underwent weekly threshold and behavioral-performance assessment, alongside recordings of electrophysiological and electrochemical data to assess correlates of paradigm reliability.
RESULTS: Threshold values initially fell in an exponential-like manner from weeks 5-12 post-implantation before approaching a fitted asymptote of ~1.1 nC/ph per electrode across 10 stimulating electrodes. Thereafter, thresholds remained stable through week 30 in animals retaining detectable percepts. Over this period, behavioral performance stabilized, with animals correctly responding to the conditioned stimulus ~90% of the time. Notably, neither neural recording nor electrochemical properties of the arrays provided a robust, cross-animal explanation for perceptual threshold trends, leaving the underlying mechanism unresolved. Compared with naïve cortical tissue, gene expression profiling of the implanted tissue expressed elevated Gfap and Cd68 alongside reduced NeuN and Bdnf-findings common to prior neuroinflammation studies.
COMPARISON WITH EXISTING METHODS: This positive-reinforcement rodent paradigm offers a dependable preclinical alternative for long-term ICMS-threshold assessment.
CONCLUSION: Despite sensation loss in two animals, this behavioral framework offers investigational value for chronic ICMS threshold tracking while sensory percepts remain detectable.

title: DO Generations MAtter for Treatment of Outpatient Pyelonephritis With Cephalosporins in the Emergency Department? DOGMA-ED Study.
abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study was to compare the effectiveness between first-, second-, and third-generation oral cephalosporins for the treatment of pyelonephritis in adult patients discharged from the emergency department (ED).
METHODS: This was a multicenter, retrospective, observational cohort study of 11 geographically distributed academic US EDs. Patients aged ≥18 years who were diagnosed with pyelonephritis and discharged home on an oral cephalosporin from the ED between August 1, 2023 and January 1, 2025 were included. The primary outcome was treatment failure at 14 days between the cephalosporin generations. The composite outcome was defined as one of the following: (1) recurrence of symptoms, (2) repeat ED/urgent care visit due to urinary tract infection, (3) receipt of a new antibiotic prescription for urinary symptoms, or (4) hospitalization due to urinary tract infection. Secondary outcomes included the need to modify the patient's initial antimicrobial regimen based on culture and susceptibility.
RESULTS: A total of 1,147 patients met inclusion, with 618 (53.9%) receiving a first-generation, 91 (7.9%) a second-generation, and 438 (38.2%) a third-generation cephalosporin. Baseline characteristics were similar across cohorts, with women comprising over 85% of the study population. The most prescribed agents were cephalexin (85% of first generation), cefuroxime (100% of second generation), and cefdinir (79% of third generation). There was no statistically significant difference in 14-day treatment failure rates across generations (first versus second: 19.6% versus 17.6%, difference 2.0%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -7.1 to 11.1; first versus third: 19.6% versus 18.0%, difference 1.6%, 95% CI -3.4 to 6.5).
CONCLUSION: First-, second-, and third-generation oral cephalosporins demonstrated comparable 14-day treatment failure rates for the treatment of acute pyelonephritis in patients discharged from the ED.

title: Plasma eMTBR-tau as a robust biomarker for Alzheimer’s disease tangle pathology up to 10 years before death
abstract: Abstract Scalable and accessible biomarkers of neurofibrillary tangle pathology are needed for Alzheimer’s disease prognosis, diagnosis and monitoring. Here, we show that a blood-based immunoassay for an endogenously-cleaved “eMTBR-tau” fragment of tau protein is strongly associated with autopsy-diagnosed Alzheimer neuropathologic change (ADNC) and predominantly reflects the burden and anatomical progression of tangle pathology but not amyloid plaque load despite being most elevated in amyloid-positive symptomatic individuals. Plasma eMTBR-tau was significantly more accurate than plasma p-tau217 in classifying Braak staging and ADNC statuses at autopsy. Importantly, neuropathologic classification by plasma eMTBR-tau remained high (AUC=0.91-0.95) even when increasing intervals between blood collection and death up to a decade, while maintaining superior sensitivity and specificity over p-tau217. Higher baseline plasma eMTBR-tau was associated with worse cognition cross-sectionally and longitudinally predicted faster worsening. These results were replicated in a living cohort with in vivo tangle and plaque neuroimaging. Plasma eMTBR-tau concordance with tau neuroimaging was up to 94%, suggesting surrogacy. Together, plasma eMTBR-tau captures biological signatures of Braak staging and ADNC over a prolonged pre-mortem window, highlighting potential for early disease detection, biological staging, prognosis and therapeutic development.

title: A hospitalist-led short-stay rehabilitation unit reduced inpatient discharge delays.
abstract: Hospitalized patients requiring post-acute rehabilitation often remain in acute care while awaiting skilled nursing facility placement. In July 2023, the San Francisco VA Health Care System opened a hospitalist-led short-stay rehabilitation unit within its Community Living Center, called the Lotus. Mean referral-to-discharge time, excluding referral hold periods, decreased from 6.89 days in fiscal year (FY) 2023 to 4.58 days in FY2024 and 3.35 days in FY2025. The Lotus became the lowest-delay post-acute care destination and the facility's most frequently used individual rehabilitation destination. This model suggests hospitalist integration into post-acute care may improve hospital throughput without expanding post-acute bed capacity.

title: Identifying Incident Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw and Antiresorptive Drug Holidays Using Natural Language Processing on Clinical Notes in Men and Women Prescribed Bisphosphonates or Denosumab for Fracture Prevention.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a rare complication of antiresorptive therapy for osteoporosis, with risk potentially influenced by "drug holidays" around dentoalveolar procedures. MRONJ risk is higher in rheumatic diseases. Epidemiologic studies are limited by poor administrative code performance for MRONJ identification and lack of structured pharmacy data capturing drug holidays. We developed and validated a natural language processing (NLP) algorithm to classify MRONJ and detect drug holidays from free-text clinical notes in electronic health records (EHRs).
METHODS: Using US Veterans Health Administration EHRs, we identified adults aged ≥50 years old with at least one filled prescription for a bisphosphonate or denosumab for fracture prevention (October 1, 1999, to December 31, 2022). An NLP codebook defined 11 targets with 16 attributes. Two annotators independently labeled notes to create a reference set (n = 870; 200 held out for validation) and an independent validation set (n = 100) for performance assessment (precision, recall, and F-measure). A decision tree-based machine-learning model used NLP-extracted features to classify MRONJ. Drug holiday was an NLP target directly.
RESULTS: The reference set included 6,421 annotations, informing a curated vocabulary of >1,350 terms. For MRONJ classification excluding unclassifiable outputs across all validation notes, precision was 1.00 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.86-1.00), recall 0.96 (95% CI 0.80-1.00), and F-measure 0.95 (95% CI 0.88-1.00). For drug holiday detection in the held-out validation set, precision was 0.90 (95% CI 0.83-0.95), recall 0.98 (95% CI 0.93-1.00), and F-measure 0.94.
CONCLUSION: We developed an NLP algorithm that is sufficiently accurate in classifying MRONJ and detecting drug holidays to be a promising tool for future studies, including in people with rheumatic diseases.

title: Carbohydrate Counting in the Real World: Mealtime Insulin Dosing Behaviors and Smartphone App Use in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Strategies for prandial insulin dosing are not well characterized but have important implications for diabetes care in real-world practice. Our objective for this study was to characterize mealtime insulin dosing strategies, evaluate discrepancies between patient-reported and provider-documented dosing approaches, and assess smartphone app use for carbohydrate counting among adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D). RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Adults with T1D with an ICD diagnosis code for T1D and an active patient portal account within an academic health system were invited to complete a survey assessing mealtime insulin dosing behaviors and smartphone application (app) use for carbohydrate counting. Responses were linked to electronic health record data. RESULTS: Among 903 participants, mean age was 45 years and mean diabetes duration was 23 years; 53% were women, 67% were White non-Hispanic, 95% used CGM, and 58% used automated insulin delivery. Overall, 54% reported carbohydrate counting, 39% used experience-based estimation, and 2% used fixed dosing; A1c did not differ by dosing strategy. Among participants with provider-documented carb counting, 36% reported experience-based estimation. App use was infrequent, with 51% reporting never using apps; common barriers were memorization of commonly eaten foods and perceived time burden. CONCLUSIONS: Many adults with T1D rely on heuristic insulin dosing approaches that prioritize practicality over maximal precision and were not associated with worse glycemic outcomes, underscoring the need for practical, sustainable self-management strategies.

title: Acute Effects of Transcutaneous Spinal Cord Stimulation (tSCS) on Gait Symmetry in People with Chronic Stroke
abstract: Objectives To determine whether transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (tSCS) modulates gait symmetry after a single bout of 25 minutes of treadmill gait training and to establish whether a particular combination of tSCS frequency and intensity elicits greater gait symmetry changes. Materials and Methods In each of six sessions, 20 chronic stroke participants received 25 minutes of treadmill gait training while they received either SHAM stimulation or one of four unique STIM (tSCS) parameter combinations: 30 or 50Hz frequency, and intensity at participant tolerance (TOL) or 30% of minimum resting motor threshold (RMT min ). In each session, our primary outcomes were step length (m) and swing duration (sec) symmetry during the 10-meter Walk Test (10MWT) PRE and POST treadmill training. We also computed an "overall" symmetry measure, the Combined Gait Asymmetry Metric (CGAM), and 10MWT gait speed. PRE to POST-intervention changes and how they differ among stimulation parameters were assessed via the Timepoint x Intervention interaction effect of a two-way repeated measures ANOVA. A complementary exploratory analysis was performed to determine individualized "best" vs "worst" stimulation parameters compared to SHAM. Results Among the five interventions tested, we found no statistically significant difference in the PRE to POST change in the primary outcome variables – step length symmetry ( Timepoint x Intervention effect, p=0.0564) and swing duration symmetry (p=0.6215) – or in CGAM (p=0.5350) or 10MWT gait speed (p=0.4828). Conclusions We found that 25 minutes of tSCS plus treadmill training did not significantly change gait symmetry or speed compared to treadmill training alone. These findings also suggest that in a single session setting there may not be a best frequency or intensity that is optimal for everyone. Future work should investigate whether person-specific stimulation parameters may yield single-day gait symmetry changes, as well as potential longitudinal effects of tSCS plus gait training.

title: Decomposed arterial stiffness and NfL–cognition association in older adults: The IGNITE study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) indexes neuroaxonal injury and relates to poorer cognition. Higher carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) arterial stiffness strengthens NfL-cognition associations, but reflects both pressure-standardized structural stiffness (S-PWV) and transient hemodynamic load-dependent pulse wave velocity (LD-PWV). We tested which component drives this interaction. METHODS: Plasma NfL and cfPWV were measured in 552 cognitively unimpaired older adults. cfPWV was decomposed into S-PWV and LD-PWV. Five latent cognitive domains were modeled. Linear regression tested PWV moderators of NfL-cognition associations. RESULTS: > 0.09). DISCUSSION: Nominal interactions were more consistent for S-PWV. Findings did not provide multiplicity-adjusted evidence of component-specific moderation.ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02875301.

title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Region-Specific Remodeling in Vein Grafts After Peripheral Arterial Bypass
abstract: Abstract Background Vein graft failure due to intimal hyperplasia and maladaptive remodeling remains a major limitation of peripheral bypass surgery. Although vascular remodeling is recognized as a multilayered process, layer-specific molecular mechanisms that distinguish adaptive from negative remodeling remain incompletely understood. We aimed to investigate the vascular microenvironment of patent and stenotic grafts using spatial transcriptomics. Methods Vein specimens were obtained from three patients undergoing revision surgery. For each patient, a matched set of three samples was collected: unused saphenous vein (Denovo), normally healed vein graft (Non-stenosed), and stenosed vein graft (Stenosed) (n = 3 patients). GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiling with the Human Whole Transcriptome Atlas was used to map gene expression across intima, medial, and adventitial layers. Differential expression, gene ontology, spatial deconvolution, and immunohistochemistry were integrated for analysis. Results Non-stenosed and Stenosed grafts shared transcriptional features distinct from Denovo veins, particularly in pathways related to cell proliferation. Non-stenosed grafts showed increased expression of CDKN1A across all vascular layers, whereas Stenosed grafts exhibited enhanced mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway activity, reduced DUSP1 -mediated regulation, and increased macrophage accumulation. ECM remodeling showed layer-specific organization, with VCAN and ACAN enriched in the intima and DCN in the adventitia, while Stenosed grafts demonstrated a trend toward collagen-dominant remodeling. Cell deconvolution suggested a shift toward vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC)-dominant architecture after arterialization, with modest enrichment of synthetic VSMC signatures in stenotic regions. Conclusions Vein graft stenosis appears to be associated with layer-specific alterations in cell cycle regulation, inflammatory signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, and VSMC phenotype. Spatial transcriptomic analysis reveals molecular heterogeneity not captured by bulk approaches and provides preliminary insight into graft remodeling. These findings may inform future studies to improve long-term graft patency.

title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Regional Myocardial Flow Reserve Beyond Global Flow and Perfusion: REFINE PET
abstract: Abstract Background The incremental prognostic value of regional myocardial flow reserve (MFR) assessed by positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) beyond global MFR remains unclear. We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of regional MFR in the international multicenter REFINE PET registry. Methods This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 35,391 patients from 13 sites in the international REFINE PET registry who underwent rubidium-82 ( 82 Rb) and 13 N-ammonia ( 13 NH 3 ) PET MPI. Abnormal MFR was defined as <2.0. Patients were classified into three groups: MFR-Group 1 (normal global and regional MFR; n=19,744), MFR-Group 2 (normal global MFR but abnormal regional MFR; n=3,184), and MFR-Group 3 (abnormal global and regional MFR; n=12,463). Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) included all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, late revascularization (>90 days), and hospital admission for unstable angina. Results During a mean follow-up of 4.0 ± 2.9 years, 9,903 patients (28.0%) experienced MACE. Annualized MACE rates increased stepwise across MFR-Groups 1-3 (4.0%/year, 7.5%/year, and 11.8%/year, respectively; p <0.001). Abnormal regional MFR independently predicted MACE after adjustment for clinical risk factors, global MFR, and stress total perfusion deficit (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.25–1.43). Adding regional MFR to a model including global MFR significantly improved model fit (χ² 4,784 to 4,871; p <0.001), discrimination (AUC 0.710 to 0.729; p <0.001), and reclassification (NRI 41.9%). Among patients with normal perfusion and preserved global MFR, abnormal regional MFR identified higher risk (5.0%/year vs. 2.8%/year; p <0.001). Conclusions Regional MFR provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional PET MPI findings, including global MFR, and may refine risk stratification, particularly when global MFR is preserved. Clinical perspectives Global myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is widely used for risk stratification in patients undergoing positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). However, regional abnormalities in MFR may be overlooked when global MFR is preserved. In this international multicenter study of 35,391 patients, abnormal regional MFR was independently associated with major adverse cardiovascular events and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical and PET-MPI findings, including global MFR and myocardial perfusion abnormalities. Importantly, even among patients with normal perfusion and preserved global MFR, those with abnormal regional MFR had a substantially higher annualized event rate than those with normal regional MFR (5.0% versus 2.8%). These findings highlight the importance of assessing regional MFR in addition to global MFR during routine PET-MPI interpretation. Graphic Abstract

title: Disrupted microbial queuosine biosynthesis contributes to dysbiosis in human inflammatory bowel disease
abstract: Background and Aims: As a microbiome/diet-derived vitamin, queuine (q) is a micronutrient that eukaryotes acquire from microbiota or diet. Vitamin q, the free base form of queuosine (Q), is used for Q-modification of transfer RNA (tRNA). Although tRNA-Q-modification in regulating eukaryotic cell physiology is recognized, the relationship between Q-tRNA-modification and the human microbiome in health and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) remains unknown. Which bacteria produce q and how the q-producing bacteria contributing to human health and IBD are not explored. Here, we hypothesize that disrupted microbial Q-biosynthesis contributes to the dysbiosis of human IBD. We performed comprehensive multi-omics integrative analyses using publicly available datasets. Specifically, we re-analyzed publicly available shotgun metagenomic, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), metabolic datasets, and completed meta-analysis. Methods: To systematically investigate microbial Q-biosynthesis in healthy individuals and IBD patients, we performed a systematic secondary analysis by integrating 9 publicly available metagenomic datasets, 15 scRNA-seq datasets and one metabolic dataset published prior to 2026. We present a novel secondary bioinformatic reanalysis of sequence outputs mapped to the latest microbial taxonomy, functional pathways and microbial Q-related genes. Longitudinal study of shotgun metagenomics across the human lifespan (3146 samples) enabled taxonomic and functional profiling. Results: . The longitudinal stability of the q-producing bacteria community across the human lifespan (1638 samples). We observed a significant negative correlation between host age and the abundance of q-producing bacteria in patients with UC. Moreover, Queuine tRNA-ribosyltransferase 1 (QTRT1) expression in human intestinal epithelial cells was significantly reduced in patients with IBD compared to healthy controls. Conclusions: Our study used multi-omics datasets to define a novel functional dysbiosis characterized by a reduction of microbial Q-biosynthesis in patients with IBD. Vitamin q and its tRNA modification is lesser-recognized in human IBD. Understanding the cellular and organismal mechanisms of this microbiome-dependent micronutrient will advance the prevention of IBD and improve the quality of life of patients with IBD. What is already known on this topic?: Queuine, vitamin q, is a highly conserved hypermodified nucleoside micronutrition could only be acquired from microbiota or diet. It is used for modification of transfer RNA to protein transitional fidelity, but the specific microbial pathways evolved and the relationship with IBD are unclear. What this study adds: ) and the downregulated microbial Q biosynthesis pathways, which correlates with host QTRT1 deficiency to potentially drive IBD pathogenesis. How this study might affect research practice or policy: 1. Identifies the altered Q-biosynthesis pathway in human IBD. Establishes the "Microbial Q-synthesis-Host tRNA modification" axis as a novel mechanistic link, shifting human IBD microbiome research from taxonomic description to functional epitranscriptomics.Overcomes the inherent biases of traditional meta-analyses through a unified secondary bioinformatic reanalysis, leveraging HMP unified metabolic analysis network 3 (HUMAnN3)-based modeling of 3,000+ samples, to reveal a universal breakdown of the microbial Q-biosynthetic supply chain across all IBD subtypes.Recognize vitamin q as a critical gut-health micronutrient, influencing dietary guidelines and the regulation of functional medical foods for IBD management.

title: Echocardiographic estimates of pulmonary artery acceleration time and mortality risk in older adults.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary artery acceleration time (PAAT) is an echocardiographic measure associated with pulmonary artery pressure. Although reduced PAAT has been linked to pulmonary hypertension and adverse outcomes in selected patient populations, less is known about its prognostic significance in community-dwelling older adults, which was the focus of the present study.
METHODS: Using baseline echocardiographic PAAT measurements, we categorized 2758 participants in the Cardiovascular Health Study into PAAT >130 ms (N = 758), 100-130 ms (N = 1089), and <100 ms (N = 911). Cox regression models were used to estimate associations with mortality (reference, PAAT >130 ms), and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess nonlinearity of the associations (reference, PAAT 130 ms), during a median follow-up of 13.4 years.
RESULTS: All-cause mortality occurred in 75.2%, 82.9%, and 85.5% of participants with PAAT >130 ms, 100-130 ms, and <100 ms, respectively. Corresponding age-sex-race-adjusted HRs (95% CIs) were 1.00, 1.11 (0.99-1.23) and 1.20 (1.08-1.34). Associations were attenuated primarily by adjustment for World Health Organization Group 2 (cardiac) but not Group 3 (pulmonary) pulmonary hypertension physiology and by adjustment for subclinical biomarkers and were no longer significant in fully adjusted models. Associations and attenuations were stronger for cardiovascular mortality than non-cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated no significant nonlinearity in age-sex-race-adjusted HRs for total mortality, which increased progressively at PAAT values below 130 ms.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower PAAT is associated with higher risks of death in community-dwelling older adults. The association appears to be explained largely by cardiovascular disease and systemic health status rather than pulmonary disease alone. PAAT may serve as an integrated marker of cardiopulmonary and systemic vulnerability in older adults.

title: Abstract 17638: Residual Coronary Inflammation is Common Despite Low hsCRP in Chronic Post-Myocardial Infarction Patients
abstract: Background: High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) is a systemic inflammatory biomarker associated with recurrent cardiovascular events, despite contemporary secondary prevention therapy. The perivascular Fat Attenuation Index (FAI-Score), derived from coronary CT angiography (CCTA), is a novel imaging biomarker of local coronary inflammation that independently predicts adverse cardiovascular outcomes. We investigated whether local coronary inflammation (reflected by FAI-Score) correlates with systemic inflammation (reflected by hsCRP) in stable post-myocardial infarction (MI) patients. Methods: FORTIFY (NCT06927739) is an ongoing, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, phase 2 trial evaluating orticumab in clinically stable post-MI participants with elevated coronary inflammation, defined as FAI ≥75 th centile in at least 1 coronary artery or ≥50 th centile in ≥2 arteries. Eligible participants had a prior MI ≥6 months before enrollment and received guideline-directed secondary prevention therapy with well-controlled traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Results: As of June 1, 2026, 405 prospective trial participants had been screened (mean age 63 years). Patients were receiving lipid-lowering therapy with median LDL-C 54 mg/dL (IQR 43-70). Levels of hsCRP were generally low (median 0.8 mg/L, IQR 0.4-1.7), with 76% of participants having hsCRP <2 mg/L. Nonetheless, coronary inflammation was prevalent: 63% of participants had at least one coronary artery with an FAI-Score ≥50th centile, a threshold associated with increased cardiovascular risk in prior studies. There was no correlation between mean FAI centile and hsCRP (R 2 =0.004, p=0.23; figure). Moreover, screened participants meeting (eligible) vs not meeting (not eligible) trial FAI-Score criteria for coronary inflammation had identical hsCRP concentrations (median 0.8 mg/L in both groups; table). Conclusions: Many stable post-MI patients receiving contemporary secondary prevention therapies have no evidence of systemic inflammation as reflected by hsCRP; however, many have evidence of ongoing coronary inflammation as assessed by FAI-Score. The absence of correlation between FAI-Score and hsCRP suggests that local coronary and systemic inflammatory activity represent distinct biological processes.

title: Reducing Dietary Sodium Exposure in Chronic Kidney Disease: Challenges and Opportunities.
abstract: Over 750 million individuals worldwide experience chronic kidney disease (CKD), which is a major contributor to cardiovascular disease and kidney failure as well as increased morbidity and mortality. Diet is a key lifestyle factor in CKD risk prevention and management. Overall public dietary quality and sodium intake have shown limited improvement despite decades of public health efforts. Excessive sodium consumption is a challenging dietary risk factor because exposure is largely passively embedded within the modern food environment. Furthermore, the consequences of overconsumption of dietary sodium are often delayed, invisible, or difficult for patients to recognize. The complexity of dietary behavior approaches coupled with conventional education approaches also contributes to persistently high sodium intake across the CKD spectrum. In this review, we discuss three major overarching challenges to sodium reduction, which comprise the invisible nature of sodium-related risk, the ubiquity of sodium within commercially prepared and processed foods, and the limitations of knowledge-based interventions alone. We also highlight subsequent opportunities to improve implementation. These include practical, patient-centered, and personalized nutrition strategies; food environment and food supply improvements that make lower-sodium choices the default; and expansion of Food Is Medicine and culinary medicine approaches. Reducing dietary sodium exposure and its consequences requires coordinated efforts that extend beyond individual patients and health care providers to include multidisciplinary collaboration across health care systems, public health, industry, community organizations, professional societies, and policymakers. Such multilevel approaches offer important opportunities to improve kidney health trajectories as well as cardiovascular health. Semin Nephrol 36:x-xx © 20XX Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

title: Abbreviated 13-Item Version of the Multi-Component Gratitude Measure (MCGM): Development and Evaluation.
abstract: The Multi-Component Gratitude Measure (MCGM) is a 29-item instrument that assesses emotions, attitudes, and behaviors related to gratitude. This brief report describes the development and exploratory evaluation of a 13-item abbreviated MCGM (aMCGM). A nationally representative sample of 1,028 low-income US veterans collected December 2022-January 2023 was used to develop and test the aMCGM. All MCGM items were evaluated for reliability, factor structure, and construct validity to derive the aMCGM. The aMCGM consists of Emotion/Expressed Emotion (8 items), Introspection (3 items), and Unconditionality (2 items) scales. The aMCGM scales showed good internal consistency as well as preliminary convergent and discriminant validity in relation to other constructs using the total sample and split subsamples. These findings provide preliminary support for the use of the aMCGM as a multi-dimensional measure of gratitude and suggest low-income US veterans, on average, report high gratitude.

title: Cell-type-resolved mRNA 3'-end remodeling in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alternative polyadenylation diversifies messenger RNAs by altering coding sequences and 3' untranslated regions, but its organization across human brain cell types and disruption in neurodegeneration remain poorly understood. By analyzing 3'-capture single-nucleus RNA sequencing data of 6.3 million nuclei from the prefrontal cortex of 1,494 human donors, we defined 108,768 polyadenylation sites across 25,274 genes, most of which were absent from the GENCODE polyadenylation-site annotation. Polyadenylation-site usage was strongly cell-type-specific and revealed regulatory differences not captured by gene expression. With increasing Alzheimer's disease clinicopathological severity, excitatory neurons, oligodendrocytes and immune cells showed increased distal-site preference, including reduced relative usage of intronic sites and increased distal 3' untranslated region usage in synaptic and RNA-processing genes. External single-nucleus data supported neuronal and oligodendrocyte patterns, while complementary analyses of purified microglia supported selected immune-cell findings. Integrative analyses of cleavage and polyadenylation factor expression, co-regulated usage networks, sequence motifs and published perturbations prioritized the cleavage factor Im complex as a candidate regulator. These findings identify cell-type-specific messenger RNA 3'-end remodeling as a reproducible dimension of Alzheimer's disease molecular pathology that is only partly captured by gene-level analyses.

title: Kidney Epithelial AKT Controls Potassium Homeostasis and Metabolic Adaptation.
abstract:
KEY POINTS: Renal epithelial AKT is required for potassium conservation, kidney growth, and adaptation to dietary potassium restriction. AKT linked potassium availability to renal metabolism and promoted glycolysis and lipogenesis, while suppressing ketogenesis. Loss of renal epithelial AKT caused glycosuria and improved systemic glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity.
BACKGROUND: Potassium intake is strongly associated with cardiometabolic health, yet the mechanisms linking electrolyte balance to systemic metabolism remain poorly defined. We hypothesized that renal epithelial AKT acts as a potassium-responsive signaling node that coordinates potassium homeostasis and metabolic adaptation.
METHODS: Inducible nephron-wide and proximal tubule-specific AKT1/AKT2 knockout mice were generated to define the role of epithelial AKT in renal potassium handling and metabolism. Physiologic, molecular, proteomic, and metabolic analyses were performed under normal and potassium-restricted dietary conditions, complemented by mechanistic studies in cultured cells.
RESULTS: Proteomic analysis revealed that dietary potassium restriction stimulated AKT-dependent pathways in the kidney, including glycolysis and de novo lipogenesis. Nephron-wide and proximal tubule-specific AKT deletion impaired adaptation to potassium deprivation, resulting in urinary potassium wasting, reduced kidney hypertrophy, diminished proximal tubule transporter expression, and hypokalemia. Mechanistically, AKT loss suppressed low K + -induced glycolytic and lipogenic programs, reduced de novo palmitate synthesis, and promoted a renal catabolic, ketogenic phenotype characterized by increased 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 2 expression and ketone production. In vitro studies showed that low-potassium-induced AKT activation required mammalian target of rapamycin activity, but was independent of Rictor, whereas Sin1 and mLST8 were essential. AKT deletion also reduced expression of the proximal tubule glucose transporters sodium-glucose cotransporter 1 and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2, causing glycosuria. These renal adaptations were accompanied by lower fasting glucose levels, improved glucose tolerance, enhanced insulin sensitivity, and increased AKT signaling in liver and skeletal muscle.
CONCLUSIONS: Renal epithelial AKT was required for adaptation to dietary potassium restriction. AKT deletion impaired potassium conservation, reduced kidney growth and proximal tubular transport function, and promoted a shift from anabolic to catabolic renal metabolism. These changes were accompanied by glycosuria and systemic metabolic alterations, including lower fasting glucose levels, improved glucose tolerance, and enhanced insulin sensitivity.

title: Effects of Aging and Early-Onset Menopause on Intraocular Pressure and Aqueous Humor Conventional Outflow Facility.
abstract: Biomechanical parameters play a crucial role in glaucoma development, the world-leading cause of irreversible blindness. Although age is known to affect the tissues' biomechanical properties, early-onset menopause has recently been associated with the risk of developing glaucoma, and the effects of aging relative to early-onset menopause on eyes' biomechanical parameters remain underexplored. This work's goals were to study the effects of aging and early-onset menopause on intraocular pressure (IOP), aqueous humor outflow facility, and ocular compliance. Female Brown Norway rats underwent Sham or surgical menopause (ovariectomy; OVX) at 3-4 months of age and were split into young (5-6 months) or middle-aged groups (9-10 months). We monitored IOP until the established aging time points and performed ex vivo biomechanical measurements via the iPerfusion system. IOP was higher for the middle-aged Sham and OVX animals by 25% and 35%, respectively (p < 0.001), when compared to their respective initial IOPs. Furthermore, middle-aged OVX animals had an 11% higher IOP compared to Sham animals (p = 0.005), and a 20% lower outflow facility (p = 0.031). Ocular compliance decreased with age in the Sham (24.9%, p = 0.011) and OVX (24.5%, p = 0.005) cohorts and by 24.1% independent of cohort (p = 0.0001). Elucidating the effects of age and early-onset menopause on biomechanical parameters that contribute to glaucoma pathology is necessary to move the field forward and help preserve the eyesight of millions of patients.

title: Stim-CODE: PNS and CNS Constraint Optimized Diffusion-Encoding for Neuroimaging on 200 mT/m Whole-Body Gradients.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Ultra-high-performance whole-body MRI gradients ( G max ≥ 200mT/m, S max ≥ 200 T/m/s) can reduce echo times (TE) in diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), improving SNR. However, full hardware utilization is limited by cardiac (CNS) and peripheral (PNS) nerve stimulation thresholds. This work demonstrates Stimulation Constraint Optimized diffusion-encoding (Stim-CODE) for neuro diffusion.
METHODS: Stim-CODE uses the gradient optimization (GrOpt) toolbox to optimally design diffusion-encoding gradient waveforms subject to a CNS or PNS "constraint envelope" based on other gradient events in the sequence. Stim-CODE was evaluated in simulations and in vivo protocols with in-plane resolutions of 1.5 × 1.5 mm 2 and 1.0 × 1.0 mm 2 across G max = [45, 80, 200] mT/m and S max = 200 T/m/s. Healthy volunteers (N = 10) underwent neuro DWI at b = 1000 s/mm 2 with Monopolar, Stim-CODE- M 0 , Bipolar, and Stim-CODE- M 1 encoding. SNR, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, and ADC uncertainty were quantified. One volunteer underwent DTI with the same encoding schemes acquired at b = [1000, 3000]s/mm 2 .
RESULTS: Stim-CODE reduced TEs across all b -values, with larger gains for higher resolutions, greater G max , and M 1 -nulled waveforms. Phantom and in vivo experiments confirmed equivalent diffusion-weighting with TE savings and SNR improvements. Stim-CODE- M 1 had significant SNR gains over Bipolar scans, but some differences in global ADC were observed. DTI metrics were similar across scans, with Stim-CODE showing lower uncertainty.
CONCLUSION: Stim-CODE maximizes hardware capabilities to achieve time-optimized diffusion-encoding while respecting CNS and PNS, enabling similar diffusion-weighting as conventional approaches with reduced TE and higher SNR.

title: Renin Kinetics and Hemodynamic Response During Treatment of Vasoplegic Shock With Angiotensin II (TENSINTEST): Protocol for a Multicenter Observational Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shock is a life-threatening condition that can lead to multiorgan failure and death. Vasopressors are needed for the treatment of vasoplegic (distributive) shock. Angiotensin II (AT II) is a novel vasopressor. Approximately two-thirds of patients respond to AT II, and one-third do not. AT II is part of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). Renin is the limiting enzyme of the RAAS, and among other mechanisms, its concentration is regulated by AT II concentration through a negative feedback loop. It might be an indicator of response to AT II therapy.
OBJECTIVE: We designed a study with a primary objective of developing and standardizing an AT II stress test, which could help predict the responsiveness to AT II in patients with distributive shock, regardless of its origin.
METHODS: This is an investigator-initiated, multicenter observational clinical study of renin kinetics before and 6 hours after starting an infusion of AT II in patients with vasoplegic shock and adequate fluid resuscitation who are severely ill. Prior to AT II, patients will receive an infusion of norepinephrine base of 0.3 mcg per kilogram per minute or higher, and vasopressin of 0.03 IU per minute according to institutional protocol. Blood samples for serum renin determination will be obtained immediately prior to and after 6 hours of AT II infusion. We hypothesize that patients who demonstrate a negative trend in relative renin ratio (defined as renin plasma concentration at baseline or at 6 hours after treatment with AT II divided by upper normal concentration of plasma renin [50 mU/L]) will have a greater number of 28-day organ failure-free days (days without vasopressors, mechanical ventilation, or renal replacement therapy). The primary analysis will assess the association between early renin reduction and organ failure-free days using an adjusted proportional odds ordinal regression model.
RESULTS: The research was funded in December 2024. After obtaining ethics approval in July 2025, data collection started on August 1, 2025. As of July 2026, a total of 70 patients had been enrolled. Data collection is expected to be completed in 2027, after which the results will be analyzed and published.
CONCLUSIONS: The goal of our study is to determine whether renin 0-6 h kinetics (difference between renin levels before and 6 hours after starting an AT II infusion) are associated with clinical outcomes in patients who require AT II. Our study could contribute to the development of a more individualized approach to vasopressor therapy and avoidance of inappropriate use of AT II in patients who are not responders, allowing earlier discontinuation of AT II and consideration of alternative therapies.

title: The last gift cohort: advancing HIV reservoir research through single-cell and spatial approaches.
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Despite effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), persistent HIV reservoirs remain the primary obstacle to achieving an HIV cure. Understanding persistence requires defining not only reservoir size but also the identity and state of infected cells and their anatomical microenvironments - features that blood-based bulk measurements cannot resolve. We synthesize published findings from the Last Gift end-of-life cohort, in which longitudinal sampling and tissue donation via rapid autopsy have advanced our understanding of HIV persistence across anatomical compartments. We then highlight how integrated single-cell and spatial profiling can link proviral features to host-cell states and local tissue neighborhoods, helping to define the cellular and microenvironmental niches that sustain persistence.
RECENT FINDINGS: The Last Gift studies have mapped HIV DNA and envelope diversity across up to 33 anatomical compartments, inferred lymphoid and gastrointestinal tissues to be dominant sources of viral dispersal, shown that >85% of expanded proviral clones are shared across tissues, and recovered inducible, replication-competent virus from parietal-cortex microglia. Single-cell profiling has resolved heterogeneous microglial transcriptional and chromatin states containing rare HIV RNA or accessible proviral DNA and has identified a transcriptomic definition of cells expressing HIV RNA despite viral suppression on ART. Additionally, mass cytometry of viral sensors and restriction factors has defined tissue- and cell subset-specific antiviral programs, including restriction-factor profiles in lymph-node follicular helper T-cells predicted to favor HIV persistence. In parallel, imaging-based spatial transcriptomics with custom HIV probes, immunoPET/CT-guided tissue sampling, and duplex RNAscope/DNAscope have made direct localization of viral nucleic acids within annotated tissue neighborhoods technically feasible. No single assay, however, establishes proviral intactness, transcriptional activity, cellular identity, spatial position, and neighborhoods at once.
SUMMARY: Reservoir measurements should be reported by what each assay can establish rather than as interchangeable estimates of reservoir size. Cohorts such as the Last Gift, which yield matched blood and multiorgan tissue from the same donor with longitudinal clinical context, are well suited to applying direct proviral characterization, single-cell phenotyping and spatially resolved viral detection in parallel on the same specimens. This combination defines the resolution - intact provirus, in an identified cell, in a defined tissue niche - that cure trials should increasingly be expected to measure.

title: Reactions to Sexual Assault Disclosure: Differential Effects on Posttraumatic Cognitions by Race/Ethnicity.
abstract: Survivors of sexual assault often disclose their experiences to close support members to seek emotional and practical support. Research consistently demonstrates that post-assault outcomes are shaped by the responses survivors receive following disclosure. Negative responses, in particular, are associated with worsened posttrauma outcomes; however, limited research has examined disclosure experiences among non-White/Latine women. The present study aimed to address this gap by examining associations between specific disclosure response types (Positive, Turning Against, Unsupportive Acknowledgment) and negative posttraumatic cognitions among 201 women survivors of sexual assault. Descriptive analyses indicated that racial/ethnic minority participants reported higher rates of both positive and unsupportive acknowledgment responses compared to White/non-Latine women. Hierarchical regression analyses demonstrated that turning against responses were the most consistently associated with stronger negative cognitions about the self, the world, and self-blame. Moderation analyses revealed that turning against responses had stronger negative effects on self-related cognitions among racial/ethnic minority survivors. In contrast, positive responses were associated with reduced negative world-related cognitions only among White/non-Latine participants. These findings highlight important racial/ethnic differences in disclosure experiences and recovery processes. Moreover, they emphasize the need for increased empirical attention to developing culturally responsive models of social support.

title: Factors associated with primary care dissemination and implementation concordance for chronic pain
abstract: Background Chronic pain affects millions of people worldwide and is most often managed by primary care practitioners (PCPs). It is essential that PCPs receive timely access to updates in chronic pain implementation support to put these changes into practice. The purpose of this analysis was to explore the effect of individual characteristics and clinic context on the concordance between dissemination approaches and preferred implementation strategies for chronic pain management among PCPs. Methods This cross-sectional study included a secondary analysis of a survey of Pennsylvania PCPs. Dissemination and implementation strategy concordance were defined as the degree to which there was agreement between PCP reported preferences for dissemination and implementation strategies and reality. We used multiple linear regression models, with covariates including demographic characteristics, urbanicity, and academic affiliation to identify factors associated with concordance. Results This survey of 101 Pennsylvania PCPs identified factors associated with dissemination concordance in bivariable analyses included gender, profession, and days per week in clinic, while and implementation concordance was associated with gender, days per week in clinic, and years of experience. Dissemination concordance was significantly lower for women than for men after controlling for other factors, (0.15; β = −0.24, p < 0.05). Implementation concordance was significantly associated with increased years of experience (0.01; β = 0.34, p < 0.01) in the final multivariable models. Conclusion Clinician perspectives are critical for improving implementation. We demonstrate a method to better understand these perspectives and the factors associated with concordance between preferred and received dissemination and implementation support. This work can offer a more implementer-centered approach to identifying strategies for dissemination and implementation.

title: Inhibitory neurochemistry and network dedifferentiation in adults aged 85 and older
abstract: Analysis code, model specifications and group-level derived outputs supporting a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the McKnight Brain Aging Registry (MBAR). The study related medial frontal GABA+, measured with MEGA-PRESS spectroscopy over dorsal anterior cingulate and pre-supplementary motor cortex, to resting-state association-network segregation and processing speed in 86 cognitively healthy adults aged 85–99 years scanned at four sites (broad QC, n = 82; strict QC, n = 67). Spectra were processed in Osprey 2.9.6 (MATLAB R2023b) with SPM12 tissue segmentation. GABA+ was quantified under three water-relaxation assumptions: conventional fixed tissue constants, region-specific atlas values, and region- plus age-specific atlas values. Statistical models were run in Python 3.12.14 (NumPy 2.3.5, pandas 2.2.3, SciPy 1.17.0) using ordinary least squares with HC3 robust standard errors, adjusted for age, gender, education and site. This record contains the analysis scripts, model specifications, input file checksums, expected results, and group-level derived data (mean difference spectra and model fits for each QC set, assigned relaxation parameters, and model output tables). Participant-level MBAR imaging, spectroscopy and cognitive data are not included. They are available to qualified investigators through the registry's data access procedures. See README.md for contents and reproduction steps.

title: Intramyocardial Granulomatous Histoplasmosis Presenting as Narrow-Complex Ventricular Tachycardia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac histoplasmosis is rare, typically manifesting as pericarditis or endocarditis; tissue-proven intramyocardial granulomatous histoplasmosis has not been previously described.
CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man with immunosuppression presented with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and recurrent narrow-complex tachyarrhythmias attributed to supraventricular tachycardia (SVT). Echocardiography showed a hyperechoic basal septal mass. Autopsy confirmed a 1.8 × 1.1 cm partially hyalinized necrotizing granuloma of the high interventricular septum containing Histoplasma on silver staining. Retrospective aVR algorithm analysis reclassified the arrhythmia as ventricular tachycardia (VT), anatomically concordant with the granuloma.
DISCUSSION: Granulomatous histoplasmosis of the upper interventricular septum can produce high septal VT mimicking SVT, expanding the differential of granulomatous myocarditis in immunocompromised hosts.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Histoplasmosis should be included in the differential of granulomatous myocarditis, particularly in immunocompromised patients from endemic regions. Systematic use of the Vereckei aVR algorithm can prevent misclassification of relatively narrow-complex VT as SVT and guide management.

title: Hepatitis C Treatment Access With Implementation of an Antenatal Linkage-to-Care Bundle.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate a health system-wide quality-improvement bundle (HALT-C [hepatitis C antenatal linkage-to-care]) on its ability to integrate proactive patient identification, care coordination, and treatment timing options on direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum.
METHODS: We implemented our quality-improvement initiative at a large midwestern health system and evaluated its effect by comparing outcomes among eligible pregnancies identified preimplementation (December 1, 2021-May 31, 2023) with those identified postimplementation (March 1, 2024-August 31, 2025). Eligible patients were aged at least 18 years, with detectable hepatitis C virus RNA and at least one encounter in the health system before 35 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients prescribed direct-acting antivirals by 6 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes included linkage to care, the treatment timing decision, treatment completion, sustained virologic response (SVR), infant screening, and perinatal transmission. Comparison of antenatal initiation of treatment and postpartum initiation of treatment was also performed.
RESULTS: We identified 62 bundle-eligible pregnancies in the preimplementation period and identified 35 in the postimplementation period. Direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum increased from 48.4% to 77.1% (P=.009); treatment completion improved from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Treatment increases were greatest among patients who delivered regionally, rather than at the main hospital, with an increase in direct-acting antiviral prescription rates of 14.3% to 72.7% (P<.001). Thirty of 35 individuals identified postimplementation were successfully linked to care, and 75.0% of clinic attendees preferred antenatal treatment over postpartum treatment. Known treatment completion and SVR increased from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Those treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment than those who deferred postpartum (92.3% vs 45.5%; P=.02). Infant screening and perinatal transmission rates did not change; however, no perinatal transmissions occurred among infants where treatment occurred antenatally.
CONCLUSION: The HALT-C bundle was associated with significantly improved direct-acting antiviral receipt across a regional health system. Most patients preferred treatment during pregnancy. Patients treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment, highlighting pregnancy as an important opportunity to initiate curative therapy.

title: Directional Brain Connectivity Changes Induced by Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback: A Spectral Dynamic Causal Modeling Study.
abstract: Heart rate variability biofeedback (HRVB) is a non-pharmacological intervention that trains individuals to breathe at their cardiovascular resonance frequency to enhance autonomic regulation. While HRVB improves cardiovascular function across clinical conditions, the directional neural pathways through which it modulates the central autonomic network (CAN) remain poorly understood. Using a publicly available open-access dataset, we conducted a secondary analysis of effective (directional) neural connectivity (EC) data from 32 healthy participants randomized to an 8-week HRVB intervention (n = 15) or a video game Control intervention (n = 17). Pre- and post-intervention resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were analyzed using spectral dynamic causal modeling (DCM) combined with parametric empirical Bayes to examine group differences in EC changes (ΔEC). We also evaluated whether connectivity changes correlated with changes in peripheral autonomic regulation, indexed by the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (ΔSDNN). Compared with the Control group, HRVB showed strong evidence (posterior-probability = 1) of increased ΔEC from the medial prefrontal cortex to the anterior cingulate cortex and bilateral thalamus post-treatment, along with reduced ΔEC from the right hippocampus to the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (VLPFC). Furthermore, the regression coefficient linking hippocampus-to-VLPFC ΔEC with ΔSDNN was more (posterior-probability = 1) negative in the HRVB group than in Controls, indicating an intervention-dependent association between autonomic changes and effective connectivity. These findings indicate that HRVB may alter directional fronto-limbic communication within the CAN. Given the relatively small sample sizes, these findings need replication, but provide preliminary understanding about the neural circuitry through which resonance breathing may modulate central autonomic control.

title: Nanobodies against Plasmodium vivax AMA1 block parasite invasion
abstract: Abstract Plasmodium vivax is the most widespread malaria species to infect human populations. P. vivax invades young red cells called reticulocytes to replicate and proliferate. An essential protein in parasite invasion is the Apical Membrane Antigen 1, PvAMA1, which forms the tight junction between parasite and red cell membrane through its interaction with Rhoptry Neck Protein 2, PvRON2. Here we report the identification of PvAMA1 nanobodies using phage display in combination with Sanger sequencing, next-generation sequencing and structure prediction tools. We show that these nanobodies bind with high affinities and across several different epitopes on PvAMA1. Several nanobodies recognize PvAMA1 in merozoites of late-stage schizonts and inhibit parasite invasion of red blood cells. These growth inhibitory nanobodies bind to conformational epitopes of PvAMA1 and most bind to a site distinct from a known potent human monoclonal antibody 826827. Crystal structures of two inhibitory nanobodies in complex with PvAMA1 show that they bind novel neutralizing epitopes which are outside the hydrophobic groove that contacts PvRON2. Furthermore, we show that two other PvAMA1 nanobodies also inhibit Plasmodium falciparum invasion. These results demonstrate the potential of PvAMA1 nanobodies to inhibit malaria parasite invasion across multiple Plasmodium species. Author Summary Malaria parasites are exquisitely adapted for invasion and survival within human red blood cells. Merozoites are the form of the malaria parasites that invade red cells. Parasite invasion begins with initial attachment of the merozoite to the red blood cell surface, followed by tight junction formation between the parasite and the red blood cell membrane. Active invasion proceeds as the tight junction moves from the apical to posterior pole of the merozoite and pulls the parasite into the red blood cell. In Plasmodium vivax , PvAMA1 is critical for tight junction formation during parasite invasion. Here we describe the identification of nanobodies that bind to PvAMA1 at different sites using phage display combined with Sanger sequencing, next-generation sequencing and structure prediction approaches. We show that PvAMA1 nanobodies potently inhibit malaria parasite invasion in multiple Plasmodium species, demonstrating their potential to reduce malaria infection of red blood cells.

title: Identification of C3d Complement Fragments in Lesional Tissues in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is typically described as "pauci-immune" due to the absence or weak detection of Igs and complement activation within AAV tissue lesions. However, complement fragments have been recently reported in significant amounts in damaged tissue in AAV, notably in traps formed by neutrophil extravasation. This study aimed to characterize complement activation, in particular the long-lasting fragment C3d, in affected tissue in AAV.
METHODS: Biopsies from patients with AAV (kidney, n = 40; lung, n = 5; sinus, n = 2; and skin, n = 3), IgA nephropathy (IgAN; kidney, n = 29), C3 glomerulonephritis (C3G; kidney, n = 9), lupus nephritis (LN; kidney, n = 30), and cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis (skin, n = 41) were stained using a novel anti-C3d monoclonal antibody (3d8b), and, in some instances, a commercially available anti-C3c polyclonal antibody.
RESULTS: Both semiquantitative scoring and digital quantification revealed moderate glomerular staining in AAV and IgAN and higher signal in C3G and LN. A distinct C3c/C3d glomerular staining pattern was seen in AAV and IgAN with more deposition in mesangium than capillaries. C3G and LN exhibited more homogenous deposition. Three of seven biopsies that tested negative for C3 by routine diagnostic immunostaining were positive for C3d. C3d deposition was also detected in extra-glomerular small vessels in the kidney, in superficial dermal vasculature in leukocytoclastic vasculitis, and in lung and sinus lesional tissues in AAV.
CONCLUSION: Immunostaining for complement fragments, particularly C3d, reveals evidence of complement activation in multiple tissues in AAV, including biopsies deemed negative by routine C3 staining. These data indicate that glomerulonephritis in AAV is less pauci-immune than previously appreciated.

title: Circulating Plasma Adiposomes as a Partial Lipidomic Readout of Matched Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue: Implications for Interorgan Communication.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies established adipose-derived extracellular vesicles, or adiposomes, as mediators of interorgan communication with lipidomic signatures linked to cardiometabolic health. Because adiposomes signal to distant organs via the circulation, we examined whether circulating adiposome lipidomes reflect matched subcutaneous adipose tissue adiposomes.
METHODS: This cross-sectional paired lipidomic study included 22 subjects with matched circulating and subcutaneous adipose tissue adiposome samples. Untargeted lipidomics quantified 773 lipid features across 18 detected broad classes. Spearman correlation was the primary across-subject species-level metric; pooled and within-subject Pearson and Spearman correlations, principal component analysis, Bland-Altman analysis, class composition, and matched-versus-mismatched similarity were complementary measures. Additional analyses evaluated sex, cardiometabolic phenotypes, and focused species-clinical associations.
RESULTS: Across 770 species with valid across-subject estimates, the median plasma-subcutaneous Spearman ρ was 0.101 and no species survived Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, although 553 (71.8%) correlations were positive. Mean broad-class composition was highly conserved (Spearman ρ = 0.996; Pearson r on log2 percentages = 0.996). Matched whole-profile similarity was not greater than mismatched similarity (median ρ = 0.818 vs. 0.811; p = 0.620), and the matched sample was the closest pair for 0 of 22 participants. Neither sex nor any prespecified cardiometabolic phenotype explained matched-profile similarity after correction, and no focused species-clinical association survived full-screen FDR correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Circulating and subcutaneous adiposome lipidomes share a highly conserved mean class architecture, but individual species, subject-specific matching, and clinical-association patterns are not interchangeable. Plasma adiposomes may therefore serve as complementary circulating readouts of adipose-derived interorgan lipid signaling rather than direct tissue substitutes.

title: The novel role of T2R14 antagonism, by LW129, on VEGF-induced lung endothelial neovascularisation processes in vitro.
abstract: Pulmonary vascular remodelling, driven by dysregulated angiogenesis, is a hallmark of several cardiopulmonary diseases, yet the molecular pathways regulating endothelial responses remain incompletely understood. Bitter taste receptors (T2Rs), traditionally recognised as chemosensory receptors, have emerged as important modulators of vascular function. However, the contribution of T2Rs to pulmonary angiogenesis remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the role of T2R14 in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-mediated angiogenic responses in human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (HPMECs). Using the selective T2R14 antagonist LW129, we examined the effects of T2R14 inhibition on key endothelial angiogenic processes, including VEGF-induced proliferation, migration and capillary-like tube formation in vitro. Pharmacological antagonism of T2R14 significantly attenuated VEGF-driven endothelial proliferative, migratory and morphogenic responses, revealing a novel contribution of T2R14 signalling to pulmonary microvascular angiogenesis. Proteome Profiler analysis identified a range of molecular regulators of angiogenic processes which were dysregulated by LW129 and VEGF exposure, suggesting a potential role for CXCL16, endoglin, FGF-7, and VEGF-C. These findings identify T2R14 as a novel regulator of VEGF-dependent endothelial activation and suggest that targeting T2R14 signalling may represent a therapeutic strategy to limit pathological pulmonary vascular remodelling associated with aberrant angiogenesis.

title: Steroid-Resistant Bullous Pemphigoid After Leuprolide Acetate Exposure in a Patient With Multiple Sclerosis
abstract: Bullous pemphigoid is the most common autoimmune blistering disorder and is associated with medications and neurologic diseases, including multiple sclerosis. An association with leuprolide acetate has rarely been reported. A 52-year-old woman with a history of untreated multiple sclerosis developed severe bullous pemphigoid approximately 1 week after a single leuprolide acetate injection for uterine fibroids. A biopsy specimen confirmed bullous pemphigoid with eosinophilic inflammation at the D-E-J and IgG/C3 on the direct immunofluorescence. The disease progressed despite the escalating administration of corticosteroids and mycophenolate mofetil, and the patient ultimately required dupilumab. This case highlights leuprolide as a potential bullous pemphigoid trigger in patients who are neurologically susceptible and the role of early biological escalation in refractory cases.

title: Aligning Treatment with Mechanism: A Scoping Review of Integrated Neurocognitive and Metacognitive Interventions for Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders
abstract: Neurocognitive deficits are central to schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs) and predict functional outcomes; yet interventions such as cognitive remediation show limited effects on real-world recovery. Metacognitive deficits have also been proposed as central to functional deficits and personal recovery in SSDs. Emerging evidence suggests that metacognitive capacity, or the ability to reflect on and integrate one’s own and others’ mental states, may mediate the relationship between neurocognition and functioning. This scoping review maps psychosocial interventions for SSDs that target both neurocognitive and metacognitive processes. We examine how these interventions conceptualize and integrate these domains and their impact on related outcomes, including neurocognitive performance, metacognition, and functional recovery. Across studies, improvements were reported most consistently for neurocognitive outcomes, while findings for metacognitive, functional, and clinical outcomes were more variable. Metacognition was consistently conceptualized within a cognitive-regulatory framework and no included intervention explicitly targeted integrative metacognitive capacities. Interpretation is limited by substantial methodological heterogeneity, including several uncontrolled or small-sample studies. Findings highlight the promise of integrated treatment approaches while suggesting that future interventions may benefit from incorporating broader, recovery-oriented models of metacognition.
