title: Seizure detection using multiple wearable sensors and multi-class linear discriminant analysis
abstract: Objective Reliably detect a range of seizure types using multiple physiological sensors and multi-class linear discriminant analysis (LDA). Methods We instrumented epilepsy patients with a 3-axis accelerometer, a microphone, and electrodermal-activity, electromyography and electrocardiograph sensors. Epileptologists reviewed concurrently recorded video- electroencephalography to identify seizure events. We also time-stamped periods of normal activities (eating, sleeping, etc.). We post-processed the data into 5-s epochs of multiple features from each sensor to train several LDAs: seizure vs non-seizure, vs multiple activity classes, vs sleep and vs movement. We then coupled the LDAs with Bayesian inference to detect seizures relative to normal activities. Results We recorded 66 epileptic seizures across 16 patients with diverse seizure types. Non-seizure data separated well from seizure data, with sleep and movement data often separating perfectly. Median detection sensitivity was 95% for both multi-class and seiz-nonseiz LDA, although the latter had lower false alarms (0.003/h vs 0.14/h). Seizures were detected perfectly against sleep data for 9 of 14 patients, with zero false alarms for 11 of 14. Conclusions Multiple physiological sensors combined with LDA and Bayesian inference can form the basis of reliable seizure detectors. Strong separation of sleep and movement data from seizure data enables user-selectable modes for long-duration activities. Batch LDA updating using patient-labeled seizures and false alarms will improve detector performance during real-world use. Significance Our work supports the hypothesis that multiple wearable sensors, coupled with multi-class LDA, can detect and chronicle a broad range of seizure types.

title: Simulated Microgravity Reprograms Human Megakaryocyte Biology: Phenotypic, Transcriptomic, and Autophagic Evidence from a Ground-Based Analogue Study
abstract: Megakaryocytes (MKs) integrate inflammatory, immune, and hemostatic functions, and their dysregulation may promote inflammation and thrombosis, key risks for spaceflight crew health. Despite this relevance, MK responses to spaceflight-related gravitational changes remain poorly defined. Using a NASA-approved randomizing gravitational-vector system (RCCS), CD34⁺ hematopoietic progenitor cells were differentiated into MKs under simulated microgravity conditions. Viability, proliferation, proplatelet formation, morphology, flow cytometry, and transcriptomic profiling (RNA-seq) were used to identify gravity-sensitive processes. Simulated microgravity altered MK growth dynamics and showed a trend toward reduced viability, and flow cytometry demonstrated significantly enhanced expression of megakaryocytic maturation markers. Microgravity conditions further revealed disrupted autophagic flux indicative of an early-stage inhibition. RNA-seq identified significant transcriptional changes involving immune and inflammatory signaling, transcription, protein biogenesis, lipid regulation, and mitochondrial management. Together, these findings uncover previously unrecognized gravitational control of MK development and function, addressing critical knowledge gaps in spaceflight-associated thromboinflammatory risk and informing countermeasure development for long-duration and deep-space missions.

title: Takotsubo Syndrome with Ventricular Fibrillation Cardiac Arrest Following Uncomplicated Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing
abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a transient left ventricular (LV) dysfunction characterized by regional wall-motion abnormalities that extend beyond a single coronary artery distribution, in the absence of obstructive coronary disease, and typically follows a recognizable stressor.1 Although it predominantly affects postmenopausal women, physical stressors—including medical and surgical procedures—account for a growing proportion of cases and are disproportionately implicated in men.2,3 Permanent pacemaker implantation, though typically low-risk, is an uncommon trigger, with most reported cases involving elderly women undergoing conventional right ventricular (RV) apical pacing for high-grade atrioventricular (AV) block.4,5 Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) provides more physiological ventricular activation and a lower risk of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, yet can still produce secondary repolarization changes, because ventricular activation is not completely physiologic and involves varying degrees of direct septal capture.6,7 Whether LBBAP carries the same risk of triggering TTS as conventional RV pacing—and whether such an event can precipitate life-threatening arrhythmias—has not been established.

title: Frailty Assessment and Treatment Effects in Clinical Trials of Disease-Modifying Therapies for CKD.
abstract: Frailty is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and is independently associated with disability and mortality. However, evidence on the optimal treatment of frail adults with CKD remains limited. Consequently, regulators have encouraged routine assessment of frailty and the reporting of outcomes stratified by frailty in clinical studies. In this narrative review, we found that several recent clinical trials of disease-modifying therapies for CKD evaluated treatment effects across frailty strata and reported consistent benefits, with potentially greater benefits in the highest frailty subgroup. However, frailty was not formally assessed in any of these trials, and the proxy measures used may not have fully captured the multidimensional aspects of frailty needed to inform treatment decisions.

title: The State of Health in Jordan, 1990–2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study
abstract: Background: Jordan's health system has evolved amid rapid urbanization and the strain of hosting one of the world's largest refugee populations per capita. This study comprehensively evaluates national disease burden trends in Jordan from 1990 to 2023 to inform health priorities. Methods: Using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 framework, we analyzed age-standardized rates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and years of life lost (YLLs) across 370 diseases and 88 risk factors. Data were derived from national censuses, health surveys, disease registries, and hospital records, and harmonized using standardized GBD modeling and estimation procedures. Analyses were stratified by age, sex, and cause. Results: Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardized DALYs declined by 33.88% (95% UI: -37.38 to -30.59), with greater reductions in males (-38.83%; -42.22 to -35.60) than females (-27.22%; -31.33 to -23.58). YLLs decreased by 49.38% (-50.93 to -47.68), while YLDs remained comparatively stable (2.49%; -2.37 to 7.47). Using mutually exclusive GBD Level 3 causes, ischemic heart disease and diabetes mellitus were the two leading causes of DALYs in 2023. Diabetes mellitus rose from 7th place in 1990 to 2nd place in 2023, while neonatal disorders declined from 1st to 7th place. Metabolic risks remained important contributors to the overall disease burden. Jordan's age-standardized diabetes DALY rate in 2023 was approximately 1.56 times the global rate. Conclusion: Jordan's health profile has shifted toward a greater burden from noncommunicable diseases, while age-standardized health loss and premature mortality have declined substantially. In contrast, nonfatal disability changed comparatively little. These findings provide an evidence base for primary prevention of NCDs and for long-term strategies addressing the country's evolving health challenges.

title: Lung Allograft Function After Primary Graft Dysfunction in the Lung Transplant Outcomes Group Cohort.
abstract:
RATIONALE: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplant is associated with increased mortality. Whether PGD increases mortality via long-term effects on allograft function is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the association of PGD with potential lung function and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD).
METHODS: We included lung transplant recipients enrolled in an 8-center prospective cohort study from 2007-2018. PGD was defined by ISHLT criteria. Linear mixed effects and logistic regression models evaluated the association between PGD and maximum potential forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) and whether Global Lung Function Initiative defined (GLI) predicted FEV1 was attained, respectively. Flexible parametric survival models evaluated the association between PGD and CLAD, accounting for confounding and mortality as a competing risk.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 2419 recipients, 510 had PGD. Recipients with PGD had lower maximum potential FEV1 (-311 ml, 95% CI -245 to -377 ml) and were less likely to achieve GLI-predicted FEV1 (probability difference -12.5%, 95% CI -17 to -8%). 930 recipients developed CLAD (405 obstructive, 525 restrictive) over median (IQR) 5.9 (3.0-8.0 years). The 5-year cumulative incidence of CLAD did not differ by PGD (cumulative difference: -2.2%, 95% CI - 6.4% to 1.9%). This association was not modified by age, sex, BMI, pretransplant diagnosis, or transplant type. PGD was not associated with a difference in cumulative incidence of obstructive or restrictive CLAD (cumulative difference -1.2% and -0.8%, respectively).
CONCLUSION: PGD is associated with reduced lung function and lower likelihood of achieving GLI-predicted maximum potential lung function but not CLAD.

title: Subtle Angioid Streaks Point to Underlying Paget’s Disease
abstract: Paget’s disease of the bone (PDB) is a chronic and progressive abnormal remodeling of bones throughout the body and can result in several complications, including deafness and potential paraplegia. Fifty percent of patients with the ocular finding of angioid streaks within the retina are found to have an associated systemic condition, with PDB being one of them.1 This case review highlights the clinical findings of angioid streaks, as well as the necessary laboratory testing, imaging, and referrals required for the detection and management of PDB.

title: The Risk of Scleroderma Renal Crisis After Intravenous Corticosteroid Administered with Rituximab
abstract: Background/Objectives: This retrospective study determined whether high-dose intravenous (IV) corticosteroid administered during biologic therapy for systemic sclerosis (SSc) was associated with scleroderma renal crisis (SRC). Methods: The outcomes in SSc patients who received high-dose IV methylprednisolone were compared to non-corticosteroid SSc controls. Blood pressure (BP), serum creatinine and glucose, urine protein, and episodes of SRC were determined at baseline, 4 h, 2 weeks, and 24 weeks after IV corticosteroid. Results: The SSc corticosteroid infusion (37 subjects) and non-corticosteroid (120 subjects) cohorts were similar in age, race, disease duration, antinuclear and topoisomerase-1 antibody positivity, interstitial lung disease, and pulmonary artery hypertension (all p > 0.05). However, the corticosteroid group was characterized by a higher proportion of men (18.9 vs. 6.7%, p = 0.04), diffuse cutaneous SSc (75.7 vs. 45.9%, p < 0.001), and anti-RNA polymerase III positivity (21.6 vs. 10%, p = 0.04). No patients in the control group developed SRC. In the corticosteroid group, after a total of 827 infusions (21 ± 23 infusions/subject) with 135 mg ± 66 mg methylprednisolone/infusion and a cumulative dose of 2983 mg ± 5198 mg methylprednisolone, none developed SRC. All-cause mortality (37.8 vs. 19.2%, HR 2.23, 95% CI 1.14–4.37, p = 0.02) during the mean 11.6 ± 6.2-year disease duration was increased in the corticosteroid group; however, 5-year (92% vs. 91%, p > 0.05) survival rates were similar. In the high-risk anti-RNA polymerase III antibody subgroup, there were no episodes of SRC or significant changes in blood pressure or renal function at 4 h, 2 weeks, and 24 weeks after corticosteroid. Conclusions: These data suggest that intermittent high-dose IV corticosteroid premedication for biologic infusions may have a lower risk for SRC.

title: Comparison of Biomechanics at the Cervicothoracic Junction in C3-6, C3-7, and C2-T2 Constructs: A Parametric, Finite Element Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior Cervical Decompression and Fusion (PCDF) is a treatment for degenerative cervical spinal disorders; however, there remains uncertainty about the most effective instrumentation, particularly near the cervicothoracic junction. This study examines the biomechanics of C3-6, C3-7, and C2-T2 constructs using patient-specific finite element analysis.
METHODS: A CT scan of the cervical spine was segmented and meshed. C3-6, C3-7, and C2-T2 constructs created in fusion and analyzed with FEBioStudio. Five bone density conditions were created by applying a global bone density modifier to the elastic modulus values of the bone materials for each construct. A pure compressive 100N follower load was applied and 1.5 Nm moment applied to the odontoid used to elicit flexion, extension, and lateral bending. Von Mises stress was extracted from the screw-rod construct and C7-T1 disc, and segmental motion was measured at the C7-T1 level.
RESULTS: 75 total finite element solver runs were conducted on 15 models. Compared with the C2-T2 construct, the C3-7 and C3-6 constructs experienced lower rod stress and had greater segmental ROM. However, for C7-T1 disc stress, both the C3-6 and C3-7 constructs experienced higher stress. Bone density was not associated with differences in these outcomes. There were significant differences in rod stress, C7-T1 disc stress, and C7-T1 segmental ROM based on construct type, with C2-T2 constructs experiencing the highest rod stress, but the lowest C7-T1 disc stress and C7-T1 segmental motion.
CONCLUSION: C3-6 may represent a happy medium, given its low rod stress, middling C7-T1 disc stress, and C7-T1 segmental ROM.

title: Beyond referral: social prescribing as an access-producing system
abstract: Social prescribing is commonly represented as a referral from healthcare to non-clinical community resources, but referral does not ensure use. This perspective argues that social prescribing should be designed and evaluated as an access-producing system. Drawing primarily on food-access interventions as an analytic case, it distinguishes financial, geographic, and relational access as dimensions of practical access that can function as intermediate implementation mechanisms when strategies change them. They are not the antecedent barriers themselves or the downstream outcome of participation; they are the conditions linking a strategy to use. The added value of this framing is therefore not a new taxonomy of familiar barriers, but a more explicit causal question: what changed that made a prescribed resource affordable, reachable, legitimate, and sufficiently trustworthy to use? The three access pathways may interact as complements or bottlenecks, and participation may occur only after each necessary pathway reaches a context-dependent threshold. This parsimonious framing directs evaluation toward proximal evidence of access before distal health outcomes are attributed to social prescribing and offers propositions for prospective testing rather than a validated comprehensive theory.

title: The Emerging Functional Landscape of piRNAs in Ocular Health and Disease.
abstract: P-element-induced wimpy testis (PIWI)-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) are a distinct class of small non-coding RNAs increasingly recognized as regulators of gene expression beyond their canonical function in PIWI-dependent transposon silencing. First characterized in the germline, recent evidence demonstrates that PIWI-piRNA pathways are active in somatic tissues and contribute to cellular homeostasis and adaptive stress responses through epigenetic, transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and translational mechanisms. Although piRNAs regulate several diseases, their roles in ocular physiology and pathology remain poorly understood. In the eye, piRNA pathways may govern retinal homeostasis and responses to oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, and fibrosis. This review synthesizes current knowledge on piRNA biogenesis, molecular mechanisms, and emerging functions in ocular tissues and examines evidence linking PIWI-piRNA dysregulation to major ocular diseases, including age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, retinopathy of prematurity, and subretinal fibrosis. We evaluate the current evidence and highlight that, although disease-associated piRNA signatures and emerging mechanistic links to angiogenesis, oxidative stress, fibrosis, and cellular stress responses have been reported, most findings remain correlative and lack physiological validation. We discuss key challenges, including incomplete piRNA annotation, cell-type-specific activity, and variability in PIWI-piRNA regulatory mechanisms. We also outline future perspectives for defining the roles of PIWI-piRNA networks in ocular physiology and evaluating their potential as biomarkers and therapeutic targets for vision-threatening diseases.

title: Price Variation in Outpatient Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
abstract: ore than 600 000 percutaneous coronary interventions (PCIs) are performed annually in the United States. 1 Increasing procedural safety, same-day discharge pathways, and expansion of Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement have accelerated the transition of elective PCI into outpatient settings, including hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs) and ambulatory surgical centers (ASCs).[2][3][4] Although outpatient PCI may reduce resource utilization and overall spending, little is known about how negotiated prices vary across outpatient sites of care. 2 The 2021 Hospital Price Transparency Rule requires hospitals to disclose payer-specific negotiated rates for all services and has enabled national analyses of pricing variation for cardiovascular services.5 Previous work leveraging these data has demonstrated substantial variation in commercial prices for common cardiovascular procedures, but outpatient PCI pricing remains poorly characterized.5 We used national price transparency data to quantify variation in prices for outpatient PCI across HOPDs versus ASCs and to evaluate associations between facility characteristics and negotiated commercial prices.

title: The Mixed Neutrophilic-Eosinophilic Endotype of CRSwNP Blunts Postsurgical Improvement as Determined by the Completeness of Surgery Index.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Completeness of Surgery Index (CoSI) is a novel metric for assessing surgical quality in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP). Structured histopathology (SHP) is helpful for characterizing drivers of inflammation. Integrating these two tools to identify patients at higher risk for surgically recalcitrant disease has not been explored.
METHODS: CRSwNP patients with a preoperative CoSI < 70 undergoing primary or revision functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) followed by steroid irrigations from 2018 to 2025 were included. CT images and data about comorbidities, SHP, biologic use, and SNOT-22 scores were retrospectively reviewed. Logistic regression, Mann-Whitney U, and Chi-squared tests were used for analysis.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 207 patients achieving significant SNOT-22 improvement 12 months post-FESS (-29.1 ± 22.1; p < 0.001). Mean age was 48.4 years; 53 (25.2%) had aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD), and 114 (54.3%) were revision cases. Mean preoperative CoSI was 37.2 among revisions. Mean postoperative CoSI was 80.0. Among SHP variables, only neutrophilic infiltrate correlated with less improvement in SNOT-22 at 12 months (median -22.4 vs. -33.8; p = 0.007). The effect of neutrophils was seen only with high tissue eosinophilia, with a statistically significant interaction term in the multivariable model. Neutrophil infiltrates were not associated with increased postoperative biologic use.
CONCLUSION: Complete surgery affords significant, sustained SNOT-22 improvement even with high tissue eosinophilia or abnormal tissue architecture. Comorbid tissue neutrophilia and eosinophilia may represent a mixed endotype of CRSwNP with reduced improvement in SNOT-22 after FESS. Combining SHP with CoSI may be helpful for decision-making regarding adjunct medical therapy postoperatively to optimize patient outcomes.

title: Hospital-Initiated Guardianship for Older Adults: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guardianship is a legal process by which a court-appointed individual assumes decision-making authority over a person deemed to be incapacitated. Despite granting significant authority over vulnerable individuals, guardianship remains poorly regulated and understudied. Social determinants of health (SDOH) may influence guardianship outcomes, yet data are limited. This study characterizes guardianship petitions filed by a large academic healthcare system and examines the role of SDOH in petition outcomes.
METHODS: We identified adults aged 60 years or older for whom our healthcare system filed guardianship petitions using publicly available county probate court records from January 2019 through September 2024. Petition outcomes, demographics, and hospitalization data were abstracted from court records and the electronic medical record. Logistic regression models were used to identify demographic factors associated with guardian type (known entity vs. professional) and guardianship scope (full vs. limited).
RESULTS: Among 236 unique individuals, 215 (91.1%) petitions resulted in the appointment of a guardian. Nineteen petitions were not heard by the court for various reasons. Of the remaining 217 petitions heard in court, 215 (99.0%) resulted in guardianship assignment. Medicaid recipients had lower odds of being assigned to a guardian with whom they had a prior, personal relationship (p = 0.04). Lower educational attainment was associated with full guardianship (p = 0.02). More restrictive forms of guardianship were associated with decreased likelihood of being discharged home. There were variations in ethics, palliative care, and psychiatry consults and the relationship of the assigned guardian.
CONCLUSIONS: SDOH, including socioeconomic status and educational attainment, correlated with guardianship outcomes. Guardianship type and scope appear to impact care delivery and discharge destination. Policy reform and community-based interventions are needed to protect vulnerable older adults while preserving autonomy.

title: Non-traumatic vitreous base detachment in an adult with neurofibromatosis type 1: a case report
abstract: Purpose Although neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is best known for its optic pathway and anterior segment manifestations, posterior segment involvement can occur. Vitreoretinal traction and retinal detachment (RD) have been most commonly reported, but spontaneous vitreous base detachment has been only infrequently reported. Observations We describe a 33-year-old woman with NF1 in whom multimodal retinal imaging of the right eye revealed a well-demarcated vitreous base detachment with peripheral tractional RD, nasal vascular tortuosity, and no evidence of retinal breaks or active inflammation, in the absence of any history of ocular or head trauma. The tractional changes remained stable during follow-up, and no intervention was required. Conclusions and importance This case highlights an unusual posterior segment manifestation of NF1 and underscores the importance of careful peripheral retinal examination, with consideration of wide-field imaging when clinically indicated, during the ophthalmic follow-up of adults with NF1.

title: Frailty Is Associated With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Adults With and Without HIV
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is a risk factor for lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in older adults. People with HIV (PWH) have a heightened frailty burden, but the association of HIV and frailty with LUTS in people with and at risk for HIV is unknown. METHODS: Data from 1356 PWH (505 men, 851 women) and 820 without HIV (419 men, 401 women) enrolled in the MACS-WIHS Combined Cohort Study who completed the Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network 10-Item Symptom Index (LURN SI-10) from 10/2021 to 9/2022 were included. Frailty was determined using the Fried frailty phenotype (robust, pre-frail, and frail). Regression models stratified by sex evaluated the cross-sectional associations of HIV and frailty with LUTS severity, urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), and overactive bladder (OAB). Due to low prevalence in men, mixed urinary incontinence (MUI) was analyzed only in women. Effect modification by sex and HIV was tested using the interaction terms with frailty. RESULTS: Mean age was 56 years (SD 11), and 58% of participants were Black. For women, 53% were pre-frail and 23% were frail. For men, 46% were pre-frail and 13% were frail. There was no association of HIV with LUTS. Among women, 21% reported UUI, 61% reported OAB, and 14% reported MUI at least weekly. Compared to robust women, frail women had higher LURN SI-10 scores (absolute difference = 3.3 (95% CI: 2.3, 4.3)). Similarly, frail men had higher LURN SI-10 scores than robust men (absolute difference = 1.6 (95% CI: 0.4, 2.9)). Frailty was associated with greater odds of UUI and OAB in women and men, and MUI in women. There was no evidence of effect modification by sex. CONCLUSIONS: LUTS are common in people with and at-risk for HIV and are more severe among those who are frail. More research is needed to investigate the sex-independent mechanisms that underlie frailty and LUTS in this population.

title: DGAT1 is associated with pathogenic T-cell programs in multiple sclerosis and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis
abstract: Raw flow cytometry data (FCS files) for: DGAT1 is associated with pathogenic T-cell programs in multiple sclerosis and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis This dataset contains the raw flow cytometry data underlying Figures 3C–3F and 4D–4E of DGAT1 is associated with pathogenic T-cell programs in multiple sclerosis and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (submitted to PeerJ). The study examines the relationship between diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase-1 (DGAT1) and autoimmune neuroinflammation. FoxP3-GFP Dgat1-deficient mice showed enlarged peripheral lymph nodes with increased frequencies and absolute numbers of regulatory T cells (Tregs), and developed less severe experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) than wild-type controls. The data come from FoxP3-GFP reporter mice that were wild type, heterozygous or knockout for Dgat1. Figure 3 covers steady-state lymphoid tissues: peripheral and mesenteric lymph nodes, spleen, blood, thymus, Peyer’s patches and bone marrow. Figure 4 covers lymph node and spinal cord at days 7 and 15 of EAE. All samples were acquired on a BD LSRFortessa with FACSDiva v8.0.1 and saved as FCS 3.0 files. The dataset includes 404 FCS files from 11 independent experiments, with one zip archive per experiment. Each archive contains the sample files plus that experiment’s single-stain compensation controls and unstained control. See README.txt for the figure panels, acquisition date, tissues, mouse genotype and sex, and staining panel for each experiment. Note that in one experiment (d15 spinal cord, expt 5) two channel labels were entered incorrectly at acquisition; the README gives the correct assignments.

title: Hemispheric Asymmetry in Global and Focal Processing of Navon Figures in Older and Younger Adults: Behavioral Evidence From a Monocular Viewing Paradigm
abstract: Background: Hemispheric lateralization plays a central role in attentional processing, with relative left-hemisphere advantages for linguistic and focal information and right-hemisphere advantages for visuospatial and global processing. Hierarchical Navon figures provide a useful method for examining interactions between focal and global attention and hemispheric specialization. Monocular viewing, which biases visual input to the contralateral hemisphere, has been proposed as a method to modulate attentional processing. However, its influence on attentional level and stimulus-type interactions in healthy adults remains unclear. Objective: To examine how attentional condition (focal vs global), stimulus type (letter vs shape), and monocular viewing eye (left vs right) influence reaction times during a hierarchical figure task. Methods: Fifty-four healthy, right-handed adults ages 18–86 years completed a choice reaction time task using hierarchical Navon figures (letter “A,” triangle, or both stimuli) under left- or right-eye monocular viewing. Linear mixed-effects models were used to test main effects and interactions. Results: Participants responded faster in focal than global conditions, and faster to the letter than the triangle. Focally presented letter stimuli elicited the fastest responses. In dual-stimulus trials, responses were faster when letters were focal and triangles global, particularly under right-eye viewing. Age was associated with slower reaction times overall, but there was no significant difference in pattern. Conclusion: Stimulus characteristics influenced attentional response speed, with focal verbal information eliciting the fastest responses, particularly during right-eye viewing. This is consistent with relative left-hemisphere advantages for focal and language processing. Findings suggest attentional specialization persists across adulthood despite generalized age-related slowing.

title: Maternal E-cigarette Exposure Augments Murine Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
abstract: Background: Smoking and family history are major risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Smoking and nicotine are modulators of DNA methylation, capable of causing heritable epigenetic alterations. Nicotine infusion and e-cigarette (e-cig) vaping augment murine AAA. We investigated the effects of murine maternal e-cig vaping on offspring experimental AAA, and impacts on transgenerational DNA methylation and accessibility. Methods: We performed perinatal e-cig nicotine vaping in two strains of adult female mice (ApoE-/- and C57BL/6J). Mice were mated to control males, and treated through gestation. A parallel group were instead sacrificed after treatment, for DNA analysis. Offspring were aged to adulthood, and AAAs were then induced by elastase (C57BL/6J) or angiotensin-II infusion (ApoE-/-), and ultrasound-tracked for 4 weeks. In a second cohort, parental and offspring aortic tissue and blood DNA underwent RRBS and ATAC-seq analysis respectively. Offspring abdominal aortic anatomy was examined, and stiffness was assessed with ex vivo arterial myography. Results: Maternal e-cig exposure increased offspring AAA growth in both models and genders. AAA incidence was increased in ApoE-/- males, and observed effects were overall more pronounced in males. Maternal vape exposure altered aortic DNA methylation and blood DNA accessibility in mothers and offspring, with differential sites in numerous genes identified, including AAA-related genes and pathways. Pathways were enriched for transcription factors, inflammation/immune-related genes, and angiogenesis genes, with similar changes identified in exposed mothers. Male offspring displayed more differential genes. Significant changes were located in genes known to harbor AAA risk loci in humans, and overlapped with published epigenetic alterations in human smokers. Differences also occurred in offspring aortic structure and stiffness. Conclusions: Maternal e-cig nicotine exposure augments AAA growth in multiple models across generations. These effects are accompanied by broad epigenetic DNA reprogramming of key AAA modulator genes and pathways.

title: Crystalline silica exposure causes latent biomechanical abnormalities along the cardiopulmonary axis
abstract: Rationale: Crystalline silica exposure is a major global health burden linked to chronic lung disease and cardiopulmonary morbidity, but early lung-vascular-cardiac abnormalities preceding overt functional decline are poorly defined. Objectives: To determine whether a single crystalline silica exposure produces subclinical abnormalities across the integrated axis of cardiopulmonary response (lung→pulmonary artery→right ventricle) and identify associated sex-dependent physiologic patterns and molecular programs. Methods: proximal pulmonary artery biomechanics and microstructural second harmonic generation imaging, right ventricular pressure, transthoracic echocardiography, and bulk RNA sequencing of lung and right ventricle. Results: Despite recovery of body weight and preserved voluntary exercise, silica-exposed mice demonstrated reduced diffusion capacity, ultrastructural thickening, and disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier. Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed persistent inflammation with elevated macrophages, lymphocytes, neutrophils, and protein, alongside retained particulate and surfactant-rich debris (silicoproteinosis). Lung mechanics were sex-dependent; females showed a parenchymal-dominant phenotype and males showed increased airway resistance. Elevated pulmonary circulatory pressures caused increased functional stiffness and reduced distensibility of the proximal pulmonary arteries. Right ventricular free wall thickening was noted in females. Lung transcriptomics indicated persistent immune activation and extracellular matrix remodeling, while the right ventricle demonstrated metabolic reprogramming with downregulation of structural and reparative programs. Conclusions: A single crystalline silica exposure induces a subclinical, multi-compartment cardiopulmonary phenotype characterized by persistent alveolar-capillary injury, pulmonary vascular stiffening, increased right ventricular afterload, sex-dependent pulmonary mechanics, and divergent organ-level transcriptomic responses.

title: Exponential-family random graph models in resident-healthcare provider networks: An application using data from long-term healthcare facilities in the United States
abstract: Infectious pathogens have a high burden in long-term care facilities [LTCFs]. Contact is a primary route of pathogen transmission in these settings, so describing resident-healthcare provider [HCP] contact networks can clarify how routine care assignments may shape opportunities for transmission. In this study, we analyze a large sample of resident-HCP networks in LTCFs across the US. Using multilevel exponential-family random graph models [ERGMs] applied to bipartite graphs, in one of the first applications of these models to healthcare contact data, we investigate network structures associated with resident cohorting based on resident-level characteristics. Methodologically, the fitted pooled bipartite ERGM uses mode-specific, mean-centered log-size interactions and combines Monte Carlo maximum likelihood estimation [MC-MLE] point estimates with stochastic approximation [SA] bootstrap inference, a combination that makes these models practical when the pooled networks differ widely in size. Our analysis suggests that residents with wound care, bedridden status, and ventilator use were associated with more HCP contacts. In contrast, no evidence of cohorting-like HCP sharing was found for measured resident clinical characteristics, including Multi-Drug Resistant Organism [MDRO] status. These results do not estimate intervention effects; rather, they identify contact patterns that infection-control teams and transmission modelers can use to audit resident-HCP assignment practices and to parameterize network-based simulation studies.

title: Transcriptional Signatures Associated with Etiology of Post-Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Lung Injury.
abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (alloHCT) is a potentially curative therapy for many hematologic disorders but is frequently complicated by infectious and noninfectious pulmonary injury. Differentiating these etiologies is challenging in clinical practice, and it remains unclear whether response signatures can distinguish infectious from non-infectious lung injury following transplantation. We performed bulk RNA sequencing of whole-blood samples from 52 alloHCT recipients within 120 days of transplantation who developed lung injury due to bacterial, viral, or fungal pathogens as well as idiopathic pneumonia syndrome (IPS). We compared expression of genes and immune programs across etiologies of lung injury. Distinct transcriptional programs were observed across etiologies. Viral pneumonia showed enrichment of interferon and adaptive immune signaling pathways. Bacterial pneumonia demonstrated enrichment of innate immune and heme metabolism pathways. Fungal pneumonia exhibited the strongest enrichment of cellular proliferation pathways. IPS showed lower enrichment of immune signaling pathways than infectious etiologies. Transcriptomic responses differ between infectious and noninfectious lung injury following alloHCT. These findings highlight the potential utility of transcriptomic profiling to support diagnosis, guide therapeutic management, and risk-stratify patients following transplantation.

title: Video-assisted resident education is associated with improved ankle joint reduction: A prospective controlled study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Proper fracture reduction and splinting technique is critical for soft tissue protection and fracture stability in the acute management of ankle fractures. However, residency education for acute ankle fracture reduction and splinting techniques remains poorly standardized and streamlined. This study evaluated the effect of implementing a video-assisted ankle fracture management education program administered to first-year orthopaedic residents on ankle joint reduction and splint quality. METHODS: This was a prospective controlled study conducted at a single level I trauma center. All consecutive ankle fractures (OTA/AO: 4F, 44) requiring the placement of a bivalved short leg cast or AO splint from January 1, 2019, to June 30th, 2022 were included. Exclusion criteria included skeletal immaturity, missing imaging, delayed fracture presentation more than two weeks from injury, concurrent ipsilateral injury/polytrauma interfering with ankle reduction, open fracture, or ankle fractures treated without an AO splint or cast. The primary outcome was joint reduction quality defined as radiographic post-reduction tibiofibular overlap, tibiofibular clear space, and medial clear space. Secondary outcomes included splint padding thickness and ankle dorsiflexion angle to assess splint quality. RESULTS: A total of 280 consecutive ankle fracture cases were included for evaluation of splint quality: 111 in the intervention group (mean age 46; [range 14-92]; 44% female) versus 169 in the control group (mean age 44; [range 14-90]; 41% female). Comparable injury severity was observed between groups. In the supination-external rotation IV (SER4) and type IV-equivalent (SER4e) subgroup, there was significant improvement in joint reduction quality in the intervention group as compared to control (55% versus 36%, respectively; Risk Ratio: 1.52, [95% CI: 1.03-2.25], p = 0.04). In the entire cohort, splint padding thickness was not significantly improved in the intervention group (p > 0.05), however, there was a significant increase in the percentage of ankles splinted in an appropriately dorsiflexed position (p = 0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of video-assisted ankle fracture management education program was associated with improvements in overall ankle joint reduction quality. While the clinical significance of the improvements observed in ankle reduction remains yet to be established, orthopaedic surgery residency programs should consider incorporating video technique guides into their educational curricula. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II, Therapeutic Study.

title: Atypical Atrial Flutter From Lipomatous Hypertrophy of the Interatrial Septum in a Procedure-Naive Patient.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum (LHIS) is generally benign and often discovered incidentally; however, it can occasionally serve as a substrate for atrial arrhythmias.
CASE SUMMARY: An 86-year-old man with no prior cardiac history presented with new onset atrial flutter (AFL) with an atrial rate of 280 beats/min. During an electrophysiology study, intracardiac echocardiography identified LHIS. Three-dimensional electroanatomic activation mapping demonstrated the earliest focal activation at the superior posteroseptal right atrium, corresponding to the location of the LHIS. Radiofrequency ablation at this site terminated the AFL, rendering the tachycardia noninducible.
DISCUSSION: LHIS can act as an isolated arrhythmogenic substrate for atypical AFL. The combination of intracardiac echocardiography and high-density electroanatomic mapping allows precise localization of the arrhythmogenic focus, facilitating safe and effective catheter ablation.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: LHIS should be considered a potential arrhythmogenic substrate in patients with atypical AFL. Catheter ablation of LHIS-associated AFL is safe and effective.

title: Availability of resources to apply the 2024 McDonald criteria: A global perspective.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 3rd ECTRIMS Winter School highlighted regional and global disparities in resources needed to implement the 2024 McDonald diagnostic criteria for multiple sclerosis.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the availability of paraclinical tools and regional differences in access reported by neurologists in an online survey.
RESULTS: The survey was completed by 328 neurologists from 44 countries. Core diagnostic tools, including magnetic resonance imaging and oligoclonal band testing, were widely available. Access to advanced imaging, optic nerve assessment, and laboratory biomarkers varied across regions.
CONCLUSIONS: Variability in access to key paraclinical tests may impact on the implementation of the 2024 McDonald criteria globally.

title: Human Metapneumovirus Diagnosis, Pathogenesis, and Therapeutics
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a globally prevalent respiratory pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections across all age groups, with the greatest disease burden in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Clinical manifestations range from mild upper respiratory tract symptoms, including cough, wheezing, and sore throat, to severe lower respiratory tract disease such as bronchiolitis, pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and secondary bacterial infections that may require intensive care and mechanical ventilation. Despite its widespread circulation and substantial healthcare impact, important aspects of hMPV transmission, pathogenesis, and host immune responses remain incompletely understood, hindering the development of effective therapeutics and vaccines. This review summarizes the current knowledge of hMPV epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostics, pathogenesis, and prevention strategies, with emphasis on recent outbreaks that highlight its seasonal and geographic variability. We discuss the viral life cycle and the contributions of the major surface glycoproteins—fusion (F), attachment (G), and small hydrophobic (SH) proteins—to viral infectivity, immune evasion, and disease progression. Advances in molecular diagnostics, including reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), next-generation sequencing, metagenomic approaches, and nanopore sequencing, are also examined. While supportive care remains the cornerstone of clinical management, existing antiviral therapies demonstrate limited and inconsistent efficacy. Emerging preventive and therapeutic strategies, including mRNA-based vaccines and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, offer promising avenues for disease control. Improved understanding of hMPV biology and host-pathogen interactions will be critical for developing effective interventions to reduce the global burden of this increasingly recognized respiratory pathogen.

title: Early Experience of a Dedicated Outpatient Palliative Hepatology Clinic: Referral Patterns, Patient Characteristics, and Outcomes
abstract: Background and AimsDedicated outpatient palliative hepatology clinics remain uncommon despite the substantial symptom burden of advanced liver disease. We describe the early experience of a newly established outpatient palliative hepatology clinic.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients scheduled for an initial consultation during the first months of clinic operation. Demographic and clinical characteristics, referral indications and sources, symptoms, advance care planning, follow-up, and outcomes were collected from the electronic medical record and summarized using descriptive statistics.ResultsAmong 26 scheduled patients, median age was 60 years (IQR, 41-71), median MELD 3.0 was 21 (IQR, 14-30), and 23 (89%) had prior cirrhosis-related hospitalization(s). Common referral indications included supportive care needs (81%), goals-of-care discussions (65%), and symptom management (39%). Referrals primarily came from hepatology/gastroenterology (54%) and inpatient palliative care (31%). Eighteen patients (69%) attended; 4 (15%) died before their scheduled appointment. Among those evaluated, pain and nausea were most common (56% each). Goals-of-care discussions occurred in 67%, advance directives were discussed in 72%, and surrogate decision makers in 83%. During a median follow-up of 192 days, 61% returned for follow-up and 33% died. Median time from the initial clinic visit to death was 51 days.ConclusionsPatients referred to our palliative hepatology clinic had advanced disease and substantial supportive care needs. High rates of goals-of-care and advance care planning among those evaluated highlight the potential value of dedicated palliative hepatology clinics.

title: Haemostasis in Liver Disease
abstract: Haemostasis in advanced liver disease is altered, but rebalanced. This balance is precarious, and bleeding or thrombosis may occur with disturbance. Changes to primary haemostasis in liver disease involve platelet quantity and function. When endothelial injury occurs, exposure of collagen triggers platelet activation as in healthy patients. Patients with cirrhosis, however, have thrombocytopenia due to portal hypertension and splenic sequestration. A drawback inherent to all laboratory haemostatic measures is the loss of contextual interplay between the vascular endothelium and other effectors of coagulation. Spontaneous bleeding in liver disease can be categorized into portal hypertension-related bleeding and non-portal hypertensive bleeding. Risk factors for procedural bleeding in cirrhosis can be organized into patient-related risk factors and procedure-related risk factors. Foremost to any procoagulant prophylaxis or rescue intervention for active bleeding is careful attention to the aetiology with consideration of the underlying drivers of bleeding.

title: Ascites
abstract: Ascites is the most common decompensating event in patients with cirrhosis and one that is associated with the highest mortality. Ascites in cirrhosis results from sinusoidal hypertension and sodium retention. One of the most common bacterial infections in cirrhosis is spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP), an infection of ascites unique to patients with cirrhosis, particularly those with severely decompensated cirrhosis. In patients with SBP, the risk of recurrence is extremely high in the absence of antibiotic prophylaxis. Hyponatraemia in cirrhosis is dilutional. Hyponatraemia has been associated with the development of hepatic encephalopathy due to a further reduction in brain organic osmolytes, particularly myoinositol. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt acts on the pathophysiological mechanisms responsible for ascites formation. Hepatorenal Syndrome is a distinct form of kidney dysfunction that occurs in patients with cirrhosis, almost invariably in the setting of ascites, often refractory to diuretics, and frequently accompanied by hyponatraemia.

title: Getting on board with going off ward
abstract: Off-ward practices for hospitalized patients vary across medical centers, but many hospitals adopt restrictive policies that prioritize safety and liability over autonomy and dignity. Hospitalists routinely navigate competing priorities and negotiate institutional barriers, positioning them to advocate for patient-centered interventions. In this Next Steps article, we describe why limiting freedom of movement infringes upon ethical principles and display that practical frontline solutions are possible through a hospitalist-led off-ward pilot program at a Veterans Affairs hospital. This experience demonstrated that hospitalists can create safe opportunities for patients to regain meaningful independence during hospitalization.

title: Use of Skin Substitute to Facilitate Tension-Free Closure Over the Vascular Pedicle and Free Flap in Lower Extremity Reconstruction
abstract: Introduction: Free tissue transfer to the lower extremity are often challenging cases, as the lack of local tissue laxity and convex surface of the lower extremity can lead to pedicle compression after inset. Methods exist to lessen this risk of compression, including additional free tissue transfer, local tissue rearrangement, and skin grafting. We hypothesize that one cause of venous thrombosis and flap failure is excessive pressure over the flap and vascular pedicle. Veins could collapse from postoperative swelling after primary closure, causing impaired blood flow dynamics and elevating the risk of flap loss if not recognized. This study describes the use of skin substitutes to facilitate a tension-free closure over the vascular pedicle and around the flap. Methods: An IRB-approved retrospective review was conducted of patients undergoing lower limb reconstruction with free tissue transfer and skin substitute. Between June 2024 and December 2025, eighteen patients were included. Patient demographics, comorbidities, reconstruction characteristics, and surgical outcomes were recorded. Postoperative complications were monitored for at least 30 days. Results: One patient returned to the operating room within 24 hours after reconstruction secondary to venous thrombosis, and another returned within 24 hours due to an arterial bleeder. Both patients progressed without any further complications. There were two instances of partial flap loss, and there were no cases of total flap loss. Conclusions: Here, we demonstrate the use of skin substitute for pedicle coverage. This method allows additional coverage of the pedicle with minimal compression.

title: Assessing brain-behaviour coupling in non-invasive brain stimulation: Insights from reliable change indices and Monte Carlo simulations.
abstract: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NiBS) studies frequently report exploratory brain-behaviour correlations following the application of NiBS. However, these analyses are typically underpowered and rely on ratio-based change scores with known statistical limitations. We addressed these limitations by pooling individual data from three independent studies (N = 69) and combining empirical analysis with a Monte Carlo simulation framework. All studies applied 20 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) targeting the pre-supplementary motor area (preSMA) and right inferior frontal gyrus (rIFG) during a stop signal task. Changes in preSMA-rIFG EEG imaginary coherency (ImCoh) and stop-signal reaction time (SSRT) were quantified using reliable change indices (RCI), z-standardised within studies for pooled mixed-effects regression. We found no meaningful association between tACS-induced ImCoh change and SSRT change (r = .013, marginal R2 = .004), with project-wise correlations being small, non-significant, and directionally inconsistent. While sensitivity analysis using ratio-based change scores converged on the same null result (r = .014), the simulation framework revealed that ratio-based scores show near-complete failure to recover true brain-behaviour associations across all plausible effect sizes. Conversely, RCI-based scores preserved directional accuracy and provided well-calibrated Type I error control, despite moderate attenuation under realistic noise conditions. These results highlight the severe statistical limits of detecting individual-level brain-behaviour coupling following 20 Hz tACS. Rather than ruling out a true biological association, our findings demonstrate that standard sample sizes and typical measurement noise create substantial 'blindness' to realistic effect sizes, underscoring a broader need for more reliable metrics and adequately powered designs in NiBS research.

title: Treatment Mechanisms Associated With Directional Preference and Repeated Movements: A Scoping Review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the evidence for treatment mechanisms underlying repeated movements and sustained positioning, especially when matched to one's directional preference. DESIGN: Scoping review LITERATURE SEARCH: Five electronic databases were searched in November 2025 (PubMed, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and SPORTDiscus). The review was registered a priori on Open Science Framework Registries (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/SX5H7). STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: Included studies investigated adults with any form of musculoskeletal pain who completed repeated movements or sustained positioning as an intervention. The outcomes must have included a physiological proxy measure for a treatment mechanism pre- and during/post-intervention. DATA SYNTHESIS: Narrative and descriptive data were categorized by mechanistic domains and treatment fidelity. RESULTS: Thirty-six (36) articles were identified, which included treatment mechanisms from 5 domains: biomechanical domain (n=11; 31%), neurological domain (n=10; 28%), neuromuscular domain (n=11; 31%), neuroimmune domain (n=2; 6%), and neurovascular domain (n=2; 6%). Most studies were categorized with lower treatment fidelity of directional preference. CONCLUSION: We found preliminary evidence for a multisystem mechanistic response following the application of repeated movements and/or sustained positioning interventions in adults with musculoskeletal pain.

title: Compensatory Eating Disorder: Disorder, Dimension, or Diagnostic Artefact?
abstract: Compensatory eating disorder (CED) is a newly proposed 'other specified feeding and eating disorder' that is characterised by recurrent non-purging compensatory behaviours, overvaluation of weight and shape, and the absence of objective binge eating, low weight, or recent significant weight loss. Although CED has been long documented in research, it remains unclear whether CED represents a distinct clinical diagnosis or a variant presentation of extant eating disorders. In this commentary, we situate CED within the broader eating disorders landscape and call for greater diagnostic clarity. We also provide five concrete future directions that can inform the appropriate classification of CED, including: (1) clarifying core diagnostic features of CED, (2) leveraging statistical models to inform CED classification, (3) establishing CED's longitudinal and prognostic validity, (4) incorporating clinician and patient perspectives on the adoption of CED diagnostic criteria, and (5) weighing risks and benefits of adding a new clinical diagnosis. These guidelines may help our field answer a novel research question that has implications for clinical practice: Is Compensatory Eating Disorder a missing diagnosis in the eating-disorder nomenclature or is it a misclassified one?

title: Predicted high-affinity binding of Porphyromonas gingivalis peptides to 334 human leukocyte antigen (HLA) Class I and Class II molecules
abstract: Aim: To determine predicted binding affinities of peptides from Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis) proteins and identify those binding with high-affinity to human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Methods: We evaluated in silico binding affinities of all possible linear 9-mer and 15-mer peptides of 13 P. gingivalis proteins with 334 HLA alleles; strong predicted binding affinity (IC50 < 50 nM) was considered a “hit”. Results: Predicted binding affinity of HLA molecules and P. gingivalis proteins varied substantially. We identified 798 unique 15-mer peptides that were predicted to bind strongly to Class II HLA molecules and did not overlap with any 15-mers of 83,607 human proteins and, thus, may be suitable candidates for P. gingivalis vaccine development. Conclusions: Individual differences in HLA shape the adaptive immune system response to P. gingivalis and other antigens via variability in binding affinity, a crucial first step in mounting immune system responses aimed at neutralization or elimination of non-self antigens, assuming host immunocompetency otherwise. Various preventive and therapeutic strategies aimed at reducing the burden of P. gingivalis are under investigation; the current findings document specific HLA-peptide combinations that may be a useful starting point for ongoing efforts toward P. gingivalis vaccine development.

title: Quantitative UTE MRI Differences in the Meniscus Following ACL Reconstruction: A Prospective Cohort Study Using 3D Ultrashort Echo Time Adiabatic T1rho and Magnetization Transfer Imaging
abstract: BACKGROUND: ACLR is associated with altered joint loading and increased risk of post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Conventional MRI has limited sensitivity to early meniscal differences because of short-T2 signal decay and magic-angle effects. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether 3D ultrashort echo time imaging-based adiabatic T1rho (UTE-Adiab-T1rho) and ultrashort echo time imaging-based macromolecular fraction (UTE-MMF) identify regional quantitative MRI differences after ACLR. STUDY TYPE: Prospective longitudinal cohort study. POPULATION: 30 control scans, 19 ACLR scans at 6-12 months, and 13 ACLR scans at 12+ months were analyzed. Mean ages were 34.5, 34.5, and 37.2 years; female/male counts were 15/15, 9/10, and 8/5. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: Participants underwent 3-T knee MRI with 3D fat-saturated UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE magnetization transfer sequences. ASSESSMENT: UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF maps were generated with single-component exponential and two-pool magnetization transfer models. Values were extracted from four meniscal regions of interest by a blinded reader, with blinded redelineation in a subset. Patient-reported outcomes included International Knee Documentation Committee, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index scores. STATISTICAL TESTS: Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated observations. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied. RESULTS: UTE-Adiab-T1rho showed significant group (q = 0.001) and region (q < 0.001) effects. Compared with controls, UTE-Adiab-T1rho was higher in LAM at 6-12 months (+5.60 ms; q = 0.035) and 12+ months (+7.09 ms; q = 0.028), and in LPM at 12+ months (+6.35 ms; q = 0.035). UTE-MMF showed significant group (q = 0.041) and region (q < 0.001) effects. LPM UTE-MMF was lower than controls at 6-12 months (-3.56 percentage points; q = 0.028) and 12+ months (-3.10 percentage points; q = 0.049). No 6-12 versus 12+ month MRI or PROM contrast survived FDR correction. MRI-PROM associations were not FDR-significant (all q ≥ 0.383). DATA CONCLUSION: UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF mapping identified regional MRI differences after ACLR. Pairwise differences were concentrated in lateral regions, but corrected group-by-region interactions were not significant. PROMs were worse after ACLR but did not differ between postoperative windows after correction. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2. TECHNICAL EFFICACY STAGE: 2.

title: Investigating cardiorespiratory fitness, cerebral blood flow, and brain metabolism in epilepsy.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic generalized epilepsies (IGEs) are characterized by seizures that propagate through widespread thalamocortical networks including the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). Poor cardiorespiratory fitness may exacerbate neurovascular and metabolic vulnerability including heightened susceptibility to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. We aimed to examine cardiorespiratory fitness, regional cerebral blood flow (CBF), and metabolite concentrations in patients with IGEs (PwIGEs) and to determine the effect of seizure control status on these physiological and neurochemical measures.
METHODS: Forty-six participants (31 PwIGEs, 15 healthy controls) underwent a graded exercise test to assess maximal oxygen uptake (VO2peak) as a measure of cardiorespiratory fitness and completed 3T MRI including multi-delayed pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) to assess CBF and single-voxel spectroscopy (SVS) to assess ratios of N-acetylaspartate and glutamate/glutamine complex to total creatine (NAA/tCr and Glx/tCr, respectively) in the ACC and thalamus. Group differences and seizure control effects in PwIGEs were examined using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA).
RESULTS: VO2peak, thalamic CBF, ACC NAA/tCr, and ACC Glx/tCr did not significantly differ between groups. PwIGEs exhibited higher ACC CBF (p = 0.039) and lower thalamic NAA/tCr (p = 0.012) than healthy controls. PwIGEs with active seizures showed significantly lower thalamic Glx/tCr compared to those who were seizure-free (p = 0.003).
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest poor cardiorespiratory fitness is not epilepsy-specific and likely attributable to lifestyle and that region-specific alterations in perfusion and metabolic milieu in PwIGEs characterized by higher ACC CBF and lower thalamic NAA/tCr and Glx/tCr in those with active seizures. The multimodal neuroimaging approach provides convergent evidence of thalamocortical network dysregulation underlying IGE pathophysiology.

title: The Association of Gout Flare Resolution With Physical Activity and Sleep: A Prospective Remote-Monitoring Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine whether gout flare resolution is associated with physical activity and sleep. These findings were intended to inform the future development of a definition for flare resolution.
METHODS: Data from 81 participants with gout who experienced at least one flare during a six-month prospective observational study were included. Daily activity (step count) and sleep (total sleep time and deep sleep percentage) were collected remotely using wrist-worn trackers. Daily flare occurrence was captured using smartphone diaries. Activity and sleep outcomes during each flare episode were compared to those during three resolution timeframes: T1, the first day following the flare; T2, the consecutive window immediately following the flare and equal in length to the flare; and T3, the consecutive window equal in length to the flare and immediately following a washout window (equal in length to the flare). Adjusted differences in median between flare and resolution timeframes were estimated using linear quantile mixed models.
RESULTS: Daily step count was lower during flares compared with all resolution timeframes (all P ≤ 0.033). T3 provided the best overall model fit, suggesting that resolution is most clearly distinguished from the flare when using this timeframe. No significant differences between flare and resolution were observed for the sleep outcomes for any resolution timeframe.
CONCLUSION: Physical activity improves soon after flare cessation, with the clearest distinction between flare and resolution observed over a longer postflare recovery period, whereas sleep metrics do not differentiate flare from resolution states. These findings support physical activity as a useful objective domain for gout flare resolution.

title: Preserving the Dialysis Lifeline: An Updated Review on Central Venous Stenosis
abstract: Central venous stenosis (CVS) is an under-recognized yet clinically consequential complication of hemodialysis care, threatening vascular access function, limiting future access options, and contributing to substantial morbidity in patients with end-stage kidney disease. Although often detected only after access dysfunction or venous hypertension becomes clinically apparent, CVS represents the cumulative consequence of biologic, mechanical, and hemodynamic injury to the central venous circulation. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the epidemiology, pathobiology, risk factors, diagnosis, and management of CVS in hemodialysis patients, with emphasis on translational links between venous injury and clinical access failure. Central venous catheters, cardiac implantable electronic device leads, peripherally inserted central catheters, and high-flow arteriovenous access can initiate endothelial disruption, inflammation, thrombosis, and maladaptive neointimal hyperplasia. These processes are amplified by the uremic milieu, oxidative stress, impaired endothelial repair, and vascular smooth-muscle cell activation, providing a mechanistic basis for recurrent stenosis after intervention. Diagnosis requires integration of clinical suspicion with imaging, including duplex ultrasound, CT or MR venography, and catheter-based venography, which remains the procedural reference standard and enables immediate treatment. Endovascular therapy, particularly percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with selective stent placement, remains the cornerstone of management for symptomatic disease; however, elastic recoil, restenosis, and repeated reintervention continue to limit long-term durability. Emerging strategies, including drug-coated balloons, intravascular ultrasound-guided intervention, dedicated venous stents, and biologically targeted approaches, may improve outcomes but require further validation. Prevention through catheter avoidance, optimal device planning, early recognition, and multidisciplinary access stewardship remains central to preserving the hemodialysis lifeline. A mechanism-informed approach to CVS may help shift care from repeated salvage toward durable access preservation.

title: Retained Colorectal Foreign Body After Suspected Chemical Incapacitation: A Surgical and Forensic Challenge.
abstract: Retained rectal foreign bodies are an uncommon but clinically significant surgical emergency. We report the case of a 74-year-old male with multiple medical comorbidities who presented with progressive rectal pain and obstipation several days after an episode of suspected drug-facilitated assault. Plain radiography identified a large metallic aerosol can, and attempts to retrieve it under general anesthesia using surgical clamps and a magnetic probe failed. Intraoperative fluoroscopy demonstrated that the can had migrated proximal to the rectosigmoid junction into the left colon, precluding transanal extraction. The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy with longitudinal colotomy, permitting safe removal of the foreign body without evidence of perforation or visceral injury. This case illustrates the critical role of intraoperative fluoroscopy when digital examination fails, the indications for operative intervention in proximally migrated foreign bodies, and the importance of considering drug-facilitated assault as an etiology.

title: Temperature-Attributable Cardiovascular Mortality in Europe Under Future Climate Scenarios: Projected Impacts of Population Aging and Climate Change to 2080.
abstract:
AIMS: Heat and cold stress are established cardiovascular risk factors. As climate patterns shift and Europe's population ages, quantifying their separate attributable fractions-and projecting future temperature-attributable cardiovascular disease (tCVD) burden-is essential for clinical and policy decision-making.
METHODS: Europe was divided into a 0.25° × 0.25° grid (12,411 land cells across 37 countries). Annual cardiovascular disease (CVD) deaths (2016-2023) were downscaled from national estimates using population data. Temperature-mortality relative risk coefficients were drawn from a 27-country pooled study and applied via population attributable fractions with 1,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Daily mean temperature projections from five bias-corrected climate models were obtained under moderate (SSP2-4.5) and high (SSP5-8.5) emission scenarios. Population aging was incorporated using country-level age projections; climate-only analyses held age structure constant at 2020 levels.
RESULTS: At baseline, non-optimal temperature accounted for 168,586 [144,961-192,293] CVD deaths annually (31.4 [27.0-35.8] per 100,000), with a cold-to-heat ratio of 5:1. Under SSP5-8.5, total tCVD mortality is projected to nearly double to 62.4 [48.5-76.2] per 100,000 by late-century (441,772 [343,627-540,116] annual deaths), with heat-attributable rates projected to rise 472%. Population aging may amplify total projected mortality by over 80% by late century beyond climate change alone; without aging, cold-attributable rates may decline over the century rather than rise.
CONCLUSIONS: tCVD mortality across Europe is projected to double by late-century, driven by dramatic heat increases and substantially amplified by population aging. These findings support greater integration of temperature-related CVD risk into clinical practice and public health policy.

title: Racial Disparities in Longitudinal Functional Outcome After Ischemic Stroke
abstract: BACKGROUND: The burden of stroke is unequally distributed in the United States, with Black individuals experiencing more incident stroke. It remains unclear whether Black individuals also experience worse stroke recovery. We sought to study disparities in longitudinal functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke in a population-based study. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study in the Greater Cincinnati Northern Kentucky region over an 18-month period (July 2019 to December 2020). All acute ischemic stroke events were captured. The modified Rankin Scale scores were determined at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months for patients who survived the index event. We studied the association between Black race and longitudinal modified Rankin Scale (across all time points) with mixed-effects ordinal regression, initially adjusting for age, sex, and time since stroke. Hierarchical regression was used to sequentially adjust for stroke severity and management, premorbid health, and social determinants. RESULTS: Among 2796 patients with acute ischemic stroke (mean age, 69.0; 31% Black; 52% female), 2537 survived and were included (mean age, 68.4; 32% Black; 52% female). Black race was associated with a worse longitudinal modified Rankin Scale score (cOR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.89-3.60]). Excluding patients with recurrent events did not change this association (cOR, 2.69 [95% CI, 1.92-3.78]). Adding variables reflecting initial stroke severity and management partly attenuated the association (cOR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.43-2.60]). Adding variables reflecting premorbid health further attenuated the association (cOR decreased to 1.43 [95% CI, 1.09-1.87]). The remaining association between Black race and the modified Rankin Scale score was fully attenuated by social determinants, with cOR, 1.09 (95% CI, 0.80-1.47). There was no interaction between race and time since stroke. CONCLUSIONS: Starting at discharge and persisting out to 12 months, acute ischemic stroke functional outcomes are worse among Black individuals. These disparities are significantly attenuated by clinical factors and social determinants; future studies should explore whether the social determinants can be intervened upon in the recovery period.

title: Functional neural activity and connectivity deficits underlying vocal auditory feedback control in post-stroke aphasia: An fMRI study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the functional neural activity and connectivity correlates of disrupted sensorimotor integration underlying vocal production and motor control deficits in post-stroke aphasia. METHODS: fMRI data were acquired from 15 aphasia and 15 control participants during vocalization of speech vowel sounds under altered auditory feedback with randomized ± 100-cents pitch-shift stimuli. RESULTS: We found that stroke-induced brain damage in aphasia was associated with diminished activation within left-hemisphere dorsal stream networks, including premotor and motor cortices, posterior superior temporal regions, and supramarginal gyrus. Functional connectivity analysis revealed reduced left-hemisphere coupling between posterior superior temporal gyrus (pSTG) and dorsal and ventral precentral speech areas (dPSA and vPSA) in aphasia, indicating disrupted auditory-motor integration. Aphasia participants exhibited reduced following and opposing (i.e., compensatory) vocal responses to pitch-shifted auditory feedback, reflecting impairments in both rapid feedforward and slower feedback-based control mechanisms. In addition, impaired vocal compensatory behavior was associated with reduced functional connectivity between pSTG and the left dorsal precentral speech areas (dPSA) as well as the right dorsal laryngeal motor cortex (dLMC), suggesting the critical role of these networks in auditory-feedback-based laryngeal motor control during vocal production and their stroke-induced impairment in aphasia. CONCLUSIONS: Our data provide converging evidence of disrupted auditory-motor integration and impaired neural communications within dorsal stream networks in aphasia. SIGNIFICANCE: These findings emphasize that clinical interventions for aphasia therapy benefit from targeting sensorimotor mechanisms supporting vocal auditory feedback processing and control. Personalized interventions that strengthen sensorimotor integration pathways could further enhance recovery of fluent verbal communication.

title: A reproducible safety assessment model for concurrent transcranial magnetic stimulation with implanted intracranial electroencephalography electrodes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concurrent transcranial magnetic stimulation and intracranial EEG (TMS-sEEG) offers a powerful approach for interrogating human brain circuits with high spatiotemporal resolution. However, standardized safety testing procedures for TMS in the presence of implanted electrodes are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To establish and validate a reproducible methodological framework for assessing TMS safety with sEEG hardware, addressing potential risks of electrode displacement, heating, and secondary current induction.
METHODS: A conductive agarose phantom implanted with clinical-grade platinum sEEG electrodes was exposed to single-pulse TMS (0.4 Hz), repetitive TMS (1-50 Hz), and intermittent theta burst stimulation. Electrode displacement was quantified via high-speed video and motion tracking. Temperature changes were measured with fiber-optic thermal probes positioned at stimulated electrode contacts. Induced voltages were recorded using an oscilloscope and intracranial EEG hardware, and secondary current and charge density were calculated from oscilloscope outputs and impedance measurements.
RESULTS: sEEG lead displacement remained micrometer-scale across stimulation conditions, with a maximum transient displacement of 10.99 μm and a maximum 1-s mean displacement from the pre-TMS position of 16.27 μm. Temperature changes remained well within the 2°C safety threshold across all tested conditions; in the primary temperature series, the maximum observed increase was 0.073°C. Induced voltages and charge densities remained below established safety limits, exhibiting consistent exponential decay with increasing distance from the coil. All stimulation conditions, including those exceeding typical clinical ranges, remained well within safety margins.
CONCLUSIONS: Under the tested conditions in a controlled phantom environment, TMS exposure produced micrometer-scale transient and longer-timescale displacement, temperature changes within established safety thresholds, and charge densities within established safety thresholds. This validated methodological pipeline provides a standardized framework for future safety experiments involving TMS and implanted devices and supports continued development of TMS-sEEG as a tool for studying human brain circuitry and neuromodulation.

title: Efficacy and safety of litifilimab in cutaneous lupus erythematosus: 24-week results of the randomized phase 2 study, AMETHYST.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) is a serious autoimmune disease with no approved targeted treatments.
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the efficacy and safety of litifilimab in AMETHYST Part A (Phase 2).
METHODS: AMETHYST is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2/3 study that investigates litifilimab in participants with CLE. Participants were randomized to receive litifilimab 225 mg or placebo every 4 weeks during Weeks 0-24. The primary endpoint was the Cutaneous Lupus Activity Investigator's Global Assessment-Revised (CLA-IGA-R) erythema score of 0-1 at Week 16, with several Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index (CLASI)-based endpoints at Week 24 as secondary endpoints. Safety was also assessed.
RESULTS: Significantly more participants treated with litifilimab achieved clear/almost clear skin (CLA-IGA-R erythema 0-1) than those treated with placebo at Week 16 (14.7% vs 2.9%, P= .0263). Additionally, more participants treated with litifilimab achieved CLASI-70 response vs placebo at Week 24 (21.7% vs 5.8%, P = .0195). Litifilimab was generally well tolerated; safety data were consistent with prior studies.
LIMITATIONS: Study was not powered to detect statistically significant differences in secondary endpoints.
CONCLUSION: Litifilimab treatment led to greater improvements in skin disease activity vs placebo and was well tolerated in participants with CLE through Week 24.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Endobronchial Ultrasound
abstract: Abstract Purpose of review The use of bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) to aid in lymph node and lung biopsy is relatively new. This review will summarize the literature surrounding the efficacy of bronchoscopy with EBUS. Safety of bronchoscopy with EBUS is not markedly different that procedure with EBUS and is impacted by patient features including co-morbidities as well as different sedation modalities. This paper reviews the impact on both safety and diagnostic yield. Recent Findings The yield from using EBUS guided biopsy varies with the diagnosis but is high with linear EBUS. Recent data incorporating other technologies (electromagnetic navigation, robotic assistance) with bronchoscopy has potential to increase diagnostic yields, appears to be equivalent to transthoracic needle biopsies performed by radiology. Different sedation modalities are utilized, including the use of dedicated anesthesia providers, for bronchoscopy with EBUS but do not appear to significantly affect the diagnostic yield. Summary Bronchoscopy with EBUS (both linear and radial) is a safe procedure with acceptable yields. The type of sedation does not appear to affect the diagnostic yield or the safety of the procedure. Further research into incorporation of other technologies may provide for higher diagnostic yields.
