title: Transition From CIWA-Ar to a Brief Alcohol Withdrawal Scale-based Protocol in General Medical Inpatients: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The Brief Alcohol Withdrawal Scale (BAWS) is a shorter alternative to the Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol, revised (CIWA-Ar), but the two have not been compared in general medical inpatients. We evaluated a transition from CIWA-Ar to BAWS in this population.
METHODS: Interrupted time series study of adults admitted from the emergency department to internal medicine with alcohol withdrawal syndrome, April 2021-April 2023. In April 2022, CIWA-Ar was replaced by BAWS, bundled with risk stratification and a phenobarbital pathway requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission for intravenous dosing. Primary outcomes (total sedative exposure in lorazepam equivalents, length of stay, inflation-adjusted cost) were analyzed as weekly series with segmented regression; secondary outcomes were ICU transfer, 30-day readmission, in-hospital mortality, and discharge against medical advice.
RESULTS: Of 23,506 encounters, 1341 were eligible. The transition produced no immediate (level) or sustained (slope) change in total sedative exposure (level -2.9 mg, 95% CI: -8.4 to 2.6), length of stay (-0.40 d, 95% CI: -1.5 to 0.69), or cost (0.027, 95% CI: -0.040 to 0.096), and was not associated with ICU transfer (OR 1.61, 95% CI: 0.83-3.19), 30-day readmission (OR 1.16, 0.87-1.54), in-hospital mortality (OR 1.32, 0.32-5.88), or discharge against medical advice (OR 0.90, 0.58-1.37); unadjusted phenobarbital use and ICU transfer increased.
CONCLUSIONS: Replacing CIWA-Ar with BAWS did not change total sedative exposure, length of stay, cost, or clinical outcomes in general medical inpatients. BAWS can be adopted safely, although the ICU requirement for intravenous phenobarbital may have offset potential resource gains.

title: The role of comorbidities in comprehensive healthcare utilization among people with multiple sclerosis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) live with comorbid conditions, which may contribute to more complex healthcare needs. While there have been several studies on their associations with increased hospitalizations and emergency visits, there has been limited investigation into other aspects of care (e.g., imaging) or composite indices have been used rather than individual conditions.
OBJECTIVE: To determine If comorbidities in PwMS are associated with utilization of a wider range of healthcare services and which specific comorbid conditions are linked to those services.
METHODS: Participants (n = 185) were PwMS who completed a series of questionnaires about their comorbidities and healthcare utilization over the prior 12 months as part of a larger study. Regression models were used to evaluate the relationships between healthcare utilization and specific comorbidities, controlling for age, gender, race, education, and annual income.
RESULTS: PwMS with a comorbidity had higher utilization of several services, including more healthcare provider visits (p < 0.001), particularly with primary care (p = .041) and mental health providers (p = .003), unique providers seen (p < 0.001), active medications (p < .001), MRIs (p = .008), X-rays (p = .031), inpatient hospital stays (p = .038), and elective surgeries (p = .035). Several comorbidities, including anxiety, sleep apnea, autoimmune thyroid disease, and irritable bowel syndrome, were most frequently associated with increased service use.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings expand upon the previous literature, demonstrating that comorbidities are associated with greater utilization of a wide range of services and the complex needs of PwMS living with multiple chronic conditions.

title: Quantifying Meaningful Information in Incorrect Naming Responses Following Strategic Word Retrieval Treatment in Primary Progressive Aphasia
abstract: Purpose: Anomia is a core feature of both logopenic variant primary progressive aphasia (lvPPA) and semantic variant primary progressive aphasia (svPPA). Naming interventions targeting self-cueing in persons with lvPPA and svPPA have been shown to promote generalized improvement in word finding. However, studies have typically characterized response to treatment using binary scoring of naming attempts. There is no established method for evaluating how well people with aphasia communicate meaningful lexical and semantic information for items that they are unable to name. The purpose of this study is to evaluate changes in communicative value of Boston Naming Test (BNT) error responses for individuals with lvPPA and svPPA following a strategy-based naming treatment. Method: Using a novel scoring procedure, the meaningful information score (MIS), we quantified the amount of meaningful information shared on incorrectly named or unnamed items from the BNT before and after a strategy-based naming treatment administered to persons with lvPPA ( n = 20) and svPPA ( n = 14). We analyzed change in BNT naming accuracy with a linear mixed-effects model and change in MIS score using a negative binomial mixed-effects model. Individual change was tested with a bootstrapping analysis. Results: At the group level, BNT accuracy did not significantly change from pre- to posttreatment. However, participants showed a significant increase at posttreatment in the amount of meaningful information provided for items not correctly named as measured by the MIS ( p = .002). The majority of individuals showed change in the positive direction on the MIS, with 13 of 34 showing statistically significant improvement. Conclusions: The MIS is a promising tool for capturing gains in functional communication following naming treatment. Findings also indicate that strategy-based naming treatment can increase the meaningful information conveyed during naming attempts, even in the context of progressive language decline. title: Vessel Dependent Myocardium at Risk on Coronary CT Angiography Validated Against Dynamic CT Myocardial Perfusion Imaging.
abstract: Accurate assignment of myocardial territories supplied by individual coronary arteries on coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is essential for estimating myocardium at risk. Validation of coronary-based myocardial segmentation has been limited by co-registration challenges with perfusion imaging as the reference standard. By reconstructing coronary angiograms directly from the dynamic CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI), we ensured inherent co-registration between coronaries and perfusion maps. Vessel-specific myocardial territories were assigned using a minimum cost path (MCP) and validated against MBF-derived perfusion defects from the same acquisition. In 22 patients with 27 well-defined ischemic territories MCP-assigned territories showed moderate spatial overlap with CT-MPI-derived hypoperfusion (Dice coefficient 0.72 ± 0.13) with strong surface area correlation (r = 0.81, p < 0.001). Agreement was highest in the left anterior descending (LAD) territory. MCP-based tessellation using inherently co-registered CCTA and CT-MPI enables accurate vessel-specific myocardium-at-risk assessment and offers a promising platform for anatomical-functional integration in coronary disease.

title: Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ)
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Nociplastic pain is implicated in many chronic pain conditions, yet it has been defined primarily by the absence of structural causes-a diagnosis by exclusion. No validated nociplastic pain questionnaire exists. This study examined hypothesized pain-specific features of nociplastic pain and developed a brief self-report instrument, the Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ). METHODS: We generated items based on literature review and input from experts and individuals with lived experience. We administered the items and measures of other pain-related constructs (pain intensity/interference, catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, and perceived stress) to 888 participants with diverse chronic pain conditions. RESULTS: Factor analyses supported four dimensions captured by internally consistent 4-item subscales (αs ≥0.74): 1) location variability, 2) exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, 3) widespreadness, and 4) allodynia. The NociQ total score adequately discriminated presumed nociplastic and non-nociplastic conditions (AUCs 0.73-0.75). Participants who had widespread pain or reported more presumed nociplastic conditions scored higher on all scales (ps <.001, ds=0.35-1.37). NociQ scales demonstrated small-to-moderate correlations with measures of theoretically distinct constructs (rs=0.10-0.44), supporting discriminant validity, and explained additional variance in pain intensity beyond those measures (ΔR²s=.02-.07; ps <.05), supporting incremental validity. DISCUSSION: Results indicate four nociplastic pain characteristics, including two, location variability and exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, psychometrically validated here for the first time. The 16-item NociQ demonstrates promising reliability and validity as a brief questionnaire of nociplastic pain. Future research should examine its clinical utility, such as in matching patients to pain mechanism-targeted treatments.

title: Validity and Reliability of the Activity Card Sort 3 in Persons With Thumb Carpometacarpal Osteoarthritis.
abstract: ImportanceAlthough individuals with thumb carpometacarpal (CMC1) osteoarthritis (OA) commonly experience participation restrictions, participation-focused outcome measures remain underinvestigated, and clinicians primarily rely on assessments of impairments in body structures and functions.ObjectiveTo determine the concurrent validity, test-retest reliability, and precision of the Activity Card Sort 3 (ACS3) in individuals with nonoperative CMC1 OA.DesignSingle-cohort observational psychometric study with repeated measures over a 2-week interval.SettingRemote assessments conducted via videoconferencing.ParticipantsThirty-three adults with radiographically confirmed CMC1 OA completed two virtual assessments approximately 2 weeks apart.Outcomes and MeasuresConcurrent validity was examined by comparing ACS3 domain and total scores with the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 (WHODAS 2.0). Test-retest reliability of the "current," "previous," and "% retained" activities scores was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC3,1). Precision was assessed using the standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change.ResultsThe ACS3 demonstrated good concurrent validity through strong associations with conceptually related WHODAS 2.0 domains. "Current" and "% retained" scores demonstrated good-to-excellent test-retest reliability across all domains. "Current" scores consistently showed the highest reliability and precision. "Previous" scores demonstrated lower reliability and greater measurement error, suggesting recall bias. Carrying forward "previous" scores from session 1 to session 2 improved the reliability of "% retained" scores.Conclusions and RelevanceThe ACS3 is a valid and reliable measure of participation for individuals with nonoperative CMC1 OA. The "current" and "% retained" scores may support occupational therapy practitioners in conducting participation-focused assessment of persons with CMC1 OA.

title: Bibliometric and network analysis of the dissemination of health systems science in medical education.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Societal concerns regarding the outcomes of the U.S. healthcare system served as an impetus to incorporate a third pillar, health systems science (HSS), into medical education, complementing the basic and clinical sciences. Similar to the creation of the basic sciences as a unified construct, multiple fields were brought together under the HSS framework. The extent of adoption and dissemination of this construct is unknown. This study sought to determine the dissemination, adoption, and connections of HSS through bibliographic and social network analysis.
METHOD: Starting with 5 foundational HSS articles, the authors conducted bibliometric and social network analysis of HSS-related publications using data from Web of Science, excluding books, book chapters, and conference abstracts. Bibliometric performance and science mapping metrics for 269 papers published January 2017-November 2025 were analyzed including publication productivity, citation impact, and author/institution contributions. Social network analysis was used to assess the structure, growth, and interconnectedness of the HSS scholarly network for 235 papers published from 2017-October 2024.
RESULTS: Bibliometric analysis found 100 journals representing over 1087 authors at 296 institutions. The network showed consistent annual growth with increasing interconnectivity and decreasing network density, suggesting diffusion beyond early adopters. Academic Medicine was the most frequent publication outlet (59/269, 22%). Seven of the top 10 contributing institutions were part of the original AMA Accelerating Change in Medical Education Consortium. PageRank and citation analysis revealed high-impact articles were closely linked to early HSS curricular work. Social network metrics demonstrated a maturing scholarly community around HSS.
CONCLUSIONS: This bibliometric analysis starting with 5 foundational articles found dissemination through an expanding network of scholarship, sustained citation of foundational papers, and broad engagement across a diverse group of authors and institutions. As HSS becomes embedded in medical education, future research should explore how its evolution meets emerging health system challenges.

title: Preoperative Patient Communication Method and Its Impact on Postoperative Outcomes and Healthcare Utilization Following Cystectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate if utilization of secure patient portal messaging platform such as MyChart are associated with improved postoperative outcomes following cystectomy and how this compares to telephone utilization.
METHODS: Patients undergoing cystectomy at our institution between 2016-2022 were included. MyChart messages and telephone calls within 1 month preoperatively were collected. Users were defined as patients initiating contact via secure message or telephone call prior to surgery. Postoperative complications, emergency department visits, and readmissions were recorded, and a composite measure of the three was generated. We stratified by MyChart users, phone users, combination users, and non-users. Statistical analysis was performed with t-test, Kruskal-Wallis, chi-squared, and Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: The final population was 244 patients with an average age of 70 years old. There were 40 MyChart users, 84 telephone users, 26 combination users, and 104 non-users. Compared to non-users, telephone users had significantly lower rates of complications (OR 0.39, 95CI 0.19-0.76), readmissions (OR 0.35, 95CI 0.10-0.99), and composite outcome (OR 0.50, 95CI 0.26-0.94). There were no significant differences between MyChart users and non-users.
CONCLUSION: MyChart utilization was not associated with improved postoperative outcomes after cystectomy, while telephone utilization was associated with significantly fewer complications and readmissions. Phone calls may be a more timely and effective way to exchange information perioperatively.

title: Protective Effects of PD-L1-Overexpressing MSCs and Their Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: This study was conducted to address the urgent need for novel therapies for type 1 diabetes. We investigated whether programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-overexpressing mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (PD-L1-MSCs) and their extracellular vesicles (PEVs) can modulate immune responses and protect pancreatic islets, and whether these effects depend on PD-L1 signaling. Our results demonstrate that both PD-L1-MSCs and PEVs suppress T-cell activity, enhance regulatory T-cell populations, delay the onset of diabetes, and reduce immune cell infiltration in pancreatic islets. These findings suggest that PD-L1-MSCs and PEVs represent promising therapeutic strategies for type 1 diabetes by promoting immune tolerance and preserving β-cell function.

title: Unreliability of the Fecal Pancreatic Elastase-1 Test In Predicting a Response to Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The fecal elastase-1 assay is the most frequently used screening test for pancreatic enzyme insufficiency (PEI). It has a sensitivity of 73%, with lower sensitivities for mild and moderate PEI. Reliance on this test has resulted in "ruling out" PEI in patients with undiagnosed chronic gastrointestinal complaints. Some of these patients will respond dramatically to a simple and safe trial of pancreatic enzyme replacement.
METHODS: A list of all fecal elastase-1 tests performed at VA Connecticut during calendar year 2025 was obtained (N=102). The charts of patients with elastase-1 results in the low-normal to mid-normal range (200-800 mcg/gram) were reviewed (N=34). There were 10 patients with ongoing gastrointestinal complaints without a definitive diagnosis despite extensive laboratory, endoscopic, and radiological investigations and empiric trials of fiber, bile acid binding resins, and antibiotics. These patients were contacted and offered an empiric two-week trial of pancreatic enzyme replacement.
RESULTS: Five patients had clinically significant responses to pancreatic enzyme replacement with dramatic improvement in their quality of life. They are now on chronic replacement therapy.
CONCLUSION: Overreliance on the stool elastase-1 test has resulted in missed opportunities to help patients with chronic gastrointestinal complaints.

title: Management of Antiplatelet Regimen During Surgical Procedures: A Report From the MARS Registry.
abstract: Optimal perioperative management of patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial, with substantial variability in current clinical practice. The MARS registry is a prospective multicenter observational study evaluating perioperative outcomes in post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing surgery within 2 years of PCI. We assessed the incidence of Net Adverse Cardiovascular Events (NACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type ≥3 bleeding. A total of 132 consecutive patients undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery were followed from 14 days preoperatively to 30 days postoperatively. Of the 132 patients, 79 underwent noncardiac surgery (NCS) and 53 underwent cardiac surgery (CS). The mean age was 66 years, and 68% were male. Diabetes mellitus was present in 48%, chronic kidney disease in 29%, and 42% had undergone PCI for an acute coronary syndrome. Mean time from PCI to surgery was 269 ± 217 days. Previous bleeding and stent thrombosis were reported in 11% and 5% of patients, respectively. Aspirin was continued in 60% and P2Y12 inhibitors in 36%, with mean discontinuation 4 and 6 days preoperatively, respectively. Intravenous antiplatelet bridging with cangrelor was used in 12 patients (9.1%) and unfractionated heparin as anticoagulant therapy in 15 patients (11%). NACE occurred more frequently after CS compared with NCS (18.9% vs 10.1%, p = 0.17). Major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium ≥3) occurred in 5.3% with no difference between CS and NCS. There were no cardiovascular deaths and no difference in all-cause mortality. Compared with no bridging, cangrelor bridging was associated with numerically higher NACE (25% vs 12.5%, p = 0.22), without differences in bleeding. On multivariable logistic regression, cangrelor bridging was not independently associated with NACE (adjusted odds ratio 2.18, 95% confidence interval 0.43 to 8.71, p = 0.34). In conclusion, among post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery, aspirin was continued in 60%, cangrelor bridging was used in 9.1%, and although NACE rates were numerically higher after CS and with bridging, these differences were not significant after multivariable adjustment, consistent with confounding by indication.

title: Development of a Performance-Based Tool to Assess Geropsychology Competencies.
abstract: Strengthening the workforce providing mental health care to older adults is a national imperative, given the rapidly growing population of older adults in the United States. The Pikes Peak Model and corresponding Knowledge and Skills Assessment Tool represented a critical advancement in geropsychology training. However, the tool relies on self-report, which can be subject to bias, and it is recommended to be supplemented with direct supervisor observations of performance. To our knowledge, no performance-based tool currently exists that assesses geropsychology competencies. The current report addresses this gap through the development of a performance-based geropsychology competency assessment tool (PBGCAT) informed by the Pikes Peak Model and APA specialty/ABGERO competencies. Selection of core competencies for the PBGCAT was guided by a survey of geropsychology trainees and supervisors (n = 61). A patient vignette design was employed, and tool drafts were rigorously reviewed by subject matter experts and a diversity committee. The PBGCAT offers brief administration, versatility, and serial assessment of competency development. Further pilot testing with diverse groups of trainees and supervisors is needed to evaluate its feasibility, inform refinement, and guide broader dissemination to programs providing training in psychological practice with older adults.

title: Implementing the Age-Friendly 4Ms+ Framework in a Vulnerable Population at a Safety-Net Hospital.
abstract: On account of the growing proportion of older adults in the United States, thousands of health systems have implemented the Age-Friendly Health Systems' (AFHS) 4Ms framework - What Matters, Medication, Mentation, Mobility - to optimize older adult care. Safety-net hospitals serve a vulnerable older adult population characterized by adverse social determinants of health and often operate with limited financial resources. The objective of this article is to describe the process of implementing the 4Ms framework, plus two additional Ms - Malnutrition and Mal-Care Transitions - into the inpatient services of a major Southeastern safety-net hospital. The authors outline barriers, challenges, and resources applied during this process. Additionally, they present initial clinical outcomes for an inpatient cohort cared for in the most recent 2 years. An AFHS work group composed of relevant departmental heads, geriatricians, and key staff members was established to champion the design and employment of the 4Ms framework. Subcommittees were formed for each of the four Ms. Each committee developed and applied frameworks, workflows, protocols, tools, and modifications to the electronic health record to implement their respective M. A stepwise approach was developed to spread practices across inpatient units in the hospital through a combination of tests using a Plan-Do-Study-Act approach, while the creation of data dashboards and reporting workbenches permitted longitudinal monitoring of performance and documentation compliance in near real time. The authors describe adherence to the 4Ms over a 2-year period. From March 2024 to March 2026, 4647 inpatient encounters with 3427 patients (mean age of 79.3 years, 58% female, 64% African American, mean Katz functional score of 5.8) occurred on units that implemented the 4Ms framework as a set. Adherence in the AFHS units reached 100% on 5 of 14 care protocols and over 90% on an additional 5. AFHS units performed particularly well with the implementation of What Matters (74%), Mentation (98% delirium screening), and Mobility (96% functional capacity assessments). Adherence with other mobility-related assessments and medication-related practices was also high. This study shows the feasibility of implementing and sustaining the AFHS framework with high adherence to the 4Ms in a large safety-net hospital with a diverse and vulnerable older adult population.

title: Inactivation of the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) in osteoblasts increases post-natal trabecular bone mass and mechanical bone strength.
abstract: The epigenetic methyltransferases Ezh1 or Ezh2 each interact with two structural proteins (Eed and Suz12) to form Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2). Inhibition of Ezh2 stimulates osteoblast differentiation and bone formation, but Ezh2 conditional knockout (cKO) mice have variable skeletal phenotypes. Ezh1 null mice are phenotypically normal. Here, we show that combined homozygous ablation of both Ezh1 and Ezh2 alleles results in a pronounced bone phenotype, suggesting genetic redundancy between Ezh1 and Ezh2. Transient loss of Eed, Suz12 or Ezh2 by siRNA depletion or treatment with distinct PRC2 inhibitors (A395, EED226 and GSK126) enhances differentiation of MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts (i.e., increased Bglap, Ibsp and mineralization). We compared Ezh2 cKO mice with Ezh1 null (KO) mice, and mice with both Ezh2 cKO and Ezh1 KO alleles (dKO mice) in the presence of the Osterix/Sp7-Cre recombination driver. During active bone development (post-natal 8 weeks), both male and female dKO mice exhibit significantly increased L5 trabecular bone mass, femoral cortical thickness and the relative midshaft bone volume (μCT), as well as bone strength (3-point bending) compared to Ezh1 KO or Ezh2 cKO mice. Suppression of Cre recombination using doxycycline (DOX) for 8 weeks prevents the dKO phenotype, but subsequent DOX removal increases trabecular bone mass in dKO mice by 14 weeks. Conditional Eed ablation (which inactivates PRC2/Ezh1 and PRC2/Ezh2) results in a similar high- bone and increased mechanical strength phenotype in male and female Eed cKO. Our findings identify PRC2 as a suppressor of post-natal bone accrual in Osx/Sp7 lineage cells, and a potential target for strategies to improve bone mass accrual.

title: Mechanistic insights into age- and vascular-related microstructure differences in the corpus callosum using biophysical modeling of diffusion MRI.
abstract: Corpus callosum microstructure is a proposed risk biomarker for vascular contributions to cognitive impairment. This study compared corpus callosum microstructure measures from the "Standard Model" biophysical diffusion model with diffusion tensor and kurtosis imaging (DTI, DKI) measures for differences related to age and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) in a population-based sample of cognitively unimpaired older adults (n = 112, mean age 69.9). Standard Model measures included axonal water fraction (f) and intra-axonal diffusivity (Da), proposed as markers related to axonal density and integrity, respectively, and extra-axonal parallel (De∥)_and perpendicular diffusivities(De⟂), proposed as markers sensitive to neuroinflammation and demyelination, respectively. These were compared with DTI and DKI measures regarding their association with age or white matter hyperintensity (WMH) volume on T2w MRI, a proxy for cSVD burden. Of Standard Model measures, De⟂ and Da were associated with age, and De⟂ of genu and body was associated with both WMH volume and age, suggesting that demyelination may be an important mechanism in age and cSVD-related microstructural differences in the corpus callosum. Sensitivity to age and WMH volume was overall similar to DTI and DKI measures. Mediation analyses showed that De⟂ mediated the relationship between mean and axial kurtosis in the genu and body, respectively, when evaluating associations with WMH volume, suggesting that demyelination is a potential important mechanism underlying microstructural differences quantified by kurtosis in cSVD. Overall, the Standard Model-derived measures provides compartment-specific biophysical insight into aging and cSVD, with high sensitivity comparable to conventional DTI and DKI.

title: Collapse and Thrombosis of an Iliac Branch Endovascular Device Following Blunt Force Trauma
abstract: Iliac branch endovascular device thrombosis following blunt force trauma has rarely been reported. We describe an 81-year-old man who developed proximal aortobiiliac endograft collapse with subsequent thrombosis after blunt force trauma occurring two months following endovascular aneurysm repair. The patient delayed vascular follow-up for one year and later presented at routine surveillance with progressive bilateral hip and buttock claudication. Despite chronic therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, the patient developed progressive thrombosis with ischemic symptoms. The case highlights a rare mechanical cause of post-EVAR aortoiliac thrombosis and demonstrates the importance of early vascular imaging and consultation following traumatic injury in post-EVAR patients.

title: Demystifying credentialing and privileging for clinical nurse specialists
abstract: ABSTRACT: A clinical nurse specialist (CNS) is an advanced practice registered nurse who holds a graduate degree and specializes in managing specific patient populations or disease types, bringing advanced clinical expertise to diagnose, treat, and oversee care for individuals and improve population health conditions. CNSs serve as clinical leaders, educators, and practitioners of evidence-based care, driving improvements in patient outcomes and instigating transformational organizational change within health care systems. Their scope of practice is broad, encompassing assessment, care coordination, consultation, and, where permitted, prescribing and procedural privileges, all founded upon rigorous academic and clinical standards. The process of credentialing ensures that CNSs meet established educational, training, licensure, and competency criteria before providing care, while privileging authorizes them to perform specialized clinical activities within health care facilities. Unfortunately, CNSs often face regulatory and institutional barriers, such as misclassification, restrictive state laws, and inconsistent privileging criteria, which undermine their ability to fully utilize their advanced skills and impede the recognition of their contributions. Such obstacles can limit professional growth and restrict independent practice and reimbursement opportunities. This article discusses credentialing, privileging, mapping, patient encounters, and workload for CNSs, who are often overlooked and underutilized in advanced practice conversations despite providing safe, high-quality, and cost-effective care for specialty populations.

title: Glycosaminoglycans differentially modulate meniscus pericellular matrix micromechanics and mechanosensing.
abstract: In the meniscus, cells reside within a specialized pericellular matrix (PCM) microniche that exhibits distinct molecular and structural features compared to the surrounding fibrous extracellular matrix (ECM). The PCM is enriched in negatively charged sulfated glycosaminoglycans (sGAGs), primarily contributed by localized proteoglycans such as aggrecan. Using the murine meniscus as the model, this study delineates the specific contributions of sGAGs to the elastic and viscoelastic micromechanics of the PCM and explores their influence on resident cell mechanosensing. Enzymatic removal of sGAGs markedly decreases the PCM micromodulus and alters its viscoelastic properties, including faster relaxation time constants. Finite element modeling suggests that the localized fixed charges and mechanical buffering provided by sGAGs in the PCM serve as a protective mechanism for resident cells under tensile loading, the predominant loading mode of the meniscus outer zone in vivo. Nevertheless, despite these pronounced contributions to PCM micromechanics, sGAG depletion induces only a modest increase in intracellular calcium signaling ex vivo under hypertonic, but not isotonic or hypotonic, conditions. Collectively, these findings establish sGAGs as critical regulators of fibrocartilage PCM integrity and highlight their differential roles in local PCM micromechanics versus cell mechanosensing.

title: Implementation of the Universal Femoral Access Protocol Decreases Complications of Peripheral Vascular Interventions.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Common femoral artery (CFA) is the most common access site for peripheral vascular interventions (PVI). Ultrasound (US) use has been shown to decrease access-related complications. However, the recommended site for femoral artery puncture has not been well defined, and the access technique varies significantly based on the operator specialty and training. This study describes the development of a multidisciplinary universal femoral access (UFA) protocol and its implementation at a tertiary care centre.
METHODS: Femoral artery access zones in relation to the femoral head were described based on prior cadaveric groin dissection study. The UFA was developed with an emphasis on dual image guidance using US and fluoroscopy for optimal access. A technical video was created and shared with the specialists and trainees performing PVI, and via online platforms. A single center retrospective review of pre-UFA patients from September 2020 to November 2020 and post-UFA patients from September 2022 to November 2022 was conducted. The institutional Vascular Quality Initiative database was used to compare patient characteristics and access complications before the development of the UFA (pre-UFA) and after its implementation (post-UFA). All fluoroscopic images of the procedures were retrospectively reviewed to assess the needle location and use of dual imaging guidance during PVI.
RESULTS: A total of 375 procedures were analysed with 63.2% in the pre-UFA group (n=237). After the implementation of the UFA, the rate of overall access complications significantly decreased from 12.7% pre-UFA vs 5.1% post-UFA, p=0.019. There was a statistically significant decrease in thrombotic complications (3.7% pre-UFA vs 0% post-UFA, p=0.029), with a trend towards a decrease in the bleeding rates without reaching a statistical significance (9.3% pre-UFA vs 5.1% post-UFA, p=0.154). A significant increase in the use of dual image guidance was observed in the post-UFA group (27.4% pre-UFA vs 55.8% post-UFA, p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: The UFA protocol emphasizing use of dual image guidance and a comprehensive understanding of femoral anatomy can reduce access site complications during PVI. Expansion of the UFA to other procedures using femoral artery access and to other institutions can improve patient care.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: CFA access can lead to limb or life-threatening complications. Understanding of the femoral anatomy, and optimization of access technique with dual imaging can reduce complications. This study highlights the importance of establishing a standardized femoral access protocol to improve patient outcomes.

title: Self-Report of Cannabis Dispensaries in Neighborhoods and Tobacco and Cannabis Co-Use among US Adults.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: With cannabis legalization, the number of cannabis dispensaries and rates of tobacco and cannabis co-use (past 30-day use of both substances) have increased. However, the impact of living near a dispensary on tobacco and cannabis co-use remains understudied. Examining factors associated with co-use is important for public health, as co-use may pose increased health risks compared to single product use.
METHODS: We conducted a web-based survey in English and Spanish in November 2023 using Ipsos KnowledgePanel, a probability-based panel designed to be representative of the U.S. population. We restricted our survey to those over 18 years old who reported past 30-day use of cigarettes or e-cigarettes and lived in states with medical or non-medical legal cannabis (n=1929). We used weighted, multivariable logistic regression models to estimate the adjusted association of self-reported awareness of a cannabis dispensary in the neighborhood and tobacco/cannabis co-use.
RESULTS: Awareness of vs. no awareness of a cannabis dispensary in the neighborhood was associated with increased odds of tobacco/cannabis co-use (OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.33-2.44). This association of dispensary awareness and co-use was found for smoking (p<.001), vaping (p<.001), and edible forms of cannabis (p=.003), but not cannabis concentrates (p=.11).
CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported awareness of a cannabis dispensary in the neighborhood was associated with nearly twice the odds of co-use of tobacco and cannabis, independent of sociodemographic factors. As more states legalize cannabis, laws and public policies need to take into account the locations of dispensaries and their impact on community health.

title: Laparoscopic and Robotic Device Malfunction: A Scoping Review
abstract: Laparoscopic and robotic surgeries have become the gold standard for many operations. Device malfunctions during these procedures represent a preventable source of patient harm; however, the trends in malfunction reporting and their implications for surveillance systems, surgical training, and reporting infrastructure have not been comprehensively reviewed. Our aim is to conduct a scoping review of device malfunctions during minimally invasive abdominopelvic surgeries. Four databases (Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, and PubMed) were searched for relevant articles published between January 1, 1974, and March, 15, 2024. Studies analyzing the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database for device malfunctions involving staplers or energy-based devices in laparoscopic and robotic abdominopelvic surgeries were included. Reviews, case series, animal studies, and investigations of user error or implanted device failures were excluded. Two independent reviewers screened each article. Of 770 identified articles, 15 met the inclusion criteria. Nine focused on robotic surgical instruments (7 on the da Vinci Surgical System), 5 on laparoscopic staplers (4 nephrectomy-related), and 1 on staplers across specialties. Death was the least common outcome, followed by injuries and malfunctions without patient harm. In laparoscopic nephrectomy, stapler misfiring caused 22 deaths (5.7% of complications). Robotic surgery deaths ranged from 1.2% to 2.3%, depending on the study. This first comprehensive synthesis of MAUDE-based analyses in minimally invasive surgery reveals substantial variability in reporting practices and highlights system-level gaps in surveillance, staff training, and accountability. Standardized, multicenter reporting frameworks are needed to accurately characterize the risk of malfunction and support targeted preventive interventions.

title: The Burden of Psychiatric Illness Scale (BPIS): A Preliminary Validation of a Measure of the Self-reported Impact of Psychiatric Illness on Psychosocial Functioning and Stress Related to Managing Psychiatric Illness.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Little is known about stress related to managing a psychiatric illness, especially for racial and ethnic minority adults. This preliminary study examined the construct and concurrent validity of the Burden of Psychiatric Illness Scale (BPIS) which measures the self-perceived impact of psychiatric symptoms on functioning and stress associated with managing psychiatric illness.
METHODS: Adults receiving outpatient mental health treatment completed measures including the BPIS, sociodemographics, and surveys measuring financial, relationship, and work stress. Principal component analyses were conducted on the BPIS and the revised BPIS (BPIS-r) to identify the core components of the scale and their relationship, and Pearson-r correlations between the BPIS-r and thematically similar and empirically linked constructs were calculated to establish concurrent validity.
RESULTS: In a sample of 95 majority Latinx and Black adults with psychiatric diagnoses, the BPIS demonstrated partial construct validity. This partial construct validity of the BPIS led to a revised BPIS-r scale, in which the Interference with Functioning subscale was trimmed to only include its three relationship items. The BPIS-r demonstrated good construct validity and partial convergent validity. Cronbach's alpha was acceptable for the BPIS-r (α = 0.74) and questionable for the revised Psychiatric Interference with Functioning subscale (α = 0.63).
CONCLUSIONS: Identifying areas of functioning impacted by psychiatric symptoms may help inform areas of focus for treatment. Given that this initial BPIS-r validation study occurred in a sample of Latinx and Black individuals, the BPIS-r may be used to help reduce psychiatric illness burden among these groups. Research is needed in larger, more heterogenous samples.

title: Clinical Use of Tissue Systems Pathology-9 Test for Risk Stratification in Barrett’s Esophagus: A Multidisciplinary Expert Consensus
abstract: Background: Endoscopic surveillance of Barrett’s esophagus (BE) aims to detect dysplasia early, but the risk of neoplastic progression in BE is highly variable. Histology, the current gold standard for risk stratification, has limitations that may contribute to the modest impact of surveillance on esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) mortality. The Tissue Systems Pathology-9 (TSP-9) test provides personalized prognostic data on progression to high grade dysplasia (HGD) or EAC within 5 years and may improve risk stratification. Methods: The American Foregut Society convened a panel of 10 gastroenterologists and 4 foregut surgeons with BE expertise. The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method was used to evaluate the role of TSP-9 across clinical scenarios and BE phenotypes (nondysplastic [NDBE], indefinite for dysplasia [IND], and low-grade dysplasia [LGD]). A literature review informed the scientific basis, rationale and clinical integration of TSP-9. Results: Consensus was reached on 15 statements; 5 did not reach agreement. The panel supported TSP-9 for risk assessment in NDBE, IND, and LGD independent of histology. In NDBE/IND, low-risk scores support guideline-based surveillance. Intermediate risk scores warrant consideration of closer surveillance or endoscopic eradication therapy (EET), while high-risk scores favor closer surveillance or EET. For LGD EET was supported for intermediate or high-risk scores, but no consensus was reached for low-risk scores. TSP-9 was considered useful for identifying prevalent dysplasia and high-risk patients for early intervention. Uncertainty remained regarding performance in erosive esophagitis and relative to expert pathology in IND/LGD. Conclusions: These consensus-based recommendations support the use of TSP-9 to enhance BE risk stratification and guide management.

title: Code Surgical Emergency Team (SET) is the "Missing Code:" An Emerging Perioperative Hemorrhage Best Practice.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Managing the heightened risks of hemorrhage and hematoma vital organ compression due to surgical complications is a challenge for health care systems pursuing the ultimate goal of Zero Harm. Although a certain number of surgical complications are expected, the catastrophic outcomes that ensue are often preventable. This paper aims to contribute to the understanding of processes to address perioperative hemorrhage morbidity and mortality.
METHODS: The authors first identified a broad opportunity to optimize surgical safety in the Veterans Health Administration through perioperative hemorrhage Root Cause Analysis studies from 2022 to 2023. In 2023, we verified and defined risk pain points through task analysis and identified and optimized a solution through iterative rounds of simulation from 2023 to 2024.
RESULTS: Code Surgical Emergency Team (Code SET), a hospital-wide activation of existing personnel, resources, and services to implement emergency clauses in perioperative safety protocols, was designed to address gaps in quality and safety through 7 process steps: (1) activation; (2) code announcement; (3) kit mobilization; (4) activation of emergency clauses; (5) anesthetic and surgical care; (6) poststability pause; and (7) debrief and review.
CONCLUSION: In this paper, we describe the implementation of a comprehensive surgical safety package to reduce perioperative morbidity and mortality. Preliminary pilot findings suggest that the Code SET process may reduce surgical patient morbidity and mortality and improve outcomes. This process demonstrates how institutions can use existing resources in a standardized approach to improving patient safety.

title: Noun vs. Verb processing in aphasia: new data from matched comprehension and production tasks
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Existing studies in aphasia show conflicting results regarding the presence and the nature of differences between nouns and verbs across comprehension and production modalities. While studies generally report greater difficulty with verb production, the results are more mixed for comprehension tasks. In this study, for the first time, we directly compare noun and verb processing using fully balanced, parallel tasks for both comprehension and production in a large sample of Russian-speaking individuals with aphasia. METHOD: We analyzed data from 156 individuals with post-stroke aphasia. Participants completed four tasks from the detailed language assessment tool in Russian (Russian Aphasia Test): noun comprehension, verb comprehension, object naming, and action naming. Tasks were carefully matched for key psycholinguistic variables, allowing for direct comparison of performance. RESULTS: Participants performed significantly better on comprehension tasks than on production tasks. Crucially, across both modalities, nouns had higher accuracy than verbs. Error analysis revealed differing patterns: semantic paraphasias were more common in action naming, while phonological paraphasias predominated in object naming. CONCLUSIONS: The results indicate that word production is more impaired than comprehension in individuals with aphasia, reflecting the greater demands of lexical retrieval relative to semantic recognition. Verbs were consistently more difficult than nouns across modalities, supporting a modality-general noun-verb dissociation. The greater difficulty associated with verbs likely stems from their increased grammatical and semantic complexity, as also evidenced by the higher rate of semantic errors in verb production. In all, these findings have significant implications for models of lexical processing and clinical assessments.

title: Percussion Pacing as a Rescue for Peri-Stimulus Asystole During Electroconvulsive Therapy
abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) can provoke a brief parasympathetic surge, commonly causing transient sinus bradycardia or a short sinus pause. Most events last only seconds and resolve without intervention. Rarely, however, bradyarrhythmia or asystole may persist long enough to threaten cerebral perfusion, requiring anesthesia teams to respond immediately. We report the case of a male patient with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder who underwent bilateral ECT under methohexital and succinylcholine. Baseline sinus bradycardia was present at 47 beats per minute. Immediately after the ECT stimulus, the monitor demonstrated high-grade atrioventricular block that progressed to ventricular asystole with a flat plethysmographic waveform. Within 10 to 15 seconds, while glycopyrrolate and epinephrine were being prepared, percussion pacing was delivered using the ulnar aspect of a closed fist over the left lower sternal edge at ∼ the fourth-to-fifth intercostal space. Each blow produced a QRS complex on electrocardiography and a pulsatile deflection on the plethysmogram. An organized intrinsic rhythm returned after 3 impulses. The patient recovered uneventfully, and subsequent ECT sessions were preceded by prophylactic intravenous glycopyrrolate without recurrence. This case describes percussion pacing as an immediately deployable, equipment-free bridge within the cardiovascular rescue strategy for ECT services, with a low threshold to escalate to chest compressions and advanced cardiac life support.

title: Moving On is Hard to Do: Barriers and Facilitators to Graduation from Intensive Community Mental Health Recovery Programming.
abstract: Intensive Community Mental Health Recovery (ICMHR) Services provide interdisciplinary mental health care in the community for veterans with serious mental illness. While initially recommended as time-unlimited, studies have shown that transition from such services to a lower level of care, termed "graduation," can occur safely and with sustained improvement. This study aimed to understand the perceived barriers and facilitators to the transition process from ICMHR services to lower levels of care. Semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted with 15 ICMHR team members across the VA Connecticut Healthcare System. Data was analyzed using a rapid content and matrix analysis approach to generate consensus codes and themes. This study identified individual, programmatic, and systemic factors that influence veteran transition from ICMHR services to a lower level of care. Perceived barriers included: programmatic requirements, lack of comprehensive outpatient services, perception of ICMHR programs as time-unlimited, and clinician concerns around balancing caseload acuity. Perceived facilitators included: standardized tools for graduation readiness evaluation, positive team member attitudes towards graduation, early discussion of graduation, and team member advocacy for veteran graduation. Two factors were identified as both barriers and facilitators to graduation: strong team member-veteran relationship and balancing availability and quality of care. Despite acknowledgement of barriers, ICMHR team members expressed belief in and hope for veteran graduation with sustained improvement in function and quality of life. This study informs future research and quality improvement efforts aimed at facilitating individualized and recovery-oriented mental health care for individuals transitioning from intensive community-based to lower levels of care.

title: B cells regulate T cell transfer colitis by partially reconstituting luminal IgA and modulating the colonic microbiota.
abstract: Loss of immune tolerance to commensal microbial antigens is a central driver of inflammatory bowel disease. While regulatory T cells are well recognized in maintaining intestinal homeostasis, the contribution of B cells-particularly IgA-secreting cells-remains incompletely defined. In the T cell transfer colitis model, cotransfer of splenic B cells attenuates disease, an effect largely attributed to IL-10-producing regulatory B cells (Bregs). However, alternative B cell-dependent mechanisms have not been fully explored. Here, we investigated whether splenic B cells regulate T cell transfer colitis through IgA-dependent mechanisms independent of Breg-associated cytokines. We show that splenic B cells from wild-type C57BL/6 (B6) mice reconstitute bone marrow and peripheral B cell compartments in RAG1⁻/⁻ recipients, undergo class switching, migrate to the colonic lamina propria as sIgA⁺ B lineage cells, and partially restore luminal secretory IgA. B cell cotransfer significantly attenuated clinical and histological colitis without increased expression of canonical Breg-associated cytokines, including interleukin-10, transforming growth factor β, and interleukin-35 subunits. In contrast, splenic B cells from IgA-deficient mice failed to attenuate colitis despite comparable peripheral B cell reconstitution. Restoration of secretory IgA was associated with increased bacterial IgA coating, reduced fecal bacterial burden, and remodeling of the colonic microbiota, including enrichment of beneficial commensal taxa. Importantly, because IgA-deficient B cells failed to attenuate colitis despite comparable peripheral B cell reconstitution, these findings support an important role for IgA in mediating the protective effect of B cell transfer. Collectively, these findings identify IgA-mediated modulation of the microbiota as an alternate mechanism by which B cells attenuate T cell transfer colitis, highlighting a Breg-independent regulatory pathway with potential relevance to inflammatory bowel disease pathogenesis.

title: Kidney Tubule Aging Across Adulthood.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aging is associated with declining kidney health as defined by lower eGFR and higher albuminuria. Age-related changes in kidney tubule health have not been well studied.
METHODS: We analyzed a subset of participants from 2 cohorts, the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Year 20 (n=939) and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Exam 1 (n=1,014); 780 and 668, respectively, who completed 10-year follow-up. Seven urine biomarkers were measured reflecting tubular synthetic function (EGF and UMOD), tubule reabsorption function (α1m), proximal tubular injury (IL-18 and KIM-1), and interstitial fibrosis/repair (MCP-1 and YKL-40), and were compared with albuminuria and eGFR. In pooled data, cross-sectional analyses evaluated age associations across the range of 37-84 years, and longitudinal analyses were performed to quantify changes over 10-years of follow-up.
RESULTS: Age ranges were 37-55 and 45-84 years for CARDIA and MESA at baseline, respectively; mean eGFR was 96±15 and 78±16 ml/min/1.73m2, and median urine albumin-to-creatinine ratios (UACR) were 4.5 [IQR: 3.3, 1.2] and 5.2 [3.3, 11] mg/g. In multivariable cross-sectional analyses, older age (per decade) was associated with higher urine α1m/UCr (23%, 95% CI: 17, 28%), IL-18/UCr (5%: 0.4, 9%), KIM-1/UCr (16%:12, 20%), MCP-1/UCr (20%: 16, 23%), YKL-40/UCr (12%: 5, 20%), UACR (30%: 23, 38%), and lower urine EGF/UCr (-13%: -15, -11%) and eGFR (-9%; -10, -8%). Age at baseline was not significantly associated with urine UMOD/UCr. In longitudinal analyses over 10-years of follow up, EGF/UCr (-20%: 95% CI: -22, -19%) and UMOD/UCr (-22%: -25, -18%) decreased and α1m/UCr (30%: 24, 35%), MCP-1/UCr (9%: 6, 13%), and YKL-40/UCr (29%: 20, 39%) increased; additionally, albuminuria increased by 29% (23, 36%) and eGFR decreased by 10% (9, 10.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: In community-based adults aged 37-84 years, aging was associated with worsening tubular function and injury.

title: Debating targets for systolic blood pressure lowering in CKD.
abstract: For several decades, there was no clinical-trial evidence to demonstrate that intensive blood pressure (BP)-lowering is a therapeutic strategy that prolongs survival and reduces the cardiorenal risk of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). In 2015, the landscape changed after the publication of the SPRINT (Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial). Compared with a standard (<140 mmHg) systolic BP (SBP), an impressive cardiovascular and survival benefit was observed with an intensive (<120 mmHg) SBP target in non-diabetic patients with hypertension and high cardiovascular risk provoking premature termination of SPRINT. In 2017, a prespecified subgroup analysis of SPRINT showed that the benefit of intensive BP-lowering was similar in patients with or without CKD. As expected, this landmark trial has substantially influenced the BP target recommendations from the guidelines released thereafter. In 2021, the KDIGO guideline made a breakthrough with the adoption of the intensive SBP target of SPRINT for the management of hypertension in CKD. However, other major medical panels, like ESC, ERA, NICE, ACC and AHA have been reluctant to follow the same approach and the optimal BP goal in CKD continues to be debated. In this article, we provide evidence defending and opposing the position that the SBP target in CKD should be <120 mmHg. We conclude with a consensus and suggestions for the successful implementation of this intensive SBP target in daily clinical practice.

title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG
abstract: PURPOSE: Continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) is the gold standard for detecting electrographic seizures in the intensive care unit (ICU), but limited resources limit prolonged monitoring for all patients. We developed an automated, interpretable pipeline that uses a single hour of cEEG to estimate near-term seizure risk across multiple prediction windows. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 50 adults who underwent ICU cEEG monitoring at a single tertiary center. From a 1-hour segment, we computed automated interictal-ictal continuum (IIC) burden probabilities for lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs), generalized periodic discharges (GPDs), and lateralized rhythmic delta activity (LRDA), along with quantitative background EEG features reflecting signal organization and hemispheric asymmetry. Segments were labeled by seizure occurrence within the subsequent 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, or 24 hours. Support vector machine (SVM) and bagged-tree classifiers were trained using clinical-only, background-only, and combined feature sets with a 70/30 patient-level train-test split and cross-validation within the training set. RESULTS: For the 4-hour horizon, the combined-feature SVM achieved 76% accuracy and the lowest Brier score (0.25), outperforming clinical-only (72%) and background-only (70%) models. Across horizons, SVM accuracy declined from 94% (1 hour) to 79% (24 hours) with increasing Brier scores, indicating reduced calibration at longer intervals. AUC-receiver operating characteristic increased with wider prediction windows, consistent with higher seizure prevalence at longer lead times. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating automated IIC probabilities with quantitative background EEG features enables moderate, interpretable near-term seizure prediction from a single hour of ICU cEEG. Initial external validation on an independent multicenter ICU cohort supports generalizability, although broader prospective and multicenter evaluation are needed before clinical deployment.

title: Association Between Interhospital Transfer, Readmission, and Inpatient Mortality Among Older Adults.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interhospital transfer (IHT) is a key strategy for providing access to specialty care; however, it is associated with multiple adverse outcomes, including prolonged length of stay, increased risk of inpatient mortality, and reduced rates of discharge home, particularly among older adults. We hypothesized that older patients who experience IHT would have a higher rate of acute-care hospital readmissions compared to older adults who do not experience IHT.
METHODS: We used the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project's 2019 National Readmissions Database to identify adults 65+ who had and had not undergone IHT. We used unadjusted and adjusted logistic regression stratified by region, clustered by hospital and weighted by individual to measure the association between IHT and the odds of readmission and in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Of the 11,836,556 older adults included in the weighted analysis, 0.9% experienced IHT. After adjusting for confounders including mortality risk, risk of readmission, admitting service, insurer, procedure characteristics, and others, IHT was associated with increased readmission rates (AOR 1.09, 95% CI: 1.01-1.18) and with increased risk of in-hospital mortality (AOR 1.91, 95% CI: 1.81-2.02). In a sensitivity analysis, odds of readmission within 30 days were 29% higher for older adults who had undergone IHT compared to those who had not (AOR 1.29, 95% CI: 1.19-1.40). All comparisons are p < 0.001.
CONCLUSION: IHT is associated with increased readmission and mortality risk among older adults. These findings add to a burgeoning evidence base suggesting that IHT is associated with many long-term risks to older adults. Further research is needed to characterize the underlying drivers of these findings and to develop evidence-based practices to improve IHT processes for older adults.

title: New CRS control tests: development and validation by EUFOREA.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Measuring control in Chronic Rhinosinusitis (CRS) is important in clinical evaluation. We developed and validated 2 new tests for the evaluation of control in CRS, the 6-item CRS Control Test (CCT) and the 14-item CRS Patient Control Test (CPCT) and investigated their correlations with existing tools.
METHODS: An international survey was conducted in 1,102 CRS patients in 19 centres in 7 countries using a questionnaire including the newly developed CCT and CPCT, VAS scores for CRS severity and control, the EPOS control test (EPOSCT), the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test 22 (SNOT-22) and the Patient Global Assessment Tool (PGAT). We evaluated convergent and discriminative validity, internal consistency and cross-cultural validity. Furthermore, we performed an Item Response Theory (IRT) analysis and determined cut-off points for CCT and CPCT. Sub-analyses were performed for CRS patients with and without nasal polyps.
RESULTS: Both CCT (0-24) and CPCT (0-56) demonstrated a high correlation with SNOT-22 and the PGAT. Moderate correlations were observed for all other comparisons. Both tests showed good internal consistency, discriminative validity and cross-cultural validity. We propose for CCT ≤15 to indicate uncontrolled, 16-19 partially controlled, and ≥20 well controlled disease. For the CPCT we propose ≥22 for uncontrolled, 13-21 for partially controlled and ≤12 for well controlled disease.
CONCLUSION: The brief CCT and the longer CPCT are new CRS control tests that show moderate to high correlations with existing tools. Both instruments demonstrated good psychometric properties and therefore can be recommended for use in clinical practice and research.

title: Genotype-Guided Dosing Improves Attainment of Therapeutic Troughs in CYP3A5 Normal Metabolizers After Kidney Transplantation
abstract: PURPOSE: CYP3A5 expressors experience delayed therapeutic tacrolimus concentrations after kidney transplantation, thus, requiring higher tacrolimus doses. Although genotype-guided dosing has demonstrated benefit with immediate-release tacrolimus, data evaluating tacrolimus extended-release (XR) formulations is limited. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included adult kidney transplant recipients with CYP3A5 normal or intermediate metabolizer phenotypes initiated on tacrolimus XR between November 2020 and August 2025. Patients received either conventional fixed-dose tacrolimus XR 4 mg daily or genotype-guided dosing (8 mg daily for normal metabolizers and 6 mg daily for intermediate metabolizers). The primary outcome was time to therapeutic tacrolimus trough concentration (≥8 ng/mL). Secondary outcomes included total dose adjustments, rate of supratherapeutic troughs, intrapatient variability, rejection rate, and renal function. RESULTS: Eighty-one patients met inclusion criteria, including 43 patients in the conventional dosing group and 38 patients in the genotype-guided group. Genotype-guided dosing significantly improved time to therapeutic troughs ≥8 in the normal metabolizers (median 13 vs 25 days; P=0.007), but not in the overall cohort. Both normal and intermediate metabolizers in the genotype-guided group demonstrated significantly higher tacrolimus trough concentrations that were closer to the therapeutic target on post-operative day 3. Genotype-guided dosing was not associated with an increased incidence of supratherapeutic tacrolimus concentrations or adverse clinical outcomes. CONCLUSION: Genotype-guided tacrolimus XR dosing improved early tacrolimus concentrations and significantly shortened time to therapeutic trough attainment among CYP3A5 normal metabolizers. These findings support the use of pre-transplant CYP3A5 genotyping to optimize tacrolimus XR dosing in normal metabolizers.

title: Neutrophil Elastase Regulates CFTR Function in Airway Disease.
abstract: The airways of chronic neutrophilic lung disorders, such as chronic obstructive lung disease (COPD), cystic fibrosis (CF), and non-CF bronchiectasis (NCFBE) are characterized by unrelenting inflammation and alterations in mucociliary transport, leading to chronic bronchitis, recurrent infections, and bronchiectasis. Neutrophil elastase (NE) has classically been associated with lung parenchymal remodeling in airways disease such as COPD, CF and NCFBE, but its contribution to the airway phenotype is less understood. Here, we identify NE as a modulator of decreased cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) function in airway epithelia through protease activated receptor-2 (PAR-2) activation. Decreased CFTR activity is recapitulated in vivo, with reduced nasal potential difference (NPD) in mice exposed to NE. Primary human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells demonstrate a decrease in CFTR function and reduction in airway surface liquid (ASL) depth after NE administration, which affects mucociliary transport. Samples from patients with COPD decrease CFTR function on HBE cells and this effect is partially ameliorated by direct NE inhibition. This important signaling pathway modulates an acquired loss of CFTR function, highlighting new therapeutic targets for addressing the underlying mucociliary defects in chronic airway diseases.

title: Comparison of DXA- and CT-based measurements of abdominal visceral adipose tissue in premenopausal women.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and computed tomography (CT) for estimating visceral adipose tissue (VAT) area in premenopausal women, and to evaluate whether DXA can track VAT changes over time.
METHODS: VAT area (cm²) was measured using DXA and CT on the same day in 66 premenopausal women before (baseline) and after a 20-week prospective intervention trial; the current study is a secondary analysis of these data. Correlation, Bland-Altman, and regression analyses were performed. A regression-based adjustment equation was developed to align DXA with CT values and applied to baseline and follow-up data, with robustness assessed using bootstrap resampling. Analyses were stratified by body mass index (BMI: normal, overweight, obese).
RESULTS: At baseline, DXA significantly overestimated VAT compared with CT (DXA: 98.7 ± 49.5 cm² vs CT: 67.7 ± 33.1 cm²; mean difference +31.0 ± 7.3 cm², p ≤ 0.001), though measures were strongly correlated (r² = 0.87, p ≤ 0.001). Overestimation increased with higher BMI. However, DXA and CT measures of VAT change over 20 weeks were not correlated (r² = 0.00, p = 0.834). A regression-based adjustment equation reduced baseline bias (+31.0 cm² to +4.0 ± 5.8 cm² difference) but did not improve agreement for longitudinal changes.
CONCLUSIONS: DXA provides a correlated but biased estimate of VAT area at a single time point compared with CT, with greater overestimation at higher BMI. A regression-based adjustment equation improves baseline agreement but does not enhance the detection of VAT change over time. DXA should be used cautiously for monitoring longitudinal VAT changes in women.

title: The Feasibility of Using Virtual Reality With Debriefing as a Treatment Modality for Chronic Pain.
abstract: ImportanceChronic pain is a leading cause of disability. Traditional rehabilitation approaches may not produce meaningful functional improvement, necessitating innovative approaches.ObjectiveTo assess the feasibility and acceptability of integrating fully immersive virtual reality (FIVR) and debriefing into occupational therapy (OT) for chronic pain management. We hypothesized that FIVR plus debriefing (IVRSOT) would improve pain, fear of movement, and confidence compared to standard OT (SOT).DesignIn this mixed methods feasibility study, participants were randomized to SOT or IVRSOT. Data were analyzed using nonparametric statistics and content analysis.SettingOutpatient interdisciplinary pain clinic using a biopsychosocial model.ParticipantsAdults with chronic pain, with 31 enrolled and 16 having data suitable for analysis.Outcomes and MeasuresPain intensity, pain interference, kinesiophobia, self-efficacy, and social functioning were assessed using validated tools.ResultsIVRSOT participants showed significant improvement in pain self-efficacy, fatigue, and pain interference, accompanied by a decline in physical function; between group comparisons for physical function and social role participation favored SOT. Qualitative data revealed enhanced engagement, insight, and functional carryover.Conclusion and RelevanceFIVR with debriefing is a feasible and engaging approach for chronic pain intervention, with the potential to enhance self-efficacy and functional outcomes.

title: Clarifying the Concept of "Unanticipated Transfer to the ICU": A Scoping Review.
abstract: Unanticipated transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU), typically defined as an unscheduled escalation of care from inpatient general wards, is widely used in clinical research as a marker of adverse events, clinical deterioration, and system failure. However, its conceptual meaning, definition, and operationalization vary substantially across the literature, complicating interpretation and cross-study comparison. We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to map how unanticipated ICU transfers are defined, framed, and used in empirical research. Searches of PubMed, CINAHL, and Web of Science identified 4,019 studies through August 7, 2025. After removing duplicates, 2,092 studies were screened for title and abstract, 565 underwent full-text review, and 219 studies met the inclusion criteria. Most studies were observational studies and terminology varied widely, with "unplanned admission to ICU" being the most common. Definitions were heterogeneous but generally focused on unscheduled ICU admission from inpatient wards, often excluding transfers from the emergency department or operating room and sometimes incorporating triggers such as rapid response activation or time-based thresholds. Unanticipated ICU transfer was predominantly used as a dependent variable and was overwhelmingly framed as a negative outcome or proxy for clinical deterioration. However, a smaller body of literature conceptualized these transfers as appropriate or beneficial escalations of care, particularly when occurring early in the course of deterioration. Our findings highlight definitional and conceptual inconsistency and suggest that unanticipated ICU transfer is a context-dependent process measure influenced by both patient condition and institutional factors. Greater standardization and a reframing toward appropriateness and timing of escalation may improve its utility in research and practice.

title: Tryptophan metabolomic profiling in persons with and without HIV.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Full tryptophan (T) profiling allows determination of T-metabolites from the serotonin, kynurenine (K) and gut-integrity/indole pathways. We assessed T-metabolites, depressive symptoms, cognitive function and sleep measures in persons with and without HIV.
METHODS: Persons with HIV on ART and lifestyle-similar persons without HIV completed depressive symptoms questionnaire (PHQ-9), cognitive testing (T-score), actigraphy sleep measures and early morning fasting blood sampling for metabolomic profiling (LC-MS, UK National Phenome Centre). Statistical analysis used Mann-Whitney U tests and Spearman rank correlation.
RESULTS: Of 468 individuals (345 with HIV), 81% were male individuals and median age was 58 (IQR 53-63) years. Several metabolites, including K, K/T ratio, citrulline and 5-hydroxyindole-acetic-acid, differed in those with and without HIV. Median (IQR) PHQ-9 scores were 5 (1-10) and 1 (0-3) in those with and without HIV, respectively. In those with HIV, higher PHQ-9 scores were associated with higher K-pathway markers [quinolinic acid (P = 0.05), K (P = 0.02) and K/T ratio (P = 0.02)] but associations were generally weaker in those without HIV. Cognitive testing T-score [with HIV: 50 (44-54.9); without HIV: 52 (48.3-55.8)] was positively associated with higher gut-integrity/indole-markers in those with HIV [citrulline (P < 0.0001), indole-3-acetic-acid (P < 0.0001)], but less so in those without HIV. No associations between any actigraphy sleep measures and T-metabolites were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: K-pathway metabolites (driven by peripheral inflammatory responses) are associated with depressive symptoms and metabolites of gut health associated with cognitive function in those with HIV; these observations were less evident in those without HIV. Further understanding of these mechanisms could assist the development of future therapeutic interventions.

title: Pharmacist-driven allergy to beta-lactam evaluation in the emergency department.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Penicillin (PCN) is the most common drug allergy in medical records and have been linked to suboptimal antibiotic regimens and negative externalities.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the successful de-labeling of PCN allergies following the implementation of a pharmacist-driven PCN de-labeling protocol in an emergency department (ED) PRACTICE DESCRIPTION: VA Indiana Healthcare System (VAIHCS) is a tertiary level 1A VAMC that registers about 30,000 ED visits annually.
PRACTICE INNOVATION: An Allergy to Beta-Lactam Evaluation (ABLE) VA template is available that guides pharmacists through allergy history and provides recommendations on alternative beta-lactam agents. Although a recent pharmacist-led efforts in ED has been described, literature specifically in the ED remains limited.
EVALUATION METHODS: This study included patients who presented to the ED over a six-month period and underwent the ABLE protocol. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients whose PCN allergy was de-labeled. Secondary outcomes included the percentage of patients de-labeled within the ED versus de-labeled at follow-up, percentage of patients presenting to the ED with a PCN allergy compared to the number of patients de-labeled, and the number of patients who received beta-lactam antibiotics immediately following pharmacist assessment.
RESULTS: From May 15, 2024, to October 31, 2024, 44 patients met inclusion criteria. A total of 64% (28/44) had their PCN allergy de-labeled. Of the 28 patients de-labeled, 75% (21/28) were de-labeled via direct oral amoxicillin challenge, and the remainder were de-labeled based on allergy history review alone. Following de-labeling, 36% (10/28) received a beta-lactam antibiotic during the same ED visit. No adverse reactions were observed. There was a 95% follow-up rate at 72 hours post amoxicillin challenge.
CONCLUSION: A pharmacist-led PCN de-labeling protocol in the ED is feasible, safe, and facilitates access to beta-lactam antibiotics for eligible patients, while highlighting practical barriers that must be addressed for broader implementation.

title: A Phase 2b Randomized Trial of Belimumab to Reduce Atherogenic Autoantibodies in COPD Patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We hypothesized autoantibodies with specificity for glucose-regulated protein 78 (anti-GRP78), a ubiquitous heat shock protein and key component of the unfolded protein response (UPR), are associated with development of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patients. Treatments focused on the underlying autoimmune processes reduce CVD events in those afflicted with connective tissue diseases, but analogous therapies have not yet been tested in COPD patients, in whom atherosclerotic disease is a significant cause of mortality.
METHODS: Plasma anti-GRP78 IgG was measured by ELISA in two independent cohorts of COPD subjects who had coronary artery calcium (CAC) determinations by chest CT. Another COPD cohort was randomized to belimumab (10 mg/kg i.v. every two weeks x 3, followed by five monthly infusions) (n=10) or placebo (n=6). The primary endpoint was changes of circulating anti-GRP78 levels.
RESULTS: Anti-GRP78 levels in COPD patients (n=37) were highly correlated with CAC scores (rs=0.56, p<0.001). Autoantibody concentrations were reduced by ~17% (from 0.50+0.11 to 0.40+0.09 OD units, p=0.02) but unchanged by placebo (p=0.75) , and the reductions were proportionate to pre-treatment autoantibody levels (rs=-0.65, p=0.05). There were no reductions of protective anti-pneumococcal antibody levels or serious adverse events definitively attributable to belimumab treatment.
CONCLUSION: Belimumab therapy reduces circulating anti-GRP78 autoantibodies, which have been linked to CVD and other COPD comorbidities. Autoantibody reduction may be a novel approach to mitigate COPD-associated. These findings support a larger trial to thoroughly assess efficacy and safety of belimumab, or other specific autoimmune-targeted therapies, in COPD patients with CVD.

title: Meeting Bouted versus Non-Bouted Physical Activity Guidelines and Health Outcomes in CARDIA.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical activity (MVPA) guidelines recommend ≥150 minutes/week. Initial guidelines required bouts lasting ≥10 minutes, yet recent guidelines include non-bouted MVPA, despite less established benefits. This analysis sought to compare associations of meeting bouted vs. non-bouted MVPA guidelines on incident hypertension, diabetes, ≥10% weight gain, and cardiorespiratory endurance.
METHODS: This secondary analysis in the CARDIA cohort study used 15-year follow-up data during midlife. Participants (n=1,924) recruited from four U.S. centers wore an ActiGraph 7164 when 38-55 years old. Accelerometer data were used to define three groups: below guidelines, meeting non-bouted guidelines only, and meeting bouted guidelines. Incident stage 2 hypertension, diabetes, and ≥10% weight gain were assessed during clinical visits at baseline and 5-, 10-, and 15-year follow-up. Follow-up cardiorespiratory endurance was estimated by a 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at the 15-year follow-up. Associations between MVPA guideline group and outcomes were evaluated using survival analysis or ordinal logistic regression in nested models with progressive covariate adjustment.
RESULTS: Mean MVPA differed across groups: below guidelines, 93±36 minutes/week; non-bouted guidelines, 291±120 minutes/week; bouted guidelines, 551±530 minutes/week (p<0.001). Prior to adjustment, hypertension-free, diabetes-free, and ≥10% weight gain-free survival, and follow-up endurance were higher in those meeting bouted guidelines compared to other groups. After covariate adjustment, meeting bouted guidelines remained associated with lower risk of ≥10% weight gain (hazard ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.48, 0.92) and higher endurance (odds ratio, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.47, 3.30). When meeting guidelines and controlling for MVPA volume, a greater proportion of bouted vs. non-bouted MVPA was associated with higher endurance only.
CONCLUSIONS: Meeting recommendations with bouted MVPA compared to non-bouted MVPA may provide greater health benefits for weight control and endurance.
